# Getting Started

Source: https://dartondox.dev/latest/3.x

<div class="dox-hero" markdown>

<div class="dox-hero__text" markdown>

<img class="dox-hero__mascot" src="assets/mascot.png" alt="Doxie, the Dox mascot" width="140" height="137">

# Fast backends<br>in Dart

<p class="dox-hero__lead"><strong>Write in Dart. Serve with Rust.</strong></p>

<p class="dox-hero__lead">
Dox is a web backend framework for Dart, like Laravel.
Routing, an ORM, migrations, validation, auth and a CLI come in one place.
It runs one isolate per CPU core and builds to a small native binary.
</p>

<p class="dox-hero__actions" markdown>
[Build your first API](tutorial/index.md){ .md-button .md-button--primary }
[GitHub](https://github.com/dartondox/dox){ .md-button }
</p>

</div>

<div class="dox-hero__code" markdown>

```dart
Route.get('/blogs', BlogController.index); // (1)!

enum Status { active, draft }

@Dto() // (2)!
class BlogFilter {
  final Status status; // ?status=active, else 422
  const BlogFilter({required this.status});
  static const DtoSchema<BlogFilter> schema =
      $BlogFilterDto; // (3)!
}

class BlogController {
  static Future<List<Blog>> index(
    BlogFilter query, // (4)!
  ) async {
    return Blog()
        .where('status', query.status.name)
        .get(); // (5)!
  }
}
```

1.  A route points at a static method. No reflection, no controller registry.
2.  `@Dto()` marks an input class. `build_runner` generates the checks from the fields and their types.
3.  The generated schema. The same schema feeds the OpenAPI docs.
4.  Ask for the DTO as a parameter. Dox reads the query (or the body), checks it, and gives you a typed object. Bad input gets a `422` before your code runs.
5.  The ORM. The same code runs on Postgres, MySQL and SQLite, through native Rust drivers.

</div>

</div>

## How fast

<div class="dox-bench" markdown>

<p class="dox-bench__title">1.5× Bun. 2.3× Go. 7× plain Dart.</p>
<p class="dox-bench__sub">A real route: read one row from Postgres and return JSON (<code>GET /db</code>). Requests per second on one CPU core, higher is better.</p>

  </div>
</div>

<p class="dox-bench__foot"><span>Dox 3.0.0-alpha.3 · Bun 1.4 · Go 1.27 · Dart 3.13 · Postgres 18 · 256 connections · wrk · median of 3 runs</span><a href="digging-deeper/performance/#app-benchmark">All results</a></p>

</div>

Dox also has the lowest p99 (the slowest 1% of requests). Your code is plain
Dart. The speed comes from the Rust HTTP server and the Rust database drivers
that Dox uses by default. On 2 cores Dox stays ahead on the database routes.
Without a database (`GET /json`), Bun is faster.
See [Performance](digging-deeper/performance.md) for every route and how to run the benchmark yourself.

!!! warning "You are reading the 3.x docs (alpha)"
    `3.0.0-alpha.4` is a preview. Things can still change before the stable release.

## Run it in two minutes

You need [Dart](https://dart.dev/get-dart) 3.13 or newer. Nothing else: the
starter project uses SQLite, so there is no database to install.

```bash
dart pub global activate dox 3.0.0-alpha.4   # install the CLI
dox create my_app                            # download the starter project
cd my_app
dart pub get
cp .env.example .env
dox s                                        # start the server
```

Open a second terminal and call the first route:

```bash
curl localhost:3000/ping
```

```text
pong
```

That is a Dox app. Keep going with the [tutorial](tutorial/index.md): it adds a
model, a database table, validation, login and a Docker image, one short step
at a time.

!!! note "The CLI is not found?"
    `dart pub global activate` puts `dox` in `$HOME/.pub-cache/bin`.
    Add that folder to your `PATH`. See [Installation](the-basic/installation.md).

## Pick your path

| You are... | Start here | Then |
| --- | --- | --- |
| New to Dox | [Tutorial: build a blog API](tutorial/index.md) | [Routing](the-basic/routing.md), [Request](the-basic/request.md), [Validation](the-basic/validation.md) |
| Coming from Laravel | [Coming from Laravel](concepts/coming-from-laravel.md) | [How Dox works](concepts/how-dox-works.md) |
| Looking for one answer | [Guides](guides/index.md) (uploads, auth, Docker, pagination...) | [Reference](reference/index.md) |
| Going to production | [Deployment](digging-deeper/deployment.md) | [Docker](guides/docker.md), [Troubleshooting](reference/troubleshooting.md) |

## What you get

<div class="grid cards" markdown>

-   :material-lightning-bolt: **Fast by default**

    A Rust HTTP server, one isolate per CPU core and streamed bodies.
    `dox build` makes one native binary. See [Performance](digging-deeper/performance.md).

-   :material-database-outline: **ORM and query builder**

    Models, relations, migrations and transactions for Postgres, MySQL/MariaDB and SQLite,
    with native Rust drivers. See [Database](database/index.md).

-   :material-check-decagram-outline: **Typed validation**

    Write a `@Dto` class. Dox checks the input and gives your controller a typed object.
    See [Validation](the-basic/validation.md).

-   :material-file-document-outline: **OpenAPI**

    OpenAPI 3.1 docs and a Scalar docs page, made from your routes and DTOs.
    See [`dox_openapi`](packages/openapi.md).

-   :material-folder-outline: **File storage**

    Local disk and S3 behind one API, with signed URLs. See [`dox_storage`](packages/storage.md).

-   :material-cached: **Cache**

    Memory, file and Redis cache with tags and locks. See [`dox_cache`](packages/cache.md).

-   :material-access-point: **Real time**

    [WebSocket](digging-deeper/websocket.md) or [Socket.IO](packages/socketio.md), with Redis for many servers.

-   :material-shield-lock-outline: **Security**

    JWT [authentication](security/authentication.md), [CORS](security/cors.md),
    [encryption](security/encryption.md) and [hashing](security/hashing.md).

-   :material-console: **CLI**

    Create projects, controllers, models and migrations. Run, build and migrate.
    See [CLI reference](reference/cli.md).

</div>

- Want to help? Read [Contribute](others/contribute.md).

# Installation

Source: https://dartondox.dev/latest/3.xthe-basic/installation/

# Installation

This page shows how to install the Dox CLI, make a new project and start the server.

!!! warning "3.x is alpha"
    The latest version is `3.0.0-alpha.4`. It needs **Dart 3.13** or newer.

## Install the CLI

```bash
dart pub global activate dox 3.0.0-alpha.4
```

Check that it works:

```bash
dox version
```

!!! warning "`dox: command not found`"
    The shell can not find the CLI when the pub `bin` folder is not in your `PATH`.
    Add this line to `~/.bashrc` or `~/.zshrc`, then open a new terminal:

    ```bash
    export PATH="$PATH":"$HOME/.pub-cache/bin"
    ```

## Create a new project

```bash
dox create new_blog
```

`dox create` downloads the newest 3.x release of
[dox-sample](https://github.com/dartondox/dox-sample), the starter project.
To get one exact version, add `--version`:

```bash
dox create new_blog --version 3.0.0-alpha.4
```

Then get the packages and make your `.env` file:

```bash
cd new_blog
dart pub get
cp .env.example .env
```

The starter project uses SQLite, so there is no database to install.
The file `db/dox.sqlite` is created at the first start.
To use Postgres or MySQL instead, change `DB_CONNECTION` and the `DB_*`
values in `.env`. See [Database](../database/index.md).

!!! info "Add Dox to an existing Dart project"
    Add the packages you need to `pubspec.yaml`. All Dox packages share one
    version, so use `^3.0.0-alpha.4` for each of them.

```yaml title="pubspec.yaml"
dependencies:
  dox_core: ^3.0.0-alpha.4
  dox_orm: ^3.0.0-alpha.4
  dox_migration: ^3.0.0-alpha.4

dev_dependencies:
  dox_builder: ^3.0.0-alpha.4
  build_runner: ^2.17.1
```

## Start the server

```bash
dox s
```

`dox s` does two things:

- It runs `dart run build_runner watch`, so generated files stay up to date.
- It runs `dart run bin/server.dart`, and restarts it when a `.dart` file changes.

To skip the builder, use `dox s --ignore-build-runner`.
To start the server without the CLI, run `dart run bin/server.dart`.

At the first start it also runs the migrations in `db/migration`.
The server uses the port in `APP_PORT` in the `.env` file (`3000` by default).
Check it:

```bash
curl localhost:3000/ping
```

```text
pong
```

## Start the server with Docker

```bash
docker-compose up -d --build
```

!!! tip "Production"
    Do not use `dox s` or `dart run` in production.
    Build a native binary with `dox build`. See [Deployment](../digging-deeper/deployment.md).

## Run the code generator

Dox makes code for models and DTOs with `build_runner`.
`dox s` already runs it. To run it alone:

```bash
dox build_runner:watch   # runs again on every file change
dox build_runner:build   # runs once
```

## Packages

All Dox packages use the same version.

| Package | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `dox` | the CLI |
| `dox_core` | HTTP server, routing, requests, responses, validation |
| `dox_orm` | query builder and models |
| `dox_migration` | database migrations |
| `dox_auth` | JWT authentication |
| `dox_websocket` | WebSocket server |
| `dox_builder`, `dox_annotation` | code generation for models and DTOs |
| `dox_validation` | [typed validation schemas](../packages/validation.md) |
| `dox_openapi` | [OpenAPI docs](../packages/openapi.md) |
| `dox_storage` | [file storage: local, S3](../packages/storage.md) |
| `dox_cache` | [cache: memory, file, Redis](../packages/cache.md) |
| `dox_socketio` | [Socket.IO server](../packages/socketio.md) |
| `dox_http_native` | [native HTTP server](../digging-deeper/native-server.md) (Rust) |
| `dox_postgres_native`, `dox_mysql_native` | native database drivers for Postgres and MySQL/MariaDB |


---

# Build a blog API

Source: https://dartondox.dev/latest/3.xtutorial/

# Build a blog API

This tutorial takes you from an empty folder to a small blog API that runs as one native binary.
Every step has the full code and a `curl` command to check it.

The finished project is on GitHub: [examples/blog-api](https://github.com/dartondox/dox/tree/develop/examples/blog-api).
CI builds it and runs its tests on every push, so the code on these pages keeps working.

## What you will build

A JSON API for blog posts.

| Method | Path | Who | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `GET` | `/api/posts` | anyone | list all posts |
| `GET` | `/api/posts/{id}` | anyone | one post, or `404` |
| `POST` | `/api/posts` | logged in user | make a post (`201`, or `422` on bad input) |
| `PUT` | `/api/posts/{id}` | logged in user | change a post |
| `POST` | `/api/auth/register` | anyone | make an account, get a token |
| `POST` | `/api/auth/login` | anyone | log in, get a token |
| `GET` | `/api/auth/user` | logged in user | the user of the token |

You will use these parts of Dox:

- a model and a Dart migration (`dox_orm`, `dox_migration`),
- a controller and routes,
- a `@Dto` class for checked input,
- JWT login with `dox_auth`,
- one HTTP test,
- `dox build` for a native binary, and the `Dockerfile`.

## What you need

- Dart **3.13** or newer: `dart --version`.
- `curl`, to call the API.
- About 15 minutes.

You do not need Docker or a database server. The app uses SQLite, which is one file in your project.

## The steps

1. [Create the project](01-create-project.md)
2. [Model and migration](02-model-and-migration.md)
3. [Routes and controller](03-routes-and-controller.md)
4. [Validation](04-validation.md)
5. [Login with dox_auth](05-auth.md)
6. [Test](06-test.md)
7. [Build and deploy](07-build-and-deploy.md)

## The finished project

Files that you make or change in this tutorial are marked with `*`.

```text
blog/
├── bin/
│   ├── migrate.dart              runs the dox migration:* commands
│   └── server.dart               runs the migrations, starts the server
├── db/migration/
│   ├── ..._create_posts_table.dart   *
│   ├── ..._create_users_table.dart
│   └── migrations.dart           the list of migrations (Dox writes it)
├── lib/
│   ├── app/http/controllers/
│   │   ├── auth.controller.dart  *
│   │   └── post.controller.dart  *
│   ├── app/http/dtos/
│   │   ├── login_user.dto.dart   *
│   │   ├── register_user.dto.dart *
│   │   └── save_post.dto.dart    *
│   ├── app/models/
│   │   ├── post/post.model.dart  *
│   │   └── user/user.model.dart
│   ├── config/
│   │   ├── app.dart              * adds the DTO list
│   │   ├── database.dart
│   │   ├── env.dart              the .env keys, typed
│   │   └── services.dart         * adds AuthService
│   ├── routes/api.dart           *
│   ├── services/
│   │   ├── auth_service.dart     *
│   │   └── orm_service.dart
│   └── dtos.g.dart               * generated
├── test/http_test.dart           *
├── .env                          *
├── Dockerfile
└── pubspec.yaml                  * adds dox_auth
```

Start with [step 1: create the project](01-create-project.md).


---

# Step 1: Create the project

Source: https://dartondox.dev/latest/3.xtutorial/01-create-project/

# Step 1: Create the project

This step makes a new Dox project, points it at SQLite, starts the dev server and calls the first route.

## 1. Install the CLI and make the project

```bash
dart pub global activate dox 3.0.0-alpha.4
dox create blog
cd blog
dart pub get
```

`dox create` downloads the [dox-sample](https://github.com/dartondox/dox-sample) template from GitHub and names the package `blog`.
So every import in this tutorial starts with `package:blog/`.

!!! note "Check the versions"
    Open `pubspec.yaml`. Every Dox package must be `^3.0.0-alpha.4`.
    If the template has an older version, change it and run `dart pub get` again.

## 2. Use SQLite

Copy the example env file:

```bash
cp .env.example .env
```

The template already uses SQLite. These are the lines that matter:

```ini title=".env"
APP_PORT=3000
APP_KEY=KKep5qC6uHlAgrwaQTQewgMRSIqQnoj0

DB_CONNECTION=sqlite
DB_NAME=db/dox.sqlite
```

Dox makes the file `db/dox.sqlite` at the first start. The `db` folder is
in the template. The `DB_HOST`, `DB_PORT`, `DB_USERNAME` and `DB_PASSWORD`
lines are for Postgres and MySQL. SQLite does not read them.

The app reads these keys through `lib/config/env.dart`. It is a typed class,
so `env.appPort` is an `int` and reads `APP_PORT`. A missing `APP_KEY` stops
the app at start. See [Environment variables](../digging-deeper/env.md).

!!! note "The folder must exist"
    Dox makes the database file when it is missing, but not its folder.
    If you set `DB_NAME=storage/blog.sqlite`, run `mkdir storage` first.

## 3. Start the server

```bash
dox s
```

`dox s` runs the code generator (`build_runner watch`) and `dart run bin/server.dart`.
It restarts the server when you save a `.dart` file.
The first start takes a little longer. It prints `Running build hooks...` while it compiles the SQLite library.

The last line is:

```text
Server started at http://[::]:3000 with 8 isolate (native)
```

`[::]` means the app listens on all network interfaces. Open it at `http://localhost:3000`.
The number of isolates is the number of CPU cores on your machine.

## Check it

In a second terminal:

```bash
curl -i http://localhost:3000/api/ping
```

```text
HTTP/1.1 200 OK
content-type: text/plain; charset=utf-8
...

pong
```

The route is in `lib/routes/api.dart`. The `ApiRouter` has the prefix `api`, so `/ping` is served at `/api/ping`.

## Next

[Step 2: Model and migration](02-model-and-migration.md)


---

# Step 2: Model and migration

Source: https://dartondox.dev/latest/3.xtutorial/02-model-and-migration/

# Step 2: Model and migration

This step makes the `posts` table with a Dart migration and a `Post` model for it.

## 1. Make the model and the migration

```bash
dox create:model Post -m
```

This makes two files and updates one:

| File | What it is |
| --- | --- |
| `lib/app/models/post/post.model.dart` | the model (new) |
| `db/migration/<date>_create_posts_table.dart` | the migration (new) |
| `db/migration/migrations.dart` | the list of all Dart migrations. Dox writes it. Do not edit it. |

The template already has `bin/migrate.dart`. The `dox migration:*` commands run it.

The numbers in the migration file name are the date and time when you ran the command.

## 2. Add the columns to the migration

Open the new file in `db/migration`. Add `title` and `body`:

```dart title="db/migration/2026_10_22_205345_create_posts_table.dart"
// ignore_for_file: file_names
import 'package:dox_migration/dox_migration.dart';

class CreatePostsTable extends Migration {
  @override
  Future<void> up(Schema schema) async {
    await schema.create('posts', (Table table) {
      table.id();
      table.string('title');
      table.text('body');
      table.timestamps();
    });
  }

  @override
  Future<void> down(Schema schema) async {
    await schema.dropIfExists('posts');
  }
}
```

- `table.id()` makes an auto increment primary key on every database.
- `table.timestamps()` makes `created_at` and `updated_at`. The model fills them.

## 3. Add the fields to the model

```dart title="lib/app/models/post/post.model.dart"
import 'package:dox_orm/dox_orm.dart';

part 'post.model.g.dart';

@DoxModel(table: 'posts')
class Post extends PostGenerator {
  @override
  List<String> get hidden => <String>[];

  @Column()
  String? title;

  @Column()
  String? body;
}
```

Every column field is nullable. A new `Post()` has no values yet.
`id`, `createdAt` and `updatedAt` come from `PostGenerator`. You do not declare them.

## 4. Run the migrations on server start

There is nothing to change here. The template's `bin/server.dart` already
runs the list from `db/migration/migrations.dart` before the server starts:

```dart title="bin/server.dart"
import '../db/migration/migrations.dart';

void main() async {
  Dox().initialize(appConfig);

  await Migrator(
    migrations: migrations,
    connection: await databaseConfig
        .getConnectionConfig()
        .getDatabaseConnection(),
  ).migrate();

  await Dox().startServer();
}
```

So the server runs new migrations each time it starts. This also works in the native binary of [step 7](07-build-and-deploy.md).

## 5. Run the migration and the generator

```bash
dox migration:run
```

```text
Migrating: 2026_10_22_205345_create_posts_table
Migrated: 2026_10_22_205345_create_posts_table
```

The model needs its generated file `post.model.g.dart`.
`dox s` makes it while it runs. If `dox s` is not running, run the generator once:

```bash
dart run build_runner build --delete-conflicting-outputs
```

## Check it

```bash
dox migration:status
```

```text
Migration                             Batch  Status
2026_10_22_205345_create_posts_table  1      Ran
```

## Next

[Step 3: Routes and controller](03-routes-and-controller.md)


---

# Step 3: Routes and controller

Source: https://dartondox.dev/latest/3.xtutorial/03-routes-and-controller/

# Step 3: Routes and controller

This step adds a resource controller and the routes to list, create and show posts.

## 1. Make the controller

```bash
dox create:controller Post -r
```

`-r` makes a resource controller with the seven CRUD methods.
Replace the file with this. It keeps only `index`, `store` and `show`:

```dart title="lib/app/http/controllers/post.controller.dart"
import 'package:blog/app/models/post/post.model.dart';
import 'package:dox_core/dox_core.dart';

class PostController {
  /// GET /api/posts
  Future<List<Post>> index(DoxRequest req) async {
    return Post().all();
  }

  /// POST /api/posts
  Future<DoxResponse> store(DoxRequest req) async {
    Post post = Post()
      ..title = req.input('title')
      ..body = req.input('body');
    await post.save();
    return response(post).statusCode(201);
  }

  /// GET /api/posts/{id}
  Future<Post> show(int id) async {
    Post? post = await Post().find(id);
    if (post == null) {
      throw NotFoundHttpException();
    }
    return post;
  }
}

PostController postController = PostController();
```

How it works:

- A controller returns a model or a list of models. Dox sends it as JSON.
- `response(post).statusCode(201)` sets the status code.
- `show(int id)` gets the `{id}` from the URL. `/api/posts/abc` answers `404`, because `abc` is not an `int`.
- `req.input('title')` reads the body as it is. It is not checked yet. [Step 4](04-validation.md) fixes that.

## 2. Add the routes

```dart title="lib/routes/api.dart"
import 'package:blog/app/http/controllers/api.controller.dart';
import 'package:blog/app/http/controllers/post.controller.dart';
import 'package:dox_core/dox_core.dart';

class ApiRouter extends Router {
  @override
  String get prefix => 'api';

  @override
  List<dynamic> get middleware => <dynamic>[];

  @override
  void register() {
    Route.get('/ping', apiController.pong);

    Route.resource('posts', postController);
  }
}
```

`Route.resource` makes one route for each method the controller has:

| Method | Path | Controller method |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `GET` | `/api/posts` | `index` |
| `POST` | `/api/posts` | `store` |
| `GET` | `/api/posts/{id}` | `show` |

The controller has no `update` or `destroy`, so those routes are not made.

## 3. Start the server

```bash
dox s
```

If it is still running from step 1, it restarts by itself.

## Check it

Make a post:

```bash
curl -i -X POST http://localhost:3000/api/posts \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"title":"Hello Dox","body":"My first post."}'
```

```text
HTTP/1.1 201 Created
content-type: application/json; charset=utf-8
...

{"id":1,"title":"Hello Dox","body":"My first post.","created_at":"2026-10-22T13:58:14.062215Z","updated_at":"2026-10-22T13:58:14.062215Z"}
```

List the posts:

```bash
curl http://localhost:3000/api/posts
```

```json
[{"id":1,"title":"Hello Dox","body":"My first post.","created_at":"2026-10-22T13:58:14.062215Z","updated_at":"2026-10-22T13:58:14.062215Z"}]
```

Show one post:

```bash
curl http://localhost:3000/api/posts/1
```

```json
{"id":1,"title":"Hello Dox","body":"My first post.","created_at":"2026-10-22T13:58:14.062215Z","updated_at":"2026-10-22T13:58:14.062215Z"}
```

A post that does not exist:

```bash
curl -i http://localhost:3000/api/posts/99
```

```text
HTTP/1.1 404 Not Found
...

{"code":"not_found","message":"Not Found"}
```

## Next

[Step 4: Validation](04-validation.md)

# Step 4: Validation

Source: https://dartondox.dev/latest/3.xtutorial/04-validation/

# Step 4: Validation

This step checks the input of create and update with a `@Dto` class. Bad input gets a `422` answer, and the controller does not run.

## 1. Make the DTO

```bash
dox create:dto SavePost
```

One class is enough for create and update, because both need the same fields.
Replace the file with this:

```dart title="lib/app/http/dtos/save_post.dto.dart"
import 'package:dox_core/dox_core.dart';

part 'save_post.dto.g.dart';

/// Typed, checked input. Run `dox build_runner:build` after a change.
@Dto()
class SavePost {
  @Trim()
  @Length(min: 3, max: 100)
  final String title;

  @Trim()
  @MinLength(10)
  final String body;

  const SavePost({required this.title, required this.body});

  static const DtoSchema<SavePost> schema = $SavePostDto;
}
```

- A field that is not nullable and has no default is required.
- The rules run from top to bottom. `@Trim()` removes spaces first. An empty string then counts as missing.
- See [Validation](../the-basic/validation.md) for all rules.

## 2. Give the DTO list to the app

The generator writes a list of all DTOs to `lib/dtos.g.dart`.
Dox needs this list, because it does not use reflection.
Add two lines to `lib/config/app.dart`:

```dart title="lib/config/app.dart"
import 'package:blog/dtos.g.dart';

AppConfig appConfig = AppConfig(
  /// DTOs (generated list in lib/dtos.g.dart)
  dtos: dtos,

  // ... the rest stays the same
);
```

## 3. Use the DTO in the controller

Ask for `SavePost` as a parameter. Dox checks the body and gives you a typed object.
This also adds `update`, so `PUT /api/posts/{id}` works:

```dart title="lib/app/http/controllers/post.controller.dart"
import 'package:blog/app/http/dtos/save_post.dto.dart';
import 'package:blog/app/models/post/post.model.dart';
import 'package:dox_core/dox_core.dart';

class PostController {
  /// GET /api/posts
  Future<List<Post>> index(DoxRequest req) async {
    return Post().all();
  }

  /// POST /api/posts
  Future<DoxResponse> store(SavePost body) async {
    Post post = Post()
      ..title = body.title
      ..body = body.body;
    await post.save();
    return response(post).statusCode(201);
  }

  /// GET /api/posts/{id}
  Future<Post> show(int id) async {
    return _find(id);
  }

  /// PUT /api/posts/{id}
  Future<Post> update(int id, SavePost body) async {
    Post post = await _find(id);
    post
      ..title = body.title
      ..body = body.body;
    await post.save();
    return post;
  }

  Future<Post> _find(int id) async {
    Post? post = await Post().find(id);
    if (post == null) {
      throw NotFoundHttpException();
    }
    return post;
  }
}

PostController postController = PostController();
```

`Route.resource` in `lib/routes/api.dart` sees the new `update` method and adds `PUT` and `PATCH /api/posts/{id}`. You change nothing there.

## 4. Run the generator

`dox s` runs it for you. Without `dox s`:

```bash
dart run build_runner build --delete-conflicting-outputs
```

It writes `lib/app/http/dtos/save_post.dto.g.dart` and `lib/dtos.g.dart`.

## Check it

A title that is too short, and a body that is too short:

```bash
curl -i -X POST http://localhost:3000/api/posts \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"title":"Hi","body":"Short"}'
```

```text
HTTP/1.1 422 Unprocessable Entity
content-type: application/json; charset=utf-8
...

{"title":"The title must be between 3 and 100 characters","body":"The body must be at least 10 characters"}
```

An empty body:

```bash
curl -X POST http://localhost:3000/api/posts \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{}'
```

```json
{"title":"The title is required","body":"The body is required"}
```

Good input still gives `201`:

```bash
curl -i -X POST http://localhost:3000/api/posts \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"title":"Second post","body":"Validation works now."}'
```

```text
HTTP/1.1 201 Created
```

Update the first post:

```bash
curl -X PUT http://localhost:3000/api/posts/1 \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"title":"Hello Dox (edited)","body":"My first post, edited."}'
```

```json
{"id":1,"title":"Hello Dox (edited)","body":"My first post, edited.","created_at":"2026-10-22T13:58:14.062215Z","updated_at":"2026-10-22T13:59:13.539886Z"}
```

[Step 5: Login with dox_auth](05-auth.md)

# Step 5: Login with dox_auth

Source: https://dartondox.dev/latest/3.xtutorial/05-auth/

# Step 5: Login with dox_auth

This step adds register and login with a JWT token, and only lets a logged in user create or change posts.

## 1. Add the package

```bash
dart pub add dox_auth:^3.0.0-alpha.4
```

## 2. Make the users table

The template already has a `User` model in `lib/app/models/user/user.model.dart`:

```dart title="lib/app/models/user/user.model.dart"
import 'package:dox_orm/dox_orm.dart';

part 'user.model.g.dart';

@DoxModel(table: 'users', softDelete: true)
class User extends UserGenerator {
  @override
  List<String> get hidden => <String>['password'];

  @Column()
  String? name;

  @Column()
  String? email;

  @Column()
  String? password;
}
```

`password` is in `hidden`, so it is never in the JSON. This matters: the token holds the user as JSON, and anyone can read a JWT.

The `users` table already exists. The template has its migration, and the
server ran it at the first start in [step 1](01-create-project.md):

```dart title="db/migration/2023_07_16_131937700_create_users_table.dart"
class CreateUsersTable extends Migration {
  @override
  Future<void> up(Schema schema) async {
    await schema.create('users', (Table table) {
      table.id();
      table.string('name');
      table.string('email').unique();
      table.string('password');
      table.softDeletes();
      table.timestamps();
    });
  }
  // ...
}
```

`table.softDeletes()` makes the `deleted_at` column that `softDelete: true` needs.
`email` is unique, so a second register with the same email fails.

## 3. Make the DTOs

```bash
dox create:dto RegisterUser
dox create:dto LoginUser
```

```dart title="lib/app/http/dtos/register_user.dto.dart"
import 'package:dox_core/dox_core.dart';
import 'package:dox_orm/dox_orm.dart' hide Schema;

part 'register_user.dto.g.dart';

@Dto()
class RegisterUser {
  @Trim()
  @Length(min: 2, max: 50)
  final String name;

  @Trim()
  @Lowercase()
  @Email()
  @Unique('users', column: 'email')
  final String email;

  @MinLength(8)
  final String password;

  const RegisterUser({
    required this.name,
    required this.email,
    required this.password,
  });

  static const DtoSchema<RegisterUser> schema = $RegisterUserDto;
}
```

`@Unique` comes from `dox_orm`. It reads the database, so it runs after the other rules.
`dox_orm` also has a class named `Schema`, so the import hides it.

```dart title="lib/app/http/dtos/login_user.dto.dart"
import 'package:dox_core/dox_core.dart';

part 'login_user.dto.g.dart';

@Dto()
class LoginUser {
  @Trim()
  @Lowercase()
  @Email()
  final String email;

  final String password;

  const LoginUser({required this.email, required this.password});

  static const DtoSchema<LoginUser> schema = $LoginUserDto;
}
```

## 4. Set up the auth service

A service runs once in every isolate at start. This one tells `dox_auth` which model to use and how to sign tokens:

```dart title="lib/services/auth_service.dart"
import 'package:blog/app/models/user/user.model.dart';
import 'package:blog/config/env.dart';
import 'package:dox_auth/dox_auth.dart';
import 'package:dox_core/dox_core.dart';

/// Auth service
/// --------------------------
/// Sets up JWT login with the User model.
/// Tokens are signed with APP_KEY and last 7 days.
class AuthService implements DoxService {
  @override
  void setup() {
    Auth.initialize(
      AuthConfig(
        defaultGuard: 'api',
        guards: <String, AuthGuard>{
          'api': AuthGuard(
            driver: JwtAuthDriver(
              secret: SecretKey(env.appKey),
              expiresIn: const Duration(days: 7),
            ),
            provider: AuthProvider(model: () => User()),
          ),
        },
      ),
    );
  }
}
```

Add it to the service list:

```dart title="lib/config/services.dart"
import 'package:blog/services/auth_service.dart';
import 'package:blog/services/orm_service.dart';
import 'package:dox_core/dox_core.dart';

/// Services to register on dox
/// -------------------------------
/// Since dox run on multi thread isolate, we need to register
/// below extra services to dox so that dox can
/// register again on new isolate.
List<DoxService> services = <DoxService>[ORMService(), AuthService()];
```

## 5. Write the auth controller

```dart title="lib/app/http/controllers/auth.controller.dart"
import 'package:blog/app/http/dtos/login_user.dto.dart';
import 'package:blog/app/http/dtos/register_user.dto.dart';
import 'package:blog/app/models/user/user.model.dart';
import 'package:dox_auth/dox_auth.dart';
import 'package:dox_core/dox_core.dart';

class AuthController {
  /// POST /api/auth/register
  Future<DoxResponse> register(RegisterUser body) async {
    User user = User()
      ..name = body.name
      ..email = body.email
      ..password = Hash.make(body.password);
    await user.save();

    String? token = Auth().login(user);
    return response(<String, dynamic>{
      'token': token,
      'user': user,
    }).statusCode(201);
  }

  /// POST /api/auth/login
  Future<Map<String, dynamic>> login(LoginUser body) async {
    Auth auth = Auth();
    String? token = await auth.attempt(<String, dynamic>{
      'email': body.email,
      'password': body.password,
    });
    if (token == null) {
      throw UnAuthorizedException(message: 'Wrong email or password');
    }
    return <String, dynamic>{'token': token, 'user': auth.user<User>()};
  }

  /// GET /api/auth/user
  User? user(DoxRequest req) {
    return req.auth?.user<User>();
  }
}

AuthController authController = AuthController();
```

- `Hash.make()` makes a bcrypt hash. Never save a plain password.
- `Auth().attempt()` finds the user by email and checks the password. It gives a token, or `null`.
- `Auth().login(user)` gives a token without a password check. Register uses it, because the user was just made.

## 6. Protect the write routes

Replace `Route.resource` with single routes. The routes inside `Route.middleware` need a valid token:

```dart title="lib/routes/api.dart"
import 'package:blog/app/http/controllers/api.controller.dart';
import 'package:blog/app/http/controllers/auth.controller.dart';
import 'package:blog/app/http/controllers/post.controller.dart';
import 'package:dox_auth/dox_auth.dart';
import 'package:dox_core/dox_core.dart';

class ApiRouter extends Router {
  @override
  String get prefix => 'api';

  @override
  List<dynamic> get middleware => <dynamic>[];

  @override
  void register() {
    Route.get('/ping', apiController.pong);

    // Anyone can read posts.
    Route.get('/posts', postController.index);
    Route.get('/posts/{id}', postController.show);

    // Register and log in.
    Route.post('/auth/register', authController.register);
    Route.post('/auth/login', authController.login);

    // Only a logged in user can write posts.
    Route.middleware(<dynamic>[AuthMiddleware()], () {
      Route.get('/auth/user', authController.user);
      Route.post('/posts', postController.store);
      Route.put('/posts/{id}', postController.update);
    });
  }
}
```

`AuthMiddleware` reads the `Authorization: Bearer <token>` header and loads the user.
When the token is missing or wrong, it answers `401 Authentication failed`.

## 7. Migrate and generate

```bash
dox migration:run
dart run build_runner build --delete-conflicting-outputs
```

`dox s` runs the migration and the generator for you when it restarts.

## Check it

Register:

```bash
curl -i -X POST http://localhost:3000/api/auth/register \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"name":"Ann","email":"ann@example.com","password":"secret123"}'
```

```text
HTTP/1.1 201 Created
content-type: application/json; charset=utf-8
...

{"token":"eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiIs...","user":{"id":1,"name":"Ann","email":"ann@example.com","created_at":"2026-10-22T14:01:07.827769Z","updated_at":"2026-10-22T14:01:07.827769Z"}}
```

The same email again gives `422`:

```json
{"email":"The email has already been taken"}
```

A wrong password gives `401`:

```bash
curl -i -X POST http://localhost:3000/api/auth/login \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"email":"ann@example.com","password":"wrong"}'
```

```text
HTTP/1.1 401 Unauthorized
...

{"code":"unauthorized","message":"Wrong email or password"}
```

Log in and keep the token in a shell variable:

```bash
TOKEN=$(curl -s -X POST http://localhost:3000/api/auth/login \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"email":"ann@example.com","password":"secret123"}' \
  | sed -E 's/.*"token":"([^"]+)".*/\1/')
echo $TOKEN
```

A post without a token is refused:

```bash
curl -i -X POST http://localhost:3000/api/posts \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"title":"Third post","body":"Written with a token."}'
```

```text
HTTP/1.1 401 Unauthorized
...

{"code":"unauthorized","message":"Authentication failed"}
```

With the token it works:

```bash
curl -i -X POST http://localhost:3000/api/posts \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"title":"Third post","body":"Written with a token."}'
```

```text
HTTP/1.1 201 Created
...

{"id":3,"title":"Third post","body":"Written with a token.","created_at":"2026-10-22T14:01:08.094211Z","updated_at":"2026-10-22T14:01:08.094211Z"}
```

Who am I:

```bash
curl http://localhost:3000/api/auth/user -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN"
```

```json
{"id":1,"name":"Ann","email":"ann@example.com","created_at":"2026-10-22T14:01:07.827769Z","updated_at":"2026-10-22T14:01:07.827769Z"}
```

No `password` in the answer, because it is in `hidden`.

## Next

[Step 6: Test](06-test.md)

# Step 6: Test

Source: https://dartondox.dev/latest/3.xtutorial/06-test/

# Step 6: Test

This step writes one HTTP test for the list route and runs it.

## 1. Write the test

The template has `test/http_test.dart`. Replace it with this:

```dart title="test/http_test.dart"
import 'dart:convert';

import 'package:blog/config/app.dart';
import 'package:blog/config/database.dart';
import 'package:dox_core/dox_core.dart';
import 'package:dox_migration/dox_migration.dart';
import 'package:http/http.dart' as http;
import 'package:test/test.dart';

import '../db/migration/migrations.dart';

String baseUrl = 'http://localhost:${appConfig.serverPort}';

void main() {
  setUpAll(() async {
    Dox().initialize(appConfig);
    Dox().totalIsolate(1);
    await Migrator(
      migrations: migrations,
      connection: await databaseConfig
          .getConnectionConfig()
          .getDatabaseConnection(),
    ).migrate();
    await Dox().startServer();
  });

  tearDownAll(() async {
    await Dox().server.close();
  });

  test('GET /api/posts gives a list', () async {
    http.Response response = await http.get(Uri.parse('$baseUrl/api/posts'));
    expect(response.statusCode, 200);
    expect(jsonDecode(response.body), isA<List<dynamic>>());
  });
}
```

- The test starts the real server once, on one isolate. One isolate starts faster.
- It runs the migrations first, so the test also works on an empty database.
- `package:test` and `package:http` are already in `dev_dependencies` of the template.

## 2. Stop the dev server

The test listens on the same port as `dox s`. Stop `dox s` with `Ctrl+C` first.

## Check it

```bash
dart test test/http_test.dart
```

```text
00:01 +1: All tests passed!
```

!!! tip "Use another database for tests"
    The test uses the `.env` file, so it reads and writes `db/dox.sqlite`.
    To keep test data out of it, set another file for the test run:
    `DB_NAME=test.sqlite dart test test/http_test.dart`.

## Next

[Step 7: Build and deploy](07-build-and-deploy.md)

# Step 7: Build and deploy

Source: https://dartondox.dev/latest/3.xtutorial/07-build-and-deploy/

# Step 7: Build and deploy

This step compiles the app to one native binary, runs it, and shows the `Dockerfile` of the project.

!!! warning "Never run production with `dox s` or `dart run`"
    They use the JIT compiler. It needs about 25 times more memory and starts slower.
    Build a native (AOT) binary for production.

## 1. Build the binary

```bash
dox build
```

```text
Built with build_runner/aot in 1s; wrote 0 outputs.
Running build hooks...Running link hooks...
Generated: /.../blog/build/bundle/bin/server
[Dox] Built build/bundle. Run it with: cd build/bundle && ./bin/server
```

`dox build` runs the code generator, then `dart build cli --target bin/server.dart --output build`.
The result is in `build/bundle`:

| Path | What it is |
| --- | --- |
| `bin/server` | the binary, about 10 MB. It needs no Dart SDK. |
| `lib/` | native libraries from build hooks, like `libsqlite3`. Keep it next to `bin/`. |
| `db/` | your migrations |

## 2. Run the binary

The binary reads `.env` from the folder you start it in. Copy yours there,
and make the `db` folder for the SQLite file:

```bash
cd build/bundle
cp ../../.env .env
mkdir -p db
./bin/server
```

```text
Migrating: 2023_07_16_131937700_create_users_table
Migrated: 2023_07_16_131937700_create_users_table
Migrating: 2026_10_22_205345_create_posts_table
Migrated: 2026_10_22_205345_create_posts_table
Server started at http://[::]:3000 with 8 isolate (native)
```

The migrations run again, because `DB_NAME=db/dox.sqlite` is a new file in `build/bundle`.
The registry in `db/migration/migrations.dart` is compiled into the binary, so this works without the source code.

A real environment variable wins over `.env`. So on a server you can skip the `.env` file and set the values in the environment.

## Check it

In a second terminal:

```bash
curl http://localhost:3000/api/ping
curl http://localhost:3000/api/posts
```

```text
pong
[]
```

The list is empty, because this is a new database file. Stop the server with `Ctrl+C`.

## 3. Docker

The project has a `Dockerfile`. It builds the same bundle in a `dart:stable` image and copies it to an empty (`scratch`) image. The final image holds only the binary, the native libraries and the migrations:

```dockerfile title="Dockerfile"
FROM dart:stable AS build

# Resolve dependencies first, so this layer is cached.
WORKDIR /app
COPY pubspec.* ./
RUN dart pub get

COPY . .
RUN dart pub get --offline
RUN dart run build_runner build --delete-conflicting-outputs

# `dart build cli` is AOT like `dart compile exe`, and it also runs
# build hooks. Native libraries go to build/bundle/lib.
RUN dart build cli --target bin/server.dart --output build

# Lay out the final file tree:
# /app/bin/server, /app/lib (native libraries), /app/db/migration,
# /app/storage and a writable /tmp (uploads bigger than 1 MB are
# streamed to a temp file).
RUN mkdir -p /out/app/storage /out/tmp \
  && chmod 1777 /out/tmp \
  && cp -r build/bundle/. /out/app/ \
  && cp -r db /out/app/db \
  # the native HTTP server (Rust) needs libgcc_s, which /runtime/ does not have
  && LIBGCC=$(find / -name libgcc_s.so.1 -path '*lib*' | head -n 1) \
  && mkdir -p /out$(dirname $LIBGCC) && cp $LIBGCC /out$LIBGCC

# Minimal serving image: the AOT runtime files from the dart image
# (`/runtime/`) plus our bundle. No Dart SDK, no source code.
FROM scratch
COPY --from=build /runtime/ /
COPY --from=build /out/ /
WORKDIR /app

# Config comes from env variables. The image has no .env file,
# so secrets stay out of it.
EXPOSE 3000
CMD ["/app/bin/server"]
```

Build and run it. The image has no `.env` file, so pass the config as environment variables:

```bash
docker build -t blog .
docker run -p 3000:3000 \
  -e APP_KEY=change-me \
  -e DB_CONNECTION=sqlite \
  -e DB_NAME=storage/blog.sqlite \
  blog
```

!!! note "SQLite in Docker"
    The database file lives inside the container. It is lost when the container is removed.
    Mount a volume for it: `-v blog-data:/app/storage`.
    For a busy app, use Postgres or MySQL. See [Database](../database/index.md).

## Where to go next

- [Deployment](../digging-deeper/deployment.md): HTTPS with a proxy, systemd, many machines.
- [Model](../database/model/index.md): relationships, events, serializers.
- [Authentication](../security/authentication.md): all options of `dox_auth`.
- [OpenAPI](../packages/openapi.md): API docs from your routes and DTOs.
