# How Dox works

Source: https://dartondox.dev/latest/3.xconcepts/how-dox-works/

# How Dox works

This page explains what happens inside Dox when a request comes in.
It also explains how Dox uses isolates, where the database pools live, and what each folder of an app is for.

## The life of a request

Dox has two parts:

- A native server, written in Rust (`dox_http_native`). It owns the sockets and parses HTTP.
- Your app, written in Dart. Routes, middleware, DTOs, controllers and the ORM all run here.

A request goes through these steps:

1. Rust accepts the connection and reads the request. It parses the HTTP request line, the headers and the body.
   A bad request gets `400`. Headers over 16 KB get `431`. A body over the size limit gets `413`. Dart never sees these requests.
2. Rust hands the requests to Dart in a batch. One message holds many requests.
3. Dart finds the route. It matches the method, the `Host` (for domain routes) and the path.
   A plain path is a map lookup. A path with `{params}` is a pattern match.
   No match gives `404`. A CORS preflight (`OPTIONS`) gets `204`.
4. Dart adds the CORS headers of the route.
5. Dart reads the body, only when the request has a `Content-Type`. A request without a body skips this step.
6. Dart runs the middleware list of the route, in this order: global middleware, router middleware, group middleware, route middleware.
   A middleware returns the request to go on. Anything else is sent as the response, and the controller does not run.
7. Dart fills the controller parameters. Path params are converted first. A value that does not fit its type (`abc` for `int id`) gets `404`.
   Then the DTO is read and checked. Bad input gets `422`. A body that is not JSON gets `400`. A content type Dox can not read gets `415`.
8. The controller runs and returns a value.
9. The `responseHandler` from `AppConfig` runs, when you set one. It can change every response.
10. Dox turns the value into the response: a `String` is text, a `Map` or model is JSON, a `File` is streamed.
11. Dart sends the answers of the batch back to Rust in one call. Rust writes the bytes to the socket.

When a step throws, Dox catches the error. An `IHttpException` (like `NotFoundHttpException`) gives its own status.
Any other error gives `500` and goes to the `errorHandler` of `AppConfig`.

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    participant C as Client
    participant R as Rust (dox_http_native)
    participant D as Dart isolate
    participant M as Middleware
    participant K as Controller

    C->>R: TCP connection, HTTP request
    R->>R: parse request, check size limits
    R->>D: batch of requests (one message)
    D->>D: router: method, host, path
    D->>D: CORS headers, read body
    D->>M: global, router, group, route middleware
    M-->>D: request (go on) or a response
    D->>D: path params, DTO check
    D->>K: call with typed parameters
    K-->>D: return value
    D->>D: responseHandler, build the response
    D->>R: batch of answers (one call)
    R->>C: bytes
```

!!! note "No reflection"
    Dox reads the parameter types of every controller once, at start.
    It does not use `dart:mirrors`. DTOs come from a generated list (`lib/dtos.g.dart`).
    This is why `dox build` can make a native (AOT) binary.

### Where things are decided

| Step | Code | What it decides |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Route match | `lib/routes/*.dart`, `Route.get(...)` | which controller runs |
| Middleware | `AppConfig(globalMiddleware:)`, `Router.middleware`, `Route.middleware(...)`, the route list | go on, or answer early |
| Input | a `@Dto` class in `lib/app/http/dtos/` | what the controller gets, or `422` |
| Output | the return value, `response(...)`, `responseHandler` | status, headers, body |
| Errors | `IHttpException`, `AppConfig(errorHandler:)` | the error response, logging |

See [Routing](../the-basic/routing.md), [Middleware](../the-basic/middleware.md),
[Validation](../the-basic/validation.md) and [Response](../the-basic/response.md).

## Isolates

Dart runs code on isolates. An isolate is like a thread, but it has its own memory.
Dox starts one isolate per CPU core (`Platform.numberOfProcessors`). Every isolate runs the full app.

### One port, many isolates

Every isolate runs its own HTTP server on the same port. The operating system spreads the connections.

| System | Native server | `dart:io` server |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Linux | one socket per isolate (`SO_REUSEPORT`) | `HttpServer.bind(..., shared: true)` |
| macOS | the isolates share one socket | `HttpServer.bind(..., shared: true)` |
| Windows | only one isolate serves HTTP | `HttpServer.bind(..., shared: true)` |

Each isolate also has its own Rust network thread. `DOX_HTTP_THREAD=shared` puts all isolates on one thread. Leave it off unless you measure a gain.

### What each isolate gets

Before it starts an isolate, Dox copies three things to it:

- the `AppConfig`,
- the list of services,
- the routes you added before `startServer()`.

Then each isolate does this, once:

1. It runs `setup()` of every service, in list order. This is where a database pool is opened.
2. It registers the routes of your routers.
3. It reads the parameter types of every controller.
4. It starts its HTTP server.

Nothing in this list runs per request.

Because the config and the services are copied, they must not hold open sockets or pools.
Open these in `setup()`. See [Services](../digging-deeper/services.md).

### Each isolate has its own memory

- A static value or a singleton exists once per isolate. A change in one isolate is not seen in the others.
- The `memory` cache store is per isolate. Use the `redis` store to share cache data.
- To share data between isolates, use the database, Redis or files.
- `Dox().isolateId` tells you which isolate runs the code. The first one is `1`.

### When an isolate crashes

- An error in a request is caught. Dox answers `500` and keeps going.
- An async error outside a request is caught and passed to `errorHandler`. The isolate keeps running.
- When a worker isolate still dies, Dox prints `[dox] isolate N exited, restarting` and starts a new one after 1 second.
- When the first (main) isolate dies, the process exits with a non-zero code. A supervisor (Docker `restart:`, systemd `Restart=always`) must start it again.

### How many isolates

Set `totalIsolate` in `AppConfig`, or `APP_TOTAL_ISOLATE` in `.env`. In code, `Dox().totalIsolate(2)` before `startServer()` wins over the config.
Use `1` in tests. See [Isolate](../digging-deeper/isolate.md).

## Where the database pools live

The ORM is started in a service (`ORMService`). Every isolate runs `setup()`, so every isolate opens its own pool.

| Driver | Per isolate | Per process |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Postgres native (`dox_postgres_native`) | one pool of `maxConnectionCount` connections | one Rust runtime, shared by all pools (`extra['threads']`, default `1`) |
| MySQL native (`dox_mysql_native`) | one pool | one Rust runtime, shared by all pools |
| Dart drivers (`postgres`, `mysql_dart`) | one pool | nothing shared |
| SQLite | one connection | nothing shared |

So the total number of connections is `isolates × maxConnectionCount`.
With 8 cores and the default of 10, the app can open 80 connections. Set `maxConnectionCount` with this in mind.

!!! note "Share one native pool between isolates"
    A native pool has a `handle` (an `int`). Give it to another isolate and use
    `PostgresNativeDriver(PgNativePool.fromHandle(handle))` there. Then both isolates use one pool.
    See [Native Postgres driver](../database/postgres-native.md#options).

The native drivers are the default. When the native library does not load, the ORM uses the Dart driver and prints one warning line.
Set `DOX_DB_DRIVER=dart` to use the Dart drivers on purpose. See [Database](../database/index.md).

## The layout of a Dox app

`dox create my_app` copies the [dox-sample](https://github.com/dartondox/dox-sample) template. It looks like this:

```text
my_app/
├── bin/
│   └── server.dart          # starts the app
├── db/
│   └── migration/           # migrations (.dart with a registry, or .sql)
├── lib/
│   ├── app/
│   │   ├── http/
│   │   │   ├── controllers/     # *.controller.dart
│   │   │   ├── dtos/            # *.dto.dart, typed and checked input
│   │   │   ├── middleware/      # *.middleware.dart
│   │   │   ├── serializers/     # *.serializer.dart, custom JSON shapes
│   │   │   └── response_handler.dart
│   │   ├── models/              # one folder per model, *.model.dart
│   │   └── ws/controllers/      # WebSocket controllers (dox_websocket)
│   ├── config/
│   │   ├── app.dart             # AppConfig: port, isolates, routers, middleware
│   │   ├── cache.dart           # cache stores
│   │   ├── cors.dart
│   │   ├── database.dart        # DatabaseConfig: connections
│   │   ├── env.dart             # typed env class (@DoxEnv), optional
│   │   ├── logger.dart
│   │   ├── services.dart        # the list of DoxService
│   │   └── storage.dart         # storage disks
│   ├── routes/
│   │   ├── api.dart             # ApiRouter, prefix `api`
│   │   └── web.dart             # WebRouter
│   ├── services/
│   │   └── orm_service.dart     # opens the database in every isolate
│   ├── dtos.g.dart              # generated: the list of DTOs
│   └── openapi.g.dart           # generated: the OpenAPI docs
├── storage/                     # local disk, file cache, uploads
├── test/
├── .env                         # local settings, not in git
├── .env.example
├── Dockerfile
├── docker-compose.yml
└── pubspec.yaml
```

| Folder | What goes there |
| --- | --- |
| `bin/` | `server.dart` calls `Dox().initialize(appConfig)`, runs the migrations, then `Dox().startServer()`. `dox make:migration` adds `migrate.dart`. |
| `db/migration/` | Your migrations. Dart migrations are listed in `migrations.dart`, which the CLI writes. |
| `lib/app/http/` | Everything about HTTP: controllers, DTOs, middleware, serializers. |
| `lib/app/models/` | One folder per model. `build_runner` writes the `.g.dart` file next to it. |
| `lib/config/` | One file per config object. `app.dart` puts them together in `AppConfig`. |
| `lib/routes/` | One `Router` class per file. Add each router to `routers` in `app.dart`. |
| `lib/services/` | Classes that implement `DoxService`. Their `setup()` runs in every isolate. |
| `lib/*.g.dart` | Generated files. Do not edit them. Run `dox build_runner:build` to make them again. |
| `storage/` | Files the app writes: uploads, the file cache, SQLite files. |

Generated code comes from `build_runner` with the `dox_builder` package. It makes the model classes, the DTO checks, the typed env class and the OpenAPI docs.
Run `dox build_runner:build` after you change a model, a DTO or the env class. `dox serve` runs it in watch mode for you.


---

# Coming from Laravel

Source: https://dartondox.dev/latest/3.xconcepts/coming-from-laravel/

# Coming from Laravel

This page is for developers who know Laravel. It shows the Laravel way and the Dox way side by side.
The Dox code is real 3.x code. The Laravel code is Laravel 11.

Dox follows the ideas of Laravel: routers, controllers, middleware, an ORM with models and relations, migrations, a CLI.
But Dox is Dart. It has static types, no reflection at run time, and it compiles to one native binary.

## Routing

| Laravel | Dox |
| --- | --- |
| `Route::get('/ping', fn () => 'pong');` | `Route.get('/ping', (DoxRequest req) => 'pong');` |
| `Route::post('/blogs', [BlogController::class, 'store']);` | `Route.post('/blogs', blogController.store);` |
| `Route::get('/blogs/{id}', ...)` and `function show(int $id)` | `Route.get('/blogs/{id}', ...)` and `show(int id)` |
| `Route::get('/posts/{page?}', ...)` | `Route.get('/posts/{page?}', (int? page) => ...)` |
| `->where('path', '.*')` | `Route.get('/docs/{page*}', (String page) => ...)` |
| `Route::prefix('blogs')->group(function () { ... });` | `Route.group('/blogs', () { ... });` |
| `Route::middleware('auth')->group(...)` | `Route.middleware(<dynamic>[AuthMiddleware()], () { ... });` |
| `Route::domain('admin.app.test')->group(...)` | `Route.domain('admin.app.test', () { ... });` |
| `Route::resource('blogs', BlogController::class);` | `Route.resource('blogs', BlogController());` |
| `routes/api.php` with the `api` prefix | `lib/routes/api.dart`, a `Router` class with `prefix => 'api'` |

In Dox, a controller is an object you make yourself. There is no `BlogController::class` string.

```dart title="lib/routes/api.dart"
class ApiRouter extends Router {
  @override
  String get prefix => 'api';

  @override
  List<dynamic> get middleware => <dynamic>[];

  @override
  void register() {
    BlogController blogController = BlogController();
    Route.get('/blogs', blogController.index);
    Route.resource('users', UserController());
  }
}
```

## Controllers

| Laravel | Dox |
| --- | --- |
| `php artisan make:controller BlogController` | `dox create:controller Blog` |
| `php artisan make:controller BlogController --resource` | `dox create:controller Blog -r` |
| `public function show(Request $request, int $id)` | `Future<Blog?> show(DoxRequest req, int id)` |
| `public function store(StoreBlogRequest $request)` | `Future<Blog> store(CreateBlog body)` |
| injected by the service container | filled by type: `DoxRequest`, one `@Dto` class, path params |

Dox fills a parameter by its type, not by its name. Path params go by position.
A controller can be a class method, a static method or a plain function.

## Middleware

| Laravel | Dox |
| --- | --- |
| `php artisan make:middleware Logger` | `dox create:middleware Logger` |
| `public function handle(Request $request, Closure $next)` | `dynamic handle(IDoxRequest req)` |
| `return $next($request);` | `return req;` |
| `return response('no', 401);` | `return response('no').statusCode(401);` |
| `abort(404);` | `throw NotFoundHttpException();` |
| `$middleware->append(LogMiddleware::class)` in `bootstrap/app.php` | `AppConfig(globalMiddleware: <dynamic>[LogMiddleware()])` |

```dart title="lib/app/http/middleware/logger.middleware.dart"
class LoggerMiddleware implements IDoxMiddleware {
  @override
  dynamic handle(IDoxRequest req) {
    print('${req.method} ${req.uri.path}');
    return req; // go on. anything else is the response.
  }
}
```

A plain function `dynamic apiKey(DoxRequest req)` also works as middleware.
Dox middleware runs before the controller only. There is no "after" step; use a `responseHandler` for that.

## Requests and validation

| Laravel | Dox |
| --- | --- |
| `php artisan make:request StoreBlogRequest` | `dox create:dto CreateBlog` |
| `class StoreBlogRequest extends FormRequest` with `rules()` | `@Dto() class CreateBlog` with annotations on `final` fields |
| `'title' => ['required', 'string', 'max:50']` | `@MaxLength(50) final String title;` |
| `'age' => ['nullable', 'integer', 'min:18']` | `@Min(18) final int? age;` |
| `'email' => ['required', 'email', 'unique:users']` | `@Email() @Unique('users') final String email;` |
| `'role' => Rule::in(['admin', 'user'])` | `final Role role;` (a Dart enum) |
| `'tags' => ['array', 'max:5']`, `'tags.*' => 'string'` | `@MaxItems(5) final List<String> tags;` |
| `$request->validated()` | the DTO object itself, already typed |
| `$request->validate([...])` inside a method | `await req.validate<CreateBlog>()` |
| `$request->input('name')` | `req.input('name')` |
| `$request->file('avatar')` | a `RequestFile` field in the DTO, or `req.input('avatar')` |
| `$request->user()` | `req.auth?.user<User>()` |
| `422` with `{"errors": {...}}` | `422` with a flat map `{"email": "...", "items.1.quantity": "..."}` |

```dart title="lib/app/http/dtos/create_blog.dto.dart"
@Dto()
class CreateBlog {
  @Length(min: 3, max: 50)
  final String title;

  @Min(18)
  final int? age; // nullable = optional

  const CreateBlog({required this.title, this.age});

  static const DtoSchema<CreateBlog> schema = $CreateBlogDto;
}
```

The rules are checked by generated Dart code, not by rule strings at run time.
Run `dox build_runner:build` after you change a DTO. See [Validation](../the-basic/validation.md).

## Responses

| Laravel | Dox |
| --- | --- |
| `return 'pong';` | `return 'pong';` |
| `return ['a' => 1];` | `return <String, int>{'a': 1};` |
| `return $blog;` (JSON) | `return blog;` (JSON from `toJson()`) |
| `return response($data, 201)->header('X-A', 'b');` | `return response(data).statusCode(201).header('X-A', 'b');` |
| `return response()->json($data);` | `return data;` (a `Map` or `List` is JSON) |
| `return response()->file($path);` | `return File(path);` |
| `return response()->download($path);` | `return Storage().download(path);` |
| `->cookie('theme', 'dark')` | `.cookie(DoxCookie('theme', 'dark'))` |
| `abort(404, 'Not found');` | `throw NotFoundHttpException(message: 'Not found');` |
| `new BlogResource($blog)` | `BlogSerializer(blog)` |

## Eloquent vs Dox Model

| Laravel | Dox |
| --- | --- |
| `php artisan make:model Blog -m` | `dox create:model Blog -m` |
| `class Blog extends Model` | `@DoxModel() class Blog extends BlogGenerator` |
| `protected $table = 'blogs';` | `@DoxModel(table: 'blogs')` |
| `protected $primaryKey = 'uid';` | `@DoxModel(primaryKey: 'uid')` |
| `use SoftDeletes;` | `@DoxModel(softDelete: true)` |
| `public $timestamps = false;` | `@DoxModel(timestamps: false)` |
| `protected $hidden = ['password'];` | `List<String> get hidden => <String>['password'];` |
| `protected $fillable = [...]` | not needed. Only `@Column()` fields are saved. |
| `protected $casts = ['meta' => 'array'];` | the field type: `Map<String, dynamic>? meta;` |
| mutator `setSlugAttribute()` | `@Column(beforeSave: makeSlug)` |
| accessor `getStatusAttribute()` | `@Column(beforeGet: readStatus)` |
| `$appends` with an accessor | `@Computed() String get fullName => ...;` |
| `Blog::find(1)` | `await Blog().find(1)` |
| `Blog::where('age', '>', 18)->get()` | `await Blog().where('age', '>', 18).get()` |
| `Blog::create([...])` | `await Blog().create(<String, dynamic>{...})` |
| `$blog->save()` | `await blog.save()` |
| `$blog->delete()` | `await blog.delete()` |
| `Blog::withTrashed()` | `Blog().withTrash()` |
| `$blog->restore()` | `await blog.restore()` |
| `Blog::with('posts')->get()` | `await Blog().preload('posts').get()` |
| `$blog->load('posts')` | `await blog.$getRelation('posts')` |
| `$user->posts()->where(...)->get()` | `user.related<Post>('posts')?.where(...).get()` |
| `$with = ['posts']` | `@HasMany(Post, eager: true)` |
| `hasOne`, `hasMany`, `belongsTo`, `belongsToMany` | `@HasOne`, `@HasMany`, `@BelongsTo`, `@ManyToMany` |
| local scope `scopeActive()` | `onQuery: onlyActive` on a relation, or a static method that returns a query |
| `creating`, `saved`, `deleting` events | `onCreating()`, `onSaved()`, `onDeleting()` hooks in the model |
| `Blog::observe(BlogObserver::class)` | `Model.observe<Blog>(BlogObserver())` |
| `$blog->saveQuietly()` | `await blog.saveQuietly()` |
| `Model::withoutEvents(fn)` | `Model.withoutEvents(() async { ... })` |

```dart title="lib/app/models/blog/blog.model.dart"
@DoxModel(table: 'blogs', softDelete: true)
class Blog extends BlogGenerator {
  @Column()
  String? title;

  @Column(name: 'user_id')
  int? userId;

  @BelongsTo(User)
  User? user;

  @override
  Future<void> onCreating() async {
    title = title?.trim();
  }
}
```

Every column field is nullable, because a new model has no values yet.
Dox has no global scopes and no `$casts` list. Use the field type, `beforeSave` and `beforeGet`.
Run `dox build_runner:build` after you change a model. See [Model](../database/model/index.md).

## Query builder

| Laravel | Dox |
| --- | --- |
| `DB::table('users')->get()` | `await QueryBuilder.table('users').get()` |
| `->where('a', 1)->orWhere('b', 2)` | `.where('a', 1).orWhere('b', 2)` |
| `->whereIn('id', [1, 2])` | `.whereIn('id', <int>[1, 2])` |
| `->whereNull('deleted_at')` | `.whereNull('deleted_at')` |
| `->whereRaw('lower(name) = ?', [$n])` | `.whereRaw('lower(name) = @n', <String, dynamic>{'n': n})` |
| `->select('id', 'name')` | `.select(<String>['id', 'name'])` |
| `->orderBy('name', 'desc')->limit(10)->offset(20)` | `.orderBy('name', 'desc').limit(10).offset(20)` |
| `->join('posts', 'posts.user_id', '=', 'users.id')` | `.join('posts', 'posts.user_id', 'users.id')` |
| `->groupBy('age')` | `.groupBy('age')` on `QueryBuilder.table()` (returns maps) |
| `->count()` | `await ....count()` |
| `->paginate(10)` | `.paginate(currentPage: 1, perPage: 10)` |
| `->insert([...])` | `.insertMultiple(<Map<String, dynamic>>[...])` |
| `->update([...])` | `.update(<String, dynamic>{...})` |
| `->delete()` | `.delete()` |
| `DB::select('select ...', [$id])` | `QueryBuilder.query('select ... @id', substitutionValues: {'id': id})` |
| `DB::transaction(fn)` | `QueryBuilder.transaction(() async { ... })` |
| `->toSql()` | `.toSql()` |
| `DB::connection('mysql')` | `.withConnection('mysql')` |

Values are always bound parameters. Names you pass are quoted. Do not pass user input as a column name or an operator.

## Migrations and schema

| Laravel | Dox |
| --- | --- |
| `php artisan make:migration create_users_table` | `dox make:migration create_users_table` |
| `database/migrations/` | `db/migration/` |
| `Schema::create('users', function (Blueprint $table) {...})` | `await schema.create('users', (Table table) {...})` |
| `$table->id();` | `table.id();` |
| `$table->string('email')->unique();` | `table.string('email').unique();` |
| `$table->foreignId('user_id')->constrained()->cascadeOnDelete();` | `table.foreignId('user_id').constrained().cascadeOnDelete();` |
| `$table->timestamps();` | `table.timestamps();` |
| `$table->softDeletes();` | `table.softDeletes();` |
| `$table->string('name', 100)->nullable()->change();` | `table.string('name', 100).nullable().change();` |
| `Schema::dropIfExists('users');` | `await schema.dropIfExists('users');` |
| `php artisan migrate` | `dox migrate` (or `dox migration:run`) |
| `php artisan migrate:rollback --step=2` | `dox migration:rollback --step=2` |
| `php artisan migrate:reset`, `migrate:refresh`, `migrate:status` | `dox migration:reset`, `migration:refresh`, `migration:status` |

```dart title="db/migration/2026_10_21_120000_create_users_table.dart"
class CreateUsersTable extends Migration {
  @override
  Future<void> up(Schema schema) async {
    await schema.create('users', (Table table) {
      table.id();
      table.string('email').unique();
      table.timestamps();
    });
  }

  @override
  Future<void> down(Schema schema) async {
    await schema.dropIfExists('users');
  }
}
```

Dart can not load files at run time in an AOT binary. So the CLI keeps a list of your migrations in `db/migration/migrations.dart`. You do not edit it.
The server can run the migrations at start. See [Migration](../database/migration.md).

## Artisan vs the dox CLI

| Laravel | Dox |
| --- | --- |
| `laravel new blog` | `dox create blog` |
| `php artisan serve` | `dox serve` (or `dox s`), with hot restart and `build_runner watch` |
| `php artisan make:controller` | `dox create:controller` |
| `php artisan make:model Blog -m` | `dox create:model Blog -m` |
| `php artisan make:request` | `dox create:dto` |
| `php artisan make:middleware` | `dox create:middleware` |
| `php artisan make:resource` | `dox create:serializer` |
| `php artisan make:migration` | `dox make:migration` |
| `php artisan migrate` | `dox migrate` |
| `php artisan key:generate` | `dox key:generate` |
| `php artisan route:list` | not there. Use the OpenAPI docs page at `/docs`. |
| `php artisan tinker` | not there |
| `php artisan optimize` | `dox build` (one native binary in `build/bundle`) |

Two commands have no Laravel twin: `dox build_runner:build` makes the generated code, and `dox env:generate` makes the typed env class.
See [Dox CLI](../digging-deeper/dox-cli.md).

## Auth

| Laravel | Dox |
| --- | --- |
| `config/auth.php` guards and providers | `Auth.initialize(AuthConfig(guards: ...))` in a service |
| `Auth::attempt(['email' => $e, 'password' => $p])` | `await Auth().attempt(<String, dynamic>{'email': e, 'password': p})` gives a JWT, or `null` |
| `Auth::login($user)` | `Auth().login(user)` gives a JWT |
| `Auth::user()` | `req.auth?.user<User>()` |
| `->middleware('auth:sanctum')` | `AuthMiddleware()` from `dox_auth` |
| `Hash::make($p)`, `Hash::check($p, $hash)` | `Hash.make(p)`, `Hash.verify(p, hash)` |

Dox auth is a JWT in the `Authorization` header. There are no sessions, no cookies and no Sanctum tokens table.
See [Authentication](../security/authentication.md).

## Cache

| Laravel | Dox |
| --- | --- |
| `config/cache.php` | `lib/config/cache.dart`, `CacheConfig(defaultStore:, stores:)` |
| `Cache::put('k', $v, 600)` | `await Cache().put('k', v, duration: Duration(minutes: 10))` |
| `Cache::get('k', 'default')` | `await Cache().get('k', 'default')` |
| `Cache::remember('k', 600, fn)` | `await Cache().remember('k', Duration(minutes: 10), fn)` |
| `Cache::forget('k')` | `await Cache().forget('k')` |
| `Cache::store('redis')` | `Cache().store('redis')` |
| `Cache::tags(['a'])` | `Cache().tags(<String>['a'])` |
| `Cache::lock('k', 10)` | `Cache().lock('k', Duration(seconds: 10))` |
| drivers: file, redis, memcached, database, array | drivers: `file`, `redis`, `memory`, `null` |

A value must be a JSON type. The `memory` store is per isolate. See [Cache](../digging-deeper/cache.md).

## Storage

| Laravel | Dox |
| --- | --- |
| `config/filesystems.php` disks | `lib/config/storage.dart`, `StorageConfig(defaultDisk:, disks:)` |
| `Storage::put('a.txt', $bytes)` | `await Storage().put('files', bytes, extension: 'txt')` (a uuid file name) |
| `$request->file('f')->store('avatars')` | `await file.store('avatars')` or `Storage().putRequestFile('avatars', file)` |
| `Storage::get($path)` | `await Storage().get(path)` |
| `Storage::exists($path)` | `await Storage().exists(path)` |
| `Storage::delete($path)` | `await Storage().delete(path)` |
| `Storage::url($path)` | `await Storage().url(path)` |
| `Storage::temporaryUrl($path, now()->addMinutes(10))` | `await Storage().signedUrl(path, expiresIn: Duration(minutes: 10))` |
| `Storage::disk('s3')` | `Storage().disk('s3')` |
| `Storage::download($path)` | `return Storage().download(path);` |
| drivers: local, s3, ftp, sftp | drivers: `local`, `s3` (also R2, MinIO, Spaces), `memory` |

See [File Storage](../digging-deeper/file-storage.md).

## Config and `.env`

| Laravel | Dox |
| --- | --- |
| `config/*.php` files | `lib/config/*.dart` files, put together in `AppConfig` |
| `env('APP_KEY')` | `env.appKey` (a getter in `lib/config/env.dart`) |
| `env('APP_PORT', 3000)` | `env.appPort` (the default is in the getter: `int get appPort => 3000;`) |
| `config('app.name')` | `env.appName` from the typed env class (`@DoxEnv()`) |
| `php artisan config:cache` | not needed. The typed env is read once, at start. |

The typed env class gives you an `int` for `APP_PORT` and a build error for a bad type.
A missing key stops the app at start, with a list of every missing key. See [Environment Variables](../digging-deeper/env.md).

## Testing

| Laravel | Dox |
| --- | --- |
| `php artisan test` | `dart test` |
| `$this->get('/api/ping')->assertStatus(200)` | start the server once, then `http.get(Uri.parse('$baseUrl/api/ping'))` |
| `RefreshDatabase` | run the migrations in `setUpAll`, or use SQLite `:memory:` |
| `Storage::fake('s3')` | `Dox().storage.fake('s3')` |
| `Cache::fake()` | `Dox().cache = CacheManager(CacheConfig(...))` with a `memory` store |
| `$this->actingAs($user)` | send the JWT from `Auth().login(user)` in the `Authorization` header |

Dox has no fake HTTP kernel. A test starts the real server with `Dox().totalIsolate(1)` and sends real requests.
See [Testing](../digging-deeper/testing.md).

## What is different

- **No service container in the controller.** Laravel makes your controllers and injects what the constructor asks for.
  In Dox you make the controller yourself (`BlogController()`) and pass what it needs. Dox fills only the method parameters: the request, one DTO and the path params.
  `Dox().ioc` is a small registry (`register`, `registerSingleton`, `get`), but nothing is injected for you.
- **Isolates, not PHP-FPM workers.** One process runs one isolate per CPU core. Each isolate runs your whole app and has its own memory.
  A static value or a singleton lives once per isolate. A PHP worker starts from zero on each request. A Dox isolate keeps its state between requests, so a memory leak stays.
  Anything that must be shared goes to the database, Redis or files. See [How Dox works](how-dox-works.md#isolates).
- **Code generation, not reflection.** Laravel reads your classes at run time. Dart has no usable reflection in a compiled app.
  So `build_runner` with `dox_builder` writes the model code, the DTO checks, the env class and the OpenAPI docs into `.g.dart` files.
  Run `dox build_runner:build` after a change, or let `dox serve` watch for you.
- **One native binary.** `dox build` makes an AOT binary in `build/bundle`. There is no interpreter, no `vendor/` folder and no `composer install` on the server.
  The Docker image is about 11 MB.
- **A native HTTP server and native database drivers.** Rust parses HTTP and talks to Postgres and MySQL. Your code stays in Dart. The HTTP server comes ready-built. The database drivers need Rust (`cargo`) to build; without it, Dox uses the Dart drivers.
- **Types everywhere.** A DTO is a class with typed fields. A path param is an `int`. A model field is a `String?`. The compiler finds many mistakes before you run the app.
- **Async is explicit.** Database calls return a `Future`. You write `await`. One isolate serves many requests at the same time while it waits for the database.
- **JSON API first.** Dox returns text, JSON, files and streams. It has no view layer.

## What is missing today

Dox 3.0 does not have these Laravel features. Check the [packages](../packages/validation.md) list for what is there.

| Laravel | Dox 3.0 |
| --- | --- |
| Queues and jobs (`dispatch(new Job)`) | not there. Use a database table, Redis or a separate worker process. |
| Task scheduler (`schedule()->daily()`) | not there. Use cron or systemd timers to call a route or a Dart script. |
| Events and listeners (`Event::dispatch`, `$listen`) | not there. Model events (hooks and observers) are there. |
| Blade views, `view()` | not there. Dox is for APIs. Serve a front end from a CDN or a proxy. |
| Mail (`Mail::to()`) | not there. Use a Dart mail package or an HTTP mail API. |
| Notifications | not there |
| Sessions and session cookies | not there. Auth uses a JWT. Encrypted cookies are there. |
| Policies and gates | not there. Check the user in a middleware or in the controller. |
| Global scopes, `$casts`, `$fillable` | not there. See [Eloquent vs Dox Model](#eloquent-vs-dox-model). |
| Database seeders and factories | not there. Write a Dart script, or a migration with data. |
| Rate limiting middleware | not there. Write a middleware with the cache, or use a proxy. |
| `php artisan route:list`, `tinker` | not there |
| Savepoints in nested transactions | not there. A nested `transaction()` joins the outer one. |
| WebSocket on the native server | not there yet. An app with WebSocket routes uses the `dart:io` server. |

What is there, as separate packages: [validation](../packages/validation.md), [OpenAPI docs](../packages/openapi.md),
[storage](../packages/storage.md), [cache](../packages/cache.md), [Socket.IO](../packages/socketio.md),
[WebSocket](../digging-deeper/websocket.md) and [auth](../security/authentication.md).


---

# Dox and the other Dart backends

Source: https://dartondox.dev/latest/3.xconcepts/dart-frameworks/

# Dox and the other Dart backends

This page compares Dox with four other ways to build a backend in Dart: Dart Frog, Serverpod, Shelf (with `shelf_router`) and Alfred.
It lists facts only. Each project is good at different things.

!!! note "Checked on 2026-10-22"
    The facts about the other projects come from their own docs, READMEs and pub.dev pages, read on 2026-10-22.
    Projects change. Check their docs before you decide.
    Where this page is not sure, the table says "see their docs".

## What each one is for

- **Dox** is a full backend framework, in the style of Laravel. It has routes, controllers, typed DTOs, an ORM, migrations, auth, cache, storage and a CLI.
  It is in **3.0 alpha**. The API can still change.
- **Dart Frog** is a small backend framework. It is built on Shelf. Routes come from the files in the `routes/` folder.
  It describes itself as "a fast, minimalistic backend framework for Dart".
- **Serverpod** is a full-stack framework for Flutter. You write endpoint methods on the server. Serverpod generates a typed Dart client for the Flutter app.
  It has an ORM, auth, streaming and a hosted service (Serverpod Cloud).
- **Shelf** is the request and middleware model from the Dart team. It is a library, not a framework.
  `shelf_router` adds a router. You pick every other part yourself.
- **Alfred** is a small server in the style of Express.js. Routes, middleware, WebSocket and static files are built in.

## Feature table

"Not built in" means the project does not ship it. You can still add a package for it.

| Feature | Dox | Dart Frog | Serverpod | Shelf + shelf_router | Alfred |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Routing | Route classes: `Route.get(...)`, groups, resources, domain routes | Routes from files in `routes/`, dynamic and nested routes | Endpoint classes become typed client methods. A separate web server (Relic) has its own routing. | `Router()` with `<param>` patterns, nested routers | Express-like, `:id:int` params with types or regex |
| Typed request validation | `@Dto` classes, checks generated at build time, `422` with errors | Not in their feature list (see their docs) | Typed, generated parameters for endpoints. Rules: see their docs. | Not built in | Route params only (type or regex) |
| ORM and relations | `dox_orm`: models, has one, has many, belongs to, many to many | Not built in | Built in: filters, joins, one-to-one, one-to-many, many-to-many | Not built in | Not built in |
| Migrations | `dox migrate` (SQL or Dart files) | Not built in | Built in, versioned migrations | Not built in | Not built in |
| Auth | `dox_auth`: JWT guard, password hashing | `dart_frog_auth`: Basic, Bearer and Cookie middleware | Built in: email and password, Google, Apple, GitHub, passkeys and more | Not built in | See their docs |
| WebSocket | `dox_websocket` and a Socket.IO v4 server (`dox_socketio`) | `dart_frog_web_socket` (`webSocketHandler`) | Streaming methods over a managed WebSocket | `shelf_web_socket` | Built in |
| OpenAPI | Generated OpenAPI 3.1 (JSON, YAML) and a docs page | On their roadmap, not done | See their docs | See their docs | See their docs |
| CLI and code generation | `dox` CLI, `build_runner` for DTOs, models and OpenAPI | `dart_frog` CLI: `create`, `dev` (hot reload), `build` | `serverpod` CLI, generates server and client code | No CLI (`shelf_router_generator` for routes from annotations) | No CLI |
| Native binary | `dox build` makes an AOT binary | `dart_frog build` makes a production build with a Dockerfile | Deploy to Serverpod Cloud, Docker or Terraform. Binary: see their docs. | Your app is plain Dart. Compile it like any Dart program. | Your app is plain Dart. Compile it like any Dart program. |
| Multi-core | One isolate per CPU core by default | See their docs | One isolate per process. Scale with more processes and server roles. | `serve(..., shared: true)` and your own isolates | Yes, a multi-isolate mode is in their README |
| HTTP server | Native server in Rust (hyper) by default, `dart:io` as fallback | Shelf on `dart:io` | Relic (their own) for the web server. API server: see their docs. | `dart:io` `HttpServer` (`shelf_io`) | `dart:io` |
| Databases | Postgres, MySQL, MariaDB, SQLite | Not built in | Postgres, SQLite (also SQLite on the device). Redis for cache. | Not built in | Not built in |
| Code sharing with Flutter | `@Dto` classes in a pure Dart package, see [Share code with Flutter](../guides/share-code-with-flutter.md) | Plain Dart packages. A generated client is marked "in progress" in their feature list. | Generated client package, and shared packages for models | Plain Dart packages | Plain Dart packages |
| License | MIT | MIT | BSD-3 for most packages. The main `serverpod` package is SSPL. | BSD-3-Clause | MIT for the core. Some parts BSD. |
| First release and maturity | 3.0 alpha (2026) | First on pub.dev in 2022, 1.0 about three years ago | First on pub.dev in 2021, now 4.x | First on pub.dev in 2014, 1.0 in 2021 | First on pub.dev in 2021, 1.x |
| Maintenance (on 2026-10-22) | Active | Active. Moved to the `dart-frog-dev` group in 2025. Last `dart_frog` release: 1.2.6 (November 2025). | Active. Release 4.0.4 in October 2026. | Active. Published by `tools.dart.dev` (the Dart team). | Last release 1.1.3, about 17 months ago. Unverified uploader. |

Sources (checked on 2026-10-22):

- Dart Frog: [dart-frog.dev](https://dart-frog.dev), [github.com/dart-frog-dev/dart_frog](https://github.com/dart-frog-dev/dart_frog) (docs in `docs/src/content/docs`, the roadmap and "The Future of Dart Frog"), [pub.dev/packages/dart_frog](https://pub.dev/packages/dart_frog)
- Serverpod: [docs.serverpod.dev](https://docs.serverpod.dev), [github.com/serverpod/serverpod](https://github.com/serverpod/serverpod), [github.com/serverpod/serverpod_docs](https://github.com/serverpod/serverpod_docs) (scalability, streaming, shared packages, database connection), [pub.dev/packages/serverpod](https://pub.dev/packages/serverpod)
- Shelf: [pub.dev/packages/shelf](https://pub.dev/packages/shelf), [pub.dev/packages/shelf_router](https://pub.dev/packages/shelf_router), [github.com/dart-lang/shelf](https://github.com/dart-lang/shelf), [`serve` API docs](https://pub.dev/documentation/shelf/latest/shelf_io/serve.html)
- Alfred: [pub.dev/packages/alfred](https://pub.dev/packages/alfred), [github.com/rknell/alfred](https://github.com/rknell/alfred)

## Speed

This page does not compare speed. Dox's own numbers (hello world and a `/db` read) are on [Performance](../digging-deeper/performance.md).
To compare, run the same test on your own machine, with each server on the same number of cores.

## When to pick Dox

- You want a full framework in one place: routes, typed input, ORM, migrations, auth, cache, storage and OpenAPI docs.
- You know Laravel. See [Coming from Laravel](coming-from-laravel.md).
- You need MySQL or MariaDB, not only Postgres.
- You want typed DTOs with the same rules on the server and in a Dart or Flutter client. See [Share code with Flutter](../guides/share-code-with-flutter.md).
- You want an OpenAPI document made from your code, for clients that are not written in Dart.
- You can accept an alpha: the API can change before 3.0 is stable. See [Status and roadmap](status-and-roadmap.md).

## When to pick something else

- **You need a stable API today.** Dox is alpha. Dart Frog, Serverpod and Shelf have had 1.0 or later for years.
- **You want a hosted service.** Serverpod has Serverpod Cloud. Dox has no hosted service. You deploy it yourself (a binary or Docker).
- **Your app is Flutter only, and you want the client made for you.** Serverpod generates a typed client for every endpoint. Dox does not generate a Dart client. It generates an OpenAPI document.
- **You want a small tool with few parts.** Dart Frog is simpler. You add only what you need.
- **You want to build your own stack.** Shelf gives you the base parts, and the Dart team publishes it.
- **You need features Dox does not have yet**, like queues, a scheduler or mail. See [What Dox does not have yet](status-and-roadmap.md#what-dox-does-not-have-yet).


---

# Status and roadmap

Source: https://dartondox.dev/latest/3.xconcepts/status-and-roadmap/

# Status and roadmap

Checked on 2026-10-22, for version `3.0.0-alpha.4`.

Dox 3.0 is an **alpha**. You can build with it, but the API can still change between alpha versions.
All packages share one version number.

## Packages

What the states mean:

- **May change**: works and has tests. Names and options can still change before 3.0 is stable.
- **Experimental**: new code. It changed in a breaking way during the alphas, or it has a known gap.

No package is marked "stable API" yet. That comes with 3.0 stable.

| Package | What it does | State | Tests |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `dox_core` | Routes, middleware, controllers, request and response, isolates, config | May change | 29 test files. CI runs them on the native server and on `dart:io`. |
| `dox_orm` | Query builder, models, relations, transactions, drivers | May change | 16 test files. CI runs them on Postgres, MariaDB, MySQL 8.4 and SQLite, with the native and the Dart drivers. |
| `dox_validation` | `@Dto` rules, fluent schemas, JSON Schema, Standard Schema | May change | 6 test files |
| `dox_builder` | Code generator for models, DTOs, env classes and OpenAPI | May change | 4 test files |
| `dox_annotation` | Annotations used by the generator | May change | 1 small test file. Mostly tested through `dox_builder`. |
| `dox` (CLI) | `dox create`, `dox serve`, `dox build`, `make:*`, `migration:*` | May change | 5 test files |
| `dox_migration` | Migrations for Postgres, MySQL, MariaDB and SQLite | May change | 2 test files. CI runs them on each database. |
| `dox_auth` | JWT auth guard and middleware, password hashing | May change | 2 test files |
| `dox_cache` | Memory, file and Redis cache, tags, locks | May change | 4 test files, with Redis in CI |
| `dox_storage` | Local disk and S3 (and S3-compatible) storage | May change | 7 test files, with MinIO in CI |
| `dox_openapi` | OpenAPI 3.1 document and a docs page | May change | 4 test files |
| `dox_websocket` | WebSocket routes and events | May change | 4 test files, with Redis in CI |
| `dox_socketio` | Socket.IO v4 server with a Redis adapter | May change | 6 test files, with the real `socket.io-client` in CI |
| `dox_http_native` | Native HTTP/1.1 server (Rust hyper), the default server | Experimental | 2 Dart test files and Rust tests. No WebSocket yet. Big responses are held in memory. |
| `dox_postgres_native` | Native Postgres client (Rust tokio-postgres), the default Postgres driver | Experimental | 1 Dart test file, plus the `dox_orm` tests. No TLS yet. |
| `dox_mysql_native` | Native MySQL and MariaDB client (Rust mysql_async), the default MySQL driver | Experimental | 1 Dart test file, plus the `dox_orm` tests |

!!! note "About test coverage"
    The repo does not measure line coverage. The "Tests" column counts test files and says where CI runs them.
    The CI setup is in `.github/workflows/test.yaml` and `native.yaml`.

## What Dox does not have yet

These were checked by searching the code in `packages/*/lib` with `rg`.

| Feature | Status | What to do today |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Queues and jobs | Not there | Use a database table, Redis or a separate worker process. See [Background work](../guides/background-work.md). |
| Task scheduler | Not there | Use cron or a systemd timer to call a route or a Dart script. |
| Mail | Not there | Use a Dart mail package or an HTTP mail API. |
| Events and listeners | Not there | Model events are there. See [Model events](../database/model/events.md). |
| Views and templates | Not there | Dox is for APIs. Serve the front end on its own. |
| Rate limiting | Not there | Write a middleware with the cache, or use a proxy. |
| Sessions | Not there | Auth uses JWT. On the native server, `req.httpRequest.session` throws `UnsupportedError`. |
| Policies and gates | Not there | Check the user in a middleware or in the controller. |
| Database seeders | Not there | Write a Dart script, or a migration with data. |

## Planned

!!! warning "This is a plan, not a promise. Open an issue to discuss."
    Items come from the code (`TODO` and `ponytail:` notes in `packages/*/lib`) and from the owner.
    There are no dates.

| Item | Source |
| --- | --- |
| WebSocket on the native server. Today an app with WebSocket routes uses the `dart:io` server. | `TODO(native)` in `dox_http_native/lib/src/response.dart` and `dox_core/lib/server/dox_server.dart` |
| Stream big responses to the socket on the native server. Today a big file is held in memory. | `ponytail:` note in `dox_http_native/lib/src/response.dart` |
| TLS for the native Postgres driver | `ponytail:` note in `dox_orm/lib/src/drivers/postgres_native_driver.dart` |
| Savepoints for nested transactions. Today a nested `transaction()` joins the outer one. | `ponytail:` notes in the `dox_orm` drivers and in `dox_migration` |
| A queue package (`dox_queue`) | Wanted by the owner. Not started. |
| A mail package (`dox_mail`) | Wanted by the owner. Not started. |
| 3.0 stable | After the alpha API settles |

The package CHANGELOGs have no `Unreleased` section today. When one is added, it lists the next changes.

## How to help

- Try the alpha and open an issue when something breaks or is missing.
- Pick an item above and open an issue first, so the design can be discussed.
- See [Contribute](../others/contribute.md) to set up the repo and run the tests.

# Routing

Source: https://dartondox.dev/latest/3.xthe-basic/routing/

# Routing

A route connects a URL and an HTTP method to the code that answers it.

This is the path of one request through the router:

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    Q["Request<br>GET /blogs/42"] --> B["Router<br>method, host, path"]
    B -->|no match| N["404"]
    B -->|match| P["Params as text<br>req.param"]
    P --> M["Middleware"]
    M -->|returns a value| S["Response"]
    M -->|returns the request| T["Typed params, DTO<br>int id"]
    T --> C["Controller"]
    C --> S
```

## Where routes live

Routes are in the `lib/routes` folder. Each file has one `Router` class.
The `prefix` of the router is added in front of all its routes.

```dart title="lib/routes/api.dart"
import 'package:dox_core/dox_core.dart';

class ApiRouter extends Router {
  @override
  String get prefix => 'api';

  @override
  List<dynamic> get middleware => <dynamic>[];

  @override
  void register() {
    Route.get('/ping', (DoxRequest req) => 'pong'); // GET /api/ping
  }
}
```

Add each router to `routers` in `lib/config/app.dart`:

```dart title="lib/config/app.dart"
AppConfig appConfig = AppConfig(
  routers: <Router>[WebRouter(), ApiRouter()],
  // ...
);
```

The leading `/` in a path is optional. `'ping'` and `'/ping'` are the same route.

## Route methods

```dart
Route.get('/blogs', controller.index);
Route.post('/blogs', controller.store);
Route.put('/blogs/{id}', controller.update);
Route.patch('/blogs/{id}', controller.update);
Route.delete('/blogs/{id}', controller.destroy);
```

!!! info
    There are also `Route.options`, `Route.copy`, `Route.view`, `Route.link`, `Route.unlink`,
    `Route.purge`, `Route.lock`, `Route.unlock` and `Route.propfind`.

A `HEAD` request runs the `GET` route of the same path. The answer has the status and headers of `GET`, with no body.

## The handler

The second argument is the code that answers the request. It can be:

```dart
// a function
Route.get('/ping', (DoxRequest req) => 'pong');

// a controller method
WebController webController = WebController();
Route.get('/ping', webController.pong);

class WebController {
  String pong(DoxRequest req) {
    return 'pong';
  }
}

// a list: middleware first, the controller last
Route.get('/ping', <dynamic>[LoggerMiddleware(), webController.pong]);
```

In a list, the last item is the controller. The items before it are [middleware](middleware.md).

See [Controller](controller.md) for the parameters a handler can ask for.

## Route params

Put a param in `{}`. Ask for it as a typed parameter in the controller.

```dart
Route.get('/blogs/{id}', controller.show);

class BlogController {
  Future<Blog?> show(int id) async {
    return Blog().find(id);
  }
}
```

`/blogs/abc` answers `404`, because `abc` is not an `int`.
See [Controller: parameters](controller.md#parameters) for all the rules.

### Optional param

`{name?}` can be missing. Use a nullable type.

```dart
Route.get('/posts/{page?}', (int? page) {
  return 'page ${page ?? 1}'; // GET /posts and GET /posts/2 both match
});
```

### Catch-all param

`{name*}` matches the rest of the path, with slashes.

```dart
Route.get('/docs/{page*}', (String page) {
  return page; // GET /docs/a/b/c gives 'a/b/c'
});
```

## Group routes

```dart
// by prefix
Route.group('/blogs', () { // (1)!
  Route.get('/', controller.index);     // GET /blogs
  Route.get('/{id}', controller.show); // (2)!
});

// by domain: these routes match only when the Host header is dartondox.com
Route.domain('dartondox.com', () { // (3)!
  Route.get('/ping', controller.ping);
});

// by middleware
Route.middleware(<dynamic>[AuthMiddleware()], () { // (4)!
  Route.get('/me', controller.me);
  Route.post('/logout', controller.logout);
});
```

1.  `/blogs` goes in front of every path in the callback.
    Dox puts one `/` between the parts. `'blogs'` and `'/blogs/'` work the same.
2.  Makes `GET /blogs/{id}`. `{id}` is a route param. The controller asks for it as `int id`.
3.  These routes match only when the `Host` header is `dartondox.com`. Other hosts get `404`.
4.  `AuthMiddleware` runs before `me` and `logout`. It runs after the global and router middleware.

Groups can be nested. `Route.group('blogs', ...)` with `Route.get('all', ...)` makes `/blogs/all`.

To turn CORS on or off for some routes, see [CORS](../security/cors.md).

## Resource routes

One line makes the usual CRUD routes for a controller.

```dart
Route.resource('blogs', BlogController());
```

| Method | Path | Controller method |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `GET` | `/blogs` | `index` |
| `GET` | `/blogs/create` | `create` |
| `POST` | `/blogs` | `store` |
| `GET` | `/blogs/{id}` | `show` |
| `GET` | `/blogs/{id}/edit` | `edit` |
| `PUT`, `PATCH` | `/blogs/{id}` | `update` |
| `DELETE` | `/blogs/{id}` | `destroy` |

A method that the controller does not have is skipped. No route is made for it.
Any other error from the controller is not hidden. It stops the app at start, so you see it.
See [Resource controller](controller.md#resource-controller) to make one with the CLI.

## Serve storage files

`Route.files(path)` serves the files of a storage disk at `GET <path>/{key*}`.
By default only signed URLs work. Other requests get `403`.
See [File Storage](../digging-deeper/file-storage.md#serve-local-signed-urls).

```dart
Route.files('files');
Route.files('public', disk: 'local', signed: false);
```

## Request body for the docs

`post`, `put` and `patch` take a `body:` schema. It shows in the [OpenAPI docs](../packages/openapi.md).
It does **not** check the request. To check input, use a [DTO](validation.md).

```dart
Route.post('/posts', controller.store, body: v.object(<String, Schema<Object?>>{
  'title': v.string().min(3),
}));
```


---

# Request

Source: https://dartondox.dev/latest/3.xthe-basic/request/

# Request

This page shows how to read input, files, headers and cookies from a request.

## Typed input (recommended)

Ask for a [DTO](validation.md) in your controller. Dox reads the body (or the query for `GET`), checks it, and gives you a typed object.

```dart
Route.put('/users/{id}', controller.update);

class UserController {
  Future<User?> update( // (1)!
    int id, // (2)!
    UpdateUser input, // (3)!
  ) async {
    User? user = await User().find(id);
    user?.name = input.name;
    await user?.save();
    return user;
  }
}
```

1.  The return value is the response. Dox waits for a `Future`.
    A `String` is sent as text. A `Map` or a model is sent as JSON.
2.  A path param. It is `{id}` from the route. `/users/abc` answers `404`, because `abc` is not an `int`.
3.  A DTO. Dox reads the body, checks it, and builds the object before this method runs.

Bad input gets `422` before your method runs. See [Validation](validation.md).

## Raw input

Add a `DoxRequest` parameter to read the raw values. These values are **not** checked.

```dart
class ApiController {
  String sayHello(DoxRequest req) {
    String? name = req.input('name');
    return 'Hello $name';
  }
}
```

| Code | Gives |
| --- | --- |
| `req.input('name')` | one value from the query string or the body. The body wins when both have the key. |
| `req.all()` | all values from the query string and the body, as a `Map` |
| `req.only(<String>['name', 'email'])` | only these keys |
| `req.has('name')` | `true` when the key is there and not empty |
| `req.body` | the body only (JSON, form data) |
| `req.query` | the query string only |
| `req.add('key', value)`, `req.merge({...})` | add values, for example in a middleware |

## Route params

Ask for a path param as a typed parameter. `int id` gets `42` from `/users/42`.

```dart
Route.get('/hello/{name}', controller.sayHello);
Route.get('/users/{id}', controller.show);

class ApiController {
  String sayHello(String name) {
    return 'Hello $name';
  }

  Future<User?> show(int id) async {
    return User().find(id);
  }
}
```

The values are also in `req.param`, like `req.param['id']`.
See [Controller: parameters](controller.md#parameters).

## Form data (File)

An uploaded file is a `RequestFile`. The request must be `multipart/form-data`.
Put the file in a DTO, so Dox checks its type and size:

```dart
@Dto()
class UploadImage {
  @Image()
  @MaxSize('5MB')
  final RequestFile image;

  const UploadImage({required this.image});

  static const DtoSchema<UploadImage> schema = $UploadImageDto;
}

class ApiController {
  Future<Map<String, String>> uploadImage(UploadImage input) async {
    String uploadedPath = await input.image.store('images');
    return <String, String>{'filename': uploadedPath};
  }
}
```

Without a DTO, `req.input('image')` gives the `RequestFile`. It is not checked.

### `RequestFile`

```dart
RequestFile file = req.input('video');

file.filename;        // name from the client
file.filetype;        // content type, like video/mp4
file.extension;       // mp4
file.length;          // size in bytes
await file.size;      // size in KB
file.stream();        // read it in chunks
await file.store('videos');              // save to storage. returns the path
await file.moveTo('/data/videos/1.mp4'); // move it. returns the new File
await file.bytes;     // the whole file in memory. avoid for big files
```

!!! warning "Save the file before you return"
    A file up to 1 MB stays in memory. A bigger file is written to a temp file while it arrives.
    The temp file is **deleted when the response is sent**.
    So call `store`, `moveTo` or `stream` before your controller returns.

### Size limits

A body that is too big gets `413 Payload Too Large`. Dox checks `Content-Length` first.
It also counts the bytes while it reads the body.

```dart title="lib/config/app.dart"
AppConfig(
  maxBodySize: 10 * 1024 * 1024,        // JSON and urlencoded, default 10 MB
  maxMultipartSize: 100 * 1024 * 1024,  // form-data uploads, default 100 MB
);
```

Set the same limit in your proxy, like `client_max_body_size` in nginx.

## Headers

```dart
String? token = req.header('X-Token');
Map<String, dynamic> all = req.headers;

req.userAgent();  // User-Agent header
req.host();       // Host header
req.origin();     // Origin header, or null
req.referer();    // Referer header, or null
req.isJson();     // true for a JSON body
req.isFormData(); // true for multipart/form-data
req.locale;       // first language of Accept-Language, like 'th', or null
```

## Cookies

```dart
String? token = req.cookie('token');                 // decrypted value
String? raw = req.cookie('theme', decrypt: false);   // value as sent
```

See [Response](response.md#cookie) to set a cookie.

## Client IP and scheme

```dart
req.ip();       // client IP
req.scheme();   // http or https
req.isSecure(); // true for https
```

Behind a proxy, `req.ip()` shows the proxy, not the client.
Set `trustedProxies` in `AppConfig` to fix it. See [Deployment](../digging-deeper/deployment.md#https-put-a-proxy-in-front).


---

# Response

Source: https://dartondox.dev/latest/3.xthe-basic/response/

# Response

This page shows what a controller can return, and how to set the status, headers and cookies.

## Return a value

Return the value from your controller. Dox turns it into the response.

| You return | The client gets |
| --- | --- |
| a `String` | the text |
| a `Map` or a `List` | JSON |
| a model, a list of models, a [serializer](../database/model/serializer.md) | JSON (from `toJson()`) |
| a `DateTime` | the ISO 8601 text |
| an `IHttpException`, like `NotFoundHttpException()` | its status code and its message (text, or JSON for a `Map`) |
| a `File` (from `dart:io`) | the file, streamed |
| a `Stream<List<int>>` | the bytes, streamed |
| `StreamFile`, `DownloadableFile` from `Storage()` | the file, streamed |
| `response(...)` | full control: status, headers, cookies |

```dart
// text
String ping(DoxRequest req) {
  return 'pong';
}

// JSON
Map<String, String> hello(DoxRequest req) {
  return <String, String>{'message': 'hello world!'};
}

// a model
Future<Blog?> show(int id) async {
  return Blog().find(id);
}

// a list of models
Future<List<Blog>> index(DoxRequest req) async {
  return Blog().all();
}

// an error
Future<Blog> showOrFail(int id) async {
  Blog? blog = await Blog().find(id);
  if (blog == null) {
    throw NotFoundHttpException(); // 404 Not Found
  }
  return blog;
}
```

## Errors

Throw or return an exception to answer with an error.

| Exception | Status |
| --- | --- |
| `BadRequestException()` | `400` |
| `NotFoundHttpException()` | `404` |
| `PayloadTooLargeException()` | `413` |
| `UnsupportedMediaTypeException()` | `415` |
| `ValidationException()` | `422` |
| `InternalErrorException()` | `500` |

Each one takes `message:`, `errorCode:` and `code:`:

```dart
throw NotFoundHttpException(message: 'Blog not found');
```

The client gets `404` with `{"code":"not_found","message":"Blog not found"}`.
`code` is the `errorCode`. A `Map` message is sent as it is.

For another status, extend `IHttpException`:

```dart
import 'dart:io';

import 'package:dox_core/dox_core.dart';

class ForbiddenException extends IHttpException {
  ForbiddenException({String message = 'Forbidden'}) {
    super.code = HttpStatus.forbidden;
    super.errorCode = 'forbidden';
    super.message = message;
  }
}
```

Any other error gets `500`. It is also passed to the `errorHandler` in `AppConfig`.

## Files and big responses

Return a `File` or a `Stream<List<int>>`. Dox sends it in chunks. It does not load it all into memory.

- A `File` sets `Content-Type` (from the file name), `Content-Length` and `Accept-Ranges`.
- It answers `Range: bytes=...` with `206 Partial Content`. Video players can seek, and downloads can resume.
- `Storage().stream()` and `Storage().download()` on the local disk also stream the file.

```dart
import 'dart:io';

// a file from disk
Route.get('/video', (DoxRequest req) => File('storage/video.mp4'));

// a download from Storage
Future<DownloadableFile> download(DoxRequest req) async {
  // sends Content-Disposition, so the browser saves the file
  return Storage().download('report.pdf');
}

// a stream from Storage
Future<StreamFile> show(DoxRequest req) async {
  return Storage().stream('photo.jpg');
}
```

See [File Storage](../digging-deeper/file-storage.md).

## The `response()` helper

Use `response(content)` when you need to set the status, headers or cookies.
All methods return the response, so you can chain them.

```dart
import 'dart:io';

import 'package:dox_core/dox_core.dart';

DoxResponse store(DoxRequest req) {
  return response(<String, String>{'status': 'created'})
      .statusCode(201)
      .header('X-Request-Id', 'abc')
      .contentType(ContentType.json);
}
```

| Method | Does |
| --- | --- |
| `statusCode(201)` | sets the status code. Default `200`. |
| `header('X-Key', 'value')` | adds one header |
| `withHeaders({...})` | **replaces** all headers set before |
| `contentType(ContentType.html)` | sets `Content-Type` (`ContentType` is from `dart:io`) |
| `cache(Duration(minutes: 5))` | sets `Cache-Control: max-age=300` |
| `cookie(DoxCookie(...))` | sets a cookie |
| `content(value)` | changes the body |
| `stream(byteStream)` | sends a `Stream<List<int>>` as the body |

## Cookie

```dart
// set a cookie
DoxCookie cookie = DoxCookie('theme', 'dark');
return response('ok').cookie(cookie);

// set a cookie with options
DoxCookie token = DoxCookie(
  'token',
  'value',
  maxAge: Duration(days: 7), // sent as Max-Age in seconds. default 1 hour
  httpOnly: true,
  secure: true,
  path: '/',
);
return response('ok').cookie(token);

// delete a cookie
return response('ok').cookie(DoxCookie('token', ''), setExpire: true);

// read a cookie
String? value = req.cookie('token');
```

!!! info "Encrypt and decrypt"
    By default, Dox encrypts the cookie value with `APP_KEY`, and decrypts it when you read it.
    To turn this off, use `DoxCookie(key, value, encrypt: false)` to set it,
    and `req.cookie(key, decrypt: false)` to read it.

## Change every response

To change every response in one place (for example, to add a header), set a `responseHandler` in `AppConfig`.

```dart title="lib/app/http/handler.dart"
import 'package:dox_core/dox_core.dart';

class ResponseHandler extends ResponseHandlerInterface {
  @override
  DoxResponse handle(DoxResponse res) {
    return res.header('X-Powered-By', 'Dox');
  }
}
```

```dart title="lib/config/app.dart"
AppConfig appConfig = AppConfig(
  responseHandler: ResponseHandler(),
  // ...
);
```


---

# Controller

Source: https://dartondox.dev/latest/3.xthe-basic/controller/

# Controller

A controller holds the code that answers a route. It can be a class method, a static method or a plain function.

## Class based controller

Make one with the CLI:

```bash
dox create:controller Blog
```

It writes `lib/app/http/controllers/blog.controller.dart`.

```dart title="lib/app/http/controllers/blog.controller.dart"
import 'package:dox_core/dox_core.dart';

class BlogController {
  String index(DoxRequest req) {
    return 'all blogs';
  }
}
```

```dart title="lib/routes/api.dart"
BlogController blogController = BlogController();
Route.get('/blogs', blogController.index);
```

### Static method

```dart
class AppController {
  static String ping(DoxRequest req) {
    return 'pong';
  }
}

Route.get('/ping', AppController.ping);
```

## Function based controller

```dart
String listBlog(DoxRequest req) {
  return 'all blogs';
}

Route.get('/blogs', listBlog);
```

## Resource controller

A resource controller has the 7 methods that `Route.resource` uses.

Make one with the CLI:

```bash
dox create:controller Blog -r
```

```dart title="lib/app/http/controllers/blog.controller.dart"
import 'package:dox_core/dox_core.dart';

class BlogController {
  /// GET /resource
  Future<dynamic> index(DoxRequest req) async {}

  /// GET /resource/create
  Future<dynamic> create(DoxRequest req) async {}

  /// POST /resource
  Future<dynamic> store(DoxRequest req) async {}

  /// GET /resource/{id}
  Future<dynamic> show(DoxRequest req, int id) async {}

  /// GET /resource/{id}/edit
  Future<dynamic> edit(DoxRequest req, int id) async {}

  /// PUT|PATCH /resource/{id}
  Future<dynamic> update(DoxRequest req, int id) async {}

  /// DELETE /resource/{id}
  Future<dynamic> destroy(DoxRequest req, int id) async {}
}
```

```dart title="lib/routes/api.dart"
Route.resource('blogs', BlogController());
```

You can delete methods you do not need. `Route.resource` skips them.
See [Routing: resource routes](routing.md#resource-routes).

## Parameters

A controller asks for what it needs by **type**. Dox fills each parameter.

```dart
Route.put('/teams/{teamId}/users/{id}', controller.update);

class UserController {
  Future<User> update(int teamId, int id, UpdateUser body) async { ... }
}
```

| Parameter type | Dox gives |
| --- | --- |
| `DoxRequest` | the request |
| a `@Dto` class | the checked body or query. See [Validation](validation.md). |
| `String`, `int`, `double`, `num`, `bool` | the path params, in the order of the route |
| the same types with `?` | an optional path param (`{id?}`). `null` when it is not in the URL. |

Rules:

- The order of parameters is free. Path params are matched by position: the first path-param parameter gets the first `{...}` in the route.
- `DoxRequest` is not needed. Add it only when you use it.
- At most one `@Dto` parameter.
- Only positional parameters. Named and `[optional]` parameters are not supported.
- A catch-all `{path*}` param is a `String`.
- The same rules work for static methods and plain functions.

**Path param types.** Dox converts the text from the URL:

- `int`: `"42"` is `42`. `"abc"` or `"4.5"` answers `404 Not Found`.
- `double`, `num`: `"4.5"` is `4.5`.
- `bool`: `true` or `1` is `true`. `false` or `0` is `false`.
- Any other text answers `404` too.
- Path params are checked first. When one is wrong, the DTO is not checked.

**Checked at start.** The server does not start when:

- a parameter type is not in the list above, and not a `@Dto` (did you run `dart run build_runner build`?),
- the method has more path-param parameters than the route has `{...}` params.

!!! info "Why types, not names?"
    Dox reads the parameter types of your method once, when the routes are registered at start. It needs no `dart:mirrors`.
    So `update(int teamId, int id)` works by position, not by the names `teamId` and `id`.

## What to return

Return a `String`, a `Map`, a model, a `File` and more. See [Response](response.md).


---

# Middleware

Source: https://dartondox.dev/latest/3.xthe-basic/middleware/

# Middleware

Middleware is code that runs before the controller. Use it for checks like login, logging or rate limits.

## How it works

A middleware gets the request. It then does one of these:

- **Return the request.** Dox goes on to the next middleware, then to the controller.
- **Return something else** (a `String`, a `Map`, a `response(...)`). Dox sends it as the response. The controller does not run.
- **Throw an exception**, like `NotFoundHttpException()`. Dox sends the error response. See [Response: errors](response.md#errors).

A middleware can be `async`. Dox waits for it.

## Class based middleware

Create one with the CLI. It writes `lib/app/http/middleware/logger.middleware.dart`.

```bash
dox create:middleware Logger
```

```dart title="lib/app/http/middleware/logger.middleware.dart"
import 'package:dox_core/dox_core.dart';

class LoggerMiddleware implements IDoxMiddleware { // (1)!
  @override
  dynamic handle(IDoxRequest req) { // (2)!
    print('${req.method} ${req.uri.path}');
    return req; // (3)!
  }
}
```

1.  `IDoxMiddleware` is the interface for a class middleware. Dox calls its `handle` method.
2.  `handle` gets the request. It can be `async`. Dox waits for it.
3.  Return the request to go on to the next middleware, then the controller.
    Return anything else, like `response(...)`, and Dox sends that as the response.

Then put it on a route:

```dart title="lib/routes/api.dart"
Route.get('/ping', <dynamic>[LoggerMiddleware(), webController.pong]);
```

!!! note
    `handle` takes an `IDoxRequest`, not a `DoxRequest`. This is the type that `IDoxMiddleware` asks for.

## Function based middleware

A function that takes a `DoxRequest` also works as middleware.

```dart title="lib/app/http/middleware/api_key.middleware.dart"
import 'package:dox_core/dox_core.dart';

dynamic apiKeyMiddleware(DoxRequest req) {
  if (req.header('X-Api-Key') != 'secret') {
    return response(<String, String>{'message': 'Unauthorized'}).statusCode(401);
  }
  return req;
}
```

```dart title="lib/routes/api.dart"
Route.get('/ping', <dynamic>[apiKeyMiddleware, webController.pong]);
```

## Many middleware on one route

Put them in the list before the controller. They run from left to right.
You can mix class and function middleware.

```dart
Route.get('/ping', <dynamic>[
  LoggerMiddleware(),
  apiKeyMiddleware,
  webController.pong, // the controller is always last
]);
```

## Middleware for a group of routes

```dart
Route.middleware(<dynamic>[LoggerMiddleware()], () {
  Route.get('/me', controller.me);
  Route.post('/logout', controller.logout);
});
```

## Middleware for a router or for all routes

For one router, set its `middleware` list:

```dart title="lib/routes/api.dart"
class ApiRouter extends Router {
  @override
  String get prefix => 'api';

  @override
  List<dynamic> get middleware => <dynamic>[LoggerMiddleware()];

  @override
  void register() {
    // every route here runs LoggerMiddleware
  }
}
```

For all routes, set `globalMiddleware` in the app config:

```dart title="lib/config/app.dart"
AppConfig appConfig = AppConfig(
  globalMiddleware: <dynamic>[LogMiddleware(enabled: true)],
  // ...
);
```

The order is: global middleware, then router middleware, then group middleware, then route middleware.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    Q["Request"] --> G["Global<br>globalMiddleware"]
    G --> R["Router<br>middleware getter"]
    R --> P["Group<br>Route.middleware"]
    P --> T["Route<br>list before the controller"]
    T --> C["Controller"]
    C --> S["Response"]
    G & R & P & T -.->|"returns a value or throws"| S
```

!!! tip "Built-in middleware"
    - `LogMiddleware` from `dox_core` writes one JSON log line per request.
    - `AuthMiddleware` from `dox_auth` checks the JWT token. See [Authentication](../security/authentication.md).


---

# Validation

Source: https://dartondox.dev/latest/3.xthe-basic/validation/

# Validation

This page shows how to check request input with typed DTO classes.

Write a class with `@Dto()`. Ask for it in your controller.
Dox reads the request, checks it, and gives you a typed object.
When the input is wrong, Dox answers `422` with the errors. Your controller does not run.

This is how a DTO goes from your code to a checked object:

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    D["@Dto class<br>CreateUser"] --> B["build_runner"]
    B --> G["Generated schema<br>$CreateUserDto"]
    G --> L["dtos list<br>AppConfig(dtos: dtos)"]
    Q["Request<br>body or query"] --> V["Check against the schema"]
    L --> V
    V -->|errors| E["422 with the errors"]
    V -->|ok| T["Typed object<br>CreateUser"]
    T --> C["Controller"]
```

```dart title="lib/app/http/dtos/create_user.dto.dart"
import 'package:dox_core/dox_core.dart';

part 'create_user.dto.g.dart'; // (1)!

enum Role { admin, user }

@Dto()
class CreateUser {
  @Length(min: 3, max: 50)
  @Trim() // (2)!
  final String name;

  @Email()
  final String email;

  @Min(18)
  final int? age; // (3)!

  final Role role; // (4)!

  @MaxItems(5) // (5)!
  final List<String> tags;

  const CreateUser({
    required this.name,
    required this.email,
    this.age,
    this.role = Role.user,
    this.tags = const <String>[],
  });

  static const DtoSchema<CreateUser> schema = $CreateUserDto; // (6)!
}
```

1.  `build_runner` writes this file. It holds the checks and the code that builds the object.
2.  Rules run from top to bottom. `@Trim()` cuts the spaces, then `@Length` checks the text.
    After `@Trim()`, an empty string counts as missing.
3.  A nullable field is optional. `@Min(18)` runs only when the client sends a value.
4.  An enum matches the name exactly, so only `"admin"` or `"user"`.
    `Role.user` is used when the key is missing.
5.  `@MaxItems(5)` checks the list. A rule like `@Email()` on a list would check each item instead.
6.  `$CreateUserDto` is the generated schema. The generator also puts it in the list in `lib/dtos.g.dart`.
    Give that list to `AppConfig(dtos: dtos)`, so Dox can find the DTO when a controller asks for it.

```dart title="lib/app/http/controllers/user.controller.dart"
class UserController {
  Future<User> store(CreateUser body) async {
    // body is already checked. body.age is an int?, body.role is a Role.
    User user = User()
      ..name = body.name
      ..email = body.email;
    await user.save();
    return user;
  }
}
```

Then run the generator:

```bash
dox build_runner:build   # or: dart run build_runner build
```

## Setup

You do this once per app.

1. Put DTOs in `lib/app/http/dtos/`. Name the file `<name>.dto.dart`.
   `dox create:dto CreateUser` makes `lib/app/http/dtos/create_user.dto.dart` for you.
2. Each DTO file has `part '<name>.dto.g.dart';` and the `schema` line:
   `static const DtoSchema<CreateUser> schema = $CreateUserDto;`
3. Run `dart run build_runner build` (or `dox build_runner:watch`).
   It writes a `.dto.g.dart` file next to each DTO and one list of all DTOs in `lib/dtos.g.dart`.
4. Give that list to the app in `lib/config/app.dart`:

```dart title="lib/config/app.dart"
import 'package:my_app/dtos.g.dart';

AppConfig appConfig = AppConfig(
  dtos: dtos, // from lib/dtos.g.dart
  // ...
);
```

!!! info "Why the list?"
    Dox does not use `dart:mirrors`. So it can not find a class by its name at runtime.
    Without the list, a controller that asks for a DTO stops the server at start, with a clear error.
    The generated list tells Dox which classes are DTOs. You never edit it by hand.

**What the generator makes for each DTO** (no reflection, works with `dox build` AOT):

- the checks for every field,
- the code that turns the input map into your class,
- a JSON Schema, used by the [OpenAPI docs](../packages/openapi.md).

## Use a DTO

### As a controller parameter

Add a parameter with the DTO type. Dox checks the request before your method runs.

```dart
Future<User> store(CreateUser body) async { ... }

// with path params and the request
Future<User> update(DoxRequest req, int id, UpdateUser body) async { ... }
```

See [Controller: parameters](controller.md#parameters) for the full rules.

### Inside a method

`req.validate<T>()` does the same work. It returns the object or throws the `422` error.

```dart
Future<User> store(DoxRequest req) async {
  CreateUser data = await req.validate<CreateUser>();
  // ...
}
```

`req.validate<T>()` is always async. Always `await` it.

## Required and optional

The Dart type decides. You do not write `required` or `nullable`.

| Field | Missing key | `null` | Result |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `final String name;` (no default) | error `required` | error `required` | required |
| `final int? age;` | `null` | `null` | optional |
| `final Role role;` with `this.role = Role.user` | the default | error `required` | optional, has a default |
| `final Maybe<String?> bio;` with `this.bio = const Maybe.missing()` | `isPresent == false` | `isPresent == true`, `value == null` | optional, knows "missing" from `null` |

Rules:

- **Required** = not nullable and no default in the constructor.
- **Optional** = nullable (`T?`), or has a default.
- A default is used only when the key is missing. A default value is not checked by the rules.
- `null` is never allowed for a non-nullable field, even when it has a default.
- **An empty string counts as missing.** After `@Trim()`, `""` is treated like a missing key, in JSON, query and form data.
  So a required `String` rejects `""` and `"   "` (with `@Trim()`). A `String?` gets `null`.
  Add `@AllowEmpty()` to keep `""` as a real value.
- Rules on an optional field run only when it has a value.

### Missing or `null`? (for PATCH)

A `T?` field gives `null` for both a missing key and a `null` value.
When you must know the difference, use `Maybe<T>`. Its default must be `const Maybe.missing()`.

```dart
@Dto()
class UpdateUser {
  @Length(max: 500)
  final Maybe<String?> bio;

  const UpdateUser({this.bio = const Maybe.missing()});

  static const DtoSchema<UpdateUser> schema = $UpdateUserDto;
}

// in the controller
if (body.bio.isPresent) {
  user.bio = body.bio.value; // can be null: the client cleared it
}
```

Rules on a `Maybe<T>` field check `value` when it is present and not `null`.

## Types

| Dart type | JSON | Query and form data (text) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `String` | a string | as is |
| `int` | a whole number (`18` or `18.0`) | `"18"` |
| `double` | any number (`18` becomes `18.0`) | `"4.5"`, `"18"` |
| `num` | any number | `"18"`, `"4.5"` |
| `bool` | `true` / `false` | `true`, `1`, `yes`, `on` / `false`, `0`, `no`, `off` (any case) |
| `DateTime` | an ISO 8601 string | the same |
| an `enum` | the name, like `"admin"` | the same |
| `RequestFile` | not allowed | a file part in `multipart/form-data` |
| a `@Dto` class | an object | bracket keys, like `address[city]` |
| `List<T>` | an array | repeated keys `tags=a&tags=b`, or `tags[]=a&tags[]=b` |
| `Map<String, T>` | an object with any keys | bracket keys, like `meta[color]` |
| `Object?`, `dynamic`, `Map<String, dynamic>` | any JSON, not checked | any text, not checked |

**JSON is strict.** In a JSON body, `"18"` is not an `int`. You get the error `integer`.
**Query and form data are text,** so Dox turns the text into the field type first.
If it can not, you get the type error (like `integer` or `boolean`).

More details:

- `int` never takes a fraction. `"4.5"` or `4.5` gives the error `integer`.
- `DateTime` takes `2024-01-31` or `2024-01-31T10:00:00Z`. A value without a time zone is read as UTC.
  The result is always UTC (`isUtc == true`). A number (timestamp) is not allowed.
- An `enum` matches the name exactly. `"Admin"` does not match `Role.admin`.
- In query and form data, one value for a `List<T>` field gives a list with one item.
- In bracket keys, list indexes are sorted and packed: `items[3]` alone gives a list with one item.
  A list can have at most 1000 items, and keys can nest at most 10 levels. More gives `422`.
- The generator stops with an error for any other type.

## Where the data comes from

| Request | Dox reads |
| --- | --- |
| `GET`, `HEAD`, `DELETE` | the query string |
| `POST`, `PUT`, `PATCH` | the body |

Dox reads **one** source. It never mixes the query and the body.
So a query value can not overwrite a body value.

The body can be:

- JSON: `application/json` (or any `+json` type). Strict types.
- `application/x-www-form-urlencoded`: text, converted.
- `multipart/form-data`: text, converted. Files go to `RequestFile` fields.

Other content types get `415 Unsupported Media Type`. A body that is not valid JSON gets `400 Bad Request`.
A JSON body that is not an object (like `[1, 2]`) gets `422` with the key `_root`.

### Choose the source

Set it on the DTO, when this DTO is always read from one place:

```dart
@Dto(source: Source.query) // also for POST
class SearchUsers { ... }
```

Or set it for one call:

```dart
SearchUsers filter = await req.validate<SearchUsers>(source: Source.query);
```

`Source.auto` (the default) uses the table above. `Source.query` and `Source.body` force one source.

### Path params

Path params are not part of a DTO. Ask for them as typed controller parameters:

```dart
Route.put('/users/{id}', controller.update);

Future<User> update(int id, UpdateUser body) async { ... }
```

A path param that does not fit its type (like `abc` for `int id`) answers `404`.
See [Controller: parameters](controller.md#parameters).

## Keys: snake_case by default

The JSON key is the field name in snake_case, the same as the [ORM](../database/model/index.md).
`firstName` reads `first_name`.

```dart
@Dto()
class SignUp {
  final String firstName; // key: first_name

  @Name('emailAddress')
  final String email; // key: emailAddress

  const SignUp({required this.firstName, required this.email});

  static const DtoSchema<SignUp> schema = $SignUpDto;
}
```
