To use the field names as they are (camelCase), set it on the DTO:

```dart
@Dto(keyCase: KeyCase.field) // firstName reads firstName
```

Error keys always use the input key (`first_name`), not the Dart name.

## Unknown keys

Keys that the DTO does not have are dropped. You never see them.

With `@Dto(strict: true)`, an unknown key is an error:

```json
{ "is_admin": "The is_admin field is not allowed" }
```

## Rules

Put rules on a field as annotations. A field can have many. They run from top to bottom.
The first rule that fails gives the error for that field.

```dart
@Trim()
@Lowercase()
@Email()
@MaxLength(255)
final String email;
```

Every rule is in the [rules reference](validation-rules.md). The short list:

| Kind | Annotations |
| --- | --- |
| Text | `@Length`, `@MinLength`, `@MaxLength`, `@Email`, `@Url`, `@Uuid`, `@Ip`, `@Regex`, `@In`, `@NotIn`, `@StartsWith`, `@EndsWith`, `@Alpha`, `@AlphaNumeric`, `@AlphaDash` |
| Change text | `@Trim`, `@Lowercase`, `@Uppercase`, `@AllowEmpty` |
| Numbers | `@Min`, `@Max`, `@Range`, `@Positive`, `@GreaterThan`, `@LessThan`, `@In`, `@NotIn` |
| Lists | `@MinItems`, `@MaxItems`, `@UniqueItems` |
| Dates | `@After`, `@Before` |
| Files | `@MaxSize`, `@Mimes`, `@Image` |
| Database | `@Unique`, `@Exists` (from `dox_orm`) |
| Keys | `@Name` |

!!! tip "Rules on a list check each item"
    `@Email()` on a `List<String>` checks every item. The error key is `emails.2`.
    Only `@MinItems`, `@MaxItems` and `@UniqueItems` check the list itself.

The generator stops with an error when a rule does not fit the type, like `@Email()` on an `int`.

!!! note "Name clash"
    `dox_core` exports the rule names (`Uuid`, `Name`, `Range`, `Image`, ...).
    A file that also imports a package with the same name, like `package:uuid`, gets an "ambiguous import" error.
    Fix it with `hide`: `import 'package:dox_core/dox_core.dart' hide Uuid;`.
    `dox_orm` has a `Schema` class too: `import 'package:dox_orm/dox_orm.dart' hide Schema;`.

### Enums or `@In`

Use a Dart `enum` when you can. The allowed values are the enum names.
Use `@In([...])` for a plain `String` or `int` with a few allowed values:

```dart
final Role role;              // "admin" or "user"

@In(<String>['draft', 'published'])
final String status;
```

## Nested objects and lists

A field can be another `@Dto` class, or a list of them.

```dart
@Dto()
class Address {
  final String city;

  @Length(min: 5, max: 5)
  final String postCode;

  const Address({required this.city, required this.postCode});

  static const DtoSchema<Address> schema = $AddressDto;
}

@Dto()
class OrderItem {
  final String name;

  @Positive()
  final int quantity;

  const OrderItem({required this.name, required this.quantity});

  static const DtoSchema<OrderItem> schema = $OrderItemDto;
}

@Dto()
class CreateOrder {
  final Address address;

  @MinItems(1)
  final List<OrderItem> items;

  const CreateOrder({required this.address, required this.items});

  static const DtoSchema<CreateOrder> schema = $CreateOrderDto;
}
```

```json
{
  "address": { "city": "Bangkok", "post_code": "10110" },
  "items": [
    { "name": "Shoes", "quantity": 2 },
    { "name": "Socks", "quantity": 0 }
  ]
}
```

Error: `{"items.1.quantity": "The quantity must be greater than 0"}`.

A nested DTO has its own options (`keyCase`, `strict`). A nullable nested field (`Address?`) is optional.

## Files

A `RequestFile` field reads a file from `multipart/form-data`.

```dart
@Dto()
class UploadAvatar {
  @Image()
  @MaxSize('2MB')
  final RequestFile avatar;

  @MaxItems(5)
  @Mimes(<String>['pdf', 'docx'])
  final List<RequestFile> documents; // documents[] or repeated documents

  const UploadAvatar({required this.avatar, this.documents = const <RequestFile>[]});

  static const DtoSchema<UploadAvatar> schema = $UploadAvatarDto;
}
```

- Dox reads the first bytes of the file to find its real type. The file name and the client content type are not trusted.
- `@Image()` allows `jpg`, `jpeg`, `png`, `gif`, `webp` and `bmp`. Not `svg`, because an SVG can hold scripts.
- A text field sent where a file is expected gives the error `file`.
- Save the file before you return. See [Request: form data](request.md#form-data-file).

## Checks across fields: `validate()`

Add a method `validate(DtoErrors errors)` to the DTO. Dox calls it after every field rule passed.
At that point, all fields have their typed values.

```dart
@Dto()
class SignUp {
  @MinLength(8)
  final String password;

  final String passwordConfirmation;

  final DateTime? startsAt;
  final DateTime? endsAt;

  const SignUp({
    required this.password,
    required this.passwordConfirmation,
    this.startsAt,
    this.endsAt,
  });

  void validate(DtoErrors errors) {
    if (password != passwordConfirmation) {
      errors.add('password_confirmation', 'The passwords do not match');
    }
    if (startsAt != null && endsAt != null && !endsAt!.isAfter(startsAt!)) {
      errors.add('ends_at', 'The end must be after the start');
    }
  }

  static const DtoSchema<SignUp> schema = $SignUpDto;
}
```

The exact API:

- The method is named `validate`. It takes one `DtoErrors` and returns `void` or `Future<void>`.
- `errors.add(String key, String message)` adds an error. `key` is the input key (snake_case), not the Dart name.
  The message is used as it is (no placeholders, no message resolver).
- `errors.has(String key)` is `true` when that key already has an error.
- Use the key `_root` for an error that is not about one field.
- In a nested DTO, keys are relative. Dox adds the parent path: `address.post_code`.
- Do not throw for bad input. Add an error.

## Database rules: `@Unique` and `@Exists`

These come from `dox_orm`. They read the database, so they run last.

```dart
import 'package:dox_orm/dox_orm.dart' hide Schema;

@Dto()
class CreateUser {
  @Email()
  @Unique('users', column: 'email')
  final String email;

  @Exists('teams') // column defaults to id
  final int teamId;

  @Exists('tags')
  final List<int> tagIds; // checks every item in one query

  const CreateUser({required this.email, required this.teamId, this.tagIds = const <int>[]});

  static const DtoSchema<CreateUser> schema = $CreateUserDto;
}
```

| Annotation | Passes when |
| --- | --- |
| `@Unique(table, {column})` | no row has this value. `column` defaults to the input key. |
| `@Exists(table, {column})` | a row has this value. `column` defaults to `id`. |

For an update, skip the row you are updating. `ignoreParam` names a path param:

```dart
// PUT /users/{id}
@Unique('users', column: 'email', ignoreParam: 'id') // WHERE id != {id}
final String email;
```

- `ignoreColumn:` sets the id column. Default `id`.
- `connection:` uses another `dox_orm` connection. Default: the default connection.
- Soft-deleted rows count too.
- Upper or lower case: this depends on your database collation.
- On a `List<T>` field, each item is checked. All items use one `WHERE IN` query.

## The order of checks

1. Read the input and convert types. Change text (`@Trim`, `@Lowercase`, `@Uppercase`). Missing required fields.
2. The field rules, top to bottom.
3. The `validate()` method (nested DTOs first, then the parent).
4. Async rules (`@Unique`, `@Exists`, your `AsyncRule`), one at a time, in field order.

**Each step runs only when the step before it had no errors.**
So the database is never asked about input that is already wrong.

- Steps 1 and 2 run per DTO. A nested DTO checks its own types first, then its own rules.
  So one answer can have a type error in `address` and a rule error in `items.1`.
- Inside one step, Dox collects the errors of all fields.
- A default value is not checked by the field rules. (Async rules check the final value.)

## The error response

When a check fails, Dox answers `422 Unprocessable Entity` with a flat JSON object.
The key is the path to the value. The value is one message (the first error of that field).

```json
{
  "email": "The email is not a valid email",
  "tags.0": "The tags may not be greater than 20 characters",
  "address.city": "The city is required",
  "items.1.quantity": "The quantity must be greater than 0"
}
```

- Paths use dots. List items use the index: `tags.0`.
- Paths use the input keys (`post_code`), after `@Name` and `keyCase`.
- `_root` is for errors about the whole body.

## Messages

Every rule has a default English message. See the [rules reference](validation-rules.md).

**Placeholders:** `{field}` is the last key of the path (for list items: the list key).
`{value}` is the input value. Rules add their own, like `{min}` and `{max}`.

### On one rule

Every annotation takes `message:`.

```dart
@Email(message: 'Please check your email')
@Length(min: 3, message: 'At least {min} letters, please')
```

### On one DTO

`@Dto(messages: ...)` sets messages by code, or by `key.code`.
Use it for messages that have no annotation, like `required` or a type error.

```dart
@Dto(messages: <String, String>{
  'email.required': 'We need your email',
  'required': 'Please fill in {field}',
  'integer': 'The {field} must be a number',
})
```

### For the whole app, and other languages

Dox finds a message in this order:

1. `message:` on the annotation.
2. `@Dto(messages:)`: first `key.code` (like `email.required`), then `code`.
3. The app message resolver.
4. The default English text.

For other languages, extend `MessageResolver` and set it in the config.
`request.locale` is the first language in the `Accept-Language` header, like `th`. It is `null` when there is none.

```dart
class AppMessages extends MessageResolver {
  static const Map<String, Map<String, String>> _texts = <String, Map<String, String>>{
    'th': <String, String>{'required': 'กรุณากรอก {field}'},
  };

  @override
  String resolve(MessageRequest request) {
    String? template = _texts[request.locale]?[request.code];
    if (template == null) {
      return super.resolve(request);
    }
    return format(template, request.params);
  }
}

AppConfig appConfig = AppConfig(
  validationMessages: AppMessages(),
  // ...
);
```

`MessageRequest` has `code`, `path`, `params`, `fallback`, `customMessage` and `locale`.

## Custom rules

A rule is a class that extends `Rule<T>`. It needs a `const` constructor, so you can use it as an annotation.
`T` is the field type (or the item type, for a list).

```dart
class Slug extends Rule<String> {
  const Slug({super.message});

  @override
  String get name {
    return 'slug'; // the error code
  }

  @override
  String get defaultMessage {
    return 'The {field} must be a slug';
  }

  @override
  bool check(String value, RuleContext context) {
    return _pattern.hasMatch(value);
  }

  static final RegExp _pattern = RegExp(r'^[a-z0-9]+(-[a-z0-9]+)*$');
}

@Dto()
class CreatePost {
  @Slug()
  final String slug;

  const CreatePost({required this.slug});

  static const DtoSchema<CreatePost> schema = $CreatePostDto;
}
```

- A rule with values: add `final` fields and override `params`. They become placeholders.
- `RuleContext` gives `path`, `field`, `root` (the whole input) and `lookup('other.key')`.
- Override `toJsonSchema()` to add JSON Schema keys, like `{'pattern': '^[a-z0-9-]+$'}`.
- A check that needs the database: extend `AsyncRule<T>` and implement `Future<bool> checkAsync(T value, RuleContext context)`.
  It runs in step 4 of [the order of checks](#the-order-of-checks).

```dart
class MinValue extends Rule<int> {
  const MinValue(this.min, {super.message});

  final int min;

  @override
  String get name {
    return 'min_value';
  }

  @override
  String get defaultMessage {
    return 'The {field} must be at least {min}';
  }

  @override
  Map<String, Object?> get params {
    return <String, Object?>{'min': min};
  }

  @override
  bool check(int value, RuleContext context) {
    return value >= min;
  }
}
```

## Dynamic input: fluent schemas

Some input has a shape you only know at runtime, like custom form fields from the database.
For that, build a schema with `v.object(...)` and use `req.validateSchema()`. It returns a `Map`.

```dart
Map<String, Schema<Object?>> fields = <String, Schema<Object?>>{};
for (FormField f in form.fields) {
  fields[f.key] = f.required ? v.string().min(1) : v.string().optional();
}

Map<String, dynamic> data = await req.validateSchema(v.object(fields));
```

Use a DTO for everything else. See [`dox_validation`](../packages/validation.md#fluent-schemas-for-dynamic-input).

## Testing

**Make a DTO directly.** It is a normal Dart class. This skips all checks.

```dart
CreateUser input = const CreateUser(name: 'Ann', email: 'ann@dox.dev');
await userService.create(input);
```

**Check a map** with the rules, like a request would:

```dart
CreateUser user = await CreateUser.schema.validateMap(<String, dynamic>{
  'name': 'Ann',
  'email': 'ann@dox.dev',
});
expect(user.role, Role.user);
```

**Check the errors** with `safeValidateMap`. It never throws.

```dart
ParseResult<CreateUser> result = await CreateUser.schema.safeValidateMap(<String, dynamic>{
  'name': 'A',
  'email': 'not-an-email',
});

expect(result.success, isFalse);
expect(result.errors, <String, String>{
  'name': 'The name must be between 3 and 50 characters',
  'email': 'The email is not a valid email',
});
```

Options of both methods:

- `source: Source.query` reads the map like a query string (text is converted). Default: `Source.body` with JSON types.
- `params: {'id': '5'}` gives path params, for `@Unique(ignoreParam: 'id')`.

`@Unique` and `@Exists` need a database. Use a test database, or test those fields in an integration test.

## Not supported

- A DTO can not extend another class, and can not be generic. The generator stops with an error.
- An enum value is always its Dart name. Custom wire values (like `"ADMIN"` for `Role.admin`) are not supported.

## Performance

- The generator writes plain Dart code for each DTO. No reflection, no rule strings to parse.
- A check is a few `if` statements per field. Regexes are compiled once.
- Dox finds the DTO for a route once, then keeps it.
- It works with `dox build` (AOT).


---

# Validation rules

Source: https://dartondox.dev/latest/3.xthe-basic/validation-rules/

# Validation rules

This page lists every annotation you can put on a `@Dto` field. See [Validation](validation.md) for how DTOs work.

How to read the tables:

- **Code** is the error code. Use it in `@Dto(messages: ...)` and in a `MessageResolver`.
- **Message** is the default English text. `{field}` is the last key of the path.
- Every annotation also takes `message:`. It wins over every other message.
- All limits include the limit itself, unless the table says "exclusive".
- On a `List<T>` field, a value rule checks each item. Only the list rules check the list itself.

## Type errors

These have no annotation. They come from the field type.

| Code | When | Message |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `required` | a required field is missing, `null`, or `""` | `The {field} is required` |
| `string` | not a string | `The {field} must be a string` |
| `integer` | not a whole number | `The {field} must be an integer` |
| `numeric` | not a number (`double`, `num`) | `The {field} must be a number` |
| `boolean` | not a bool | `The {field} must be a boolean` |
| `date` | not an ISO 8601 date | `The {field} must be a date` |
| `in` | not a name of the enum | `The selected {field} is invalid. Valid options are {values}` |
| `array` | not a list | `The {field} must be an array` |
| `object` | not an object (nested DTO, `Map`) | `The {field} must be an object` |
| `file` | not a file | `The {field} must be a file` |
| `unrecognized_keys` | unknown key, with `@Dto(strict: true)` | `The {field} field is not allowed` |

## Text

For `String` fields (and `List<String>` items).

| Annotation | Code | Message | JSON Schema |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `@Length(min: 3, max: 50)` | `length_between` | `The {field} must be between {min} and {max} characters` | `minLength`, `maxLength` |
| `@Length(min: 6, max: 6)` | `length` | `The {field} must be exactly {length} characters` | `minLength`, `maxLength` |
| `@MinLength(3)` | `min_length` | `The {field} must be at least {min} characters` | `minLength` |
| `@MaxLength(50)` | `max_length` | `The {field} may not be greater than {max} characters` | `maxLength` |
| `@Email()` | `email` | `The {field} is not a valid email` | `format: email` |
| `@Url()` | `url` | `The {field} must be a url` | `format: uri` |
| `@Uuid()` | `uuid` | `The {field} is invalid uuid` | `format: uuid` |
| `@Ip()` | `ip` | `The {field} must be an ip address` | `anyOf` `ipv4` / `ipv6` |
| `@Regex(r'[a-z]+')` | `regex` | `The {field} format is invalid` | `pattern` |
| `@In(['a', 'b'])` | `in` | `The selected {field} is invalid. Valid options are {values}` | `enum` |
| `@NotIn(['root'])` | `not_in` | `The {field} field cannot be {value}` | `not: {enum}` |
| `@StartsWith('dox')` | `start_with` | `The {field} must start with {prefix}` | `pattern` |
| `@EndsWith('.dev')` | `end_with` | `The {field} must end with {suffix}` | `pattern` |
| `@Alpha()` | `alpha` | `The {field} must be an alphabetic` | `pattern` |
| `@AlphaNumeric()` | `alpha_numeric` | `The {field} must be only alphabetic and number` | `pattern` |
| `@AlphaDash()` | `alpha_dash` | `The {field} must be only alphabetic and dash` | `pattern` |

Details:

- `@Length` has `min:` and `max:`. Both are optional, but you must give one.
  With only `min:` it acts like `@MinLength`, with only `max:` like `@MaxLength`.
- Length counts characters (Unicode code points). `é` counts as 1.
- `@Url()` needs `http` or `https` and a host.
- `@Uuid()` takes any version. Upper or lower case.
- `@Regex(pattern, {message})` must match the **whole** value. You do not need `^` and `$`.
  The regex is checked when the generator runs. A bad regex stops the build.
- `@Alpha()`, `@AlphaNumeric()` and `@AlphaDash()` use ASCII letters `a-z`, `A-Z`. `@AlphaDash()` also allows `-` and `_`.
- `@In` and `@NotIn` compare exactly (case matters).

## Change text

These change the value before the rules run. They always run in this order, wherever you put them:
`@Trim`, then `@Lowercase` or `@Uppercase`, then the "empty string is missing" check.

| Annotation | Does |
| --- | --- |
| `@Trim()` | removes spaces at the start and the end |
| `@Lowercase()` | makes the text lower case |
| `@Uppercase()` | makes the text upper case |
| `@AllowEmpty()` | keeps `""` as a value. Without it, `""` counts as missing. |

They have no error and no JSON Schema output. `@Lowercase()` and `@Uppercase()` together stop the build.

## Numbers

For `int`, `double` and `num` fields (and list items).

| Annotation | Code | Message | JSON Schema |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `@Min(18)` | `min` | `The {field} must be greater than or equal {min}` | `minimum` |
| `@Max(100)` | `max` | `The {field} must be less than or equal {max}` | `maximum` |
| `@Range(1, 10)` | `between` | `The {field} must be between {min} and {max}` | `minimum`, `maximum` |
| `@Positive()` | `greater_than` | `The {field} must be greater than 0` | `exclusiveMinimum: 0` |
| `@GreaterThan(0.5)` | `greater_than` | `The {field} must be greater than {min}` (exclusive) | `exclusiveMinimum` |
| `@LessThan(100)` | `less_than` | `The {field} must be less than {max}` (exclusive) | `exclusiveMaximum` |
| `@In([1, 2, 3])` | `in` | `The selected {field} is invalid. Valid options are {values}` | `enum` |
| `@NotIn([0])` | `not_in` | `The {field} field cannot be {value}` | `not: {enum}` |

The values are `num`. `@Min(1.5)` on an `int` field stops the build.

## Lists

For `List<T>` fields. These check the list, not the items.

| Annotation | Code | Message | JSON Schema |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `@MinItems(1)` | `min_items` | `The {field} must have at least {min} items` | `minItems` |
| `@MaxItems(5)` | `max_items` | `The {field} may not have more than {max} items` | `maxItems` |
| `@UniqueItems()` | `unique_items` | `The {field} must not have duplicate items` | `uniqueItems: true` |

`@UniqueItems()` works for `String`, numbers, `bool`, enums and `DateTime`. On a list of DTOs it stops the build.

## Dates

For `DateTime` fields.

| Annotation | Code | Message | JSON Schema |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `@After('2000-01-01')` | `after` | `The {field} must be a date after {date}` | `format: date-time` |
| `@Before('now')` | `before` | `The {field} must be a date before {date}` | `format: date-time` |

- The value is an ISO 8601 date, or `'now'` (the time of the request).
- Both are exclusive: `@After('2000-01-01')` does not accept `2000-01-01T00:00:00Z`.
- To compare two fields (end after start), use [`validate()`](validation.md#checks-across-fields-validate).

## Files

For `RequestFile` and `List<RequestFile>` fields.

| Annotation | Code | Message | JSON Schema |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `@MaxSize('2MB')` | `max_size` | `The {field} may not be larger than {max}` | `maxLength` (bytes) |
| `@Mimes(['pdf', 'png'])` | `mimes` | `The {field} must be a file of type: {types}` | `contentMediaType` |
| `@Image()` | `image` | `The {field} must be an image` | `contentMediaType: image/*` |

- `@MaxSize` units: `B`, `KB`, `MB`, `GB`. `1KB` = 1024 bytes. A bad size text stops the build.
- `@Mimes` takes file extensions. Dox finds the real type from the first bytes of the file.
  For types without a byte signature (like `txt` or `csv`), it uses the file name extension.
- `@Image()` is `@Mimes(['jpg', 'jpeg', 'png', 'gif', 'webp', 'bmp'])`. No `svg`.
- The JSON Schema of a file is `{"type": "string", "format": "binary"}`, plus the keys above.

## Database

From `dox_orm`. Async: they run after all other checks passed.

| Annotation | Code | Message |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `@Unique(table, {column, ignoreParam, ignoreColumn, connection})` | `unique` | `The {field} has already been taken` |
| `@Exists(table, {column, connection})` | `exists` | `The selected {field} is invalid` |

- `@Unique` column default: the input key. `@Exists` column default: `id`.
- `ignoreParam: 'id'` skips the row where `ignoreColumn` (default `id`) equals the path param `{id}`.
- They add nothing to the JSON Schema.

See [Database rules](validation.md#database-rules-unique-and-exists).

## Keys and DTO options

| Annotation | Does |
| --- | --- |
| `@Name('emailAddress')` | the input key for this field. Default: the field name in snake_case. |
| `@Dto()` | marks the class. |
| `@Dto(source: Source.query)` | where to read: `Source.auto` (default), `Source.query`, `Source.body`. |
| `@Dto(keyCase: KeyCase.field)` | keys: `KeyCase.snake` (default) or `KeyCase.field` (the Dart name as is). |
| `@Dto(strict: true)` | unknown keys are errors. Default `false`: they are dropped. |
| `@Dto(messages: {...})` | messages by `code` or `key.code`. |

A `///` doc comment on a field becomes its `description` in the JSON Schema.

## What the generator checks

The build stops with a clear error when:

- a field is not `final`, or is not a parameter of the unnamed constructor,
- a field type is not supported (see [Types](validation.md#types)),
- a rule does not fit the field type (like `@Email()` on an `int`),
- a `Maybe<T>` field has no `const Maybe.missing()` default,
- two `@Dto` classes in the app have the same name,
- the class is generic, or extends another class (other than `Object`).


---

# Cache

Source: https://dartondox.dev/latest/3.xdigging-deeper/cache/

# Cache

`Cache()` keeps data that is slow to make, so the next request can read it fast.
It runs on [`dox_cache`](../packages/cache.md), which is built into `dox_core`.

## Drivers

| Driver | Where the data is | Shared between isolates | Locks |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `file` | files in a folder (default `storage/cache`) | yes, on the same machine | no |
| `memory` | a map inside the isolate | no | yes |
| `redis` | a Redis server | yes, also between machines | yes |
| `null` | nowhere. It stores nothing | - | no |

!!! warning "Many isolates"
    Dox runs one isolate per CPU core. Each isolate has its own `memory` store.
    So a value you put in one isolate is missing in the others.
    Use `redis` when all isolates and servers must see the same data.

## Config

Without a config, Dox has a `file` store (the default) and a `memory` store.
To change the stores, make `lib/config/cache.dart`:

```dart title="lib/config/cache.dart"
import 'package:dox_core/dox_core.dart';
import 'package:my_app/config/env.dart';

CacheConfig cache = CacheConfig(
  defaultStore: env.cacheStore,
  stores: <String, Map<String, dynamic>>{
    'file': <String, dynamic>{'driver': 'file', 'path': 'storage/cache'},
    'memory': <String, dynamic>{'driver': 'memory', 'max_size': 10000},
    'redis': <String, dynamic>{
      'driver': 'redis',
      'host': env.redisHost,
      'port': env.redisPort,
      'prefix': 'app_cache:',
    },
  },
);
```

Redis needs two keys that a new project does not have yet. Add them to
`lib/config/env.dart` and run `dart run build_runner build`:

```dart title="lib/config/env.dart"
  String get redisHost => '127.0.0.1';

  int get redisPort => 6379;
```

Then pass it to `AppConfig(cache: cache)` in `lib/config/app.dart`.
Each store is made once per isolate, the first time you use it.

### Store options

| Driver | Options |
| --- | --- |
| `file` | `path` (default `storage/cache`), `prefix` |
| `memory` | `max_size`: the most items. When it is full, the item that was used least recently is removed. No limit by default. Also `prefix`. |
| `redis` | `host` (default `127.0.0.1`), `port` (default `6379`), `username`, `password`, `db` (default `0`), `tls` (`true`/`false`), `pool_size`, `prefix` |

The default `prefix` is `dox_cache:`.

### Redis `pool_size`

`pool_size` is the most Redis connections that one store opens in one isolate. The default is 10.

You rarely need to change it. A store sends all commands on one connection. It opens more connections only while a blocking command (like `BLPOP`) waits, and the cache does not send blocking commands.
So each isolate uses about one connection: 4 isolates use about 4 connections.

## Values are JSON

A value must be a JSON type: `Map`, `List`, `String`, `num`, `bool` or `null`.
A `Map` comes back as `Map<String, dynamic>`. A `List` comes back as `List<dynamic>`.

## Usage

```dart
// no duration: the value stays forever
await Cache().put('foo', 'bar');
await Cache().put('foo', 'bar', duration: Duration(minutes: 10));

await Cache().get('foo');             // 'bar', or null when missing
await Cache().get('foo', 'default');  // 'default' when missing
await Cache().has('foo');             // true
await Cache().forget('foo');          // remove one key
await Cache().forever('settings', <String, dynamic>{'theme': 'dark'});
await Cache().flush();                // remove all items of the store
```

### `remember`

`remember` reads the value from the cache. When it is missing, the function runs and its result is stored.

```dart
List<dynamic> posts = await Cache().remember(
  'posts',
  Duration(minutes: 5),
  () => Post().all(),
);
```

`rememberForever(key, fn)` does the same with no expiry.

### `getRaw`

`get` decodes the stored JSON text into Dart values. If you then send the value as a JSON response, Dox must encode it again. That is double work.

`getRaw` gives the stored JSON text as it is. You can send it with no decode and no encode:

```dart
String? json = await Cache().getRaw('posts');
if (json != null) {
  return response(json).contentType(ContentType.json);
}
```

A missing key gives `null`. A stored `String` comes back as JSON, with its quotes: `"bar"`.

### Another store

`store(name)` uses a store from the config instead of the default store:

```dart
await Cache().store('redis').put('foo', 'bar');
await Cache().store('memory').get('foo');
```

### Tags

Put items under a tag. Then you can remove only the items of that tag:

```dart
await Cache().tag('users').put('u1', 'Ann');
await Cache().tag('users').flush(); // removes only the items of this tag
```

`tags(['a', 'b'])` uses many tags.

### Locks

A lock makes sure only one request (or one server) runs some code at a time.
The `memory` and `redis` stores support locks. Use `redis` when many isolates must share the lock.

```dart
CacheLock lock = Cache().store('redis').lock('report', Duration(seconds: 30));
if (await lock.get()) {
  try {
    await buildReport();
  } finally {
    await lock.release();
  }
}
```

- `get()` tries once. It is `true` when you got the lock.
- `block(Duration(seconds: 5))` tries again and again until the time is over.
- The lock is freed after its `ttl`, even if you never call `release()`.

### More methods

| Method | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `add(key, value, duration:)` | store only when the key is missing. `true` when it was stored |
| `pull(key)` | get the value and remove it |
| `increment(key, [by])` / `decrement(key, [by])` | change an integer. A missing key starts at 0 |
| `repository` | the `dox_cache` `CacheStore`, for everything else |

See [dox_cache](../packages/cache.md) for custom drivers.

## Tests

`Dox().cache` is the `CacheManager` that `Cache()` uses. Replace it in a test, so the test needs no files and no Redis:

```dart
Dox().cache = CacheManager(CacheConfig(
  defaultStore: 'memory',
  stores: <String, Map<String, dynamic>>{
    'memory': <String, dynamic>{'driver': 'memory'},
  },
));
```

See [Testing](testing.md).


---

# File Storage

Source: https://dartondox.dev/latest/3.xdigging-deeper/file-storage/

# File Storage

`Storage()` saves and reads files on a disk: the local folder, AWS S3 (and R2, MinIO, Spaces), or memory.
It runs on [`dox_storage`](../packages/storage.md), which is built into `dox_core`.

```dart
Route.post('/avatar', (DoxRequest req) async {
  RequestFile file = req.input('avatar');
  String path = await Storage().putRequestFile('avatars', file);
  return <String, String>{'path': path}; // /avatars/<uuid>.png
});
```

## Config

Without a config, Dox has one disk: `local`, in the `storage` folder.
To add disks, make `lib/config/storage.dart`:

```dart title="lib/config/storage.dart"
import 'package:dox_core/dox_core.dart';
import 'package:my_app/config/env.dart';

StorageConfig storage = StorageConfig(
  defaultDisk: env.storageDisk,
  disks: <String, Map<String, dynamic>>{
    'local': <String, dynamic>{
      'driver': 'local',
      'root': 'storage',
      'url': 'https://app.test/files', // for url() and signedUrl()
    },
    's3': <String, dynamic>{
      'driver': 's3',
      'bucket': env.awsBucket,
      'region': env.awsDefaultRegion,
      'key': env.awsAccessKeyId,
      'secret': env.awsSecretAccessKey,
      'endpoint': env.awsEndpoint, // R2, MinIO, Spaces
    },
    'memory': <String, dynamic>{'driver': 'memory'},
  },
);
```

The `s3` disk reads five keys that a new project does not have yet. Add them to
`lib/config/env.dart` and run `dart run build_runner build`. They are nullable,
so the app still starts without them when you do not use S3:

```dart title="lib/config/env.dart"
  String? get awsBucket;

  String get awsDefaultRegion => 'us-east-1';

  String? get awsAccessKeyId;

  String? get awsSecretAccessKey;

  /// R2, MinIO or Spaces. Null for AWS.
  String? get awsEndpoint;
```

Then pass it to `AppConfig(storage: storage)` in `lib/config/app.dart`.

| Driver | Options |
| --- | --- |
| `local` | `root` (default `storage`), `url`, `app_key` (default: your APP_KEY), `visibility` |
| `s3` | `bucket`, `region`, `key`, `secret`, `token`, `endpoint`, `path_style` (MinIO), `url` (CDN), `visibility`, `acl`, `batch_delete` |
| `memory` | none. For tests |

The `s3` disk needs `bucket`, `key` and `secret`. When one is missing or empty, the first use of the disk throws an `ArgumentError` that names the setting, like `Storage disk "s3" needs the "bucket" setting. It is missing or empty.`

## Functions

```dart
// save with a new uuid file name, returns '/images/<uuid>.png'
String path = await Storage().put('images', bytes, extension: 'png');
String path2 = await Storage().putRequestFile('images', file);

Uint8List? bytes = await Storage().get(path);  // null when missing
bool found = await Storage().exists(path);
await Storage().delete(path);

String url = await Storage().url(path);         // needs the disk `url` option
String signed = await Storage().signedUrl(path, expiresIn: Duration(minutes: 10));

// another disk
await Storage().disk('s3').put('reports', bytes, extension: 'pdf');
```

`putRequestFile` on the local disk moves the upload temp file. It does not read it into memory.

### `stream` and `download`

```dart
Route.get('/photo', (DoxRequest req) {
  return Storage().stream(req.input('path'));    // shown in the browser
});

Route.get('/report', (DoxRequest req) {
  return Storage().disk('s3').download('reports/2024.pdf'); // saved as a file
});
```

Both read the file as a stream, from any disk, with `Content-Length`.
A big file is never loaded into memory. A missing file answers `404`.

### Full disk API

`Storage().use('s3')` returns the `dox_storage` `Disk`: `copy`, `move`, `listAll`, `getMetaData`,
`putStream`, `setVisibility` and more. See [dox_storage](../packages/storage.md).

## Serve local signed URLs

```dart
// lib/routes/web.dart
Route.files('files');                    // GET /files/{key*}, signed URLs only
Route.files('public', signed: false);    // any file of the disk
Route.files('docs', disk: 'memory');     // another disk than the default
```

```dart
String url = await Storage().signedUrl('invoices/1.pdf'); // https://app.test/files/invoices/1.pdf?expires=...&signature=...
```

A missing, wrong or expired signature answers `403`.
Set the disk `url` option to the full URL of the route (`https://app.test/files`).

## Tests

`Dox().storage` is the `DriveManager` that `Storage()` uses. `fake(name)` swaps a disk with an empty memory disk:

```dart
Disk fake = Dox().storage.fake('s3');
await uploadReport();
expect(await fake.exists('reports/2024.pdf'), isTrue);
Dox().storage.restore('s3');
```

`Disk` keys have no `/` at the start. See [Testing](testing.md).

## Your own driver

Implement `DriverContract` from `package:dox_storage/dox_storage.dart`. Register it in a [service](services.md), so every isolate has it:

```dart
Dox().storage.register('dropbox', DropboxDriver());
await Storage().disk('dropbox').put('notes', bytes, extension: 'txt');
```


---

# Environment Variables

Source: https://dartondox.dev/latest/3.xdigging-deeper/env/

# Environment Variables

Declare your env keys once, in a typed class. Then `env.appPort` is an `int`, your IDE suggests every key, and a missing key stops the app at startup.

## The typed env class

A new project already has `lib/config/env.dart`, with the keys the config files read. The list is in the [Env reference](../reference/env.md#read-by-a-new-project).

This example class shows the kinds of getters you can write:

```dart
import 'package:dox_core/dox_core.dart';

part 'env.g.dart';

enum LogLevel { debug, info, error }

@DoxEnv()
abstract class AppEnv {
  static AppEnv load([EnvReader? reader]) {
    return _$AppEnv.load(reader);
  }

  String get appName;                       // APP_NAME, required
  String get appKey;                        // APP_KEY, required
  int get dbPort => 5432;                   // DB_PORT, default 5432
  bool get appDebug => false;               // APP_DEBUG, default false
  LogLevel get logLevel => LogLevel.info;   // LOG_LEVEL=debug
  Duration get cacheTtl => const Duration(minutes: 5); // CACHE_TTL=5m
  List<String> get corsOrigins => <String>[];          // CORS_ORIGINS=a.com,b.com

  @EnvKey('AWS_BUCKET')
  String? get s3Bucket;                     // optional, null when not set
}

/// The env of the app. Read and checked once, on first use.
final AppEnv env = AppEnv.load();
```

Run `dart run build_runner build` (or `dox build_runner:build`) after each change to the class. It writes `env.g.dart`.

Use it anywhere:

```dart
import 'package:my_app/config/env.dart';

DatabaseConfig databaseConfig = DatabaseConfig(
  connection: 'postgres',
  connections: <String, ConnectionConfig>{
    'postgres': ConnectionConfig(port: env.dbPort /* int */, ...),
  },
);
```

### The rules

- **Key**: the getter name in UPPER_SNAKE case. `appName` reads `APP_NAME`, `s3Bucket` reads `S3_BUCKET`. Use `@EnvKey('X')` for another name.
- **Default**: the getter body. It can be any expression, like `Platform.numberOfProcessors`. It runs only when the key is missing. A default can not read another env getter.
- **Optional**: a nullable getter with no body (`String? get s3Bucket;`). It is `null` when the key is missing.
- **Required**: any other getter with no body. A missing key stops the app.
- **Empty**: an empty value (or the text `null`) counts as missing.

### Types

| Type | Value in `.env` |
|------|-----------------|
| `String` | any text |
| `int`, `double`, `num` | `3000`, `0.5` |
| `bool` | `true`/`false`, `1`/`0`, `yes`/`no`, `on`/`off` (any case) |
| `Uri` | `https://dox.dev` |
| `Duration` | a number and a unit: `500ms`, `30s`, `5m`, `2h`, `1d`. A plain number is seconds: `300` is 5 minutes. |
| an enum | the name of a value, any case: `debug` |
| `List<String>` | comma separated: `a, b, c`. Empty items are dropped. |

Any other type is a build error.

### Fail fast

`AppEnv.load()` reads every key one time. Then it checks them all, and throws one `EnvException` that lists every missing or bad key:

```
EnvException: the env is not valid
  - APP_KEY is missing
  - DB_PORT must be an int, not "abc"
```

The `env` variable is made on first use. The config files use it, so this happens when the app starts. After that, `env.dbPort` is a plain field read. There is no lookup and no parsing on each request.

## Where values come from

Dox reads values from two places:

1. Real environment variables (set in the shell, Docker or systemd).
2. The `.env` file in the folder where you start the app.

!!! info "The environment wins"
    A real environment variable wins over the `.env` file.
    So you can keep `.env` for development and use real variables in production.
    The `.env` file is optional.

### The `.env` file

```ini title=".env"
APP_NAME=dox
APP_KEY=change-me
DB_PORT=5432
```

- One `KEY=value` per line.
- Quotes around a value are removed. So `APP_NAME="My app"` gives `My app`. Use `"`, `'` or `` ` ``.
- A `=` inside the value is kept: `TOKEN=a=b` gives `a=b`.
- A line that starts with `#` is a comment.
- A `#` after a space starts a comment: `APP_PORT=3000 # dev` gives `3000`.
- A `#` with no space before it is kept: `DB_PASSWORD=abc#123` gives `abc#123`.
- A `#` inside quotes is kept: `DB_PASSWORD="abc # 123"` gives `abc # 123`.

## Commands

```bash
dox env:generate   # make lib/config/env.dart from .env.example
dox env:check      # load the env and print every missing or bad key
```

`dox env:generate` reads `.env.example`:

- digits become an `int` with that default: `APP_PORT=3000` gives `int get appPort => 3000;`
- `true`/`false` become a `bool` with that default
- an empty value becomes an optional `String?`
- any other value becomes a required `String`. The example value is never a default, so a secret in the example can not leak into the code.
- `#` comment lines above a key become its doc comment

It does not overwrite an existing `lib/config/env.dart`. Run `dox build_runner:build` after it.

`dox env:check` loads `AppEnv` from `lib/config/env.dart`, with the real environment and `.env`. It exits with code 1 when a key is missing or bad. Use it in CI or before a deploy.

## Tests

Pass your own values to `load()`. Nothing is read from the shell or `.env`:

```dart
AppEnv env = AppEnv.load(
  EnvReader(
    environment: <String, String>{'APP_KEY': 'test'},
    dotEnv: <String, String>{'DB_PORT': '5433'},
  ),
);
```

## Env.get: the low-level way

`Env.get()` reads one key by name. Use it for a key you only know at run time. For normal config, use the typed class.

```dart
Env.get<String>('APP_KEY');             // '' when missing
Env.get('APP_KEY', 'default_value');
Env.get<int>('APP_PORT', 3000);
Env.get<bool>('SOCKETIO_ENABLED', false); // true, 1, yes, on
Env.get<String?>('AWS_BUCKET');          // null when it is not set
```

A missing or empty key gives the default. With no default:

- `String` gives an empty string `''`. It is never the text `"null"`.
- `String?` and `dynamic` give `null`. With no type, like `Env.get('KEY')`, the type is `dynamic`, so you get `null`.
- `int`, `num`, `double` and `bool` throw an `ArgumentError` with the key name. A value that is not a number throws too.

`Env.get()` looks up and converts the value on every call. Do not call it on a hot path.

!!! warning "APP_KEY"
    When `APP_KEY` is empty and `APP_ENV=production`, `Dox().startServer()` stops with an error.
    In other environments it logs a warning. Make a key with `dox key:generate`.


---

# Isolate

Source: https://dartondox.dev/latest/3.xdigging-deeper/isolate/

# Isolate

This page explains how Dox runs your app on many isolates (threads), and what that means for your code.

## How it works

Dox starts many isolates. Each one runs its own HTTP server on the same port. The operating system spreads the connections between them.

- Native server on Linux: each isolate has its own socket (`SO_REUSEPORT`).
- Native server on macOS: the isolates share one socket.
- Native server on Windows: only one isolate serves HTTP.
- `dart:io` server: `HttpServer.bind(..., shared: true)` on every system.

With the native server, each isolate has its own Rust acceptor on the port:

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    OS["Port 3000<br>the OS spreads the connections"] --> A1["Rust acceptor"]
    OS --> A2["Rust acceptor"]
    OS --> A3["Rust acceptor"]
    A1 --> I1["Isolate 1, main<br>own DB pool, own memory cache"]
    A2 --> I2["Isolate 2<br>own DB pool, own memory cache"]
    A3 --> I3["Isolate N<br>own DB pool, own memory cache"]
    I2 -. "crash: started again after 1 second" .-> I2
    I1 -. "crash: the process exits" .-> S["Supervisor restarts the process<br>Docker, systemd"]
```

See [Native server](native-server.md) for the two servers.

## How many isolates

By default Dox starts one isolate per CPU core (`Platform.numberOfProcessors`). So one process uses the whole machine.

To change it, set `totalIsolate` in `lib/config/app.dart`. A new app reads it from `APP_TOTAL_ISOLATE`:

```dart title="lib/config/app.dart"
AppConfig appConfig = AppConfig(
  // ...
  totalIsolate: env.appTotalIsolate ?? Platform.numberOfProcessors,
);
```

You can also set it in code, before `startServer()`. This wins over the config:

```dart title="bin/server.dart"
Dox().initialize(appConfig);
Dox().totalIsolate(2);
await Dox().startServer();
```

Use fewer isolates when:

- the machine also runs the database or other heavy work, or
- you use WebSocket rooms without the Redis adapter. A room only reaches clients on the same isolate. Use `1`, or see [WebSocket](websocket.md).

## Each isolate has its own memory

Isolates do not share memory. This has some effects on your code:

- A static value or a singleton exists once **per isolate**. When you change it in one isolate, the others do not see it.
- The `memory` cache store is per isolate. Use the `redis` store to share cache data. See [Cache](cache.md).
- To share data between isolates or servers, use a database, Redis or files.

`Dox().isolateId` tells you which isolate runs the code. The first isolate is `1`.

## What each isolate does at start

Dox copies the `AppConfig`, the services and the routes you added before `startServer()` to each new isolate. Then every isolate:

1. runs `setup()` of each service (for example, it opens its own database pool),
2. registers the routes of your routers,
3. reads the parameter types of each controller once,
4. starts its HTTP server.

This happens once at start, not on each request.

Because the config and services are copied, they must not hold open sockets or database pools. Open these in `setup()`. See [Services](services.md).

## When an isolate crashes

- An error in a request is caught. Dox sends a `500` and keeps going.
- An async error outside a request (for example a future that nobody awaits) is caught and passed to `errorHandler`. The isolate keeps running.
- If a worker isolate still dies, Dox prints `[dox] isolate N exited, restarting` to stderr. It starts a new isolate after 1 second.
- If the first (main) isolate dies, the process exits with a non-zero code. Let a supervisor start it again, like Docker `restart:` or systemd `Restart=always`. See [Deployment](deployment.md#keep-it-running).


---

# Services

Source: https://dartondox.dev/latest/3.xdigging-deeper/services/

# Services

A service is a class with a `setup()` method. Dox runs it at start, in every isolate. Use it to set up things like the database, auth or WebSocket.

## Why services

Dox runs your app on many isolates (see [Isolate](isolate.md)). Each isolate has its own memory.

So code that you run once in `bin/server.dart` only sets up the first isolate. The other isolates do not see it. For example, they have no database connection.

A service fixes this. Dox sends the list of services to each isolate, and each isolate runs `setup()` itself.

## Create a service

Implement `DoxService` and put your code in `setup()`. `setup()` can be `async`. Dox waits for it.

```dart title="lib/services/orm_service.dart"
import 'package:dox_core/dox_core.dart';
import 'package:dox_orm/dox_orm.dart';
import 'package:my_app/config/database.dart';

class ORMService implements DoxService {
  @override
  Future<void> setup() async {
    SqlQueryBuilder.initializeWithDatabaseConfig(databaseConfig);
  }
}
```

## Register it

Add an instance of the service to the list in `lib/config/services.dart`:

```dart title="lib/config/services.dart"
import 'package:dox_core/dox_core.dart';
import 'package:my_app/services/auth_service.dart';
import 'package:my_app/services/orm_service.dart';

List<DoxService> services = <DoxService>[
  ORMService(),
  AuthService(),
];
```

This list goes to `AppConfig(services: services)` in `lib/config/app.dart`.

You can also add a service in code, before `startServer()`:

```dart title="bin/server.dart"
Dox().initialize(appConfig);
Dox().addService(MyService());
await Dox().startServer();
```

## Example: auth

```dart title="lib/services/auth_service.dart"
import 'package:dox_auth/dox_auth.dart';
import 'package:dox_core/dox_core.dart';
import 'package:my_app/app/models/user/user.model.dart';

class AuthService implements DoxService {
  @override
  void setup() {
    Auth.initialize(AuthConfig(
      defaultGuard: 'web',
      guards: <String, AuthGuard>{
        'web': AuthGuard(
          driver: JwtAuthDriver(secret: SecretKey(env.appKey)),
          provider: AuthProvider(model: () => User()),
        ),
      },
    ));
  }
}
```

See [Authentication](../security/authentication.md).

## When `setup()` runs

In each isolate, Dox does these steps in this order:

1. It runs `setup()` of each service, one after the other, in list order.
2. It registers the routes of your routers.
3. It starts the HTTP server.

So routes can use what a service set up. For example, `Route.websocket()` needs the WebSocket service to run first.

`dox openapi:generate` also runs `setup()` of every service, because it needs the routes.

## Clean up on shutdown

On `SIGTERM` or `SIGINT` Dox stops the server gracefully (see [Deployment](deployment.md#graceful-shutdown)).
After the open requests are done, it runs `shutdown()` of each service that also implements `DoxShutdown`.
It runs in every isolate. Use it to close connections or flush data.

```dart title="lib/services/redis_service.dart"
class RedisService implements DoxService, DoxShutdown {
  late RedisConnection redis;

  @override
  Future<void> setup() async {
    redis = await RedisConnection.open();
  }

  @override
  Future<void> shutdown() async {
    await redis.close();
  }
}
```

An error in `shutdown()` goes to `errorHandler`. The other services still run.

## Rules for a service

- **Open connections in `setup()`, not in the constructor.** Dox copies the service object to each isolate. An open socket or database pool can not be copied, so the isolate fails to start.
- **Keep `setup()` short.** It runs once per isolate. Data you load in it is kept once per isolate, so 8 isolates keep 8 copies.
- **Do not depend on another isolate.** Each isolate has its own static values and singletons. To share data between isolates, use a database, Redis or the [cache](cache.md) with the `redis` driver.


---

# WebSocket

Source: https://dartondox.dev/latest/3.xdigging-deeper/websocket/

# WebSocket

`dox_websocket` adds WebSocket routes to a Dox app. Use it for live chat, notifications and other real-time updates.

!!! tip "Want Socket.IO clients?"
    Use [Socket.IO](../packages/socketio.md#in-a-dox-app-same-port-as-http). Turn it on with `AppConfig(socketIo: SocketIoConfig(enabled: true))`.
    It runs on the same port, works with the official Socket.IO clients, and has acks and namespaces.
    `dox_websocket` keeps working next to it.

!!! info "WebSocket uses the `dart:io` server"
    The native server can not upgrade a connection to WebSocket yet.
    So when your app has a WebSocket route, Dox uses the `dart:io` server by itself.
    See [Native server](native-server.md#use-dartio-instead).

## Setup

### 1. Add the package

```bash
dart pub add dox_websocket:^3.0.0-alpha.4
```

### 2. Create a WebSocket service

The service creates the WebSocket server in every isolate. See [Services](services.md).

#### Many isolates (Redis)

Pick this for production. It works with more than one isolate and more than one server.

```dart title="lib/services/websocket_service.dart"
import 'package:dox_core/dox_core.dart';
import 'package:dox_websocket/dox_websocket.dart';
import 'package:ioredis/ioredis.dart';

class WebsocketService implements DoxService {
  @override
  void setup() {
    Redis sub = Redis(RedisOptions(host: env.redisHost));
    Redis pub = sub.duplicate();

    WebsocketServer io = WebsocketServer(Dox());
    io.adapter(WebsocketRedisAdapter(subscriber: sub, publisher: pub));
  }
}
```

Add [`ioredis`](https://pub.dev/packages/ioredis) `^2.0.0-alpha.2` to your `pubspec.yaml`.

#### One isolate

Pick this for a small app or for local work, when you do not want Redis.

```dart title="lib/services/websocket_service.dart"
import 'package:dox_core/dox_core.dart';
import 'package:dox_websocket/dox_websocket.dart';

class WebsocketService implements DoxService {
  @override
  void setup() {
    WebsocketServer(Dox());
  }
}
```

Set `totalIsolate: 1` in `lib/config/app.dart` (or `APP_TOTAL_ISOLATE=1`).

!!! warning "Many isolates need Redis"
    Dox runs one isolate per CPU core by default. Each isolate has its own memory.
    Without an adapter, a message only reaches clients on the same isolate.
    The Redis adapter sends each message to all isolates and all servers.

### 3. Register the service

```dart title="lib/config/services.dart"
List<DoxService> services = <DoxService>[
  // ... other services
  WebsocketService(),
];
```

### 4. Create a controller

```bash
dox create:controller Chat -ws
```

This makes `lib/app/ws/controllers/chat.controller.dart`. Each method gets the `WebsocketEmitter` and the message from the client:

```dart title="lib/app/ws/controllers/chat.controller.dart"
import 'package:dox_websocket/dox_websocket.dart';

class ChatController {
  void intro(WebsocketEmitter emitter, dynamic message) {
    // send to the 'chat' room, but not to the sender
    emitter.room('chat').emitExceptSender('intro', message);
  }

  void noti(WebsocketEmitter emitter, dynamic message) {
    // send to the 'chat' room, also to the sender
    emitter.room('chat').emit('noti', message);
  }
}
```

A WebSocket connection stays open. So a controller method does not need to return a value.

### 5. Add the route

Use `Route.websocket(path, callback)`. In the callback, map each event name to a controller method:

```dart title="lib/routes/web.dart"
ChatController chat = ChatController();

Route.websocket('ws', (WebsocketEvent event) {
  // the client sends event `intro`: run chat.intro
  event.on('intro', chat.intro);
  event.on('noti', chat.noti);
});
```

The URL is `ws://127.0.0.1:{port}/ws`. You can add more WebSocket routes on other paths.
`Route.websocket` also takes `middleware:`, like other routes.

## Messages

Client and server send JSON text.

The client sends `event` and `message`:

```json
{"event": "intro", "message": "Mingalaba!"}
```

The server sends `event`, `message`, `sender` (the socket id of the sender) and `room`:

```json
{"event": "intro", "message": "Mingalaba!", "sender": "ws:4f1c...", "room": "chat"}
```

Two events are built in:

| Event | Direction | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `connected` | server to client | sent once after connect. `message` is `{"id": "<socket id>"}` |
| `joinRoom` | client to server | joins the room. `message` is the room name |

Each client is also in a room for its route, so `emitter.emit()` with no room reaches all clients of the same route.

## Client examples

### Dart

Use `WebSocket` from `dart:io`.

```dart
import 'dart:convert';
import 'dart:io';

void main() async {
  WebSocket socket = await WebSocket.connect('ws://localhost:3000/ws');

  socket.listen((dynamic data) {
    Map<String, dynamic> payload = jsonDecode(data as String);
    print('${payload['event']}: ${payload['message']}');
  });

  // join the chat room
  socket.add(jsonEncode(<String, dynamic>{
    'event': 'joinRoom',
    'message': 'chat',
  }));

  // send the intro event
  socket.add(jsonEncode(<String, dynamic>{
    'event': 'intro',
    'message': 'Mingalaba!',
  }));
}
```

### JavaScript

Use the browser `WebSocket`, or the client [`@dartondox/websocket`](https://github.com/dartondox/dox-web-socket-client/):

```js
import DoxWebsocket from '@dartondox/websocket';

const socket = DoxWebsocket('ws://127.0.0.1:3000/ws', {
  maxRetries: 18,
  retryAfter: 2000,
});

socket.onConnected(() => console.log(socket.id));
socket.onError(() => console.log('socket error'));
socket.onClose(() => console.log('socket closed'));

// listen for the intro event from the server
socket.on('intro', (msg) => console.log(msg));

// send the intro event
socket.emit('intro', 'Mingalaba!');
```

## WebsocketEmitter

### `room`

Pick the room to send to. Use the same name the client sent with `joinRoom`.

```dart
emitter.room('chat').emit('event-name', message);
```

`room()` returns a new emitter. The room does not stay set for later events.

### `emit`

Send to every client in the room. Without `room()`, this is every client of the same route.

```dart
emitter.emit('event-name', message);
```

### `emitExceptSender`

Send to every client in the room, but not to the sender.

```dart
emitter.emitExceptSender('event-name', message);
```

### `emitToSender`

Send only to the client that sent the event.

```dart
emitter.emitToSender('event-name', message);
```


---

# Dox CLI

Source: https://dartondox.dev/latest/3.xdigging-deeper/dox-cli/

# Dox CLI

The `dox` CLI creates projects and files, runs the dev server, builds for production and runs migrations.

Run `dox help` to see all commands. Run `dox help <command>` for one command.

## Installation

```bash
dart pub global activate dox 3.0.0-alpha.4
```

!!! warning "Add the pub bin folder to your PATH"
    If your shell can not find `dox`, add this line to `~/.bashrc` or `~/.zshrc`, and open a new terminal:

    ```bash
    export PATH="$PATH":"$HOME/.pub-cache/bin"
    ```

To remove the CLI:

```bash
dart pub global deactivate dox
```

## All commands

| Command | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `dox create <name> [--version <v>]` | create a new project |
| `dox serve` (or `dox s`) | start the dev server with build_runner watch |
| `dox build` | build the native (AOT) bundle into `build/bundle` |
| `dox build_runner:watch` / `dox build_runner:build` | run the code generator |
| `dox create:controller <name> [-r] [-ws]` | create a controller |
| `dox create:middleware <name>` | create a middleware |
| `dox create:dto <name>` | create a DTO (typed, checked input) |
| `dox create:serializer <name>` | create a serializer |
| `dox create:model <name> [-m]` (or `make:model`) | create a model, and with `-m` its migration |
| `dox make:migration <name> [--sql]` (or `create:migration`) | create a Dart migration, or a `.sql` one with `--sql` |
| `dox migration:run` (or `dox migrate`) | run new migrations |
| `dox migration:rollback [--step=N]` | undo the last batch, or the last N migrations |
| `dox migration:reset` | undo all migrations |
| `dox migration:refresh` | undo all, then run all again |
| `dox migration:status` | show which migrations ran, and their batch |
| `dox key:generate` | make a new `APP_KEY` |
| `dox env:generate` | make `lib/config/env.dart` (the typed env class) from `.env.example`, see [Environment Variables](env.md) |
| `dox env:check` | check the env against `lib/config/env.dart`. Prints every missing or bad key (exit code 1) |
| `dox openapi:generate [dir]` | write `openapi.json` and `openapi.yaml` (default `storage/openapi`), see [OpenAPI](../packages/openapi.md#write-the-files-dox-openapigenerate) |
| `dox update` | update the CLI |
| `dox version` (or `dox -v`) | show the CLI version |
| `dox help [command]` | show help |

## Project

### Create a project

```bash
dox create new_blog
dox create new_blog --version v3.0.0-alpha.4
```

`dox create` copies the [dox-sample](https://github.com/dartondox/dox-sample) template from GitHub. Without `--version`, it uses the latest release of the template.

### Run the dev server

```bash
dox serve                         # or: dox s
dox s --ignore-build-runner       # do not run build_runner watch
```

`dox serve` runs `dart run bin/server.dart`. When a `.dart` file changes, it restarts the server.
It also runs `build_runner watch`, so generated files stay up to date.

### Run the code generator

```bash
dox build_runner:watch   # watch files and build again on each change
dox build_runner:build   # build once
```

### Build for production

```bash
dox build
cd build/bundle
./bin/server
```

`dox build` does these steps:

1. It runs `build_runner` (when your app uses it).
2. It runs `dart build cli --target bin/server.dart --output build`.
3. It copies `db/` and `.env.example` into `build/bundle`.

When a step fails, it stops with exit code 1, so CI can stop too. See [Deployment](deployment.md).

### Make an app key

```bash
dox key:generate
```

It writes a new `APP_KEY` to your `.env` file.

## Create files

### Controller

```bash
dox create:controller Blog       # default controller
dox create:controller Blog -r    # resource controller
dox create:controller Chat -ws   # WebSocket controller
```

- A default or resource controller goes to `lib/app/http/controllers/`.
- A WebSocket controller goes to `lib/app/ws/controllers/`. See [WebSocket](websocket.md).
- `-r` adds the methods `index`, `create`, `store`, `show`, `edit`, `update` and `destroy`.

!!! info "File and class names"
    Word breaks are kept. `dox create:controller BlogPost` makes `blog_post.controller.dart`
    with the class `BlogPostController`. The same is true for middleware, DTOs and serializers.

### Middleware

```bash
dox create:middleware Auth
```

### DTO

```bash
dox create:dto CreateBlog
```

It makes `lib/app/http/dtos/create_blog.dto.dart`. Then run `dox build_runner:build`.
See [Validation](../the-basic/validation.md).

### Serializer

```bash
dox create:serializer Blog
```

### Model

```bash
dox create:model Blog
dox create:model Blog -m   # also makes the create_blogs_table migration
```

- `-m` (or `--migration`) makes a Dart migration `create_<table>_table`.
- The table name is the model name in plural snake case: `BlogPost` makes `blog_posts`.
- The model gets `@DoxModel(table: 'blog_posts')`, so it uses the same table.
- `make:model` is the same command.

### Migration

```bash
dox make:migration create_blogs_table          # .dart file (default)
dox make:migration create_blogs_table --sql    # .sql file
```

## Migrations

### Database settings

The migration commands read the database settings from the `.env` file:

```ini title=".env"
# postgres, mysql or sqlite
DB_CONNECTION=postgres
DB_HOST=localhost
DB_PORT=5432
# for sqlite: the file path
DB_NAME=postgres
DB_USERNAME=admin
DB_PASSWORD=password
```

- `DB_CONNECTION` is `postgres`, `mysql` or `sqlite`. The default is `postgres`.
- The default port is `5432` for postgres and `3306` for mysql.
- `DB_DATABASE` works too, in place of `DB_NAME`.
- Put comments on their own line. A `#` after a value becomes part of the value.

!!! warning "`.env` or environment, not both"
    When a `.env` file exists, these commands read only the `.env` file.
    They use the real environment variables only when there is no `.env` file.
    This is different from `Env.get()`, where a real environment variable wins.

### Run migrations

```bash
dox migration:run    # or: dox migrate
dox migration:status
```

### Undo migrations

```bash
dox migration:rollback           # undo the last batch
dox migration:rollback --step=2  # undo the last 2 migrations
dox migration:reset              # undo all migrations
dox migration:refresh            # undo all migrations, then run them again
```

`migrate:rollback`, `migrate:reset`, `migrate:refresh` and `migrate:status` also work.

- A failed migration stops the run, and the CLI exits with code 1.
- On MySQL, statements like `CREATE`, `ALTER` and `DROP` save right away. So when a migration fails half way, these changes are not undone.

## Update the CLI

`dox update` runs `dart pub global activate dox`. This installs the latest **stable** version, not a preview.
To stay on a preview version, run the install command with the version again:

```bash
dart pub global activate dox 3.0.0-alpha.4
```


---

# Deployment

Source: https://dartondox.dev/latest/3.xdigging-deeper/deployment/

# Deployment

This page shows how to build a Dox app for production and run it safely.

!!! danger "Never run production with `dart run`"
    `dart run` (and `dox serve`) uses the JIT compiler. It is made for
    development. It uses about 25x more memory at start (around 390 MB
    instead of 16 MB) and starts slower. Always build an AOT binary for
    production.

## Build

Compile the app to a native binary (AOT).

```bash
dox build
```

This makes a `build/bundle/` folder:

| File                        | What it is                                       |
| --------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------ |
| `build/bundle/bin/server`   | the native binary. No Dart SDK needed to run it  |
| `build/bundle/lib/`         | native libraries from build hooks (eg. SQLite)   |
| `build/bundle/db/`          | your migrations                                  |
| `build/bundle/.env.example` | copy it to `build/bundle/.env`, or use env variables |

`dox build` runs `build_runner` first (when your app uses it). Then it runs
`dart build cli --target bin/server.dart --output build`. It exits with code 1
when a step fails, so CI can stop.

!!! warning "Not `dart compile exe`"
    `dox_orm` depends on `sqlite3` v3. It bundles SQLite with a build hook.
    `dart compile exe` does not run build hooks, so it stops with an error.
    `dart build cli` is the same AOT compiler and runs the hooks.
    Keep `bin/` and `lib/` together: the binary loads the libraries from `../lib`.

Start the application.

```bash
cd build/bundle
./bin/server
```

The binary reads `.env` and `db/` from the folder you start it in.
A real environment variable wins over the `.env` file.

A new Dox app runs the migrations in `bin/server.dart`, before the server starts.
So the database is up to date when the first request comes in.

## Docker

The `Dockerfile` in a new Dox app is a multi-stage build:

1. The `dart:stable` image builds the AOT bundle with
   `dart build cli --target bin/server.dart --output build`.
2. The final image is `FROM scratch`. It holds only the Dart AOT runtime
   files (`/runtime/` from the dart image), the bundle (`/app/bin/server` and
   `/app/lib/`), `db/` and an empty `/tmp`.

```dockerfile
FROM dart:stable AS build
WORKDIR /app
COPY pubspec.* ./
RUN dart pub get
COPY . .
RUN dart pub get --offline
RUN dart run build_runner build --delete-conflicting-outputs
RUN dart build cli --target bin/server.dart --output build
RUN mkdir -p /out/app/storage /out/tmp \
  && chmod 1777 /out/tmp \
  && cp -r build/bundle/. /out/app/ \
  && cp -r db /out/app/db

FROM scratch
COPY --from=build /runtime/ /
COPY --from=build /out/ /
WORKDIR /app
EXPOSE 3000
CMD ["/app/bin/server"]
```

The image has no `.env` file, so secrets stay out of it. Pass config as
environment variables.

```bash
docker build -t my-app .
docker run -p 3000:3000 -e APP_PORT=3000 -e APP_KEY=... -e DB_HOST=... my-app
```

Or use `env_file: .env` in `docker-compose.yml`.

## HTTPS: put a proxy in front

Do not serve HTTPS from Dart. TLS in Dart's `HttpServer` is slow (a known
Dart SDK issue). Dox has no `bindSecure`.

Run Dox on plain HTTP on a private port. Put [Caddy](https://caddyserver.com)
or nginx in front of it. The proxy does TLS, HTTP/2 and gzip.

The whole setup looks like this:

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    C["Client"] -->|HTTPS| X["Caddy or nginx<br>TLS, HTTP/2, gzip, body size limit"]
    X -->|"plain HTTP on 127.0.0.1:3000"| D["Dox binary<br>bin/server, one isolate per core"]
    D -->|"one pool per isolate"| DB[("Database")]
    M["Migrations<br>bin/server.dart runs them once, before the server starts"] --> DB
```

Then tell Dox to trust the proxy, so `req.ip()` and `req.scheme()` show the
real client:

```dart
AppConfig(
  /// the proxy's IP, or a range like '10.0.0.0/8', or '172.16.0.0/12' for docker
  trustedProxies: <String>['127.0.0.1', '::1'],
);
```

- `req.ip()` reads `X-Forwarded-For`. Dox walks the list from the right and
  skips your proxies, so a fake value from the client is ignored.
- `req.scheme()` reads `X-Forwarded-Proto` (`http` or `https`).
  `req.isSecure()` is true for `https`.
- `trustedProxies` is empty by default. Then Dox ignores those headers,
  because any client can send them.
- `['*']` trusts everyone. Only use it when the app port is not reachable
  from outside.

### Caddy

Caddy gets a certificate for you and sets `X-Forwarded-For` and
`X-Forwarded-Proto`. Websockets work with no extra config.

```
example.com {
  encode gzip
  reverse_proxy 127.0.0.1:3000
}
```

### Nginx

```nginx
upstream dox {
  server 127.0.0.1:3000;
  keepalive 64;
}

map $http_upgrade $connection_upgrade {
  default upgrade;
  ''      '';
}

server {
  listen 443 ssl http2;
  server_name example.com;

  ssl_certificate     /etc/letsencrypt/live/example.com/fullchain.pem;
  ssl_certificate_key /etc/letsencrypt/live/example.com/privkey.pem;

  # match maxMultipartSize in AppConfig
  client_max_body_size 100m;

  gzip on;
  gzip_types application/json text/plain text/css application/javascript;

  location / {
    proxy_pass http://dox;
    proxy_http_version 1.1;

    # websocket upgrade
    proxy_set_header Upgrade $http_upgrade;
    proxy_set_header Connection $connection_upgrade;

    proxy_set_header Host $host;
    proxy_set_header X-Real-IP $remote_addr;
    proxy_set_header X-Forwarded-For $proxy_add_x_forwarded_for;
    proxy_set_header X-Forwarded-Proto $scheme;

    # stream uploads to Dox, do not buffer them in nginx first
    proxy_request_buffering off;
  }
}

server {
  listen 80;
  server_name example.com;
  return 301 https://$host$request_uri;
}
```

## Keep it running

Dox uses all CPU cores by default (see [Isolate](isolate.md)).

- When a worker isolate dies, Dox prints the error and starts it again.
- When the main isolate dies, the process exits with a non-zero code.
  Let a supervisor restart it: `restart: unless-stopped` in Docker compose,
  or `Restart=always` in systemd.

```ini
# /etc/systemd/system/dox.service
[Service]
WorkingDirectory=/srv/app/build/bundle
ExecStart=/srv/app/build/bundle/bin/server
EnvironmentFile=/srv/app/build/bundle/.env
Restart=always

[Install]
WantedBy=multi-user.target
```

## Graceful shutdown

On `SIGTERM` (docker stop, Kubernetes, Cloud Run, Fly, systemd) or `SIGINT` (Ctrl+C), Dox stops gracefully, in every isolate:

1. It stops taking new connections at once.
2. Open requests can finish. Each keep-alive connection closes after its current answer.
3. After `shutdownTimeout` (default 8 seconds), it closes the connections that are still open.
4. It runs `shutdown()` of each service that implements `DoxShutdown` (see [Services](services.md#clean-up-on-shutdown)).
5. The process exits with code `0`.

A second `SIGINT` or `SIGTERM` stops the process at once.

Set the timeout in `lib/config/app.dart`:

```dart
AppConfig(
  shutdownTimeout: Duration(seconds: 20),
  ...
)
```

Keep it shorter than the time your platform waits before it kills the process:

| Platform | Waits | Change it with |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `docker stop` | 10 seconds | `docker stop -t 30`, or `stop_grace_period` in compose |
| Kubernetes | 30 seconds | `terminationGracePeriodSeconds` |
| Cloud Run | 10 seconds | can not be changed |
| Fly.io | 5 seconds | `kill_timeout` in `fly.toml` |
| systemd | 90 seconds | `TimeoutStopSec` |

In code, `await Dox().stop()` does steps 1 to 4 and does not exit.

## Many processes or machines

One Dox process already uses every core. You only need more processes to
run on more machines, or to restart one process without downtime.
Run each one on its own port (or machine) and list them in the proxy:

```nginx
upstream dox {
  server 10.0.0.11:3000;
  server 10.0.0.12:3000;
  keepalive 64;
}
```

Websocket rooms then need a shared adapter (like Redis), because each
process has its own memory.


---

# Native server

Source: https://dartondox.dev/latest/3.xdigging-deeper/native-server/

# Native server

Dox runs on a native HTTP server by default. It comes from the package
`dox_http_native`. You do not need to set anything.

- Rust ([hyper](https://hyper.rs)) owns the sockets and parses HTTP.
- All your code stays in Dart: routes, controllers, DTOs, middleware, ORM.
- It is much faster than the `dart:io` server. In a hello world test on one
  core it served about 5 times more requests. See [Performance](performance.md).

You do not need Rust. The package downloads a ready-built library for your
system when you build the app.

## How it works

1. Rust reads the requests from the sockets.
2. It sends the requests to Dart in batches (one message per batch).
3. Dart runs your handlers, like before.
4. Dart sends all answers back to Rust in one call.

The native server has the same API as the `dart:io` `HttpServer`. So
`req.httpRequest`, `HttpResponse` and code written for `dart:io` keep working.

Each isolate runs its own server on the same port:

- Linux: one socket per isolate (`SO_REUSEPORT`). The kernel spreads the
  connections.
- macOS: the isolates share one socket.
- Windows: only one isolate serves HTTP.

## Use dart:io instead

Set `server` in `AppConfig`:

```dart
AppConfig(
  // ...
  server: ServerBackend.dartIo,
);
```

Or set the env var `DOX_SERVER=dartio`. The env var wins over the config.

Dox also uses `dart:io` by itself in these cases:

- The native library did not load. Dox prints one warning line at start:
  `[dox] warning: dox_http_native did not load, using the dart:io server (...)`.
- The app has WebSocket or Socket.IO routes. The native server can not
  upgrade a connection to WebSocket yet.

`DOX_SERVER=native` forces the native server, also for an app with WebSocket
routes. WebSocket upgrades then fail with 500. Socket.IO long-polling works.

Each isolate has its own Rust network thread. `DOX_HTTP_THREAD=shared` puts
all isolates on one thread. It is off by default: on 2 cores the one thread
was the limit and req/s fell by a quarter. Leave it off unless you measure
a gain.

## Limits

- Max size of the request line plus headers: 16 KB. Bigger gets `431`.
- A bad request gets `400`.
- A body over the bigger of `maxBodySize` and `maxMultipartSize` gets `413`
  from Rust. Each body type is checked again in Dart with its own limit.
- A response is sent when it is closed. It is kept in memory until then,
  also a big file. Use a proxy (nginx, Caddy) or a storage link for big
  downloads.
- No WebSocket upgrade yet (see above).
- `compress: true` works: Dart gzips the body.

## Where the library comes from

The build hook of `dox_http_native` (`hook/build.dart`) picks the first one
that works:

1. A path you give in the root `pubspec.yaml` of your app:

    ```yaml
    hooks:
      user_defines:
        dox_http_native:
          lib_path: /path/to/libdox_http_native.so
    ```

2. A local build in `native/target/release` of the package (for work on
   Dox itself).
3. The ready-built library from the GitHub release, checked with sha256.
   There are builds for macOS (arm64, x64), Linux (x64, arm64) and
   Windows (x64).
4. A build from source with `cargo`, when Rust is installed.

When none works, the app still builds and runs on `dart:io`.

!!! note "Use `dart build cli`"
    `dart compile exe` does not run build hooks. Use `dox build` or
    `dart build cli`. See [Deployment](deployment.md).

## Work on the native code

The Rust code is in `packages/dox-http-native/native`.

```bash
cd packages/dox-http-native/native
cargo build --release   # the hook uses this build from now on
cargo test
cd .. && dart test --concurrency=1
```

To make a release of the libraries, push a tag like
`dox_http_native-v3.0.0-alpha.4`. The version in the tag must be the
`version` in `packages/dox-http-native/pubspec.yaml`, because the build hook
downloads from the tag of its own version.

The `Native` workflow builds the 5 libraries and uploads them with a
`SHA256SUMS` file. Copy the hashes into `_sha256` in `hook/build.dart` before
you publish the package.


---

# Performance

Source: https://dartondox.dev/latest/3.xdigging-deeper/performance/

# Performance

This page shows how fast Dox is, and how to keep your app fast in production.

The short version:

1. Build with `dox build` and run the AOT binary. Never `dart run` in production.
2. Put Caddy or nginx in front for HTTPS and gzip.
3. Keep the default isolates (one per CPU core).
4. Keep the body limits on. Uploads stream to disk.

## Benchmark

A "hello world" test. Each server answers `GET /` with the plain text
`Hello World`. Dox is a small real Dox app with one route.

Hello world only measures framework overhead. A real app spends most of its
time on the database, JSON and your own code, so the gaps are much smaller
there.

### 1 core

| Server                        | req/s   | p99 ms | CPU % | peak MB |
| ----------------------------- | ------: | -----: | ----: | ------: |
| Dox, native server            | 171,042 | 0.92   | 100   | 9       |
| Dox, `dart:io` server         | 33,154  | 5.48   | 101   | 39      |
| Bun 1.4.3                     | 181,162 | 1.13   | 101   | 14      |
| Node 24.22.0                  | 81,909  | 2.26   | 101   | 54      |
| Pure Rust hyper (the ceiling) | 254,349 | 0.47   | 100   | 5       |

On one core, Dox with the native server is about as fast as Bun (0.94x).
It is 5x faster than Dox on `dart:io`.

How it was run:

- Docker on an Apple M2 (8 CPUs in the Docker VM), `linux/arm64`.
- The server and wrk run in two containers, pinned to different CPUs:
  server on CPU 0, wrk on CPUs 2-7.
- wrk 4.2.0, 100 connections (the tables) and 256 connections.
  5 seconds warm-up, then 3 runs of 10 seconds. The tables show the median.
- CPU % and peak memory come from `docker stats`. 100% = one core.
- Dart 3.13.6, Rust 1.99.1. Dox is built with `dart build cli` (this is
  what `dox build` does). The build hook of `dox_http_native` builds the
  Rust library with cargo.
- `DOX_SERVER=dartio` runs the same Dox app on `dart:io`.

## App benchmark

A small real app, the same in each language: `GET /json` returns a map,
`GET /db` reads one row by id from Postgres, `GET /queries?n=20` reads 20
rows one after another. The table has 10,000 rows. Each server runs alone
on one or two pinned CPUs, Postgres 18 and wrk on other CPUs, 256
connections, 4 database connections per core, 3 runs of 10 seconds, median.
Versions: Dox 3.0.0-alpha.3 (native server, `dox_postgres_native`), Go 1.27
(`net/http` + pgx), Bun 1.4 (`Bun.serve` + `Bun.sql`), Node 24
(`node:http` + `pg`), `dart:io` (`HttpServer` + `package:postgres`).

| Route            | Dox     | Bun     | Go      | Node    |
| ---------------- | ------: | ------: | ------: | ------: |
| /json req/s      | 251,427 | 385,553 | 175,009 | 156,389 |
| /db req/s        | 138,514 | 128,998 | 49,393  | 61,611  |
| /queries req/s   | 12,902  | 11,006  | 5,134   | 5,870   |
| /db p99 ms       | 3.62    | 5.61    | 8.53    | 8.06    |
| /db peak MB      | 51      | 57      | 22      | 297     |

Dox runs one isolate per core, Bun and Node one worker process per core.
On the database routes Dox is ahead of all of them on 2 cores, and its p99
is the lowest. On `/json` Bun is faster: its server is C++ and calls the
JavaScript handler on the same thread, while Dox hands each batch of
requests from the Rust thread to the Dart isolate.

Dox on `dart:io` with the Dart `postgres` driver is 4 to 10 times slower
than Dox with the native server and driver. Keep both on.

### Dart VM flags

We tried a bigger young generation (`DART_VM_OPTIONS=--new_gen_semi_max_size=64`
and `128`) for a better p99. Over 5 runs the change was inside the noise,
and memory did not move. So there is no flag to set. Dox never sets VM
flags for you. `DART_VM_OPTIONS` is read by the AOT binary from
`dox build`, so you can try your own.

## Request body limits

Dox reads a body while it streams in, and stops once it is too big.
It answers `413 Payload Too Large`. It checks `Content-Length` first, so a
big upload is refused before one byte is read. It also counts bytes while
reading, so a client that sends no `Content-Length` (chunked) is stopped too.

```dart
AppConfig(
  maxBodySize: 10 * 1024 * 1024,        // JSON and urlencoded, default 10 MB
  maxMultipartSize: 100 * 1024 * 1024,  // form-data uploads, default 100 MB
);
```

Set the same limit in the proxy (`client_max_body_size` in nginx).

## File uploads

- A file up to 1 MB stays in memory.
- A bigger file is written to a temp file while it arrives. So a big upload
  does not fill the memory.
- The temp file is deleted when the response is done. So save it before you
  return from the controller.

```dart
RequestFile file = req.input('video');

file.length;          // size in bytes
await file.size;      // size in KB
file.stream();        // read it in chunks
await file.store('videos');           // to storage (a cheap move on local disk)
await file.moveTo('/data/videos/1.mp4');
await file.bytes;     // whole file in memory. avoid for big files
```

## Big responses

Return a `Stream<List<int>>` or a `File`. Dox pipes it to the client and does
not load it all into memory.

```dart
Route.get('/video', (DoxRequest req) => File('storage/video.mp4'));
```

A `File` response sets `Content-Type` (from the file name),
`Content-Length` and `Accept-Ranges`. It answers `Range: bytes=...` with
`206 Partial Content`, so video players can seek and downloads can resume.

`Storage().stream()` and `Storage().download()` on the local disk also stream
the file and send `Content-Length`.

JSON and text responses are encoded once, straight to bytes, with
`Content-Length` set.

## gzip

gzip in Dart is off by default.

