```dart
AppConfig(compress: true);
```

- It saves bandwidth, but costs CPU on every response, in the same isolate
  that serves requests.
- A proxy (Caddy, nginx) does it better. Turn it on in Dart only when there
  is no proxy.
- With `compress: true`, text and JSON responses are sent chunked, without
  `Content-Length`, because `dart:io` only gzips when the length is not set.

## Logging

`LogMiddleware` prints one JSON line per request. Writing to stdout blocks
the isolate. So Dox collects log lines and writes them every 20 ms (or every
64 KB) in one write. If the process is killed hard, the last 20 ms of request logs can
be lost. Errors from `Logger` are still written right away.

Turn `LogMiddleware` off when a proxy already writes access logs.

## What Dox does for you

- Routes are grouped by method. The regex of each route is built once, not
  on every request.
- The argument types of each controller are read once at start, not on
  every request.


---

# Testing

Source: https://dartondox.dev/latest/3.xdigging-deeper/testing/

# Testing

This page shows how to test a Dox app with the `test` package: HTTP routes, cache, storage, env and the database.

## Setup

Add the test packages as dev dependencies:

```bash
dart pub add dev:test dev:http
```

Put your tests in the `test/` folder. Run them with:

```bash
dart test
```

## Test HTTP routes

Start the real server once for the whole file. Then send requests to it with `package:http`.

```dart title="test/http_test.dart"
import 'package:dox_core/dox_core.dart';
import 'package:http/http.dart' as http;
import 'package:my_app/config/app.dart';
import 'package:test/test.dart';

String baseUrl = 'http://localhost:${appConfig.serverPort}';

void main() {
  setUpAll(() async {
    Dox().initialize(appConfig);
    Dox().totalIsolate(1);
    await Dox().startServer();
  });

  tearDownAll(() async {
    await Dox().server.close();
  });

  test('GET /api/ping', () async {
    http.Response response = await http.get(Uri.parse('$baseUrl/api/ping'));
    expect(response.statusCode, 200);
    expect(response.body, 'pong');
  });
}
```

- `startServer()` returns when the server listens. You do not need to wait after it.
- `Dox().totalIsolate(1)` runs the server on one isolate. By default Dox starts one isolate per CPU core. A test does not need them, and they make the start slower.
- With one isolate, you can also add a route inside a test with `Route.get(...)`. It works right away.
- Do not run `dox serve` on the same port while you test. The test can fail to start, or send its requests to the dev server. Stop `dox serve`, or use another `APP_PORT` for tests.

## Test the cache

`Dox().cache` is the `CacheManager` that `Cache()` uses. Replace it with a memory store, so tests do not write files or need Redis:

```dart
setUp(() {
  Dox().cache = CacheManager(CacheConfig(
    defaultStore: 'memory',
    stores: <String, Map<String, dynamic>>{
      'memory': <String, dynamic>{'driver': 'memory'},
    },
  ));
});

test('caches the posts', () async {
  await Cache().put('posts', <String>['a', 'b']);
  expect(await Cache().get('posts'), <dynamic>['a', 'b']);
});
```

A new `CacheManager` in `setUp` gives each test an empty cache. See [Cache](cache.md).

## Test file storage

`Dox().storage.fake(name)` swaps one disk with an empty memory disk. `restore(name)` puts the real disk back.

```dart
setUpAll(() {
  Dox().initialize(appConfig);
});

test('saves the report', () async {
  Disk fake = Dox().storage.fake('s3');

  String path = await Storage()
      .disk('s3')
      .put('reports', <int>[1, 2, 3], extension: 'pdf'); // '/reports/<uuid>.pdf'

  expect(await fake.exists(path.substring(1)), isTrue);
  Dox().storage.restore('s3');
});
```

- Call `Dox().initialize()` first. The storage disks are made from `appConfig`.
- `Storage()` paths start with `/`. A `Disk` key does not, so remove the first `/` when you ask the `Disk` directly.

See [File Storage](file-storage.md).

## Test the env

Pass your own values to `AppEnv.load()`. Then nothing is read from the shell or the `.env` file:

```dart
AppEnv env = AppEnv.load(
  EnvReader(
    environment: <String, String>{'APP_KEY': 'test'},
    dotEnv: <String, String>{'DB_PORT': '5433'},
  ),
);
expect(env.dbPort, 5433);
```

A missing or bad key throws an `EnvException`. So you can also test that your app stops on a bad env. See [Environment Variables](env.md).

## Test the database

A test that uses models needs a real database. Run the migrations and the ORM service once, before the tests:

```dart title="test/db_test.dart"
import 'package:dox_core/dox_core.dart';
import 'package:dox_migration/dox_migration.dart';
import 'package:my_app/app/models/user/user.model.dart';
import 'package:my_app/config/app.dart';
import 'package:my_app/config/database.dart';
import 'package:my_app/services/orm_service.dart';
import 'package:test/test.dart';

void main() {
  setUpAll(() async {
    Dox().initialize(appConfig);
    await Migrator(
      connection: await databaseConfig
          .getConnectionConfig()
          .getDatabaseConnection(),
    ).migrate();
    await ORMService().setup();
  });

  test('saves a user', () async {
    User user = User()
      ..name = 'Dox'
      ..email = 'test-${DateTime.now().microsecondsSinceEpoch}@dox.dev'
      ..password = 'secret';
    await user.save();
    expect(user.id, isNotNull);
  });
}
```

- Use a separate test database. Set its name in the env of the test run, for example `DB_NAME=app_test dart test`.
- Make each test data unique (like the email above), or delete it at the end of the test. Then tests do not break each other.
- `ORMService().setup()` runs the same code as at server start. See [Services](services.md).

!!! tip "Run test files one by one"
    `dart test` runs test files at the same time. When two files start the server on the same port, or use the same tables, run them one by one: `dart test --concurrency=1`.


---

# Database

Source: https://dartondox.dev/latest/3.xdatabase/

# Database

This page shows how to connect Dox to a database.
Dox works with Postgres, MySQL, MariaDB and SQLite through the `dox_orm` package.

- [Query builder](query-builder.md): build SQL with methods.
- [Models](model/index.md): one class per table.
- [Transactions](transactions.md): many queries that succeed or fail together.
- [Migration](migration.md) and [Schema](schema.md): create and change tables.

This is how a query travels from your code to the database:

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    M["Model or QueryBuilder"] --> S["SQL text<br>quoted names, @values"]
    S --> D{"Driver"}
    D --> N["Native Rust pool<br>dox_postgres_native, dox_mysql_native"]
    D --> T["Dart driver<br>postgres, mysql_dart, sqlite3"]
    N --> DB[("Database")]
    T --> DB
```

## Install

The query builder and the models are in the `dox_orm` package.

```bash
dart pub add dox_orm
```

```dart
import 'package:dox_orm/dox_orm.dart';
```

## Supported databases

| Database | `Driver` | Default driver | Fallback Dart driver | Pool | Good for |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Postgres | `Driver.postgres` | [`dox_postgres_native`](postgres-native.md) | `postgres` | Yes | Production |
| MySQL 8+ and MariaDB | `Driver.mysql` | [`dox_mysql_native`](mysql-native.md) | `mysql_dart` | Yes | Production |
| SQLite | `Driver.sqlite` | `sqlite3` | none | No, one connection per isolate | Development, tests, small apps |

!!! info "Native drivers"
    Postgres and MySQL use a native (Rust) driver by default.
    It is faster when many requests run at the same time.
    You do not change any config for it.

    The ORM uses the Dart driver in these cases:

    - The native library can not load on your system. The ORM prints one warning line.
    - Postgres uses TLS (`useSSL: true` or `extra['sslMode']`). The native Postgres driver has no TLS yet.
    - You ask for it: set `DOX_DB_DRIVER=dart` for all connections,
      or `extra: {'native': false}` for one connection.

    See the [Postgres](postgres-native.md#use-the-dart-driver) and
    [MySQL](mysql-native.md#use-the-dart-driver) pages.

Dox picks the driver of a connection like this:

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    A["Driver.postgres or Driver.mysql"] --> B{"DOX_DB_DRIVER=dart<br>or extra native: false?"}
    B -->|yes| X["Dart driver"]
    B -->|no| C{"Postgres with TLS?<br>useSSL or sslMode"}
    C -->|yes| X
    C -->|no| L{"Native library loads?"}
    L -->|no| W["Dart driver<br>prints one warning"]
    L -->|yes| N["Native Rust driver"]
    Q["Driver.sqlite"] --> S["sqlite3<br>one connection per isolate"]
```

## Config

Put the connections in `lib/config/database.dart`.
`connection` is the name of the default connection.

```dart title="lib/config/database.dart"
import 'package:dox_core/dox_core.dart';
import 'package:dox_orm/dox_orm.dart';

DatabaseConfig databaseConfig = DatabaseConfig(
  connection: env.dbConnection,
  connections: <String, ConnectionConfig>{
    'postgres': ConnectionConfig(
      driver: Driver.postgres,
      host: 'localhost',
      port: 5432,
      user: 'postgres',
      password: 'postgres',
      database: 'postgres',
      extra: <String, dynamic>{'maxConnectionCount': 10},
      debug: false,
    ),
    'mysql': ConnectionConfig(
      driver: Driver.mysql, // also for MariaDB
      host: 'localhost',
      port: 3306,
      user: 'root',
      password: 'password',
      database: 'dox',
      extra: <String, dynamic>{'maxConnectionCount': 10},
      debug: false,
    ),
    'sqlite': ConnectionConfig(
      driver: Driver.sqlite,
      database: 'storage/app.db', // file path, or ':memory:'
      debug: false,
    ),
  },
);
```

- `debug: true` prints each SQL query and its values.
- `user`, `password`, `host` and `port` are not used by SQLite.

Start the ORM in a service.
Each isolate runs the service, so each isolate gets its own pool.

```dart title="lib/services/orm_service.dart"
class ORMService implements DoxService {
  @override
  Future<void> setup() async {
    SqlQueryBuilder.initializeWithDatabaseConfig(databaseConfig);
  }
}
```

### `.env`

The app config and the [migration](migration.md) commands read these values.

```py title=".env"
DB_CONNECTION=postgres # postgres, mysql or sqlite
DB_HOST=localhost
DB_PORT=5432           # 3306 for mysql
DB_NAME=dox            # for sqlite: the file path, like storage/app.db
DB_USERNAME=postgres
DB_PASSWORD=postgres
```

### `DATABASE_URL`

Many hosts (Fly, Render, Heroku and others) give you one database url.
Dox reads it from the `DATABASE_URL` environment variable.

The rule: **when `DATABASE_URL` is set, it wins.**
It replaces the config of the default connection (`DatabaseConfig.connection`).
That config still gives `debug`, `printer` and `extra`.
Other named connections do not change.

```bash
DATABASE_URL=postgres://app:s%40cret@db.example.com:5432/blog?sslmode=require
```

| Form | Database |
|---|---|
| `postgres://user:pass@host:5432/db` or `postgresql://...` | Postgres |
| `mysql://user:pass@host:3306/db` or `mariadb://...` | MySQL, MariaDB |
| `sqlite:///abs/path.db`, `sqlite://db/dox.sqlite`, `sqlite::memory:`, `file:db/dox.sqlite` | SQLite |

- The user, password and database name are url-decoded. Write `@` in a password as `%40`.
- No port: `5432` for Postgres, `3306` for MySQL.
- `sslmode`: `disable`, `allow` and `prefer` mean no TLS. `verify-full` checks the server certificate. Other values, like `require`, turn TLS on. For MySQL, `ssl=true` works too.
- The native Postgres driver has no TLS yet. With TLS on, Postgres uses the Dart driver.
- `host=/cloudsql/project:region:instance` connects to a Postgres Unix socket. See [Unix socket](#unix-socket).
- Any other option goes to `extra`, like `?maxConnectionCount=20`. A number becomes an `int`, `true` and `false` a `bool`.

The ORM reads `DATABASE_URL` from the real environment, not from `.env`.
To use a url from `.env`, or any other url, give it yourself:

```dart
DatabaseConfig(
  connection: 'postgres',
  connections: {...},
  url: Env.get<String?>('DATABASE_URL'),
);
```

An empty `url` (`url: ''`) turns `DATABASE_URL` off.
To make one `ConnectionConfig` from a url, use `ConnectionConfig.fromUrl(url)`.
[Migrations](migration.md#database-settings) read `DATABASE_URL` too, also from `.env`.

### Unix socket

A Postgres host that starts with `/` is a Unix socket folder, like in libpq.
Google Cloud SQL on Cloud Run uses `/cloudsql/PROJECT:REGION:INSTANCE`.

```bash
DB_HOST=/cloudsql/my-project:europe-west1:blog
# or
DATABASE_URL=postgres://blog:secret@/blog?host=/cloudsql/my-project:europe-west1:blog
```

Both the native and the Dart Postgres driver use the socket file `<folder>/.s.PGSQL.<port>`.
A host that already ends with `/.s.PGSQL.5432` works too.
MySQL sockets are not supported.

### `extra` options

`extra` is a map in `ConnectionConfig` for driver options.

| Key | Database | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|
| `maxConnectionCount` | Postgres, MySQL | `10` | Most connections in the pool. |
| `native` | Postgres, MySQL | `true` | `false` uses the Dart driver for this connection. |
| `threads` | Postgres, MySQL | `1` | Rust threads of the native driver. |
| `maxConnectionAge` | MySQL | 12 hours | A connection older than this is opened again. |
| `preparedStatementCacheSize` | MySQL, and the Dart Postgres and SQLite drivers | `100` | Prepared statements kept per connection. |
| `timeZone` | Postgres | `UTC` | Time zone of the session. |
| `applicationName` | Postgres | none | Name of the app in `pg_stat_activity`. |
| `busyTimeout` | SQLite | `5000` | Milliseconds a query waits for a lock. |

The Dart drivers read some more keys.
The Dart Postgres driver reads the `PoolSettings` keys of the `postgres` package,
like `sslMode`, `queryTimeout` and `connectTimeout`.
The Dart MySQL driver reads `collation` (default `utf8mb4_general_ci`), `timeoutMs`,
`timeZone`, `serverPublicKey` and `allowPublicKeyRetrieval`.

!!! info "MySQL 8 login without TLS"
    The MySQL 8 default login (`caching_sha2_password`) works without TLS.
    The Dart driver then asks the server for its RSA key to encrypt the password.
    To not ask, give the key in `serverPublicKey`, or set `useSSL: true`.
    Set `allowPublicKeyRetrieval: false` to turn the asking off.

### Table and column names are quoted

Table and column names you pass to `select`, `where`, `join`, `groupBy`, `orderBy`,
`insert` and `update` are quoted.
Postgres and SQLite use `"name"`. MySQL uses `` `name` ``.
So names like `order` or `key` work.

- `table.column`, `*` and `column as alias` are quoted in the right way.
- A value with `(` (for example `count(*) as total`) is kept as it is.
- For anything else, use the raw methods (`selectRaw`, `whereRaw`, `joinRaw`).
- On Postgres, a quoted name is case sensitive. `userId` is not the same column as `userid`.

### Raw queries

`QueryBuilder.query()` runs SQL on the default connection.
Use `@name` for values. The values are sent as bound parameters.

```dart
List<Map<String, dynamic>> rows = await QueryBuilder.query(
  'select * from blog where id = @id',
  substitutionValues: <String, dynamic>{'id': 1},
);
```

Pass `connection` to run it on another connection.

```dart
await QueryBuilder.query('select 1', connection: 'mysql');
```

### Other connections

Use `withConnection()` with a connection name from the config.

```dart
List<Map<String, dynamic>> rows = await QueryBuilder.table('blog')
    .withConnection('mysql')
    .get();
```

A model keeps its connection. `save()` and `delete()` use it.
Models that a query returns use the connection of the query.

```dart
Blog blog = Blog()..withConnection('mysql');
blog.title = 'Hello';
await blog.save(); // saved on 'mysql'
```

## MySQL and MariaDB

- The default driver is [`dox_mysql_native`](mysql-native.md).
  The fallback Dart driver is `mysql_dart`.
- Both have a connection pool and send values as bound parameters.
- MySQL 8 and 9 login (`caching_sha2_password`) works.
- `CREATE`, `ALTER` and `DROP` are saved right away. A transaction can not undo them.

MySQL values are converted by column type:

| MySQL / MariaDB | Dart |
|---|---|
| Integer types | `int` |
| `FLOAT`, `DOUBLE`, `DECIMAL` | `double` |
| `DATE`, `DATETIME`, `TIMESTAMP` | `DateTime`, read as UTC |
| `boolean()` columns (`TINYINT(1)`) | `bool` |
| `TIME` | `String` |
| `JSON` | `Map` or `List` |

!!! info "JSON on MariaDB"
    MariaDB stores JSON as `LONGTEXT`, so the driver can not see the column type.
    On MariaDB, text that starts with `{` or `[` and is valid JSON is decoded.
    Other text columns are not decoded.

## SQLite

SQLite is good for development, tests and small apps.
For a busy production app, use Postgres or MySQL.

!!! info "How it runs"
    The `sqlite3` package calls SQLite directly (FFI).
    A query blocks the isolate while it runs.
    Each isolate has one connection.
    While a transaction is open, the other queries of that isolate wait.
    The database file uses WAL mode, so readers do not wait for the writer.
    `busy_timeout` makes a query wait for a lock from another isolate, instead of failing.
    Foreign keys are turned on.

!!! info "Types"
    SQLite has no bool, JSON or date type. Dox converts them for you:

    - `boolean()` is saved as `0`/`1` and read back as `bool`.
    - `json()` is saved as text and read back as `Map` or `List`.
    - Dates are saved as ISO text in UTC and read back as `DateTime`.

    The driver uses the column type in `CREATE TABLE`.
    It finds the table by the table names in the query.
    So it works on tables made by `Schema`, or by SQL with the same type names
    (`BOOLEAN`, `JSON`, `TIMESTAMP`, `DATE`, `DATETIME`).
    A column with an alias (`active as is_active`) is not converted.

!!! warning "Limits"
    - `schema.table` with `.change()` makes the table again and copies the rows.
      See [SQLite notes](schema.md#sqlite-notes).
    - `dropColumn` does not work on a primary key, unique or indexed column.
    - A new column with `NOT NULL` needs a default value.
    - `truncate()` runs `DELETE FROM` and resets the id counter.
    - `insertMultiple` with rows that have different keys inserts the rows one by one,
      because SQLite has no `DEFAULT` in `VALUES`.
    - SQLite before 3.39 has no `RIGHT JOIN`.

!!! info "Native library"
    The `sqlite3` package (v3) bundles SQLite with a build hook.
    You do not install a system library.
    `dart run` and `dart test` run the hook by themselves.
    For the AOT binary, use `dox build` (it runs `dart build cli`).
    It puts the library in `build/bundle/lib/`, next to `build/bundle/bin/server`.
    Keep the two folders together.
    `dart compile exe` does not work with build hooks.
    See [Deployment](../digging-deeper/deployment.md).


---

# Query Builder

Source: https://dartondox.dev/latest/3.xdatabase/query-builder/

# Query Builder

The query builder makes SQL for you.
You chain methods, and Dox runs the query with bound values.
It works on Postgres, MySQL/MariaDB and SQLite.

- Set up the database first. See [Database](index.md).
- For transactions, see [Transactions](transactions.md).

## Start a query

There are two ways to start a query.

```dart
// with a model: the result is a list of Actor models
List<Actor> actors = await Actor().where('age', '>=', 23).get();

// with a table name: the result is a list of maps, one map per row
List<Map<String, dynamic>> rows = await QueryBuilder.table('actor')
    .where('age', '>=', 23)
    .get();
```

See [Models](model/index.md) for the model way.

The examples on this page use an `Actor` model on the table `actor`.
The SQL in the examples is for Postgres. MySQL quotes names with `` ` `` instead of `"`.

!!! tip "Start each query with a new object"
    A query object keeps its `where`, `orderBy` and other parts.
    Use `Actor()` (or `QueryBuilder.table(...)`) again for each new query.

## Read rows

### `get`

Runs the query and returns all rows that match.

```dart
List<Actor> actors = await Actor().where('name', 'John Wick').get();
// SELECT * FROM "actor" WHERE "name" = @name_p0
```

### `all`

Returns all rows of the table.
`all()` ignores `where`, `join`, `orderBy` and `limit`. Use `get()` for those.

```dart
List<Actor> actors = await Actor().all();
// SELECT * FROM "actor"
```

### `find`

Returns one row, or `null` when there is no match.

```dart
// by primary key
Actor? actor = await Actor().find(1);
// SELECT * FROM "actor" WHERE "id" = @id_p0 LIMIT 1

// by another column
Actor? byName = await Actor().find('name', 'John Wick');
// SELECT * FROM "actor" WHERE "name" = @name_p0 LIMIT 1
```

### `getFirst`

Returns the first row of the query, or `null`.

```dart
Actor? actor = await Actor().where('age', '>', 60).orderBy('age').getFirst();
// SELECT * FROM "actor" WHERE "age" > @age_p0 ORDER BY "age" LIMIT 1
```

### `count`

Returns the number of rows as an `int`.

```dart
int total = await Actor().count();
int adults = await Actor().where('age', '>=', 18).count();
// SELECT count(*) as total FROM "actor" WHERE "age" >= @age_p0
```

- `count()` ignores `limit`, `offset` and `orderBy`.
- With `groupBy`, `count()` returns the number of groups.

### `paginate`

Returns one page of rows and the page info.
It runs a `count()` query and a `get()` query.

```dart
Pagination<Actor> page = await Actor()
    .where('age', '>=', 18)
    .paginate(currentPage: 2, perPage: 10);

List<Actor> actors = page.data;
print(page.total);    // rows that match
print(page.lastPage); // number of pages
```

`page.toJson()` gives `total`, `per_page`, `last_page`, `current_page` and `data`.
So you can return a `Pagination` from a controller.

## Where

### `where`

```dart
// equal
await Actor().where('name', 'John Wick').get();
// WHERE "name" = @name_p0

// other operator
await Actor().where('age', '>=', 23).get();
await Actor().where('name', '!=', 'John Wick').get();
await Actor().where('name', 'like', 'John%').get();

// null
await Actor().where('deleted_at', null).get();
// WHERE "deleted_at" IS NULL
```

Many `where` calls are joined with `AND`.

!!! warning
    The operator is written into the SQL as it is.
    Do not pass user input as the operator or as the column name.

### `orWhere`

```dart
await Actor().where('name', 'John Doe').orWhere('name', 'John Wick').get();
// WHERE "name" = @name_p0 OR "name" = @name_p1

await Actor().where('age', '<', 18).orWhere('age', '>', 60).get();
```

### `whereIn` and `whereNotIn`

```dart
await Actor().whereIn('id', <int>[1, 2]).get();
// WHERE "id" IN (@id_p0,@id_p1)

await Actor().whereNotIn('id', <int>[1, 2]).get();
await Actor().where('age', 60).orWhereIn('id', <int>[1, 2]).get();
await Actor().where('age', 60).orWhereNotIn('id', <int>[1, 2]).get();
```

- Each value is sent as a bound parameter.
- An empty list matches no rows for `whereIn`, and all rows for `whereNotIn`.

### `whereNull` and `whereNotNull`

```dart
await Actor().whereNull('deleted_at').get();
await Actor().whereNotNull('deleted_at').get();
await Actor().where('age', 60).orWhereNull('deleted_at').get();
await Actor().where('age', 60).orWhereNotNull('deleted_at').get();
```

### `whereRaw` and `orWhereRaw`

Write the condition yourself. Put values in a map, and use `@key` in the SQL.
The column names are not quoted.

```dart
await Actor().whereRaw('name = @name', <String, dynamic>{'name': 'John Wick'}).get();

await Actor()
    .where('age', 60)
    .orWhereRaw('lower(name) = @name', <String, dynamic>{'name': 'john wick'})
    .get();
```

!!! warning
    Never put user input into the SQL text. Always send it in the map.

## Select

`select` sets the columns. Each call replaces the columns of the call before.

```dart
// a list
await Actor().select(<String>['id', 'name']).get();
// SELECT "id","name" FROM "actor"

// comma separated
await Actor().select('id, name, age').get();

// with a function
await QueryBuilder.table('actor').select('count(*) as total, name').groupBy('name').get();
// SELECT count(*) as total,"name" FROM "actor" GROUP BY "name"

// raw: nothing is quoted
await Actor().selectRaw('DISTINCT name').get();
```

A part with `(` is kept as it is. Other parts are quoted.

!!! info
    A model loaded with `select()` only has the selected fields.
    `save()` on it only updates the fields it has.

## Order, limit and group

### `orderBy`

```dart
await Actor().orderBy('name').get();
await Actor().orderBy('name', 'desc').get();
await Actor().orderBy('name', 'asc').orderBy('id', 'desc').get();
// ORDER BY "name" asc,"id" desc
```

- The direction must be `asc` or `desc`. Any other value throws an `ArgumentError`.
- The column name is quoted, but a name with `(` is kept as it is.
  Do not pass user input as the column name.

### `limit`, `take` and `offset`

`limit` and `take` do the same thing.

```dart
await Actor().limit(10).get();
await Actor().take(10).get();
await Actor().limit(10).offset(20).get();
// LIMIT 10 OFFSET 20
```

### `groupBy`

Takes one column, or a list of columns.

```dart
List<Map<String, dynamic>> rows = await QueryBuilder.table('actor')
    .select('count(*) as total, age')
    .groupBy('age')
    .get();
```

!!! info
    Use `QueryBuilder.table()` for `groupBy`. A group row is a map, not a model.
    On a model, `get()` gives models (`List<Actor>`), so a `groupBy` there throws a `StateError`.
    `count()` with `groupBy` works on a model too.

## Join

```dart
await Actor().join('actor_info', 'actor_info.actor_id', 'actor.id').get();
// JOIN "actor_info" on "actor_info"."actor_id" = "actor"."id"

await Actor().leftJoin('actor_info', 'actor_info.actor_id', 'actor.id').get();
await Actor().rightJoin('actor_info', 'actor_info.actor_id', 'actor.id').get();

// with an operator
await Actor().join('actor_info', 'actor_info.actor_id', '=', 'actor.id').get();
```

For a join condition that these methods can not build, use the raw methods.
Nothing is quoted. Values go in the map, like in `whereRaw`.

```dart
await Actor().joinRaw('actor_info on actor_info.actor_id = actor.id').get();
await Actor().leftJoinRaw('actor_info on actor_info.actor_id = actor.id').get();
await Actor().rightJoinRaw(
  'actor_info on actor_info.actor_id = actor.id and actor_info.type = @type',
  <String, dynamic>{'type': 'main'},
).get();
```

!!! note
    SQLite before 3.39 has no `RIGHT JOIN`.

## Insert

### `create` and `insert`

`create` and `insert` do the same thing.
They insert one row, then read it back and return it.

```dart
Actor actor = await Actor().create(<String, dynamic>{
  'name': 'John Wick',
  'age': 60,
});
print(actor.id);
```

- On a model, the result is the model. On `QueryBuilder.table(...)`, the result is a map.
- It works with any primary key type, for example a uuid string.
- On a model with [events](model/events.md), `create` calls `save()`, so the hooks run.

### `insertMultiple`

Inserts many rows in one query.
It does not return models.
On Postgres it returns the new ids, like `[{id: 4}, {id: 5}]`.
On MySQL it returns only one id.

```dart
await Actor().insertMultiple(<Map<String, dynamic>>[
  <String, dynamic>{'name': 'John Wick', 'age': 60},
  <String, dynamic>{'name': 'John Doe', 'age': 25},
]);
```

The columns are the keys from all rows.
When a row does not have a key, that column gets its default value.

## Update

Updates all rows that match the `where` part.

```dart
await Actor()
    .where('id', 3)
    .where('status', 'active')
    .update(<String, dynamic>{'name': 'Updated AJ', 'age': 120});
// UPDATE "actor" SET "name" = @name_p2,"age" = @age_p3
//   WHERE "id" = @id_p0 AND "status" = @status_p1
```

!!! warning
    `update` without `where` changes every row of the table.
    A query `update` does not set `updated_at` and fires no [model events](model/events.md).
    To do that, load the model, change it and call `save()`.

## Delete

### `delete`

Deletes all rows that match the `where` part.

```dart
await Actor().where('name', 'John Wick').delete();
// DELETE FROM "actor" WHERE "name" = @name_p0
```

On a model with `softDelete: true`, `delete` sets `deleted_at` and keeps the row.

### `forceDelete`

On a model with `softDelete: true`, `forceDelete` really deletes the rows.
It also deletes rows that are already soft deleted, so you do not need `withTrash()`.

```dart
await Actor().where('name', 'John Wick').forceDelete();
```

### `withTrash`

A model with `softDelete: true` hides soft deleted rows.
`withTrash()` shows them too.
On a model without soft deletes it does nothing.

```dart
List<Actor> actors = await Actor().withTrash().where('name', 'John Wick').get();
```

### `truncate`

Deletes all rows of the table and resets the id counter.

```dart
await Actor().truncate();
await Actor().truncate(resetId: false); // keep the id counter on Postgres and SQLite
```

On Postgres it runs `TRUNCATE TABLE ... RESTART IDENTITY CASCADE`.
On SQLite it runs `DELETE FROM`.

## Debug

### `toSql`

Returns the SQL of the query with the values filled in.
The values are not quoted or escaped, so use it only to read the query.

```dart
String sql = Actor().where('name', 'John Wick').toSql();
print(sql); // SELECT * FROM "actor" WHERE "name" = John Wick
```

### `debug`

Prints the SQL and the values of the query when it runs.

```dart
await Actor().debug(true).where('age', 60).get();
```

To print all queries, set `debug: true` in the `ConnectionConfig`.
See [Database](index.md#config).


---

# Transactions

Source: https://dartondox.dev/latest/3.xdatabase/transactions/

# Transactions

A transaction runs many queries as one unit. Either all of them are saved, or none of them.

`QueryBuilder.transaction()` takes a function:

- It commits when the function ends.
- It rolls back when the function throws. Then the error is thrown again.

## Use

```dart
// a transaction
await QueryBuilder.transaction(() async {
  Actor actor = Actor();
  actor.name = 'John Wick';
  await actor.save();
  await QueryBuilder.table('actor_info').insert(<String, dynamic>{
    'actor_id': actor.id,
  });
});

// return a value
int? id = await QueryBuilder.transaction(() async {
  Actor actor = Actor();
  actor.name = 'John Wick';
  await actor.save();
  return actor.id;
});

// on another connection
await QueryBuilder.transaction(() async {
  // ...
}, connection: 'mysql');
```

- All queries and models inside the function use the transaction.
  You do not pass a transaction object around.
- A transaction inside another transaction joins the outer one.
  There are no savepoints. If the inner one throws, the whole outer transaction rolls back.

!!! warning "MySQL"
    On MySQL and MariaDB, `CREATE`, `ALTER` and `DROP TABLE` are saved right away.
    A rollback can not undo them.

## Connections

- Postgres and MySQL use a connection pool.
  Set the size with `maxConnectionCount` in the `extra` map of the connection.
- A transaction uses one connection of the pool. Other queries use the other connections.
- SQLite has one connection per isolate.
  While a transaction is open, the other queries of that isolate wait.
- Values are always sent as bound parameters. They are never written into the SQL text.

!!! note "Changed in 3.x"
    Before 3.x, Postgres ran every query in its own transaction.
    Now a query only runs in a transaction when you use `QueryBuilder.transaction()`.


---

# Migration

Source: https://dartondox.dev/latest/3.xdatabase/migration/

# Migration

A migration changes your database schema step by step: create a table, add a column, and so on.
Each migration has an `up` method (make the change) and a `down` method (undo it).

Write migrations in Dart with the [schema builder](schema.md).
The same migration then works on Postgres, MySQL, MariaDB and SQLite.
Plain `.sql` migrations still work too.

## Create a migration

```bash
dox make:migration create_users_table
```

This makes `db/migration/2026_10_21_120000_create_users_table.dart`.
The numbers are the date and time when you run the command.

```dart title="db/migration/2026_10_21_120000_create_users_table.dart"
import 'package:dox_migration/dox_migration.dart';

class CreateUsersTable extends Migration {
  @override
  Future<void> up(Schema schema) async {
    await schema.create('users', (Table table) {
      table.id();
      table.timestamps();
    });
  }

  @override
  Future<void> down(Schema schema) async {
    await schema.dropIfExists('users');
  }
}
```

Add your columns in `up`, for example `table.string('email').unique();`.
See [Schema](schema.md) for all column types.

The name of the migration decides what the new file contains:

| Name | The file has |
|---|---|
| `create_users_table` | `schema.create('users', ...)` in `up`, and `dropIfExists('users')` in `down` |
| `add_avatar_to_users_table` (also `_from_`, `_in_`, `_on_`) | `schema.table('users', ...)` in `up` and `down` |
| any other name | empty `up` and `down` |

- `create:migration` is the old name of the same command.
- `dox create:model Blog -m` makes the model and a `create_blogs_table` migration.

!!! info "Raw SQL and data in a Dart migration"
    `schema.driver` runs raw SQL on the same connection and transaction:
    `await schema.driver.execute("UPDATE users SET role = 'admin' WHERE id = 1");`
    Do not use models or `QueryBuilder` in a migration. They use another connection.

## The registry

Dart can not load a file at run time in an AOT build.
So Dox keeps a list of your Dart migrations in `db/migration/migrations.dart`:

```dart
// Made by `dox make:migration` and the `dox migration:*` commands.
import 'package:dox_migration/dox_migration.dart';

import '2026_10_21_120000_create_users_table.dart' as m1;

final List<MigrationEntry> migrations = <MigrationEntry>[
  MigrationEntry(
    '2026_10_21_120000_create_users_table',
    m1.CreateUsersTable(),
  ),
];
```

- `dox make:migration` and every `dox migration:*` command write this file again.
  You do not edit it.
- It finds each file named `YYYY_MM_DD_HHMMSS_name.dart` and its `class ... extends Migration`.
- The name of a migration is its file name without `.dart`. The order is by name.

The first `dox make:migration` also makes `bin/migrate.dart` in your app:

```dart
import 'dart:io';

import 'package:dox_migration/dox_migration.dart';

import '../db/migration/migrations.dart';

Future<void> main(List<String> args) async {
  exitCode = await Migrator(migrations: migrations).run(args);
}
```

The `dox migration:*` commands run `dart run bin/migrate.dart <command>`.
So your migrations run as part of your app code.

## Run migrations

| Command | What it does |
|---|---|
| `dox migration:run` | Run the migrations that did not run yet. Short name: `dox migrate`. |
| `dox migration:rollback` | Undo the last batch. |
| `dox migration:rollback --step=2` | Undo the last 2 migrations, even across batches. |
| `dox migration:reset` | Undo all migrations. |
| `dox migration:refresh` | Undo all migrations, then run them again. |
| `dox migration:status` | Show each migration, its batch, and if it ran. |

`migrate:rollback`, `migrate:reset`, `migrate:refresh` and `migrate:status` are short names.

A batch is the group of migrations that ran in one `migration:run`.
Migrations are undone newest first.
The ran migrations are saved in the `dox_db_migration` table.

When a migration fails, the error shows its name, and the command exits with code `1`.
The failed migration is not saved, and the later ones do not run.

You can also run `dart run bin/migrate.dart run` (or `rollback --step=2`, `reset`, `refresh`, `status`) yourself.

### Run on server start

The AOT server binary can run the migrations, because the registry is compiled in.
The new app template already does this:

```dart title="bin/server.dart"
import 'package:dox_app/config/app.dart';
import 'package:dox_core/dox_core.dart';
import 'package:dox_migration/dox_migration.dart';

import '../db/migration/migrations.dart';

void main() async {
  Dox().initialize(appConfig);
  await Migrator(migrations: migrations).migrate();
  await Dox().startServer();
}
```

Keep the `db/migration` folder next to the binary if you also have `.sql` migrations.

## Database settings

The migrations read the `.env` file and the environment variables.
A real environment variable wins over `.env`, the same as `Env.get()`.

When `DATABASE_URL` is set, it wins over all `DB_*` keys. See [`DATABASE_URL`](index.md#database_url).

```bash title=".env"
DB_CONNECTION=postgres # or mysql (also MariaDB), or sqlite
DB_HOST=localhost
DB_PORT=5432
DB_NAME=postgres
DB_USERNAME=admin
DB_PASSWORD=password
```

For SQLite, only two variables are needed:

```bash title=".env"
DB_CONNECTION=sqlite
DB_NAME=storage/app.db # file path, made if missing
```

- `DB_DATABASE` works too, in place of `DB_NAME`.
- The default port is `5432` for Postgres and `3306` for MySQL.
- One run uses one database connection.
- A `DB_HOST` that starts with `/` is a Postgres Unix socket folder, like `/cloudsql/project:region:instance`.
- Migrations use TLS only with a `DATABASE_URL` that has `sslmode` (Postgres) or `ssl` (MySQL), like `?sslmode=require`.
  You can also give your own connection: `Migrator(migrations: migrations, connection: myPool)`.

## Transactions

Each migration runs in one transaction.
On Postgres and SQLite, a failed migration undoes all its changes.

!!! warning "MySQL"
    On MySQL and MariaDB, `CREATE`, `ALTER` and `DROP` save right away.
    So if a migration fails half way, these changes stay. Only data changes are undone.
    Keep each MySQL migration small: one table change per migration.

To run a migration without a transaction (for example `CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY` on Postgres):

```dart
class AddSearchIndex extends Migration {
  @override
  bool get withinTransaction => false;

  @override
  Future<void> up(Schema schema) async {
    await schema.driver.execute(
      'CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY posts_title_index ON posts (title)',
    );
  }

  @override
  Future<void> down(Schema schema) async {
    await schema.driver.execute('DROP INDEX CONCURRENTLY posts_title_index');
  }
}
```

!!! info "SQLite foreign keys"
    On SQLite, foreign key checks are off while a migration runs.
    This lets Dox make a table again (see [SQLite notes](schema.md#sqlite-notes)).
    Before the end, Dox checks all foreign keys. The migration fails if one is broken.

## SQL migrations

A `.sql` migration is still fine. Use it for SQL that only one database understands.

```bash
dox make:migration create_blog_table --sql
```

```sql
-- up
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS blog (
    id serial PRIMARY KEY,
    title VARCHAR(255) NOT NULL
);

-- down
DROP TABLE IF EXISTS blog
```

- Put the `up` SQL under a line `-- up`, and the `down` SQL under a line `-- down`.
  Each of these lines must be on its own line. Other `--` lines are normal SQL comments.
- Statements are split on `;`.
  A `;` inside quotes, comments or a postgres `$$ ... $$` body does not split.

!!! warning "SQLite ids"
    In SQLite, `id serial PRIMARY KEY` does not make an auto increment id. The id stays `NULL`.
    Use `id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT` for SQLite. `table.id()` in Dart does this for you.

### Dart and SQL in one folder

Both kinds can live in `db/migration`. They run in file name order (the timestamp).

- With `bin/migrate.dart`: the Migrator runs the Dart migrations from the registry
  and reads the `.sql` files from the folder, merged by name.
- Without `bin/migrate.dart` (a project with only `.sql` files): `dox` runs the `.sql` files itself, like before.
- A Dart and a `.sql` migration with the same name is an error.


---

# Schema builder

Source: https://dartondox.dev/latest/3.xdatabase/schema/

# Schema builder

The schema builder creates, changes and drops tables with Dart code.
The same code works on Postgres, MySQL, MariaDB and SQLite.
You mostly use it inside a [migration](migration.md).

```dart
await schema.create('posts', (Table table) {
  table.id();
  table.foreignId('user_id').constrained().cascadeOnDelete();
  table.string('title');
  table.text('body').nullable();
  table.enumeration('status', <String>['draft', 'published']).defaultTo('draft');
  table.timestamps();
});
```

## Get a schema

In a migration, `up` and `down` get a `Schema`. It runs on the migration connection.

Outside a migration, `Schema()` uses the query builder connection.
You can also give a driver: `Schema(driver)`.

```dart
Schema schema = Schema();
await schema.dropIfExists('posts');
```

## Tables

| Method | What it does |
|---|---|
| `create('t', (Table table) {...})` | Create table `t`. It fails when the table exists. |
| `table('t', (Table table) {...})` | Change table `t`: add columns, change columns, keys. |
| `drop('t')` | Drop table `t`. It fails when the table is missing. |
| `dropIfExists('t')` | Drop table `t` when it exists. |
| `rename('from', 'to')` | Rename a table. |
| `hasTable('t')` | `true` when the table exists. |
| `hasColumn('t', 'c')` | `true` when the column exists. |
| `getColumnListing('t')` | The column names, in order. |

## Column types

| Method | Postgres | MySQL / MariaDB | SQLite |
|---|---|---|---|
| `id()` / `bigIncrements('id')` | `BIGSERIAL PRIMARY KEY` | `BIGINT UNSIGNED AUTO_INCREMENT PRIMARY KEY` | `INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT` |
| `increments('id')` | `SERIAL PRIMARY KEY` | `INT UNSIGNED AUTO_INCREMENT PRIMARY KEY` | `INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT` |
| `string('c', [255])` | `VARCHAR(n)` | `VARCHAR(n)` | `VARCHAR(n)` |
| `char('c', [255])` | `CHAR(n)` | `CHAR(n)` | `CHAR(n)` |
| `text('c')` | `TEXT` | `TEXT` | `TEXT` |
| `mediumText('c')` | `TEXT` | `MEDIUMTEXT` | `TEXT` |
| `longText('c')` | `TEXT` | `LONGTEXT` | `TEXT` |
| `integer('c')` | `INTEGER` | `INT` | `INTEGER` |
| `bigInteger('c')` | `BIGINT` | `BIGINT` | `INTEGER` |
| `smallInteger('c')` | `SMALLINT` | `SMALLINT` | `INTEGER` |
| `tinyInteger('c')` | `SMALLINT` | `TINYINT` | `INTEGER` |
| `unsignedInteger('c')` (and `unsignedBigInteger`, `unsignedSmallInteger`, `unsignedTinyInteger`) | signed type | `... UNSIGNED` | `INTEGER` |
| `float('c')` | `REAL` | `FLOAT` | `FLOAT` |
| `double('c')` | `DOUBLE PRECISION` | `DOUBLE` | `DOUBLE` |
| `decimal('c', [8], [2])` | `DECIMAL(p, s)` | `DECIMAL(p, s)` | `DECIMAL(p, s)` |
| `boolean('c')` | `BOOLEAN` | `TINYINT(1)` | `BOOLEAN` |
| `date('c')` | `DATE` | `DATE` | `DATE` |
| `dateTime('c')` | `TIMESTAMP` | `DATETIME` | `DATETIME` |
| `dateTimeTz('c')` | `TIMESTAMPTZ` | `DATETIME` | `DATETIME` |
| `time('c')` | `TIME` | `TIME` | `TIME` |
| `timestamp('c')` | `TIMESTAMP` | `TIMESTAMP` | `TIMESTAMP` |
| `timestampTz('c')` | `TIMESTAMPTZ` | `TIMESTAMP` | `TIMESTAMP` |
| `json('c')` / `jsonb('c')` | `JSONB` | `JSON` | `JSON` |
| `uuid(['uuid'])` | `UUID` | `CHAR(36)` | `TEXT` |
| `binary('c')` | `BYTEA` | `BLOB` | `BLOB` |
| `enumeration('c', ['a', 'b'])` | `VARCHAR(255)` + `CHECK` | `ENUM('a', 'b')` | `VARCHAR(255)` + `CHECK` |
| `foreignId('user_id')` | `BIGINT` | `BIGINT UNSIGNED` | `INTEGER` |
| `foreignUuid('user_id')` | `UUID` | `CHAR(36)` | `TEXT` |

Helpers:

- `timestamps()`: nullable `created_at` and `updated_at` (`timestampTz`).
- `softDeletes(['deleted_at'])`: nullable `deleted_at` (`timestampTz`), for models with `softDelete: true`.
- `rememberToken()`: nullable `remember_token` `VARCHAR(100)`.
- `morphs('owner')`: `owner_id` (unsigned big integer), `owner_type` (string) and one index on both columns.

!!! info "JSON on SQLite"
    SQLite has no JSON type. The column is declared as `JSON`,
    so the SQLite driver knows to decode it when you read it.

## Modifiers

Modifiers come after the column type. They can be chained:
`table.string('email').nullable().unique()`.

| Modifier | What it does | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `nullable()` | Allow `NULL`. Columns are `NOT NULL` by default. | `nullable(false)` makes it `NOT NULL` again. |
| `defaultTo(value)` | Default value. Strings are escaped, so any text is safe. | `bool`, numbers, `null`, `Map`/`List` (saved as JSON) and `DateTime` work too. `withDefault` is the old name. |
| `defaultRaw('sql')` | Default as raw SQL. It is **not** escaped. | Put expressions in `( )`: `defaultRaw('(1 + 1)')`. MySQL and SQLite need it. |
| `useCurrent()` | Default to the current time. | Same as `defaultRaw('CURRENT_TIMESTAMP')`. |
| `useCurrentOnUpdate()` | Set the current time on each update. | MySQL only. Postgres and SQLite ignore it. Set the time in your code there. |
| `unique()` | Add a unique index `{table}_{column}_unique`. | |
| `index()` | Add an index `{table}_{column}_index`. | |
| `primary()` | Make the column the primary key. | |
| `unsigned()` | `UNSIGNED`. | MySQL only. Others ignore it. |
| `comment('text')` | Column comment. | Postgres and MySQL. SQLite ignores it. |
| `after('column')` | Put the new column after another one. | MySQL only, only in `schema.table`. Others add it at the end. |
| `change()` | Change an existing column (in `schema.table`). | See [Change columns](#change-columns). |

!!! info "MySQL defaults on TEXT and JSON"
    MySQL only allows a default on `TEXT`, `BLOB` and `JSON` as an expression.
    The schema builder writes it as `DEFAULT ('value')` for you.

## Change a table

```dart
await schema.table('users', (Table table) {
  table.string('avatar').nullable().after('email'); // add
  table.string('name', 100).nullable().change();    // change
  table.renameColumn('bio', 'about');
  table.dropColumn('age');
  table.dropColumns(<String>['a', 'b']);
});
```

A column in `schema.table` is **added**. Add `.change()` to change a column that exists.

### Change columns

`change()` sets the full new column: type, null, default and comment.
Give every modifier you want to keep.

```dart
// before: string('title') NOT NULL DEFAULT 'x'
table.string('title', 500).nullable().defaultTo('x').change();
```

How it runs:

| Driver | SQL |
|---|---|
| Postgres | One `ALTER TABLE`: `ALTER COLUMN ... TYPE ... USING col::type`, `SET/DROP NOT NULL`, `SET/DROP DEFAULT`, and the enum `CHECK` again. |
| MySQL | `ALTER TABLE ... MODIFY COLUMN <full column>`. |
| SQLite | SQLite can not change a column. Dox makes the table again (see below). |

`change()` with `unique()` or `index()` adds the index. It fails when the index already exists.

## Indexes and keys

`columns` is a column name or a list of names.

```dart
table.index(<String>['state', 'created_at']);  // posts_state_created_at_index
table.unique('slug');                          // posts_slug_unique
table.primary(<String>['post_id', 'tag_id']);  // composite primary key

table.dropIndex(<String>['state', 'created_at']); // by columns
table.dropUnique('posts_slug_unique');            // or by name
```

Index names are `{table}_{columns}_{index|unique|foreign}`.
You can give your own name as the last argument: `table.unique('slug', 'my_name')`.

### Foreign keys

```dart
table.foreignId('user_id').constrained().cascadeOnDelete();
// same as:
table.foreignId('user_id');
table.foreign('user_id').references('id').on('users').onDelete('cascade');
```

- `constrained([table], [column = 'id'])` guesses the table from the column:
  `user_id` becomes `users`, `category_id` becomes `categories`.
  Dox models use singular table names by default (`User` is `user`).
  If your table is singular, give it: `constrained('user')`.
- Actions: `onDelete('cascade' | 'set null' | 'restrict' | 'no action')`, `onUpdate(...)`,
  and the short ones `cascadeOnDelete()`, `nullOnDelete()`, `restrictOnDelete()`, `cascadeOnUpdate()`.
- Put `nullable()` before `constrained()`: `table.foreignId('editor_id').nullable().constrained('users')`.
- Drop it: `table.dropForeign(<String>['user_id'])` or `table.dropForeign('posts_user_id_foreign')`.

!!! warning "Same type on both sides"
    `id()` is a big integer. `foreignId()` is a big integer too, so they match.
    If the parent uses `increments()` (a normal integer), use `unsignedInteger()` for the child on MySQL.

## SQLite notes

SQLite `ALTER TABLE` can only add, rename and drop columns.
For these changes, Dox makes the table again:

- `change()` of a column,
- `foreign(...)` on an existing table,
- `dropForeign(...)`.

It makes a new table with the change, copies the rows, drops the old table and renames the new one.
It keeps the columns, primary key, `AUTOINCREMENT`, foreign keys, indexes and enum checks.
All of it runs in one transaction.
It fails on tables with other `CHECK` constraints or with generated columns.

Other SQLite limits:

- `primary(...)` on an existing table is not supported.
- A new column that is `NOT NULL` needs a default. A new column can not default to `CURRENT_TIMESTAMP`.
- `dropColumn` fails when the column is in an index or a foreign key. Drop those first.

## Per driver notes

| Feature | Postgres | MySQL / MariaDB | SQLite |
|---|---|---|---|
| `enumeration` | `CHECK (col IN (...))` | `ENUM(...)` | `CHECK (col IN (...))` |
| `unsigned` | ignored | `UNSIGNED` | ignored |
| `comment` | `COMMENT ON COLUMN` | inline `COMMENT` | ignored |
| `after` | ignored | `AFTER col` | ignored |
| `useCurrentOnUpdate` | ignored | `ON UPDATE CURRENT_TIMESTAMP` | ignored |
| `change()` | `ALTER COLUMN` | `MODIFY COLUMN` | table rebuild |
| add/drop foreign key on a table | `ALTER TABLE` | `ALTER TABLE` | table rebuild |
| schema changes in a transaction | yes | no, saved right away | yes |
| index name length | 63 | 64 | no limit |

## See the SQL

Every change is a `Table` blueprint. A grammar turns it into SQL, without a database:

```dart
Table table = Table('users', creating: true)
  ..id()
  ..string('email').unique();
print(table.toSql(PostgresGrammar()));
// [CREATE TABLE "users" ("id" BIGSERIAL NOT NULL PRIMARY KEY, "email" VARCHAR(255) NOT NULL),
//  CREATE UNIQUE INDEX "users_email_unique" ON "users" ("email")]
```

Grammars: `PostgresGrammar`, `MysqlGrammar` and `SqliteGrammar`.
On SQLite, the changes that need a table rebuild only run on a database.


---

# Native Postgres driver

Source: https://dartondox.dev/latest/3.xdatabase/postgres-native/

# Native Postgres driver

`dox_postgres_native` is the default Postgres driver of the Dox ORM.
Rust talks to the database. Your models, queries and transactions stay the
same. You do not change any config.

- Rust ([tokio-postgres](https://docs.rs/tokio-postgres)) owns the
  connections and the pool.
- Dart sends many queries to Rust in one call. Rust sends many results back
  in one message.
- Each connection keeps its prepared statements. The same SQL is not parsed
  again.
- Values have the same Dart types as with the `postgres` package. Errors
  are the same `ServerException` classes.

!!! warning "Alpha"
    This driver is new. If you see a problem, [use the Dart driver](#use-the-dart-driver)
    and tell us.

## Speed

One find-by-id query (`SELECT ... WHERE id = @id`), AOT build
(`dart build cli`), Postgres 14 on the same machine (Apple M-series),
4 connections:

| | Dart driver | Native driver |
|---|---|---|
| One query at a time | 95 µs | 60 µs |
| 64 queries in flight, one isolate | 45 µs per query | 12.5 µs per query |
| 4 isolates, 64 in flight each, 16 connections per pool | 39,500 queries/s | 64,000 queries/s |

The gain is biggest when many requests run at the same time, like in a web
server.

## Install

`dox_orm` depends on `dox_postgres_native`. You do not add it yourself.
Add it only to use `PgNativePool` without the ORM:

```bash
dart pub add dox_postgres_native
```

The build hook builds the Rust library with `cargo`, so you need
[Rust](https://rustup.rs) installed. Ready-built libraries (like the ones
`dox_http_native` has) are not published for this driver yet.
Without Rust, the ORM still works: it uses the Dart driver and prints one
warning line (see below).

Use `dart run`, `dart test` or `dart build cli`. `dart compile exe` does not
run build hooks.

## Native is the default

You do not change any config. The ORM picks the driver like this:

1. `driverFactory` is set: the ORM uses your driver. It wins over
   everything below.
2. You ask for the Dart driver (see below), or the connection uses TLS:
   the ORM uses the Dart driver.
3. The native library loads: the ORM uses the native driver.
4. The native library does not load (no library for your system, no
   Rust to build it, or a load error): the ORM uses the Dart driver. It
   prints one warning line to stderr, like this:

```text
[dox] warning: dox_postgres_native did not load, using the Dart postgres driver (...)
```

Named connections (`withConnection('x')`, `transaction(..., connection: 'x')`) follow
the same rules.

## Use the Dart driver

For all connections, set the env var:

```bash
DOX_DB_DRIVER=dart dart run bin/server.dart
```

For one connection, set `native: false` in `extra`:

```dart
ConnectionConfig(
  driver: Driver.postgres,
  // ... host, user, password, database as before
  extra: <String, dynamic>{'native': false},
  debug: false,
),
```

Postgres with TLS (`useSSL: true` or `extra['sslMode']`) always uses the
Dart driver, because the native driver has no TLS yet.

## Options

The driver reads these keys from `extra` of the `ConnectionConfig`:

| Key | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `maxConnectionCount` | `10` | Most connections in the pool. |
| `timeZone` | `UTC` | Time zone of the session, like the Dart driver. |
| `applicationName` | none | Name of the app in `pg_stat_activity`. |
| `threads` | `1` | Rust threads for all pools of the process. `0` is one thread with a single-thread runtime. Only the first pool sets it. |

Each isolate that runs `setup()` makes its own pool. To share one pool
between isolates, give `driver.pool.handle` (an `int`) to the other
isolates and use `PostgresNativeDriver(PgNativePool.fromHandle(handle))`
there. `PostgresNativeDriver` comes from `package:dox_orm/dox_orm.dart`.

## Use it without the ORM

```dart
PgNativePool pool = PgNativePool.open(
  host: 'localhost',
  user: 'postgres',
  password: 'postgres',
  database: 'postgres',
);

PgNativeResult result = await pool.query(
  'SELECT id, name FROM users WHERE id = @id',
  parameters: <String, dynamic>{'id': 1},
);
print(result.rows); // [{id: 1, name: Ada}]

int tx = await pool.begin();
await pool.query('UPDATE users SET name = @n', parameters: <String, dynamic>{'n': 'Bob'}, transaction: tx);
await pool.commit(tx); // or pool.rollback(tx)
```

- `parameters` is a map for `@name`, or a list for `$1, $2`.
- A transaction runs on one connection. Its queries run in the order you
  send them.

## Types

The same as the `postgres` package:

| Postgres | Dart |
|---|---|
| `int2`, `int4`, `int8` | `int` |
| `float4`, `float8` | `double` |
| `numeric` | `String` |
| `text`, `varchar`, `char` | `String` |
| `bool` | `bool` |
| `timestamp`, `timestamptz`, `date` | `DateTime` in UTC |
| `json`, `jsonb` | the decoded JSON value |
| `uuid` | `String` |
| `bytea` | `Uint8List` |
| arrays of most types above | `List` |
| `NULL` | `null` |

Other types decode with the type registry of the `postgres` package.

## Errors

A server error throws the same exception as the Dart driver:
`ServerException`, or `UniqueViolationException` and
`ForeignKeyViolationException`, with the same `code`, `detail`,
`constraintName` and other fields. Other errors (eg. the server is down)
throw `PgException`.

## Not yet

- SSL. A connection with `useSSL: true` uses the Dart driver.
- `maxConnectionAge`, `queryTimeout` and the other `extra` keys of the Dart
  driver are not read.
- A nested `transaction()` joins the outer one, like the Dart driver
  (no savepoints).


---

# Native MySQL driver

Source: https://dartondox.dev/latest/3.xdatabase/mysql-native/

# Native MySQL driver

`dox_mysql_native` is the default MySQL and MariaDB driver of the Dox ORM.
Rust talks to the database. Your models, queries and transactions stay the
same. You do not change any config.

- Rust ([mysql_async](https://docs.rs/mysql_async)) owns the connections
  and the pool.
- Dart sends many queries to Rust in one call. Rust sends many results back
  in one message.
- Each connection keeps its prepared statements. The same SQL is not
  prepared again.
- Values have the same Dart types as with the Dart driver (`mysql_dart`).
  Errors are the same `MySQLServerException` class.
- Works with MySQL 8.4 (the default `caching_sha2_password` login) and
  MariaDB 11.

!!! warning "Alpha"
    This driver is new. If you see a problem, [use the Dart driver](#use-the-dart-driver)
    and tell us.

## Speed

One find-by-id query (`SELECT * FROM t WHERE id = @id`), AOT build
(`dart build cli`), database on the same machine (Apple M-series),
10 connections, one isolate:

| | Dart driver | Native driver |
|---|---|---|
| MySQL 8.4, one query at a time | 61 µs | 67 µs |
| MySQL 8.4, 32 queries in flight | 25 µs per query | 11 µs per query |
| MySQL 8.4, CPU time of the app per query | 32 µs | 13.5 µs |
| MariaDB 11, one query at a time | 59 µs | 63 µs |
| MariaDB 11, 32 queries in flight | 25.5 µs per query | 9.7 µs per query |
| MariaDB 11, CPU time of the app per query | 32.5 µs | 12.4 µs |

The CPU time counts the Dart thread and the Rust thread. It is the limit
on one CPU core: about 31,000 queries per second with the Dart driver and
about 75,000 with the native driver.

One query at a time is about the same speed: most of the time is the trip
to the database. The gain is big when many requests run at the same time,
like in a web server.

## Install

`dox_orm` depends on `dox_mysql_native`. You do not add it yourself.
Add it only to use `MysqlNativePool` without the ORM:

```bash
dart pub add dox_mysql_native
```

The build hook builds the Rust library with `cargo`, so you need
[Rust](https://rustup.rs) installed. Ready-built libraries (like the ones
`dox_http_native` has) are not published for this driver yet.
Without Rust, the ORM still works: it uses the Dart driver and prints one
warning line (see below).

Use `dart run`, `dart test` or `dart build cli`. `dart compile exe` does not
run build hooks.

## Native is the default

You do not change any config. The ORM picks the driver like this:

1. `driverFactory` is set: the ORM uses your driver. It wins over
   everything below.
2. You ask for the Dart driver (see below): the ORM uses the Dart driver.
3. The native library loads: the ORM uses the native driver.
4. The native library does not load (no library for your system, no
   Rust to build it, or a load error): the ORM uses the Dart driver. It
   prints one warning line to stderr, like this:

```text
[dox] warning: dox_mysql_native did not load, using the Dart mysql driver (...)
```

Named connections (`withConnection('x')`, `transaction(..., connection: 'x')`) follow
the same rules.

## Use the Dart driver

For all connections, set the env var:

```bash
DOX_DB_DRIVER=dart dart run bin/server.dart
```

For one connection, set `native: false` in `extra`:

```dart
ConnectionConfig(
  driver: Driver.mysql,
  // ... host, user, password, database as before
  extra: <String, dynamic>{'native': false},
  debug: false,
),
```

## Options

The driver reads the normal fields of the `ConnectionConfig` (`host`,
`port`, `user`, `password`, `database`, `useSSL`) and these keys from
`extra`:

| Key | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `maxConnectionCount` | `10` | Most connections in the pool. |
| `maxConnectionAge` | 12 hours | A connection older than this is closed and opened again. |
| `preparedStatementCacheSize` | `100` | Prepared statements kept per connection. |
| `threads` | `1` | Rust threads for all pools of the process. Only the first pool sets it. One thread is the fastest for most apps. |

Isolates that open a pool with the same settings share one pool in Rust.
So `maxConnectionCount` is for the whole process, not per isolate. You can
also give `driver.pool.handle` (an `int`) to another isolate and use
`MysqlNativeDriver(MysqlNativePool.fromHandle(handle))` there.
`MysqlNativeDriver` comes from `package:dox_orm/dox_orm.dart`.

## Use it without the ORM

```dart
MysqlNativePool pool = MysqlNativePool.open(
  host: 'localhost',
  user: 'root',
  password: 'password',
  database: 'app',
);

MysqlNativeResult result = await pool.query(
  'SELECT id, name FROM users WHERE id = ?',
  parameters: <Object?>[1],
);
print(result.rows); // [{id: 1, name: Ada}]

MysqlNativeResult insert = await pool.query(
  'INSERT INTO users (name) VALUES (@name)',
  parameters: <String, dynamic>{'name': 'Bob'},
);
print(insert.insertId); // the new AUTO_INCREMENT id
print(insert.affectedRows); // 1

int tx = await pool.begin();
await pool.execute('UPDATE users SET name = ?', parameters: <Object?>['Cy'], transaction: tx);
await pool.commit(tx); // or pool.rollback(tx)
```

- `parameters` is a list for `?`, or a map for `@name`.
- `execute` is like `query`, but the rows are not sent back to Dart.
- A transaction runs on one connection. Its queries run in the order you
  send them.

## Types

The same as the Dox ORM on the Dart driver:

| MySQL / MariaDB | Dart |
|---|---|
| `TINYINT(1)` (`boolean()`) | `bool` |
| `TINYINT`, `SMALLINT`, `INT`, `BIGINT`, `YEAR` | `int` |
| `FLOAT`, `DOUBLE`, `DECIMAL` | `double` |
| `CHAR`, `VARCHAR`, `TEXT`, `ENUM` | `String` |
| `DATE`, `DATETIME`, `TIMESTAMP` | `DateTime` in UTC |
| `TIME` | `String`, like `12:34:56` |
| `JSON` | the decoded JSON value |
| `BLOB`, `BINARY`, `VARBINARY` | `Uint8List` |
| `NULL` | `null` |

MariaDB keeps `JSON` columns as `LONGTEXT`. So on MariaDB, `TEXT` that is a
JSON object or array comes back decoded. The Dart driver does the same.

## Errors

A server error throws the same exception as the Dart driver:
`MySQLServerException`, with the same `errorCode` (eg. `1062` for a
duplicate key) and `message`. Other errors (eg. the server is down) throw
`MySQLClientException`.

## Not yet

- The `timeZone`, `collation`, `serverPublicKey` and `timeoutMs` keys of the
  Dart driver are not read. The connection uses `utf8mb4`.
- A login with `sha256_password` (not the default) does not work. The
  default `caching_sha2_password` and `mysql_native_password` work.
- A nested `transaction()` joins the outer one, like the Dart driver
  (no savepoints).


---

# Model

Source: https://dartondox.dev/latest/3.xdatabase/model/

# Model

A model is a Dart class for one database table.
You read, create, change and delete rows through the model.
A model has all the [query builder](../query-builder.md) methods too.

## Create a model

```bash
dox create:model Blog      # only the model
dox create:model Blog -m   # the model and a migration for the table `blogs`
```

This makes `lib/app/models/blog/blog.model.dart`.
`make:model` is another name for the same command.

The model code uses a generated class (`BlogGenerator`).
Run the generator after you make or change a model:

```bash
dart run build_runner build
```

`dart run build_runner watch` runs the generator again each time you save a file.

## A model

```dart title="lib/app/models/blog/blog.model.dart"
import 'package:dox_orm/dox_orm.dart';

part 'blog.model.g.dart'; // (1)!

@DoxModel() // (2)!
class Blog extends BlogGenerator { // (3)!
  @Column() // (4)!
  String? title;

  @Column(beforeSave: makeSlug) // (5)!
  String? slug;

  @Column()
  String? status;

  @Column(name: 'body') // (6)!
  String? description;

  @Column(name: 'user_id')
  int? userId;

  static String? makeSlug(Map<String, dynamic> map) {
    return map['title']?.toString().toLowerCase().replaceAll(' ', '-');
  }
}
```

1.  `build_runner` writes this file. It holds the generated `BlogGenerator` class.
2.  Marks the class as a model. The options, like `table` and `softDelete`, go here.
    The table is `blog` by default: the class name in snake_case.
3.  The generated class gives the model `id`, `createdAt` and `updatedAt`, and the query builder methods.
4.  One `@Column()` field is one table column. The column name is the field name in snake_case.
5.  `beforeSave` runs this static function before a save. It gets all values and returns the value for this column.
6.  `name` sets the column name when it is not the snake_case of the field. `description` reads and writes `body`.

- The model gets an `id` field, and `createdAt` and `updatedAt` fields. You do not declare them.
- Each `@Column()` field is one table column.
- Make every column field nullable (`String?`, `int?`). A new model has no values yet.

## Model options

All options go in `@DoxModel(...)`.

| Option | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `table` | class name in snake_case | The table name. |
| `primaryKey` | `'id'` | The primary key column. |
| `primaryKeyType` | `int` | The Dart type of the primary key, like `String` for a UUID. |
| `createdAt` | `'created_at'` | The column that keeps the create time. |
| `updatedAt` | `'updated_at'` | The column that keeps the last update time. |
| `timestamps` | `true` | `false` turns off `createdAt` and `updatedAt`. |
| `softDelete` | `false` | `delete()` sets `deleted_at` and keeps the row. |

### `table`

The default table name is the class name in snake_case, and singular.
`Blog` uses `blog`, and `BlogPost` uses `blog_post`.

```dart
@DoxModel(table: 'blogs')
class Blog extends BlogGenerator {}
```

!!! info
    `dox create:model Blog -m` sets `table: 'blogs'` for you,
    because the migration makes the plural table `blogs`.

### `primaryKey`

```dart
@DoxModel(primaryKey: 'uid')
class Blog extends BlogGenerator {}
```

The field name is the key in camelCase. With `primaryKey: 'blog_id'`, the field is `blogId`.

### `primaryKeyType`

The primary key field is `int?` by default.
Use `primaryKeyType` for another type, like a UUID string.

```dart
@DoxModel(primaryKey: 'uuid', primaryKeyType: String)
class Device extends DeviceGenerator {}
```

```dart
Device device = Device();
device.uuid = '0b6f2c1e-1a2b-4c3d-8e9f-001122334455';
await device.save(); // insert
```

`save()` inserts a new model, also when you set the key yourself.
It updates a model that was read from the table or saved before.
`model.exists` tells which one it is.

### `createdAt` and `updatedAt`

`save()` sets these columns to the current UTC time.
Use the options when your columns have other names.

```dart
@DoxModel(createdAt: 'created', updatedAt: 'modified')
class Blog extends BlogGenerator {}
```

Read the values with `blog.createdAt` and `blog.updatedAt`.

### `timestamps`

Set `timestamps: false` when the table has no `created_at` and `updated_at` columns.

```dart
@DoxModel(timestamps: false)
class Setting extends SettingGenerator {}
```

To turn off only one of them, set it to `null`, like `@DoxModel(updatedAt: null)`.

### `softDelete`

```dart
@DoxModel(softDelete: true)
class Blog extends BlogGenerator {}
```

The table needs a nullable `deleted_at` column. In a migration, add `table.softDeletes();`.

- `delete()` sets `deleted_at` to the current time. The row stays in the table.
- Queries do not return soft deleted rows. Use `withTrash()` to get them too.
- `forceDelete()` really deletes the row.
- `restore()` sets `deleted_at` back to `NULL`.

## Columns

### Column name

The default column name is the field name in snake_case.
Use `name` when the column has another name.

```dart
@Column()
String? userId; // column: user_id

@Column(name: 'body')
String? description; // column: body
```

### Field types

The field type tells Dox how to read the value.

| Field type | Column |
|---|---|
| `String?` | text, varchar |
| `int?` | integer types |
| `double?` | float, double. MySQL also gives `DECIMAL` as `double`. Postgres gives `numeric` as `String`. |
| `bool?` | boolean |
| `DateTime?` | date, datetime, timestamp |
| `Map<String, dynamic>?` or `List<dynamic>?` | JSON |

For other conversions, use `beforeSave` and `beforeGet`.

### `beforeSave` and `beforeGet`

These options take a static function of the model class.
The function gets a map and returns the value.

- `beforeSave` runs before a save. It gets the model values (column name => value).
  It returns the value to save in this column.
- `beforeGet` runs when a row is read. It gets the row from the database.
  It returns the value for this field.

```dart
@DoxModel()
class Blog extends BlogGenerator {
  @Column()
  String? title;

  // beforeSave: make the slug from the title
  @Column(beforeSave: makeSlug)
  String? slug;

  // beforeGet: old rows have no status, show them as draft
  @Column(beforeGet: readStatus)
  String? status;

  static String? makeSlug(Map<String, dynamic> map) {
    return map['title']?.toString().toLowerCase().replaceAll(' ', '-');
  }

  static String? readStatus(Map<String, dynamic> map) {
    return map['status'] as String? ?? 'draft';
  }
}
```

## Save

`save()` inserts a new model, or updates a model that has an id.

```dart
// insert
Blog blog = Blog();
blog.title = 'My first blog';
await blog.save();
print(blog.id); // the new id

// update
Blog? found = await Blog().find(1);
found?.title = 'New title';
await found?.save();

// set a field to null
found?.slug = null;
await found?.save(); // slug is now NULL in the database

// create from a map
Blog created = await Blog().create(<String, dynamic>{
  'title': 'My first blog',
  'status': 'draft',
});
```

- On insert, `null` fields are not sent, so the database default is used.
- On update, a field is set to `NULL` only when it had a value before
  (loaded from the database, or saved).
  Fields that were not loaded, for example with `select()`, are not changed.
- `save()` returns `false` when a [model event](events.md) cancels it.

## Delete

```dart
// delete a record
Blog? blog = await Blog().find(1);
await blog?.delete(); // deletes only this record

// force delete
Blog? trashed = await Blog().withTrash().find(1);
await trashed?.forceDelete(); // deletes the row, also with softDelete

// restore
Blog? deleted = await Blog().withTrash().find(1);
await deleted?.restore(); // sets deleted_at back to NULL
```

`save()`, `delete()`, `forceDelete()` and `restore()` fire [model events](events.md).

## Convert to a map or JSON

```dart
Blog? blog = await Blog().find(1);

Map<String, dynamic>? map = blog?.toMap();  // all columns and computed values
Map<String, dynamic>? json = blog?.toJson(); // the same, without hidden fields
Map<String, dynamic>? row = blog?.toMap(original: true); // the raw database row
```

`jsonEncode(blog)` uses `toJson()`.
So you can return a model, or a list of models, from a controller.

### Hide fields

Fields in `hidden` are left out of `toJson()`.
Use the column names.

```dart
@DoxModel()
class User extends UserGenerator {
  @override
  List<String> get hidden => <String>['password', 'remember_token'];
}
```

### Computed values

A computed value is a getter that is added to `toJson()` and `toMap()`.
It is like `$appends` with an accessor in Laravel.

Add `@Computed()` to a getter in the model, then run `dart run build_runner build`.

```dart
@DoxModel()
class User extends UserGenerator {
  @Column(name: 'first_name')
  String? firstName;

  @Column(name: 'last_name')
  String? lastName;

  @Computed() // json key: full_name
  String get fullName => '$firstName $lastName';

  @Computed(name: 'initials') // custom json key
  String get shortName => '${firstName?[0]}${lastName?[0]}';
}
```

```dart
User? user = await User().find(1);
print(user?.toJson());
// {id: 1, first_name: John, last_name: Wick, ..., full_name: John Wick, initials: JW}
```

- The default key is the getter name in snake_case (`fullName` becomes `full_name`).
- A computed value is **never a column**. It is not read from the database,
  and it is not sent in `INSERT` or `UPDATE`.
- `hidden` also hides computed values. Use the json key, for example `['full_name']`.
- Computed values of loaded relations are in the nested JSON too.
- `toMap(original: true)` returns the raw database row, so it has no computed values.
- A getter runs each time `toJson()` or `toMap()` is called, so keep it fast.

!!! info "No reflection"
    `build_runner` makes the code. There is no reflection at run time.
    A model without `@Computed()` does no extra work in `toJson()`.

## New query

A model object keeps the parts of its query (`where`, `orderBy`, ...).
`query()` gives a new, empty model, so you can start another query.

```dart
Blog blog = Blog();
List<Blog> active = await blog.where('status', 'active').get();

// a new query, without the where above
List<Blog> deleted = await blog.query().where('status', 'deleted').get();
```

## Debug

`debug(true)` prints the SQL of this model in the terminal.

```dart
Blog blog = Blog();
blog.debug(true);
blog.title = 'John Wick';
await blog.save();
```

## Relationships

A model can load related models.
See [HasOne](relationship/has-one.md), [HasMany](relationship/has-many.md),
[BelongsTo](relationship/belongs-to.md) and [ManyToMany](relationship/many-to-many.md).

The relationship pages use these tables:

```mermaid
erDiagram
    user ||--o| user_info : "HasOne"
    user ||--o{ post : "HasMany"
    user ||--o{ comment : "BelongsTo, from comment"
    artist ||--o{ artist_song : "ManyToMany"
    song ||--o{ artist_song : "ManyToMany"
    user {
        int id PK
        string name
    }
    user_info {
        int id PK
        int user_id FK
        string address
    }
    post {
        int id PK
        int user_id FK
        string title
    }
    comment {
        int id PK
        int user_id FK
        string content
    }
    artist_song {
        int id PK
        int artist_id FK
        int song_id FK
    }
```


---

# Model events

Source: https://dartondox.dev/latest/3.xdatabase/model/events/

# Model events

A model fires events when you save, delete or restore it.
You can run your own code on these events.
There are two ways: hooks in the model, and observer classes.

## Hooks in the model

Override an `on...` method in the model. Then run `dart run build_runner build`.

```dart
@DoxModel(softDelete: true)
class User extends UserGenerator {
  @Column()
  String? email;

  @override
  Future<void> onCreating() async {
    email = email?.trim().toLowerCase();
  }

  @override
  Future<void> onDeleted() async {
    await AuditLog().create({'message': 'user $id deleted'});
  }
}
```

!!! info
    The hook names start with `on` (`onCreating`, not `creating`).
    This is because `created` and `deleted` are common column names.
    Declare the hooks in the model class itself. The generator looks there.

## Events and order

| Call | Events, in order |
|------|------------------|
| `save()` on a new model | `saving` → `creating` → *INSERT* → `created` → `saved` |
| `save()` on a loaded model | `saving` → `updating` → *UPDATE* → `updated` → `saved` |
| `create({...})` | the same as `save()` on a new model |
| `delete()` | `deleting` → *DELETE or soft delete* → `deleted` |
| `forceDelete()` | `forceDeleting` → `deleting` → *DELETE* → `deleted` → `forceDeleted` |
| `restore()` | `restoring` → *UPDATE deleted_at = NULL* → `restored` |

The model hook runs first. Then the observers run, in the order you added them.

!!! warning "Query updates and deletes fire no events"
    Events fire only on a model instance.
    `User().where('active', false).update({...})`, `User().where(...).delete()`
    and `insertMultiple()` run one query and fire no events. This is the same as Laravel.

## Cancel an operation

Throw `CancelModelEvent` in a "before" event
(`saving`, `creating`, `updating`, `deleting`, `forceDeleting`, `restoring`).
The query does not run. `save()`, `delete()`, `forceDelete()` and `restore()` return `false`.

```dart
@override
Future<void> onDeleting() async {
  if (isAdmin == true) throw CancelModelEvent('admins can not be deleted');
}
```

```dart
bool deleted = await user.delete(); // false
```

`create({...})` returns the unsaved model (its `id` is `null`) when an event cancels it.
Any other error from a hook is thrown to the caller.

## Observers

An observer is a class that listens to one model.
Override only the methods you need. Each method gets the model.

```dart
class UserObserver extends ModelObserver<User> {
  final Mailer mailer;

  UserObserver(this.mailer);

  @override
  Future<void> created(User user) async {
    await mailer.sendWelcome(user.email!);
  }
}
```

Add it once, for example when the app starts:

```dart
Model.observe<User>(UserObserver(mailer));
```

- You can add more than one observer to a model.
- `Model.forgetObservers<User>()` removes the observers of `User`. `Model.forgetObservers()` removes all.

## Skip events

```dart
await user.saveQuietly(); // save without events

await Model.withoutEvents(() async {
  await user.save();
  await post.delete();
});
```

## Transactions

Hooks run inside the transaction of the caller.
`save()` does **not** start a transaction by itself.

- If an "after" hook (`created`, `saved`, ...) throws, the row is already written.
- To undo the row when a hook fails, wrap the call in [`QueryBuilder.transaction()`](../transactions.md):

```dart
await QueryBuilder.transaction(() async {
  await user.save(); // if onCreated() throws, the INSERT is rolled back
});
```

## Performance

- There is no reflection. The generator sets `hasModelHooks` only for models that declare a hook.
- A model with no hooks and no observers does no event work. It is one `bool` check, plus one map lookup when some other model has observers.
- When a model has events, `create({...})` fills a model with `fromMap()` and calls `save()`.
  Only the `@Column` fields are saved then.


---

# HasOne

Source: https://dartondox.dev/latest/3.xdatabase/model/relationship/has-one/

# HasOne

Use `HasOne` when one row of this table has one row in another table.
For example, a user has one user info row.
The other table keeps the foreign key (`user_info.user_id`).

## Define it

Add a field with `@HasOne(...)` to the model. The field type is the related model, nullable.

```dart title="lib/app/models/user/user.model.dart"
import 'package:dox_orm/dox_orm.dart';

import '../user_info/user_info.model.dart';

part 'user.model.g.dart';

@DoxModel()
class User extends UserGenerator {
  @Column()
  String? name;

  @HasOne(UserInfo)
  UserInfo? userInfo;
}
```

```dart title="lib/app/models/user_info/user_info.model.dart"
import 'package:dox_orm/dox_orm.dart';

part 'user_info.model.g.dart';

@DoxModel()
class UserInfo extends UserInfoGenerator {
  @Column()
  int? userId; // column user_id

  @Column()
  String? address;
}
```

Run `dart run build_runner build` after you add a relationship.

## Load it

The relation is not loaded by default. Load it in one of these ways.
Use the field name (`'userInfo'`) as the relation name.

### `preload`

Use it when you load the models with a query.

```dart
User? user = await User().preload('userInfo').find(1);
print(user?.userInfo?.address);
```

`preload` works with `find`, `get`, `all` and `getFirst`.
For a list of users, it runs one query for all of them.

### `$getRelation`

Use it when you already have the model.

```dart
User? user = await User().find(1);
await user?.$getRelation('userInfo');
print(user?.userInfo?.address);
```

### `related`

Use it when you need more conditions on the related row.

```dart
User? user = await User().find(1);
UserInfo? info = await user
    ?.related<UserInfo>('userInfo')
    ?.where('address', '!=', '')
    .getFirst();
```

`related` gives a query. You can add more conditions before you run it.
It does not set `user.userInfo`.

### `eager`

Use it when every query of `User` should load the relation.

```dart
@HasOne(UserInfo, eager: true)
UserInfo? userInfo;
```

With `eager: true`, every query of `User` loads the relation.
You do not call `preload`.

The load runs this SQL:

```sql
SELECT *, "user_id" as "_owner_id" FROM "user_info" WHERE "user_id" IN (@user_id_p0)
```

## Options

| Option | Default | What it is |
|---|---|---|
