# File upload

Source: https://dartondox.dev/latest/3.xguides/file-upload/

# File upload

Accept an image from a form, check its size and type, save it to a disk, and return its URL.

## What you need

- A Dox app (`dox create my_app`).
- `build_runner` for the DTO (a new app has it).

## 1. Set up the disk

Give the `local` disk a `url`. `Storage().url()` uses it to build the public URL of a file.

```dart title="lib/config/storage.dart"
import 'package:dox_core/dox_core.dart';
import 'package:my_app/config/env.dart';

StorageConfig storage = StorageConfig(
  defaultDisk: env.storageDisk,
  disks: <String, Map<String, dynamic>>{
    /// uploads go to the `storage` folder.
    /// `url` is the public address of `Route.files('files', ...)`.
    'local': <String, dynamic>{
      'driver': 'local',
      'root': 'storage',
      'url': '${env.appUrl}/files',
    },
  },
);
```

`APP_URL` is a new key. Add a getter for it to the `AppEnv` class:

```dart title="lib/config/env.dart"
  /// the public URL of this app, used in file links
  String get appUrl => 'http://localhost:3000';
```

Run `dart run build_runner build` to update `env.g.dart`.
Then add `APP_URL=http://localhost:3000` to your `.env`.

## 2. Write the DTO

The DTO checks the file before your controller runs. `@Image()` reads the first bytes of the file to find the real type. It does not trust the file name.

```dart title="lib/app/http/dtos/upload_image.dto.dart"
import 'package:dox_core/dox_core.dart';

part 'upload_image.dto.g.dart';

@Dto()
class UploadImage {
  /// jpg, jpeg, png, gif, webp or bmp. Dox reads the first bytes of the
  /// file to find the real type. The file name is not trusted.
  @Image()
  @MaxSize('5MB')
  final RequestFile image;

  const UploadImage({required this.image});

  static const DtoSchema<UploadImage> schema = $UploadImageDto;
}
```

For other file types, use `@Mimes(<String>['pdf', 'docx'])` in place of `@Image()`.

## 3. Write the controller

`putRequestFile` moves the upload to the disk with a new UUID name. It does not read the file into memory.

```dart title="lib/app/http/controllers/upload.controller.dart"
import 'package:dox_core/dox_core.dart';
import 'package:my_app/app/http/dtos/upload_image.dto.dart';

class UploadController {
  /// POST /api/upload (multipart/form-data, field `image`)
  Future<Map<String, String>> store(UploadImage body) async {
    // saves the file as /images/<uuid>.<ext> on the default disk
    String path = await Storage().putRequestFile('images', body.image);
    String url = await Storage().url(path);
    return <String, String>{'path': path, 'url': url};
  }
}

UploadController uploadController = UploadController();
```

!!! warning "Save the file before you return"
    A file bigger than 1 MB is written to a temp file while it arrives.
    Dox deletes that temp file when the response is sent.
    So call `putRequestFile`, `store` or `moveTo` inside the controller, not later.

## 4. Add the routes

One route takes the upload. `Route.files` serves the saved files at `GET /files/{key*}`.

```dart title="lib/routes/api.dart"
import 'package:dox_core/dox_core.dart';
import 'package:my_app/app/http/controllers/upload.controller.dart';

class ApiRouter extends Router {
  @override
  String get prefix => 'api';

  @override
  List<dynamic> get middleware => <dynamic>[];

  @override
  void register() {
    Route.post('/upload', uploadController.store);
  }
}
```

```dart title="lib/routes/web.dart"
import 'package:dox_core/dox_core.dart';

class WebRouter extends Router {
  @override
  List<dynamic> get middleware => <dynamic>[];

  @override
  void register() {
    // GET /files/{key*}, any file of the default disk
    Route.files('files', signed: false);
  }
}
```

`signed: false` makes every file public. Leave it out to serve only signed URLs. Then use `Storage().signedUrl(path)` in place of `Storage().url(path)`.

## 5. Build and run

```bash
dart run build_runner build --delete-conflicting-outputs
dox serve
```

Make sure `lib/config/app.dart` has `dtos: dtos` from `lib/dtos.g.dart`. See [Validation: setup](../the-basic/validation.md#setup).

## Check it

Upload a PNG:

```bash
curl -F image=@photo.png http://localhost:3000/api/upload
```

```json
{"path":"/images/074aa0d0-ce21-11f1-938a-57265e28c4a3.png","url":"http://localhost:3000/files/images/074aa0d0-ce21-11f1-938a-57265e28c4a3.png"}
```

Open the `url` in the browser. The image shows.

Upload a text file. You get `422`:

```bash
curl -F image=@notes.txt http://localhost:3000/api/upload
```

```json
{"image":"The image must be an image"}
```

Send no file at all. You get `422` with `{"image":"The image is required"}`.

## Bigger files

The default limit for a `multipart/form-data` body is 100 MB. Change it in `AppConfig(maxMultipartSize: ...)`.
Set the same limit in your proxy (`client_max_body_size` in nginx).

## See also

- [Request: form data](../the-basic/request.md#form-data-file) for `RequestFile`
- [Validation: files](../the-basic/validation.md#files) for `@Image`, `@Mimes`, `@MaxSize`
- [File storage](../digging-deeper/file-storage.md) for S3 and signed URLs


---

# Pagination

Source: https://dartondox.dev/latest/3.xguides/pagination/

# Pagination

Make a list route that takes `page` and `per_page` from the query string and returns one page of rows.

## What you need

- A Dox app with a database and a `User` model (`dox create:model User -m`).
- `build_runner` for the DTO.

## 1. Write the query DTO

A DTO with `source: Source.query` reads the query string, also for `POST`.
The query key of `perPage` is `per_page`, because keys are snake_case by default.

```dart title="lib/app/http/dtos/list_users.dto.dart"
import 'package:dox_core/dox_core.dart';

part 'list_users.dto.g.dart';

/// GET /api/users?page=2&per_page=10
@Dto(source: Source.query)
class ListUsers {
  @Min(1)
  final int page;

  @Range(1, 100)
  final int perPage; // query key: per_page

  const ListUsers({this.page = 1, this.perPage = 20});

  static const DtoSchema<ListUsers> schema = $ListUsersDto;
}
```

Both fields have a default, so both are optional. `@Range(1, 100)` stops a client from asking for 10000 rows.

## 2. Write the controller

`paginate()` runs one `count` query and one `select` query. It returns a `Pagination`.
A controller can return it as it is. Dox sends `toJson()`.

```dart title="lib/app/http/controllers/user.controller.dart"
import 'package:dox_core/dox_core.dart';
import 'package:dox_orm/dox_orm.dart';
import 'package:my_app/app/http/dtos/list_users.dto.dart';
import 'package:my_app/app/models/user/user.model.dart';

class UserController {
  /// GET /api/users?page=1&per_page=20
  Future<Pagination<User>> index(ListUsers query) async {
    return User()
        .orderBy('id', 'desc')
        .paginate(currentPage: query.page, perPage: query.perPage);
  }
}

UserController userController = UserController();
```

Always add an `orderBy`. Without it, the database may return the rows in a different order on each page.

Add a `where` before `paginate` to filter: `User().where('role', 'admin').orderBy('id').paginate(...)`.

## 3. Add the route

```dart title="lib/routes/api.dart"
Route.get('/users', userController.index);
```

## 4. Build and run

```bash
dart run build_runner build --delete-conflicting-outputs
dox serve
```

## Check it

With 3 users in the table:

```bash
curl 'http://localhost:3000/api/users?page=2&per_page=2'
```

```json
{
  "total": 3,
  "per_page": 2,
  "last_page": 2,
  "current_page": 2,
  "data": [
    {"id": 1, "name": "User 1", "email": "user1@example.com", "created_at": "2026-10-22T14:01:07.843207Z", "updated_at": "2026-10-22T14:01:07.843207Z"}
  ]
}
```

| Key | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `total` | rows that match the query, on all pages |
| `per_page` | rows per page |
| `last_page` | the number of the last page |
| `current_page` | the page you asked for |
| `data` | the rows of this page, from `toJson()` of the model |

A page after the last one gives an empty `data` list.

Bad input gets `422` before the controller runs:

```bash
curl 'http://localhost:3000/api/users?page=0&per_page=500'
```

```json
{"page":"The page must be greater than or equal 1","per_page":"The per_page must be between 1 and 100"}
```

## Change the shape of a row

Return a serializer for each row, when the model has fields you do not want to send.
`page.data` gives the typed rows (`List<User>`):

```dart
Future<Map<String, dynamic>> index(ListUsers query) async {
  Pagination<User> page = await User()
      .orderBy('id', 'desc')
      .paginate(currentPage: query.page, perPage: query.perPage);
  return <String, dynamic>{
    ...page.toJson(),
    'data': UserSerializer(page.data).toJson(),
  };
}
```

## See also

- [Query builder: paginate](../database/query-builder.md#paginate)
- [Validation: where the data comes from](../the-basic/validation.md#where-the-data-comes-from)
- [Serializer](../database/model/serializer.md)


---

# JWT authentication

Source: https://dartondox.dev/latest/3.xguides/jwt-auth/

# JWT authentication

Let users register and log in, give them a JWT token, protect routes with it, and read the user in a controller.

## What you need

- A Dox app with a database and a `users` table with `name`, `email` and `password` columns.
- The `dox_auth` package: `dart pub add dox_auth`. A new app has it.
- `build_runner` for the DTOs.

## 1. Hide the password in the model

The token holds `user.toJson()`. Anyone with the token can read it. So the password hash must be in `hidden`.

```dart title="lib/app/models/user/user.model.dart"
import 'package:dox_orm/dox_orm.dart';

part 'user.model.g.dart';

@DoxModel(table: 'users', softDelete: true)
class User extends UserGenerator {
  @override
  List<String> get hidden => <String>['password'];

  @Column()
  String? name;

  @Column()
  String? email;

  @Column()
  String? password;
}
```

## 2. Set up the auth service

`APP_KEY` signs the tokens. `expiresIn` is how long a token works.

```dart title="lib/services/auth_service.dart"
import 'package:dox_auth/dox_auth.dart';
import 'package:dox_core/dox_core.dart';
import 'package:my_app/app/models/user/user.model.dart';
import 'package:my_app/config/env.dart';

class AuthService implements DoxService {
  @override
  void setup() {
    Auth.initialize(
      AuthConfig(
        defaultGuard: 'api',
        guards: <String, AuthGuard>{
          'api': AuthGuard(
            driver: JwtAuthDriver(
              // APP_KEY signs the tokens. A new key logs every user out.
              secret: SecretKey(env.appKey),
              // a token stops working after this time
              expiresIn: const Duration(days: 7),
            ),
            provider: AuthProvider(model: () => User()),
          ),
        },
      ),
    );
  }
}
```

```dart title="lib/config/services.dart"
import 'package:dox_core/dox_core.dart';
import 'package:my_app/services/auth_service.dart';
import 'package:my_app/services/orm_service.dart';

List<DoxService> services = <DoxService>[
  ORMService(),
  AuthService(),
];
```

## 3. Write the DTOs

`@Unique` makes sure the email is not taken. It comes from `dox_orm`, so hide its `Schema` class.

```dart title="lib/app/http/dtos/register_user.dto.dart"
import 'package:dox_core/dox_core.dart';
import 'package:dox_orm/dox_orm.dart' hide Schema;

part 'register_user.dto.g.dart';

@Dto()
class RegisterUser {
  @Length(min: 2, max: 50)
  @Trim()
  final String name;

  @Trim()
  @Lowercase()
  @Email()
  @Unique('users', column: 'email')
  final String email;

  @MinLength(8)
  final String password;

  const RegisterUser({
    required this.name,
    required this.email,
    required this.password,
  });

  static const DtoSchema<RegisterUser> schema = $RegisterUserDto;
}
```

```dart title="lib/app/http/dtos/login_user.dto.dart"
import 'package:dox_core/dox_core.dart';

part 'login_user.dto.g.dart';

@Dto()
class LoginUser {
  @Trim()
  @Lowercase()
  @Email()
  final String email;

  final String password;

  const LoginUser({required this.email, required this.password});

  static const DtoSchema<LoginUser> schema = $LoginUserDto;
}
```

## 4. Write the controller

```dart title="lib/app/http/controllers/auth.controller.dart"
import 'package:dox_auth/dox_auth.dart';
import 'package:dox_core/dox_core.dart';
import 'package:my_app/app/http/dtos/login_user.dto.dart';
import 'package:my_app/app/http/dtos/register_user.dto.dart';
import 'package:my_app/app/models/user/user.model.dart';

class AuthController {
  /// POST /api/auth/register
  Future<Map<String, dynamic>> register(RegisterUser body) async {
    User user = User()
      ..name = body.name
      ..email = body.email
      ..password = Hash.make(body.password);
    await user.save();

    String? token = Auth().login(user);
    return <String, dynamic>{'token': token, 'user': user};
  }

  /// POST /api/auth/login
  Future<Map<String, dynamic>> login(LoginUser body) async {
    Auth auth = Auth();
    String? token = await auth.attempt(<String, dynamic>{
      'email': body.email,
      'password': body.password,
    });
    if (token == null) {
      throw UnAuthorizedException(message: 'Wrong email or password');
    }
    return <String, dynamic>{'token': token, 'user': auth.user<User>()};
  }

  /// GET /api/auth/me (behind AuthMiddleware)
  User? me(DoxRequest req) {
    return req.auth?.user<User>();
  }

  /// POST /api/auth/logout (behind AuthMiddleware)
  /// A JWT can not be cancelled on the server. The client deletes the
  /// token. The token still works until `expiresIn` passes.
  Map<String, String> logout(DoxRequest req) {
    return <String, String>{'message': 'Delete the token on the client'};
  }
}

AuthController authController = AuthController();
```

`Hash.make` makes a bcrypt hash. `auth.attempt` finds the user by `email` and checks the password against that hash.

## 5. Add the routes

`AuthMiddleware` reads the `Authorization: Bearer <token>` header, checks the token and loads the user from the database.
A missing or bad token stops the request with `401`.

```dart title="lib/routes/api.dart"
import 'package:dox_auth/dox_auth.dart';
import 'package:dox_core/dox_core.dart';
import 'package:my_app/app/http/controllers/auth.controller.dart';

class ApiRouter extends Router {
  @override
  String get prefix => 'api';

  @override
  List<dynamic> get middleware => <dynamic>[];

  @override
  void register() {
    Route.post('/auth/register', authController.register);
    Route.post('/auth/login', authController.login);

    Route.middleware(<dynamic>[AuthMiddleware()], () {
      Route.get('/auth/me', authController.me);
      Route.post('/auth/logout', authController.logout);
      // put every protected route here
    });
  }
}
```

## 6. Build and run

```bash
dart run build_runner build --delete-conflicting-outputs
dox serve
```

## Check it

Register:

```bash
curl -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"name":"Ann","email":"ann@example.com","password":"secret123"}' \
  http://localhost:3000/api/auth/register
```

```json
{"token":"eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiIs...","user":{"id":1,"name":"Ann","email":"ann@example.com","created_at":"...","updated_at":"..."}}
```

Log in with a wrong password. You get `401`:

```json
{"error":{"code":"unauthorized","message":"Wrong email or password"}}
```

Log in and use the token:

```bash
TOKEN=$(curl -s -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"email":"ann@example.com","password":"secret123"}' \
  http://localhost:3000/api/auth/login | jq -r .token)

curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" http://localhost:3000/api/auth/me
```

```json
{"id":1,"name":"Ann","email":"ann@example.com","created_at":"...","updated_at":"..."}
```

Without the header, `/api/auth/me` gives `401 Authentication failed`.

!!! note "The error shape"
    The `401` body above is the plain message of the exception. With the response handler from
    [Custom errors](custom-errors.md), it becomes `{"error":{"code":"unauthorized","message":"..."}}`.

## Logout and expiry

A JWT is checked by its signature, not by a list on the server. So the server can not cancel one token.
This is what you can do:

| You want | Do this |
| --- | --- |
| Log out on this device | The client deletes the token. That is all `logout` does. |
| Limit the damage of a stolen token | Keep `expiresIn` short, for example `Duration(hours: 12)`. |
| Log every user out at once | Change `APP_KEY`. Every old token stops working. |
| Block one user | Delete or disable the user. `AuthMiddleware` loads the user from the database on each request, so a deleted user gets `401`. |

For a real "log out everywhere" button, add a `token_version` column to `users`, put it in the token, and compare the two in a middleware after `AuthMiddleware`.

## See also

- [Authentication](../security/authentication.md) for all options of `AuthGuard`, `JwtAuthDriver` and `AuthProvider`
- [Hashing](../security/hashing.md)
- [Middleware](../the-basic/middleware.md)


---

# Custom errors

Source: https://dartondox.dev/latest/3.xguides/custom-errors/

# Custom errors

Give your app its own exception classes, send every error in one JSON shape, and log the unexpected ones.

## What you need

- A Dox app.

## How Dox handles an error

When a controller or a middleware throws:

| Error | Status | What Dox does |
| --- | --- | --- |
| an `IHttpException`, like `NotFoundHttpException` | its `code` | sends its `message`. Does **not** call `errorHandler` |
| a validation error (bad DTO input) | `422` | sends the field errors. Does not call `errorHandler` |
| any other `Exception` or `Error` | `500` | sends `error.toString()`. Calls `errorHandler` |

The response goes through the `responseHandler` of `AppConfig` last. That is where you set the shape.

## 1. Write your own exceptions

Extend `IHttpException`. Set `code` (the HTTP status), `errorCode` (a short text for the client) and `message`.

```dart title="lib/app/exceptions/app_exception.dart"
import 'dart:io';

import 'package:dox_core/dox_core.dart';

/// 403. Thrown when the user may not do this.
class ForbiddenException extends IHttpException {
  ForbiddenException({String message = 'Forbidden'}) {
    super.code = HttpStatus.forbidden;
    super.errorCode = 'forbidden';
    super.message = message;
  }
}

/// 409. Thrown when the row already exists or was changed by someone else.
class ConflictException extends IHttpException {
  ConflictException({String message = 'Conflict'}) {
    super.code = HttpStatus.conflict;
    super.errorCode = 'conflict';
    super.message = message;
  }
}
```

Throw them anywhere in a controller, a middleware or a service:

```dart title="lib/app/http/controllers/user.controller.dart"
import 'package:dox_core/dox_core.dart';
import 'package:my_app/app/exceptions/app_exception.dart';
import 'package:my_app/app/models/user/user.model.dart';

class UserController {
  /// GET /api/users/{id}
  Future<User> show(int id) async {
    User? user = await User().find(id);
    if (user == null) {
      throw NotFoundHttpException(message: 'User $id not found');
    }
    return user;
  }

  /// DELETE /api/users/{id}
  Future<Map<String, bool>> destroy(int id) async {
    if (id == 1) {
      throw ForbiddenException(message: 'The first user can not be deleted');
    }
    User user = await show(id);
    await user.delete();
    return <String, bool>{'deleted': true};
  }
}

UserController userController = UserController();
```

## 2. One JSON shape for every error

The response handler sees every response before it is sent. For an error, the content is the exception object.
Turn it into your shape here.

```dart title="lib/app/http/response_handler.dart"
import 'dart:io';

import 'package:dox_core/dox_core.dart';

/// Gives every error the same JSON shape:
/// `{"error": {"code": "not_found", "message": "..."}}`.
/// A validation error (422) also has `"errors": {field: message}`.
class ResponseHandler extends ResponseHandlerInterface {
  @override
  DoxResponse handle(DoxResponse res) {
    dynamic content = res.getContent();

    if (content is ValidationException) {
      return res.statusCode(content.code).content(<String, dynamic>{
        'error': <String, dynamic>{
          'code': content.errorCode,
          'message': 'The input is not valid',
        },
        'errors': content.message,
      });
    }

    if (content is IHttpException) {
      return res.statusCode(content.code).content(<String, dynamic>{
        'error': <String, dynamic>{
          'code': content.errorCode,
          'message': content.message.toString(),
        },
      });
    }

    // any other exception: hide the details from the client
    if (content is Exception || content is Error) {
      return res.statusCode(HttpStatus.internalServerError).content(
        <String, dynamic>{
          'error': <String, String>{
            'code': 'server_error',
            'message': 'Something went wrong',
          },
        },
      );
    }

    return res;
  }
}
```

The last `if` matters. Without it, a `500` sends `error.toString()` to the client. That can show a SQL query or a file path.

## 3. Log unexpected errors

`errorHandler` runs for every `500`, and for errors outside a request (a future nobody awaited, a timer).
Write one JSON line. A log collector reads it, or you send it to Sentry here.

```dart title="lib/app/error_handler.dart"
import 'dart:convert';

/// Dox calls this for every unexpected error (a `500`, or an error
/// outside a request). It does not run for `IHttpException` errors
/// like `404` or `422`, because those are expected.
/// One JSON line per error. Send it to Sentry or Datadog from here.
void reportError(Object? error, StackTrace stackTrace) {
  print(
    jsonEncode(<String, String>{
      'level': 'ERROR',
      'message': error.toString(),
      'stack': stackTrace.toString(),
      'timestamp': DateTime.now().toIso8601String(),
    }),
  );
}
```

## 4. Register both

```dart title="lib/config/app.dart"
import 'package:my_app/app/error_handler.dart';
import 'package:my_app/app/http/response_handler.dart';

AppConfig appConfig = AppConfig(
  responseHandler: ResponseHandler(),
  errorHandler: reportError,
  // ...
);
```

## Check it

Add a route that throws, only for this check:

```dart
Route.get('/boom', (DoxRequest req) => throw StateError('boom'));
```

| Request | Status | Body |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `GET /api/users/999` | `404` | `{"error":{"code":"not_found","message":"User 999 not found"}}` |
| `GET /api/users/abc` | `404` | `{"error":{"code":"not_found","message":"Not Found"}}` |
| `DELETE /api/users/1` | `403` | `{"error":{"code":"forbidden","message":"The first user can not be deleted"}}` |
| `POST /api/auth/register` with `{}` | `422` | `{"error":{"code":"validation_failed","message":"The input is not valid"},"errors":{"name":"The name is required", ...}}` |
| `GET /api/boom` | `500` | `{"error":{"code":"server_error","message":"Something went wrong"}}` |

After `GET /api/boom`, the server prints one line:

```json
{"level":"ERROR","message":"Bad state: boom","stack":"#0  ApiRouter.register.<anonymous closure> (package:my_app/routes/api.dart:40:44) ...","timestamp":"2026-10-22T14:01:12.000Z"}
```

Remove the `/boom` route when you are done.

!!! note "A URL with no route"
    A URL that matches no route is a `NotFoundHttpException` with the message `GET /nothing not found`.
    It goes through the response handler too, so it gets the same JSON shape:
    `{"error":{"code":"not_found","message":"GET /nothing not found"}}`.

## See also

- [Response: errors](../the-basic/response.md#errors) for the built-in exceptions
- [Response: change every response](../the-basic/response.md#change-every-response)
- [Validation: the error response](../the-basic/validation.md#the-error-response)
- [Isolate: when an isolate crashes](../digging-deeper/isolate.md#when-an-isolate-crashes)

# Background work

Source: https://dartondox.dev/latest/3.xguides/background-work/

# Background work

Answer the request now and do the slow work after. Use another thread for CPU work. Run a job on a timer.

## What you need

- A Dox app.

## What Dox gives you

Dox has no job queue. It has three building blocks from Dart itself:

| You want | Use | Runs where |
| --- | --- | --- |
| I/O work after the response (send an email, call an API, write rows) | a `Future` you do not await | the same isolate, between requests |
| CPU work (resize an image, parse a big file, compute) | `Isolate.run()` | a new thread |
| work every N minutes (cleanup, sync) | `Timer.periodic` in a service | one isolate of your choice |

None of them survive a restart. See [When you need a real queue](#when-you-need-a-real-queue).

## 1. Work after the response

Start the future and return. `unawaited` tells the linter you did this on purpose.
An error in the future goes to the `errorHandler` of `AppConfig`. The isolate keeps running.

```dart title="lib/app/http/controllers/report.controller.dart"
import 'dart:async';
import 'dart:isolate';

import 'package:dox_core/dox_core.dart';

class ReportController {
  /// POST /api/reports
  /// Answers at once. The work runs after the response, in this isolate.
  Map<String, String> store(DoxRequest req) {
    String id = DateTime.now().microsecondsSinceEpoch.toString();
    unawaited(_build(id));
    return <String, String>{'id': id, 'status': 'queued'};
  }

  /// I/O work (database, HTTP calls, email) is fine here. It shares the
  /// event loop with the requests, so it must not block the CPU.
  Future<void> _build(String id) async {
    await Future<void>.delayed(const Duration(seconds: 2));
    print('report $id is ready');
  }

  /// GET /api/primes/{limit}
  /// CPU work runs on another thread with `Isolate.run`.
  /// The request waits for the result, but other requests are not blocked.
  Future<Map<String, int>> primes(int limit) async {
    int count = await Isolate.run(() => countPrimes(limit));
    return <String, int>{'limit': limit, 'primes': count};
  }
}

/// Must be a top level or static function with plain arguments.
/// The new isolate has no Dox, no database and no services.
int countPrimes(int limit) {
  List<bool> sieve = List<bool>.filled(limit + 1, true);
  int count = 0;
  for (int i = 2; i <= limit; i++) {
    if (!sieve[i]) continue;
    count++;
    for (int j = i * i; j <= limit; j += i) {
      sieve[j] = false;
    }
  }
  return count;
}

ReportController reportController = ReportController();
```

!!! warning "Do not block the event loop"
    `_build` runs on the same thread as the HTTP requests of this isolate.
    `await` on the database or on HTTP is fine. A long loop is not. Every request on this isolate waits for it.
    Put a long loop in `Isolate.run`.

## 2. CPU work on another thread

`Isolate.run` starts a new isolate, runs the function, and sends the result back.
The function only gets what you pass in. It has no `Dox()`, no models and no `Storage()`.
So pass plain data in (an `int`, a `String`, bytes), get plain data out, and save the result in the request isolate.

Both patterns are in the controller above: `primes` waits for the result. To not wait, combine them:

```dart
unawaited(Isolate.run(() => countPrimes(limit)).then(saveResult));
```

## 3. Work on a timer

`setup()` of a service runs in **every** isolate. Dox starts one per CPU core.
So start the timer on isolate 1 only. Otherwise 8 isolates run the same cleanup.

```dart title="lib/services/cleanup_service.dart"
import 'dart:async';

import 'package:dox_core/dox_core.dart';
import 'package:my_app/app/models/user/user.model.dart';

/// Work on a timer. `setup()` runs in every isolate, so the timer is
/// started on isolate 1 only. Otherwise 8 isolates do the same job.
class CleanupService implements DoxService {
  @override
  void setup() {
    if (Dox().isolateId != 1) return;
    Timer.periodic(const Duration(hours: 1), _run);
  }

  Future<void> _run(Timer timer) async {
    DateTime limit = DateTime.now().subtract(const Duration(days: 30));
    List<User> old = await User()
        .withTrash()
        .where('deleted_at', '<', limit)
        .get();
    for (User user in old) {
      await user.forceDelete();
    }
    print('cleanup: removed ${old.length} users');
  }
}
```

```dart title="lib/config/services.dart"
List<DoxService> services = <DoxService>[
  ORMService(),
  CleanupService(), // after ORMService, so the database is ready
];
```

When you run more than one process (two machines), each process has an isolate 1. Then the job runs twice. Use a database lock, or run the job from one place only.

## 4. Add the routes

```dart title="lib/routes/api.dart"
Route.post('/reports', reportController.store);
Route.get('/primes/{limit}', reportController.primes);
```

## Check it

```bash
curl -X POST http://localhost:3000/api/reports
```

The answer comes at once:

```json
{"id":"1792677668393002","status":"queued"}
```

Two seconds later, the server prints `report 1792677668393002 is ready`.

```bash
curl http://localhost:3000/api/primes/100000
```

```json
{"limit":100000,"primes":9592}
```

## When you need a real queue

The work above is lost when the process stops, and it does not retry.
When that is not OK (payments, emails that must arrive), save the job as a row in a table first.
Then a `Timer.periodic` service, or a second small Dart program, reads the table, does the work, and marks the row as done.
A failed row stays in the table, so you can retry it. This is a queue with one extra table and no new service.

## See also

- [Isolate](../digging-deeper/isolate.md) for what each isolate shares, and what it does not
- [Services](../digging-deeper/services.md)
- [Custom errors](custom-errors.md) for the `errorHandler` that gets the errors of a future nobody awaits


---

# Static files and SPA

Source: https://dartondox.dev/latest/3.xguides/static-files/

# Static files and SPA

Serve a folder of files, or a single page app (React, Vue, Flutter web), from the Dox app, with the right cache headers.

## What you need

- A Dox app.
- A `public` folder with the built front-end (`index.html`, `assets/...`).

## Serve a folder: one line

`Route.files` serves every file of a storage disk. Make a disk for the folder, and add the route.

```dart title="lib/config/storage.dart"
StorageConfig storage = StorageConfig(
  defaultDisk: 'local',
  disks: <String, Map<String, dynamic>>{
    'local': <String, dynamic>{'driver': 'local', 'root': 'storage'},

    /// the front-end files
    'public': <String, dynamic>{'driver': 'local', 'root': 'public'},
  },
);
```

```dart title="lib/routes/web.dart"
Route.files('static', disk: 'public', signed: false); // GET /static/{key*}
```

`GET /static/app.js` sends `public/app.js`, streamed, with the right `Content-Type`. A missing file answers `404`.
The disk rejects `..` in the path, so a client can not read files outside `public`.

This is enough for a few files. It sends no `Cache-Control` header. For an SPA, go on.

## Serve an SPA

An SPA needs two things:

- `index.html` for every URL the SPA router handles, with no cache.
- The built assets with a long cache. Build tools put a hash in the file name (`app.3f9c2b.js`), so a new build has new names.

### 1. Write the controller

```dart title="lib/app/http/controllers/static.controller.dart"
import 'dart:io';

import 'package:dox_core/dox_core.dart';

class StaticController {
  /// GET /assets/{path*}
  /// Built files have a hash in the name, so the browser may keep them
  /// for one year. The `public` disk rejects `..` in the path.
  Future<DoxResponse> asset(String path) async {
    StreamFile file = await Storage().disk('public').stream(path);
    return response(file).cache(const Duration(days: 365));
  }

  /// GET / and GET /{path*}
  /// Every other URL gets index.html, so the router of the SPA can
  /// handle it. Never cache it, so a new deploy shows at once.
  /// An unknown API URL stays a 404, it does not get the page.
  DoxResponse index(DoxRequest req) {
    if (req.uri.path.startsWith('/api/')) {
      throw NotFoundHttpException();
    }
    return response(File('public/index.html')).cache(Duration.zero);
  }
}

StaticController staticController = StaticController();
```

`cache(duration)` sets `Cache-Control: max-age=<seconds>`. `Duration.zero` gives `max-age=0`, so the browser asks again each time.

### 2. Add the routes

The catch-all route must come **last**. Put the API router before the web router in `AppConfig`.

```dart title="lib/routes/web.dart"
import 'package:dox_core/dox_core.dart';
import 'package:my_app/app/http/controllers/static.controller.dart';

class WebRouter extends Router {
  @override
  List<dynamic> get middleware => <dynamic>[];

  @override
  void register() {
    // the SPA: assets with a long cache, every other URL gets index.html
    Route.get('/assets/{path*}', staticController.asset);
    Route.get('/', staticController.index);
    Route.get('/{path*}', staticController.index);
  }
}
```

```dart title="lib/config/app.dart"
AppConfig appConfig = AppConfig(
  /// the SPA catch-all route is in WebRouter, so it comes last
  routers: <Router>[ApiRouter(), WebRouter()],
  // ...
);
```

Keep the route for `/` as well, so the start page is always served.

### 3. Put the build in `public`

```bash
# React (Vite)
npm run build && cp -r dist/. public/

# Flutter web
flutter build web && cp -r build/web/. public/
```

Vite puts the files in `assets/`. Flutter web puts them next to `index.html`. For Flutter, change the asset route to match, or serve everything with `Route.files` and give `index.html` the catch-all.

## Check it

```bash
curl -i http://localhost:3000/
```

```text
HTTP/1.1 200 OK
cache-control: max-age=0
content-type: text/html
```

```bash
curl -i http://localhost:3000/settings/profile   # same answer: index.html
curl -i http://localhost:3000/assets/app.js
```

```text
HTTP/1.1 200 OK
cache-control: max-age=31536000
content-type: text/javascript
```

`GET /assets/nope.js` answers `404`. `GET /assets/..%2Fpubspec.yaml` answers `404` too.
`GET /api/nothing` answers `404`, not the page.

## In production

Put the proxy in front of Dox, and let it do gzip. See [Deployment](../digging-deeper/deployment.md#https-put-a-proxy-in-front).
For a big site, serve `public` from the proxy or a CDN, and keep Dox for the API only.

## See also

- [Routing: serve storage files](../the-basic/routing.md#serve-storage-files)
- [Response: files and big responses](../the-basic/response.md#files-and-big-responses)
- [File storage](../digging-deeper/file-storage.md)


---

# CORS for a browser front-end

Source: https://dartondox.dev/latest/3.xguides/cors-for-spa/

# CORS for a browser front-end

Let a web app on another origin (`http://localhost:5173` in development, `https://my.app` in production) call your API.

## What you need

- A Dox app.
- A front-end that runs on its own origin, like Vite, Next.js or Flutter web.

## 1. Write the config

```dart title="lib/config/cors.dart"
import 'package:dox_core/dox_core.dart';
import 'package:my_app/config/env.dart';

/// `enabled` is true by default, so every route sends the headers.
CORSConfig cors = CORSConfig(
  /// One origin, or a list of origins. Set CORS_ORIGIN to the real
  /// front-end URL in production.
  origin: env.corsOrigin,

  methods: <String>['GET', 'POST', 'PUT', 'PATCH', 'DELETE'],

  /// the request headers the front-end sends
  headers: <String>['Content-Type', 'Authorization'],

  /// the response headers the front-end may read
  exposeHeaders: <String>['Content-Disposition'],

  /// true only when the front-end sends cookies. Not needed for a
  /// `Authorization: Bearer` token.
  credentials: false,

  /// the browser keeps the preflight answer for 10 minutes
  maxAge: 600,
);
```

```dart title="lib/config/app.dart"
AppConfig appConfig = AppConfig(
  cors: cors,
  // ...
);
```

## 2. Set the origin per environment

`CORS_ORIGIN` is a new key. Add a getter for it to the `AppEnv` class:

```dart title="lib/config/env.dart"
  /// the front-end URL that may call the API
  String get corsOrigin => 'http://localhost:5173';
```

Run `dart run build_runner build` to update `env.g.dart`. Then set the value in `.env`:

```ini title=".env"
CORS_ORIGIN=http://localhost:5173
```

In staging and production, set `CORS_ORIGIN` as a real environment variable: `https://my.app`.
The origin is scheme, host and port. No path, no `/` at the end.

## 3. Choose `credentials`

| Your front-end sends | `origin` | `credentials` |
| --- | --- | --- |
| a token in `Authorization: Bearer` (see [JWT authentication](jwt-auth.md)) | your front-end URL | `false` |
| cookies (`fetch(url, {credentials: 'include'})`) | your front-end URL, never `*` | `true` |
| nothing, a public API | `'*'` | `false` |

Browsers do not send cookies when `origin` is `*`.

!!! note "Two or more front-ends"
    Set `origin` to a list, like `['https://a.com', 'https://b.com']`.
    Dox compares the `Origin` header of the request with the list.
    It sends back only the origin that matches. If none matches, it sends no `Access-Control-Allow-Origin` header, and the browser blocks the call.

## Check it

The browser sends a preflight `OPTIONS` request before a `POST` with JSON or a custom header. Dox answers it by itself. You do not need an `OPTIONS` route.

```bash
curl -i -X OPTIONS http://localhost:3000/api/users \
  -H 'Origin: http://localhost:5173' \
  -H 'Access-Control-Request-Method: POST' \
  -H 'Access-Control-Request-Headers: Authorization'
```

```text
HTTP/1.1 204 No Content
access-control-allow-origin: http://localhost:5173
access-control-allow-methods: GET,POST,PUT,PATCH,DELETE
access-control-allow-headers: Content-Type,Authorization
access-control-expose-headers: Content-Disposition
access-control-allow-credentials: false
access-control-max-age: 600
```

A normal request gets the origin header too:

```bash
curl -i http://localhost:3000/api/ping -H 'Origin: http://localhost:5173' | grep -i access-control-allow-origin
```

```text
access-control-allow-origin: http://localhost:5173
```

In the browser, open the front-end and call the API with `fetch`. The console shows no CORS error.

## When it still fails

| The console says | The fix |
| --- | --- |
| `No 'Access-Control-Allow-Origin' header` | `CORS_ORIGIN` does not match the page origin exactly. Check `http` or `https`, and the port. |
| `The value of ... header is 'a.com,b.com'` | `origin` is one text with commas. Use a `List<String>` instead. |
| `Request header field x-foo is not allowed` | Add the header to `headers`. |
| `credentials mode is 'include'` with `*` | Set `origin` to the front-end URL and `credentials: true`. |

## Webhooks and server-to-server calls

CORS only matters for browsers. A webhook from Stripe or a call from another server ignores these headers.
Turn CORS off for such routes to send fewer headers:

```dart
Route.disabledCors(() {
  Route.post('/webhooks/stripe', webhookController.handle);
});
```

## See also

- [CORS](../security/cors.md) for every option
- [JWT authentication](jwt-auth.md)


---

# Environments

Source: https://dartondox.dev/latest/3.xguides/environments/

# Environments

Run the same app in development, staging and production with different config, and keep secrets out of git and out of the image.

## What you need

- A Dox app.
- `build_runner` for the typed env class (a new app has it).

## How Dox reads config

1. A real environment variable (shell, Docker, systemd) wins.
2. Then the `.env` file in the folder where the app starts.

So: use `.env` on your machine. Use real environment variables on a server. The `.env` file is optional there.

## 1. The typed env class

A new project already has `lib/config/env.dart`. Its `AppEnv` class lists every key, its type and its default. A missing required key stops the app at start, with a list of all problems.

This is the file of the guides app. The last two getters, `corsOrigin` and `appUrl`, are keys this app added. The rest comes with a new project.

```dart title="lib/config/env.dart"
import 'package:dox_core/dox_core.dart';

part 'env.g.dart';

/// The env of the app, typed. Made by `dox env:generate`.
/// -------------------------------
/// Each getter reads one key: `appName` reads `APP_NAME`.
/// A getter body is the default. A nullable getter is optional.
/// Other getters are required: the app stops at startup when one is missing.
/// Run `dart run build_runner build` after you change this class.
@DoxEnv()
abstract class AppEnv {
  /// reads and checks every key once
  static AppEnv load([EnvReader? reader]) {
    return _$AppEnv.load(reader);
  }

  String get appName => 'dox';

  /// development, staging or production
  String get appEnv => 'development';

  bool get isDevelopment => appEnv == 'development';

  int get appPort => 3000;

  /// required: used to sign tokens and encrypt cookies
  String get appKey;

  /// isolates (threads) of the HTTP server. Null: one per CPU core.
  int? get appTotalIsolate;

  String get logLevel => 'info';

  /// memory, file or redis
  String get cacheStore => 'file';

  /// local, s3 or memory
  String get storageDisk => 'local';

  /// sqlite, postgres or mysql
  String get dbConnection => 'sqlite';

  /// the database name. For SQLite: the file path.
  String get dbName => 'db/dox.sqlite';

  String get dbHost => 'localhost';

  /// null: 5432 for Postgres, 3306 for MySQL
  int? get dbPort;

  String get dbUsername => 'postgres';

  String get dbPassword => '';

  /// the front-end URL that may call the API
  String get corsOrigin => 'http://localhost:5173';

  /// the public URL of this app, used in file links
  String get appUrl => 'http://localhost:3000';
}

/// The env of the app. Read and checked once, on first use.
final AppEnv env = AppEnv.load();
```

The key is the getter name in UPPER_SNAKE case: `dbPort` reads `DB_PORT`.

- A getter with a body has a default: `int get appPort => 3000;`.
- A nullable getter with no body is optional: `int? get dbPort;` is `null` when the key is not set.
- Any other getter with no body is required: `String get appKey;`.

The part file `env.g.dart` is made by `build_runner`. It is in `.gitignore`.

## 2. Add a key

Say the app needs a mail host. Add one getter to `AppEnv`:

```dart
  /// the SMTP server for mails
  String get mailHost => 'localhost';
```

Then run `build_runner` again:

```bash
dart run build_runner build --delete-conflicting-outputs
```

Now `env.mailHost` reads `MAIL_HOST`. Add `MAIL_HOST` to `.env.example` too.

## 3. Use it in the config files

The config files read the typed getters. Things that differ per environment become one `if` or one `bool`.

```dart title="lib/config/logger.dart"
import 'package:dox_core/dox_core.dart';
import 'package:my_app/config/env.dart';

LoggerConfig logger = LoggerConfig(
  name: env.appName,
  enabled: true,
  level: env.logLevel,
  // colors on your machine, one JSON line per log in staging and production
  prettyPrint: env.isDevelopment,
);
```

```dart title="lib/config/database.dart"
import 'package:dox_orm/dox_orm.dart';
import 'package:my_app/config/env.dart';

DatabaseConfig databaseConfig = DatabaseConfig(
  connection: env.dbConnection,
  connections: <String, ConnectionConfig>{
    'postgres': ConnectionConfig(
      driver: Driver.postgres,
      host: env.dbHost,
      port: env.dbPort ?? 5432,
      user: env.dbUsername,
      password: env.dbPassword,
      database: env.dbName,
      // print every query on your machine only
      debug: env.isDevelopment,
    ),
    'sqlite': ConnectionConfig(
      driver: Driver.sqlite,
      database: env.dbName,
      debug: env.isDevelopment,
    ),
  },
);
```

## 4. Write the env files

Commit `.env.example`. It lists every key with a safe value. Never commit `.env`.

```ini title=".env.example"
APP_NAME=my_app
APP_ENV=development
APP_PORT=3000
# run `dox key:generate`
APP_KEY=
APP_URL=http://localhost:3000

DB_CONNECTION=postgres
DB_HOST=localhost
DB_PORT=5432
DB_NAME=my_app
DB_USERNAME=postgres
DB_PASSWORD=postgres

CORS_ORIGIN=http://localhost:5173
LOG_LEVEL=debug
```

```bash
cp .env.example .env
dox key:generate   # writes a new APP_KEY into .env
```

```text title=".gitignore"
.env
.env.*
!.env.example
```

| Environment | Where the values live | `APP_ENV` |
| --- | --- | --- |
| your machine | `.env` | `development` |
| staging | real env variables (compose `environment:`, a secrets manager) | `staging` |
| production | real env variables | `production` |

On a server you can also keep a `.env` next to the binary, outside git, with `chmod 600`. systemd reads it with `EnvironmentFile=`. See [Deployment](../digging-deeper/deployment.md#keep-it-running).

## 5. `APP_KEY`

`APP_KEY` encrypts cookies and signs JWT tokens and local signed URLs.

- Make one per environment with `dox key:generate`. Never share the production key with staging.
- When `APP_ENV=production` and `APP_KEY` is empty, the app does not start.
- A new key makes every cookie, token and signed URL invalid. Every user is logged out. Plan it.

## 6. Check the env before a deploy

`dox env:check` loads `AppEnv` with the real environment and `.env`, and prints every missing or bad key. It exits with code 1, so CI stops.

```bash
dox env:check
```

## Check it

Start with a key missing:

```bash
APP_KEY= dart run bin/server.dart
```

```text
Unhandled exception:
EnvException: the env is not valid
  - APP_KEY is missing
```

Start as staging on another port. The real variables win over `.env`:

```bash
APP_ENV=staging APP_PORT=4000 dart run bin/server.dart
```

The app listens on `4000`. `env.appEnv` is `'staging'`, and `env.isDevelopment` is `false`.

## Things that differ per environment

| Setting | Development | Staging and production |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `prettyPrint` of the logger | `true` | `false` (one JSON line per log) |
| `debug` of the database | `true` | `false` |
| `totalIsolate` | `1` or `2` is enough | one per core (the default) |
| `CORS_ORIGIN` | `http://localhost:5173` | the real front-end URL |
| the server | `dox serve` (JIT) | the `dox build` binary (AOT) |

## See also

- [Environment variables](../digging-deeper/env.md) for all types and rules of the typed env class
- [Docker](docker.md)
- [Deployment](../digging-deeper/deployment.md)


---

# Testing with a database

Source: https://dartondox.dev/latest/3.xguides/testing-with-database/

# Testing with a database

Run model tests against a real database: SQLite for fast local tests, or a test Postgres for the real thing.
Migrations run once, and every test starts with an empty table.

## What you need

- A Dox app with Dart migrations in `db/migration` (see [Migration](../database/migration.md)).
- `test` as a dev dependency: `dart pub add dev:test`.

## 1. Write the migration

If you do not have one yet:

```bash
dox make:migration create_users_table
```

```dart title="db/migration/2026_10_22_000000_create_users_table.dart"
import 'package:dox_migration/dox_migration.dart';

class CreateUsersTable extends Migration {
  @override
  Future<void> up(Schema schema) async {
    await schema.create('users', (Table table) {
      table.id();
      table.string('name');
      table.string('email').unique();
      table.string('password');
      table.timestamps();
      table.softDeletes();
    });
  }

  @override
  Future<void> down(Schema schema) async {
    await schema.dropIfExists('users');
  }
}
```

The command also writes `db/migration/migrations.dart`, the list of all migrations. The test imports that list.
A Dart migration works on Postgres, MySQL and SQLite, so the same test runs on all of them.

## 2. Write the test (SQLite)

SQLite needs no server. The test makes its own config, so your `.env` does not matter.

```dart title="test/user_test.dart"
import 'dart:io';

import 'package:dox_core/dox_core.dart';
import 'package:dox_migration/dox_migration.dart';
import 'package:dox_orm/dox_orm.dart';
import 'package:my_app/app/models/user/user.model.dart';
import 'package:test/test.dart';

import '../db/migration/migrations.dart';

/// One SQLite file for this test file. No server, no Postgres.
const String dbFile = 'storage/test.sqlite';

DatabaseConfig testDatabase = DatabaseConfig(
  connection: 'sqlite',
  connections: <String, ConnectionConfig>{
    'sqlite': ConnectionConfig(
      driver: Driver.sqlite,
      database: dbFile,
      debug: false,
    ),
  },
);

Future<void> deleteDbFile() async {
  for (String suffix in <String>['', '-wal', '-shm']) {
    File file = File('$dbFile$suffix');
    if (await file.exists()) await file.delete();
  }
}

void main() {
  setUpAll(() async {
    await deleteDbFile();
    await Migrator(
      migrations: migrations,
      connection: await testDatabase
          .getConnectionConfig()
          .getDatabaseConnection(),
    ).migrate();
    SqlQueryBuilder.initializeWithDatabaseConfig(testDatabase);
  });

  // every test starts with an empty table
  setUp(() async {
    await User().truncate();
  });

  tearDownAll(() async {
    await deleteDbFile();
  });

  test('saves and finds a user', () async {
    User user = User()
      ..name = 'Ann'
      ..email = 'ann@example.com'
      ..password = Hash.make('secret123');
    await user.save();

    User? found = await User().where('email', 'ann@example.com').getFirst();
    expect(found?.id, user.id);
    expect(found?.name, 'Ann');
    expect(Hash.verify('secret123', found!.password!), isTrue);
  });

  test('the table is empty again', () async {
    expect(await User().count(), 0);
  });
}
```

What happens:

1. `setUpAll` deletes an old database file, runs the migrations, and starts the ORM on the same file.
2. `setUp` empties the table before each test. `truncate()` also resets the id counter.
3. `tearDownAll` deletes the file.

!!! note "A file, not `:memory:`"
    The migrator and the ORM each open their own connection.
    Two connections to `:memory:` are two different databases. A file is shared.
    Put `storage/test.sqlite` in `.gitignore`.

## 3. Run it

```bash
dart test test/user_test.dart
```

## Check it

```text
00:00 +0: (setUpAll)
Migrating: 2026_10_22_000000_create_users_table
Migrated: 2026_10_22_000000_create_users_table
00:00 +1: saves and finds a user
00:00 +2: the table is empty again
00:00 +2: All tests passed!
```

## The same test on Postgres

Use a separate database for tests. Never the one you develop on.

Start one with Docker:

```bash
docker run -d --name my_app_test -p 5433:5432 \
  -e POSTGRES_PASSWORD=postgres -e POSTGRES_DB=my_app_test postgres:18
```

Change the config at the top of the test:

```dart
DatabaseConfig testDatabase = DatabaseConfig(
  connection: 'postgres',
  connections: <String, ConnectionConfig>{
    'postgres': ConnectionConfig(
      driver: Driver.postgres,
      host: 'localhost',
      port: 5433,
      user: 'postgres',
      password: 'postgres',
      database: 'my_app_test',
      debug: false,
    ),
  },
);
```

Delete `deleteDbFile()` and its two calls. The rest is the same.
Or read the values from the env, and run `DB_PORT=5433 DB_NAME=my_app_test dart test`.

## Many test files

Each test file runs in its own process. Two files that use the same table at the same time break each other.
Either give each file its own SQLite file (`storage/test_users.sqlite`, `storage/test_posts.sqlite`), or run them one by one:

```bash
dart test --concurrency=1
```

## Test a route with the database

Start the server in `setUpAll` and send real requests. The server runs the services, so the ORM is set up by `ORMService`.
Set the database with env variables, so `lib/config/database.dart` picks the test database:

```bash
DB_CONNECTION=sqlite DB_NAME=storage/test.sqlite APP_PORT=3999 dart test test/api_test.dart
```

See [Testing: test HTTP routes](../digging-deeper/testing.md#test-http-routes) for the server setup.

## See also

- [Testing](../digging-deeper/testing.md)
- [Migration](../database/migration.md)
- [Database: SQLite](../database/index.md#sqlite)


---

# Share code with Flutter

Source: https://dartondox.dev/latest/3.xguides/share-code-with-flutter/

# Share code with Flutter

Your server and your Flutter app are both written in Dart. So they can use the same code.
This guide puts a `@Dto` class in a shared package. The server checks requests with it.
The Flutter app checks the form with it, with the same rules and the same error messages, before it sends the request.

!!! note "This works, and it was tested"
    The generated DTO code imports only `dox_validation`. It does not need `dox_core`.
    `dox_validation` is pure Dart: it imports only `dart:async`. No `dart:io`, no `dart:mirrors`.
    Tested on 2026-10-22 with Dart 3.13.6 and Dox `3.0.0-alpha.4`. See [What was tested](#what-was-tested).

## The layout

```text
my_blog/
  packages/
    blog_shared/     # the DTOs. Pure Dart.
  server/            # the Dox app
  app/               # the Flutter app
```

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    S[packages/blog_shared<br>SaveBlog + SaveBlog.schema] --> A[app: Flutter<br>checks the form]
    S --> B[server: Dox<br>checks the request]
    A -- "POST /api/blogs (JSON)" --> B
```

## 1. The shared package

```yaml title="packages/blog_shared/pubspec.yaml"
name: blog_shared
description: DTOs shared by the Dox server and the Flutter app.
version: 0.1.0
publish_to: none

environment:
  sdk: ^3.13.0

dependencies:
  dox_validation: ^3.0.0-alpha.4

dev_dependencies:
  build_runner: ^2.17.1
  dox_builder: ^3.0.0-alpha.4
```

`dox_builder` is a dev dependency. It only runs when you generate code. The Flutter app does not get it.

Write the DTO. Import `dox_validation`, not `dox_core`:

```dart title="packages/blog_shared/lib/src/save_blog.dart"
import 'package:dox_validation/dox_validation.dart';

part 'save_blog.g.dart';

/// A new blog post. The server and the app check it with the same rules.
@Dto()
class SaveBlog {
  @Trim()
  @Length(min: 3, max: 255)
  final String title;

  @Trim()
  @MinLength(10)
  final String description;

  const SaveBlog({required this.title, required this.description});

  static const DtoSchema<SaveBlog> schema = $SaveBlogDto;
}
```

Export the DTOs. Also export `dox_validation`, so the app gets `ParseResult` and `ValidationException` from one import:

```dart title="packages/blog_shared/lib/blog_shared.dart"
export 'package:dox_validation/dox_validation.dart';

export 'src/save_blog.dart';
```

Generate the code:

```bash
cd packages/blog_shared
dart pub get
dart run build_runner build
```

This writes two files:

- `lib/src/save_blog.g.dart`: the checks, the converter and the JSON Schema of `SaveBlog`.
- `lib/dtos.g.dart`: the list of every DTO in this package. The server uses it.

Commit both files. Then the Flutter app does not need to run the generator.

!!! warning "Rules that need the database stay on the server"
    `@Unique` and `@Exists` come from `dox_orm`. Do not use them in the shared package: the app can not import `dox_orm`.
    Check them on the server, in the service or in a server-only DTO.
    A `validate()` method that is `async` also can not run with `safeParse`. Use `safeParseAsync` for it.

## 2. The Dox server

Add the shared package to the server:

```yaml title="server/pubspec.yaml"
name: server
publish_to: none

environment:
  sdk: ^3.13.0

dependencies:
  dox_core: ^3.0.0-alpha.4
  blog_shared:
    path: ../packages/blog_shared

dev_dependencies:
  build_runner: ^2.17.1
  dox_builder: ^3.0.0-alpha.4
```

Dox finds a DTO in the `dtos` list of `AppConfig`. The server's own `lib/dtos.g.dart` lists only the DTOs in the server.
So add the list of the shared package too:

```dart title="server/lib/config/app.dart"
import 'package:blog_shared/dtos.g.dart' as shared;
import 'package:dox_core/dox_core.dart';
import 'package:server/dtos.g.dart';

AppConfig appConfig = AppConfig(
  // ...
  dtos: <DtoSchema<Object>>[...dtos, ...shared.dtos],
);
```

When the server has no DTOs of its own, there is no `server/lib/dtos.g.dart`. Then use `dtos: shared.dtos`.

The controller asks for `SaveBlog` like any other DTO. Dox checks the body before the method runs. Bad input gets `422`.

```dart title="server/lib/app/http/controllers/blog.controller.dart"
import 'package:blog_shared/blog_shared.dart' show SaveBlog;

class BlogController {
  Future<Map<String, dynamic>> store(SaveBlog body) async {
    // body.title is already trimmed and checked.
    return <String, dynamic>{'title': body.title, 'saved': true};
  }
}
```

```dart title="server/lib/routes/api.dart"
Route.post('/blogs', BlogController().store);
```

!!! note "Why `show SaveBlog`"
    `dox_core` has its own `ValidationException` (it answers `422`). `blog_shared` exports the one from `dox_validation`.
    `show` keeps only the DTO from `blog_shared`, so the two names do not clash in server code.

A bad request gets the errors as `{"key": "message"}`:

```text
POST /api/blogs  {"title": "ab", "description": "short"}
422 {"title":"The title must be between 3 and 255 characters","description":"The description must be at least 10 characters"}
```

## 3. The Flutter app

```yaml title="app/pubspec.yaml"
name: app
publish_to: none

environment:
  sdk: ^3.13.0

dependencies:
  flutter:
    sdk: flutter
  http: ^1.6.0
  blog_shared:
    path: ../packages/blog_shared
```

The app does not depend on `dox_core`. It gets only `blog_shared` and `dox_validation`.

One widget: it checks the form with `SaveBlog.schema.safeParse(...)`. It sends the request only when the input is good.
`result.errors` has the same shape as the server's `422` body, so one `_errors` map shows both.

!!! note "Not run here"
    The Flutter widget below was not run in a Flutter app. The same calls were run in a plain Dart program and in JavaScript (see below).

```dart title="app/lib/new_blog_form.dart"
import 'dart:convert';

import 'package:blog_shared/blog_shared.dart';
import 'package:flutter/material.dart';
import 'package:http/http.dart' as http;

class NewBlogForm extends StatefulWidget {
  const NewBlogForm({super.key});

  @override
  State<NewBlogForm> createState() {
    return _NewBlogFormState();
  }
}

class _NewBlogFormState extends State<NewBlogForm> {
  final TextEditingController _title = TextEditingController();
  final TextEditingController _description = TextEditingController();
  Map<String, String> _errors = <String, String>{};

  Future<void> _submit() async {
    ParseResult<SaveBlog> result = SaveBlog.schema.safeParse(<String, dynamic>{
      'title': _title.text,
      'description': _description.text,
    });
    if (!result.success) {
      setState(() {
        _errors = result.errors;
      });
      return;
    }

    http.Response response = await http.post(
      Uri.parse('https://api.example.com/api/blogs'),
      headers: <String, String>{'Content-Type': 'application/json'},
      body: jsonEncode(SaveBlog.schema.toMap(result.value!)),
    );
    setState(() {
      _errors = response.statusCode == 422
          ? Map<String, String>.from(jsonDecode(response.body) as Map)
          : <String, String>{};
    });
  }

  @override
  void dispose() {
    _title.dispose();
    _description.dispose();
    super.dispose();
  }

  @override
  Widget build(BuildContext context) {
    return Column(
      children: <Widget>[
        TextField(
          controller: _title,
          decoration: InputDecoration(labelText: 'Title', errorText: _errors['title']),
        ),
        TextField(
          controller: _description,
          decoration: InputDecoration(labelText: 'Description', errorText: _errors['description']),
        ),
        ElevatedButton(onPressed: _submit, child: const Text('Save')),
      ],
    );
  }
}
```

The API of the schema:

| Call | Gives | On bad input |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `SaveBlog.schema.safeParse(map)` | `ParseResult<SaveBlog>` | `success` is `false`. `errors` has the first message per key. |
| `SaveBlog.schema.parse(map)` | `SaveBlog` | throws `ValidationException` |
| `SaveBlog.schema.toMap(blog)` | the JSON map, with the input keys (snake_case) | - |
| `SaveBlog.schema.toJsonSchema()` | the JSON Schema of the DTO | - |

Use `safeParseAsync` or `parseAsync` when the DTO has an `async` `validate()` method.
See [Validation](../the-basic/validation.md) and [dox_validation](../packages/validation.md) for all rules.

## What was tested

Three packages were made in a temp folder, with path dependencies to the Dox packages:

1. `blog_shared` with the `SaveBlog` DTO above. `dart run build_runner build` wrote `save_blog.g.dart` and `dtos.g.dart`.
   Both import only `package:dox_validation`. `dart analyze` found no issues.
2. A plain Dart console app that depends on `blog_shared` only. Its dependency tree has `dox_validation` and nothing else from Dox.
   `dart run` gave this output:

    ```text
    bad input ok? false
    errors: {title: The title must be between 3 and 255 characters, description: The description must be at least 10 characters}
    good input ok? true
    title after trim: "Hello Dox"
    json to send: {title: Hello Dox, description: A post about sharing code with Flutter.}
    parse threw: ValidationException
    ```

    The same app compiled with `dart compile js` and run in Node gave the same output. So the code also runs on the web.
3. A Dox server with `dox_core` and `blog_shared`, `dtos: shared.dtos`, and `Route.post('/blogs', BlogController().store)`.
   A bad body got `422` with the errors shown above. A good body got `200 {"title":"Hello Dox","saved":true}` (the title was trimmed).

Not tested here: the Flutter widget itself.


---

# API docs with OpenAPI

Source: https://dartondox.dev/latest/3.xguides/api-docs-with-openapi/

# API docs with OpenAPI

Your API gets docs for free. Turn on OpenAPI for the blog API, open the docs page, and make the docs better with a few comments and annotations.

## What you need

- The blog API from the [tutorial](../tutorial/01-create-project.md), or any Dox app.
- `build_runner` and `dox_builder`. A new app has both.

You do not add a package. `dox_core` already has `dox_openapi` in it.

## 1. Write the config

`dox_builder` already writes `lib/openapi.g.dart` when you run `build_runner`. It holds `openApiRegistry`: what the builder found in your routes, controllers, DTOs and models.
Pass it to an `OpenApiConfig`:

```dart title="lib/config/openapi.dart"
import 'package:dox_core/dox_core.dart';
import 'package:blog/openapi.g.dart';

OpenApiConfig openApi = OpenApiConfig(
  info: Info(title: 'Blog API', version: '1.0.0'),
  registry: openApiRegistry,
);
```

Add it to `AppConfig`:

```dart title="lib/config/app.dart"
import 'package:blog/config/openapi.dart';

AppConfig appConfig = AppConfig(
  // ...
  /// OpenAPI docs (config/openapi.dart)
  openApi: openApi,
);
```

## 2. Build and start

```bash
dart run build_runner build --delete-conflicting-outputs
dox serve
```

`.env` has `APP_ENV=development`, so the docs routes are on.

## 3. Open the docs page

Open `http://localhost:3000/docs` in a browser. It is a [Scalar](https://github.com/scalar/scalar) page.
It lists every route, with "Try it" buttons. It loads Scalar from the jsDelivr CDN and reads `/openapi.json`.

The app now has three new routes:

| Route | What it gives |
| --- | --- |
| `GET /docs` | the Scalar docs page (HTML) |
| `GET /openapi.json` | the OpenAPI 3.1 document as JSON |
| `GET /openapi.yaml` | the same document as YAML |

## 4. Read the JSON

```bash
curl http://localhost:3000/openapi.json
```

This is the real output for the blog API, shortened. The top level:

```json
{
  "openapi": "3.1.0",
  "info": {"title": "Blog API", "version": "1.0.0"},
  "paths": {
    "/ping": {},
    "/api/ping": {},
    "/api/posts": {},
    "/api/posts/{id}": {},
    "/api/auth/register": {},
    "/api/auth/login": {},
    "/api/auth/user": {}
  },
  "components": {
    "schemas": {"Post": {}, "SavePost": {}, "RegisterUser": {}, "LoginUser": {}, "User": {}, "ValidationError": {}},
    "securitySchemes": {
      "bearerAuth": {"type": "http", "scheme": "bearer", "bearerFormat": "JWT"}
    }
  }
}
```

`POST /api/posts`, as the builder found it. You wrote no docs code for it:

```json
{
  "tags": ["Post"],
  "summary": "POST /api/posts",
  "operationId": "PostController.store",
  "requestBody": {
    "required": true,
    "content": {"application/json": {"schema": {"$ref": "#/components/schemas/SavePost"}}}
  },
  "responses": {
    "200": {"description": "Successful response"},
    "401": {"description": "Not logged in"},
    "422": {
      "description": "Validation failed",
      "content": {"application/json": {"schema": {"$ref": "#/components/schemas/ValidationError"}}}
    },
    "500": {"description": "Server error"}
  },
  "security": [{"bearerAuth": []}]
}
```

Where each part comes from:

| Part | Comes from |
| --- | --- |
| `tags: ["Post"]` | the class name `PostController`, without `Controller` |
| `summary` | the first line of the `///` comment: `/// POST /api/posts` |
| `requestBody` | the argument `SavePost body` of `store` |
| `401` and `bearerAuth` | `AuthMiddleware` on the route |
| `422` | the route has a request class |
| `200` with no body | `store` returns `DoxResponse`, so the builder can not see the body. Step 6 fixes this |

## 5. See how a DTO becomes a schema

This is the `SavePost` DTO of the tutorial:

```dart title="lib/app/http/dtos/save_post.dto.dart"
@Dto()
class SavePost {
  @Trim()
  @Length(min: 3, max: 100)
  final String title;

  @Trim()
  @MinLength(10)
  final String body;

  const SavePost({required this.title, required this.body});

  static const DtoSchema<SavePost> schema = $SavePostDto;
}
```

And this is its schema in `/openapi.json`:

```json
"SavePost": {
  "type": "object",
  "title": "SavePost",
  "properties": {
    "title": {"type": "string", "minLength": 3, "maxLength": 100},
    "body": {"type": "string", "minLength": 10}
  },
  "required": ["title", "body"]
}
```

| In the DTO | In the schema |
| --- | --- |
| `String title` (not nullable) | `"type": "string"` and `title` in `required` |
| `@Length(min: 3, max: 100)` | `"minLength": 3, "maxLength": 100` |
| `@MinLength(10)` | `"minLength": 10` |
| `@Email()` (in `RegisterUser`) | `"format": "email"` |
| `@Trim()`, `@Lowercase()`, `@Unique(...)` | nothing. They change or check the value on the server only |

A model becomes a schema too. `Post` has `id`, the `@Column` fields `title` and `body`, and `created_at` and `updated_at`.
Keys in `hidden` are left out. That is why `User` has no `password`.

The docs and the validation come from the same DTO. When you change a rule, run `build_runner` again, and the docs change with it.

## 6. Make the docs better

Write a `///` comment on a controller method. The first line is the summary. The rest is the description.
Add `@Tags` and `@Response` when the automatic result is not what you want. They come from `dox_core`, so there is no new import.

```dart title="lib/app/http/controllers/post.controller.dart"
class PostController {
  /// List all posts
  ///
  /// Newest posts are not first. There is no paging yet.
  Future<List<Post>> index(DoxRequest req) async {
    return Post().all();
  }

  /// Create a post
  @Tags(<String>['Posts'])
  @Response(201, Post, description: 'The new post')
  Future<DoxResponse> store(SavePost body) async {
    Post post = Post()
      ..title = body.title
      ..body = body.body;
    await post.save();
    return response(post).statusCode(201);
  }

  // ...
}
```

Run `dart run build_runner build` again and restart the app. The real result:

```json
"get": {
  "tags": ["Post"],
  "summary": "List all posts",
  "description": "Newest posts are not first. There is no paging yet.",
  "operationId": "PostController.index"
},
"post": {
  "tags": ["Posts"],
  "summary": "Create a post",
  "operationId": "PostController.store",
  "responses": {
    "201": {
      "description": "The new post",
      "content": {"application/json": {"schema": {"$ref": "#/components/schemas/Post"}}}
    },
    "401": {},
    "422": {},
    "500": {}
  }
}
```

- `@Response(201, Post)` replaces the empty `200`. The docs now match the real status code.
- `@Tags(['Posts'])` moves the route to the group "Posts" in the docs page.
- `@Summary('...')` and `@Description('...')` set the text without a `///` comment.
- `@ApiIgnore()` leaves a method (or a whole controller) out of the docs.

See [OpenAPI: change the docs](../packages/openapi.md#change-the-docs-optional) for all annotations.

## 7. Turn it off in production

You do not need to do anything. `enabled` is `null` by default. Then the docs routes are on only when `APP_ENV` is `development` or `local`.

With `APP_ENV=production` all three routes give `404`:

```bash
curl -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}\n' http://localhost:3000/docs           # 404
curl -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}\n' http://localhost:3000/openapi.json   # 404
```

To show the docs on staging too, but never in production, set `enabled` yourself:

```dart title="lib/config/openapi.dart"
OpenApiConfig openApi = OpenApiConfig(
  enabled: env.appEnv != 'production',
  info: Info(title: 'Blog API', version: '1.0.0'),
  registry: openApiRegistry,
);
```

!!! warning
    `enabled: true` in production shows every route of your API to anyone. Only do it for a public API.

To give the document to a front-end team without a running server, write it to files with `dox openapi:generate`.
See [OpenAPI: write the files](../packages/openapi.md#write-the-files-dox-openapigenerate).

## Check it

```bash
curl -s http://localhost:3000/openapi.json | head -n 5
```

```text
{
  "openapi": "3.1.0",
  "info": {
    "title": "Blog API",
    "version": "1.0.0"
```

Open `http://localhost:3000/docs`, find "Create a post" under "Posts", and send a request with "Try it".

## See also

- [OpenAPI](../packages/openapi.md) for all options, the Scalar look, Swagger UI and login schemes
- [Validation rules](../the-basic/validation-rules.md) for the rules and their JSON Schema keys
- [Environments](environments.md) for `APP_ENV`
