# Docker

Source: https://dartondox.dev/latest/3.xguides/docker/

# Docker

Build a small production image with `dox build`, and run it with Postgres in Docker Compose, with a health check.

## What you need

- A Dox app with a database.
- Docker with Compose.

## 1. Add a health route

The health check asks this route. It fails when the database does not answer.

```dart title="lib/app/http/controllers/health.controller.dart"
import 'package:dox_core/dox_core.dart';
import 'package:dox_orm/dox_orm.dart';

class HealthController {
  /// GET /health. 200 when the app and the database answer.
  /// Any database error becomes a 500, so the health check fails.
  Future<Map<String, String>> check(DoxRequest req) async {
    await QueryBuilder.query('select 1');
    return <String, String>{'status': 'ok'};
  }
}

HealthController healthController = HealthController();
```

```dart title="lib/routes/web.dart"
Route.get('/health', healthController.check);
```

## 2. Add the health check binary

The final image is `FROM scratch`. It has no shell and no `curl`. So the health check is a second small Dart binary.

```dart title="bin/health.dart"
import 'dart:io';

/// Docker health check. The final image has no shell and no curl,
/// so this small binary asks the app itself. Exit 0 = healthy.
Future<void> main() async {
  String port = Platform.environment['APP_PORT'] ?? '3000';
  HttpClient client = HttpClient()
    ..connectionTimeout = const Duration(seconds: 3);
  try {
    HttpClientRequest request = await client.getUrl(
      Uri.parse('http://127.0.0.1:$port/health'),
    );
    HttpClientResponse response = await request.close();
    exit(response.statusCode == 200 ? 0 : 1);
  } catch (_) {
    exit(1);
  }
}
```

## 3. Write the Dockerfile

Two stages. The first one has the Dart SDK and the `dox` CLI, and builds the AOT bundle.
The second one has only the Dart runtime files and the bundle. No SDK, no source, no shell.

```dockerfile title="Dockerfile"
# Stage 1: build the AOT bundle with the Dart SDK and the dox CLI.
FROM dart:stable AS build

WORKDIR /app

# Resolve dependencies first, so Docker caches this layer.
COPY pubspec.* ./
RUN dart pub get

COPY . .
RUN dart pub get --offline

# `dox build` runs build_runner, then `dart build cli`.
# The bundle is in build/bundle: bin/server, lib/, db/, .env.example
RUN dart pub global activate dox 3.0.0-alpha.4 \
  && /root/.pub-cache/bin/dox build

# The health check binary. Plain dart:io, so `dart compile exe` is fine.
RUN dart compile exe bin/health.dart -o build/bundle/bin/health

# Lay out the final file tree. /tmp must be writable: uploads bigger
# than 1 MB are streamed to a temp file.
RUN mkdir -p /out/app/storage /out/app/public /out/tmp \
  && chmod 1777 /out/tmp \
  && cp -r build/bundle/. /out/app/ \
  && cp -r public/. /out/app/public/ \
  # the native HTTP server (Rust) needs libgcc_s, which /runtime/ does not have
  && LIBGCC=$(find / -name libgcc_s.so.1 -path '*lib*' | head -n 1) \
  && mkdir -p /out$(dirname $LIBGCC) && cp $LIBGCC /out$LIBGCC

# Stage 2: the Dart AOT runtime and the bundle only. No SDK, no source.
FROM scratch
COPY --from=build /runtime/ /
COPY --from=build /out/ /
WORKDIR /app

# Config comes from env variables. The image has no .env file.
EXPOSE 3000
HEALTHCHECK --interval=15s --timeout=5s --start-period=10s --retries=3 \
  CMD ["/app/bin/health"]
CMD ["/app/bin/server"]
```

Delete the `public` lines when your app has no `public` folder.

Check the start log in the container. It must end with `(native)`:

```text
Server started at http://[::]:3000 with 8 isolate (native)
```

Without the `libgcc_s` lines, the native HTTP server does not load in a
`scratch` image. Dox then prints `dox_http_native did not load, using the
dart:io server` and runs on the slower `dart:io` server.

!!! warning "`dox build`, not `dart compile exe`"
    `dox_orm` bundles SQLite with a build hook. `dart compile exe` does not run build hooks and stops with an error.
    `dox build` runs `dart build cli`, which does. It puts the native libraries in `build/bundle/lib`, next to `bin/server`.

Keep the build context small:

```text title=".dockerignore"
.dart_tool/
.git/
.github/
.idea/
build/
storage/
.env
.env.*
!.env.example
Dockerfile
docker-compose.yml
pubspec_overrides.yaml
```

## 4. Write the compose file

The app reads its config from env variables. `env_file: .env` gives it your `.env`. The lines under `environment` win over the file, so the app always talks to the `postgres` service.

```yaml title="docker-compose.yml"
services:
  app:
    build: .
    # secrets and config come from .env, never from the image
    env_file: .env
    environment:
      APP_ENV: production
      APP_PORT: 3000
      DB_CONNECTION: postgres
      DB_HOST: postgres
      DB_PORT: 5432
    ports:
      - "3000:3000"
    volumes:
      # uploads survive a new image
      - uploads:/app/storage
    depends_on:
      postgres:
        condition: service_healthy
    restart: unless-stopped

  postgres:
    image: postgres:18
    environment:
      POSTGRES_USER: ${DB_USERNAME:-postgres}
      POSTGRES_PASSWORD: ${DB_PASSWORD:?set DB_PASSWORD in .env}
      POSTGRES_DB: ${DB_NAME:-dox}
    volumes:
      - postgres:/var/lib/postgresql
    healthcheck:
      test: ["CMD", "pg_isready", "-q", "-U", "${DB_USERNAME:-postgres}"]
      interval: 5s
      retries: 10
    restart: unless-stopped

volumes:
  postgres:
  uploads:
```

- `depends_on` with `service_healthy`: the app starts after Postgres answers. The app runs the migrations at start, so the database must be up.
- `${DB_PASSWORD:?...}`: compose stops with a clear message when `.env` has no password.
- `restart: unless-stopped`: when the main isolate dies, the process exits and Docker starts it again.

## 5. Write the `.env`

```ini title=".env"
APP_NAME=my_app
APP_ENV=production
APP_KEY=<output of dox key:generate>
APP_PORT=3000

DB_CONNECTION=postgres
DB_NAME=my_app
DB_USERNAME=postgres
DB_PASSWORD=<a real password>
```

`.env` is in `.dockerignore` and `.gitignore`. It never goes into the image or into git.

## 6. Build and run

```bash
docker compose up -d --build
docker compose ps
```

## Check it

```bash
docker compose ps
```

```text
NAME             STATUS
my_app-app-1       Up 30 seconds (healthy)
my_app-postgres-1  Up 35 seconds (healthy)
```

```bash
curl http://localhost:3000/health
```

```json
{"status":"ok"}
```

Stop Postgres with `docker compose stop postgres`. After about 45 seconds, `docker compose ps` shows the app as `unhealthy`.

## HTTPS

Do not add TLS to the app. Put Caddy or nginx in front, and set `trustedProxies` in `AppConfig`.
See [Deployment: HTTPS](../digging-deeper/deployment.md#https-put-a-proxy-in-front).

## See also

- [Deployment](../digging-deeper/deployment.md) for `dox build`, the bundle layout and systemd
- [Environments](environments.md) for dev, staging and production config
- [Migration: run on server start](../database/migration.md#run-on-server-start)


---

# Deploy to a Linux server

Source: https://dartondox.dev/latest/3.xguides/deploy-vps/

# Deploy to a Linux server

Run the blog API on your own Linux server (a VPS), with systemd to keep it running and Caddy in front for HTTPS.

!!! note
    These steps follow the systemd and Caddy docs as of 2026-10-22. They were not run on a real VPS in CI.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  client[Browser or app] -- "HTTPS :443" --> caddy[Caddy]
  caddy -- "HTTP 127.0.0.1:3000" --> dox["/opt/blog/bin/server (systemd)"]
```

## What you need

- A Linux server (Debian 12, Ubuntu 22.04 or newer) with SSH and `sudo`.
- A domain name. Its `A` (and `AAAA`) record points to the server.
- Docker on your machine, to build a Linux binary.
- The blog API from the [tutorial](../tutorial/01-create-project.md), or any Dox app.

## 1. Build the bundle for Linux

`dox build` makes a native binary for the system it runs on. A binary built on macOS does not run on Linux.
So build it inside the `dart:stable` image (it is Debian):

```bash
docker run --rm -v "$PWD":/app -w /app dart:stable sh -c \
  'dart pub get && dart pub global activate dox 3.0.0-alpha.4 && /root/.pub-cache/bin/dox build'
```

The result is `build/bundle/`:

```text
build/bundle/
  bin/server                         the AOT binary
  lib/dox_http_native-linux-*.so     the native HTTP server
  lib/libsqlite3.so                  SQLite
  db/                                the migrations
  .env.example
```

The container shares your project folder. It writes Linux paths into `.dart_tool/`.
So run `dart pub get` on your machine again before you use `dox serve`.

Keep `bin/` and `lib/` together. The binary loads the libraries from `../lib`.
See [Deployment](../digging-deeper/deployment.md#build) for more about the bundle.

!!! warning "Match the CPU of the server"
    Docker builds for the CPU of your machine. On a Mac with Apple silicon that is `arm64`.
    Most VPS plans are `x86_64`. For them, add `--platform linux/amd64` after `docker run`.
    Check the server with `uname -m`.

## 2. Make a user and the folders

Run this on the server. The app runs as the user `dox`. This user can not log in.

```bash
sudo useradd --system --no-create-home --shell /usr/sbin/nologin dox
sudo mkdir -p /opt/blog
sudo install -d -o dox -g dox /opt/blog/storage
```

| Path | What it holds | Owner |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `/opt/blog` | the bundle (`bin/`, `lib/`, `db/`) | `root` |
| `/opt/blog/storage` | files the app writes (uploads, file cache) | `dox` |
| `/var/lib/blog` | the SQLite file. systemd makes it (see step 5) | `dox` |
| `/etc/blog.env` | config and secrets | `root`, mode `600` |

## 3. Copy the bundle to the server

```bash
rsync -a --delete --exclude storage/ build/bundle/ you@server:/tmp/blog-bundle/
ssh you@server 'sudo rsync -a --delete --exclude storage/ /tmp/blog-bundle/ /opt/blog/'
```

## 4. Write the env file

```ini title="/etc/blog.env"
APP_NAME=blog
APP_ENV=production
APP_PORT=3000
APP_KEY=<output of dox key:generate>

DB_CONNECTION=sqlite
DB_NAME=/var/lib/blog/blog.sqlite
```

```bash
sudo chown root:root /etc/blog.env
sudo chmod 600 /etc/blog.env
```

systemd reads this file as `root`, before it starts the app as `dox`. So `dox` does not need to read it.

For Postgres, set `DB_CONNECTION=postgres` and add `DB_HOST`, `DB_PORT`, `DB_USERNAME`, `DB_PASSWORD` and `DB_NAME`.
Or set one `DATABASE_URL`, like `postgres://app:secret@localhost:5432/blog`. It wins over the `DB_*` keys. See [`DATABASE_URL`](../database/index.md#database_url).
See [Environments](environments.md) for all keys.

!!! note "Which value wins"
    `Env.get()` reads a real environment variable first. It reads the `.env` file in the working folder only when the variable is not set.
    systemd gives the app the lines of `EnvironmentFile` as real environment variables.
    So `/etc/blog.env` wins over a `/opt/blog/.env`. Do not put a `.env` in `/opt/blog`, so there is only one place to look.

## 5. Write the systemd unit

```ini title="/etc/systemd/system/blog.service"
[Unit]
Description=Blog API (Dox)
After=network-online.target
Wants=network-online.target

[Service]
Type=simple
User=dox
Group=dox
# the binary reads db/ and .env from this folder
WorkingDirectory=/opt/blog
EnvironmentFile=/etc/blog.env
ExecStart=/opt/blog/bin/server
# start again after a crash, and after `kill`
Restart=always
RestartSec=2
# makes /var/lib/blog, owned by the user dox
StateDirectory=blog
# small safety settings
NoNewPrivileges=true
PrivateTmp=true
ProtectSystem=full

[Install]
WantedBy=multi-user.target
```

```bash
sudo systemctl daemon-reload
sudo systemctl enable --now blog
systemctl status blog
```

- `Restart=always`: when the main isolate dies, the process exits and systemd starts it again. See [Deployment: keep it running](../digging-deeper/deployment.md#keep-it-running).
- The app runs the migrations at start, before it takes requests.
- Dox starts one isolate per CPU core. Set `APP_TOTAL_ISOLATE` in `/etc/blog.env` to change it.

## 6. Close the app port

Caddy runs on the same machine. So let Dox listen on `127.0.0.1` only. Add this line to `/etc/blog.env`:

```ini title="/etc/blog.env"
APP_HOST=127.0.0.1
```

Now only programs on this machine can reach port `3000`.
Also turn on a firewall, so only SSH, HTTP and HTTPS are open:

```bash
sudo ufw default deny incoming
sudo ufw allow OpenSSH
sudo ufw allow 80/tcp
sudo ufw allow 443/tcp
sudo ufw enable
```

## 7. Put Caddy in front

Install Caddy from its [install page](https://caddyserver.com/docs/install). The Debian package runs Caddy with systemd and reads `/etc/caddy/Caddyfile`.

```text title="/etc/caddy/Caddyfile"
api.example.com {
	encode zstd gzip

	reverse_proxy 127.0.0.1:3000 {
		# while the app restarts, wait up to 10s for it instead of failing
		lb_try_duration 10s
		lb_try_interval 250ms
	}
}
```

```bash
sudo caddy validate --config /etc/caddy/Caddyfile
sudo systemctl reload caddy
```

- Caddy gets a TLS certificate for `api.example.com` by itself. Ports 80 and 443 must be open.
- `reverse_proxy` sets `X-Forwarded-For` and `X-Forwarded-Proto`.

## 8. Trust Caddy in the app

Dox ignores `X-Forwarded-For` and `X-Forwarded-Proto` until you list the proxy in `trustedProxies`.
Caddy talks to the app from the same server:

```dart title="lib/config/app.dart"
AppConfig appConfig = AppConfig(
  // ...
  trustedProxies: <String>['127.0.0.1', '::1'],
);
```

Now `req.ip()` is the real client IP and `req.scheme()` is `https`.
Build and copy again after this change (steps 1 and 3). See [Deployment: HTTPS](../digging-deeper/deployment.md#https-put-a-proxy-in-front).

## Check it

```bash
curl https://api.example.com/api/ping
```

```text
pong
```

Read the logs. In production the app writes one JSON line per log.

```bash
journalctl -u blog -f                     # follow new lines
journalctl -u blog --since "1 hour ago"   # the last hour
journalctl -u blog -b                     # since the last boot
```

The first lines after a start look like this:

```text
Migrating: 2026_10_22_205345_create_posts_table
Migrated: 2026_10_22_205345_create_posts_table
{"level":"INFO","name":"dox","message":"Server started at http://127.0.0.1:3000 with 2 isolate (native)", ...}
```

`(native)` means the native HTTP server loaded. `(dart:io)` means it did not, and the line before it says why.

Check that the app port is closed. From your machine:

```bash
curl -m 5 http://api.example.com:3000/api/ping   # must time out
```

## Update the app

1. Build a new bundle (step 1).
2. Copy it to the server (step 3). Keep the old one first, so you can go back:

    ```bash
    ssh you@server 'sudo rm -rf /opt/blog.prev && sudo cp -a /opt/blog /opt/blog.prev'
    rsync -a --delete --exclude storage/ build/bundle/ you@server:/tmp/blog-bundle/
    ssh you@server 'sudo rsync -a --delete --exclude storage/ /tmp/blog-bundle/ /opt/blog/'
    ```

3. Restart the app. It runs new migrations at start.

    ```bash
    ssh you@server 'sudo systemctl restart blog'
    ```

4. Read the logs (`journalctl -u blog -n 20`) and run the check.

To go back: copy `/opt/blog.prev` to `/opt/blog` and restart. A migration that already ran is not undone.

!!! note "A restart is short, but not zero"
    A restart takes about one second. Dox does not wait for open requests when it stops, so a request that is running at that moment fails.
    New requests do not fail: `lb_try_duration` makes Caddy wait for the app to come back.
    For a real zero-downtime update, run two copies on two ports and list both in Caddy. See [Deployment: many processes](../digging-deeper/deployment.md#many-processes-or-machines).

## See also

- [Deployment](../digging-deeper/deployment.md) for `dox build`, Docker, nginx and many processes
- [Environments](environments.md) for config per environment and `APP_KEY`
- [Docker](docker.md) to run the app and Postgres with Docker Compose
- [Native server](../digging-deeper/native-server.md)


---

# Deploy to Fly.io

Source: https://dartondox.dev/latest/3.xguides/deploy-fly/

# Deploy to Fly.io

Run the blog API on [Fly.io](https://fly.io) from the `Dockerfile` of your project, with SQLite on a volume or with Postgres.

!!! note
    These steps follow the Fly.io docs as of 2026-10-22 (checked on 2026-10-22). They were not run on Fly.io in CI.
    The Docker image itself was built and run locally.

## What you need

- A Fly.io account and the `fly` CLI (`fly auth login`).
- The blog API from the [tutorial](../tutorial/01-create-project.md), or any Dox app, with the `Dockerfile` of a new Dox app.
  See [Deployment: Docker](../digging-deeper/deployment.md#docker) for how that file works.

The image is small. For the blog API it is about 17 MB. Fly builds it for you on `fly deploy`.

!!! note "Check for `(native)`"
    The project's `Dockerfile` copies `libgcc_s.so.1` into the image, so the
    native HTTP server loads. The start log ends with `(native)`. If it says
    `using the dart:io server`, see [Docker](docker.md).

## 1. Make the app on Fly.io

In the project folder:

```bash
fly launch --no-deploy
```

`fly launch` finds the `Dockerfile`, asks for an app name and a region, and writes `fly.toml`.
`--no-deploy` stops before the first deploy, so you can set the config first.

## 2. Write `fly.toml`

Replace the file with this one. Change `app` and `primary_region` to your values.

```toml title="fly.toml"
app = "blog-api"
primary_region = "ams"
# Dox waits up to 8 seconds for open requests on stop. Fly waits 5 by default.
kill_timeout = 10

[build]
  dockerfile = "Dockerfile"

# config that is not secret. Secrets come from `fly secrets set`.
[env]
  APP_ENV = "production"
  APP_PORT = "3000"
  DB_CONNECTION = "sqlite"
  DB_NAME = "/data/blog.sqlite"

[http_service]
  internal_port = 3000
  force_https = true
  # one machine, always on: the SQLite file is on its volume
  auto_stop_machines = "off"
  auto_start_machines = true
  min_machines_running = 1

  [[http_service.checks]]
    grace_period = "10s"
    interval = "30s"
    method = "GET"
    timeout = "5s"
    path = "/api/ping"

# the volume with the SQLite file
[mounts]
  source = "blog_data"
  destination = "/data"

[[vm]]
  memory = "256mb"
  cpu_kind = "shared"
  cpus = 1
```

- `internal_port` is the port the app listens on. Dox reads it from `APP_PORT` (or `PORT` when `APP_PORT` is not set). Keep the two the same.
- Values in `[env]` must be strings, so write `"3000"`, not `3000`.
- `[[vm]]` wins over `fly scale vm`. Each `fly deploy` sets the machine to these values.
- `kill_timeout` is how long Fly waits after `SIGINT` before it kills the app. Keep it above `shutdownTimeout` of `AppConfig` (8 seconds by default). See [Graceful shutdown](../digging-deeper/deployment.md#graceful-shutdown).

## 3. Set the secrets

```bash
fly secrets set APP_KEY=<output of dox key:generate>
```

A secret is an environment variable on every machine of the app. `fly secrets list` shows the names, not the values.
A secret with the same name as an `[env]` key wins.

## 4. Choose a database

### SQLite on a volume

Make the volume that `[mounts]` asks for, in the same region:

```bash
fly volumes create blog_data --region ams --size 1
```

- One volume is attached to one machine only. Fly.io does not copy the data between volumes.
- So with SQLite, run exactly one machine.

### Postgres

Create a Fly.io Managed Postgres cluster with `fly mpg create`.

Attach it to the app:

```bash
fly mpg attach <cluster-id> --app blog-api
```

`fly mpg attach` sets one secret, `DATABASE_URL`. Dox reads it. When `DATABASE_URL` is set, it wins over `DB_CONNECTION` and the other `DB_*` keys. The app and the migrations both use it. See [`DATABASE_URL`](../database/index.md#database_url).

Then delete `DB_CONNECTION` and `DB_NAME` from `[env]`, and delete the `[mounts]` section.
If the database asks for TLS, add `?sslmode=require` to the url with `fly secrets set DATABASE_URL=...`.

## 5. Deploy

```bash
fly deploy
```

`fly deploy` builds the image from the `Dockerfile`, makes the machine and starts it.
The app runs the migrations at start.

Check that there is one machine:

```bash
fly scale show
```

If the count is more than 1 and you use SQLite, run `fly scale count 1`.

## Check it

```bash
curl https://blog-api.fly.dev/api/ping
```

```text
pong
```

```bash
fly status    # the machines and their state
fly logs      # the app logs, live
```

The first log lines after a start:

```text
Migrating: 2026_10_22_205345_create_posts_table
Migrated: 2026_10_22_205345_create_posts_table
{"level":"INFO","name":"dox","message":"Server started at http://[::]:3000 with 1 isolate (native)", ...}
```

## HTTPS and the client IP

Fly.io ends TLS and sends plain HTTP to port 3000. `force_https = true` sends HTTP visitors to HTTPS.
To make `req.ip()` and `req.scheme()` show the real client, set `trustedProxies` in `AppConfig`.
The app port is reachable only through the Fly.io proxy, so `['*']` is safe here:

```dart title="lib/config/app.dart"
AppConfig appConfig = AppConfig(
  // ...
  trustedProxies: <String>['*'],
);
```

See [Deployment: HTTPS](../digging-deeper/deployment.md#https-put-a-proxy-in-front).

## More CPU, more machines

Dox starts one isolate per CPU core it sees. On `cpus = 1` that is one isolate.

| You want | Do this |
| --- | --- |
| more speed on one machine | raise `cpus` in `[[vm]]` (and `memory`), then `fly deploy`. Dox uses the new cores by itself |
| more machines | use Postgres, then `fly scale count 2`. With SQLite, stay at one machine |
| a fixed number of isolates | set `APP_TOTAL_ISOLATE` in `[env]` |

Each machine is its own process. WebSocket rooms and the memory cache are not shared between machines.

## Update the app

```bash
fly deploy
```

- Change config in `[env]` and run `fly deploy` again.
- `fly secrets set` restarts the machines with the new value. With `--stage` it only saves the value, and the next deploy uses it.
- The app runs new migrations at start.
- With one machine there is a short gap while it restarts.

## See also

- [Deployment](../digging-deeper/deployment.md) for the bundle and the `Dockerfile`
- [Environments](environments.md) for all env keys and `APP_KEY`
- [Docker](docker.md) for a health check binary and Docker Compose
- Fly.io docs: [fly.toml](https://fly.io/docs/reference/configuration/), [secrets](https://fly.io/docs/apps/secrets/), [volumes](https://fly.io/docs/volumes/overview/), [Managed Postgres](https://fly.io/docs/mpg/)

# Deploy to Google Cloud Run

Source: https://dartondox.dev/latest/3.xguides/deploy-cloud-run/

# Deploy to Google Cloud Run

Run the blog API on [Cloud Run](https://cloud.google.com/run) from the `Dockerfile` of your project, with Postgres on Cloud SQL and secrets in Secret Manager.

!!! note
    These steps follow the Cloud Run docs as of 2026-10-22 (checked on 2026-10-22). They were not run on Cloud Run in CI.
    The Docker image itself was built and run locally.

## What you need

- A Google Cloud project with billing, and the `gcloud` CLI (`gcloud auth login`, `gcloud config set project PROJECT_ID`).
- The blog API from the [tutorial](../tutorial/01-create-project.md), or any Dox app, with the `Dockerfile` of a new Dox app.
  See [Deployment: Docker](../digging-deeper/deployment.md#docker) for how that file works.
- A Cloud SQL for PostgreSQL instance with a database and a user. See step 3.

The image is small. For the blog API it is about 17 MB.

!!! note "Check for `(native)`"
    The project's `Dockerfile` copies `libgcc_s.so.1` into the image, so the
    native HTTP server loads. The start log ends with `(native)`. If it says
    `using the dart:io server`, see [Docker](docker.md).

## The port: `PORT` and `APP_PORT`

Cloud Run sends requests to one port of the container. It puts that port in the `PORT` env variable. The default is `8080`.

Dox listens on `APP_PORT` when it is set. When `APP_PORT` is not set, Dox listens on `PORT`.
So do not set `APP_PORT` on Cloud Run. The app then follows `PORT`, and you can leave out `--port`.

If you do set `APP_PORT`, tell Cloud Run the same port:

```bash
gcloud run deploy blog --port 3000 ...
```

## 1. Turn on the APIs

```bash
gcloud services enable run.googleapis.com cloudbuild.googleapis.com \
  artifactregistry.googleapis.com secretmanager.googleapis.com sqladmin.googleapis.com
```

## 2. Save the secrets in Secret Manager

```bash
openssl rand -hex 16 | tr -d '\n' | gcloud secrets create blog-app-key --data-file=-
printf '%s' '<the database password>' | gcloud secrets create blog-db-password --data-file=-
```

Let the Cloud Run service account read them. By default this is the Compute Engine service account, `PROJECT_NUMBER-compute@developer.gserviceaccount.com`:

```bash
for s in blog-app-key blog-db-password; do
  gcloud secrets add-iam-policy-binding "$s" \
    --member="serviceAccount:PROJECT_NUMBER-compute@developer.gserviceaccount.com" \
    --role="roles/secretmanager.secretAccessor"
done
```

## 3. Reach Cloud SQL

Cloud Run has two ways to reach Cloud SQL: a Unix socket in `/cloudsql/...`, or the private IP over a VPC.

Dox can use both. The Unix socket needs no VPC, so this guide uses it:

1. Find the connection name of the instance: `gcloud sql instances describe INSTANCE --format='value(connectionName)'`. It looks like `PROJECT_ID:europe-west1:INSTANCE`.
2. Deploy with `--add-cloudsql-instances <connection name>` (step 4). Cloud Run then makes the socket in `/cloudsql/<connection name>`.
3. Give the service account the `roles/cloudsql.client` role.
4. Set `DB_HOST=/cloudsql/<connection name>`. A host that starts with `/` is a Unix socket folder. See [Unix socket](../database/index.md#unix-socket).

The same with one url: `DATABASE_URL=postgres://blog:<password>@/blog?host=/cloudsql/<connection name>`.

To use the **private IP** instead: give the instance a private IP on your VPC network, deploy with Direct VPC egress (`--network default --subnet default --vpc-egress private-ranges-only`), and use the private IP as `DB_HOST`.

Do not use SQLite on Cloud Run. The file system of an instance is in memory, and each instance has its own. The data is lost when the instance stops.

## 4. Deploy from source

`--source .` uploads the folder. Cloud Build builds the image with your `Dockerfile` and saves it in Artifact Registry (in a repository named `cloud-run-source-deploy`).

```bash
gcloud run deploy blog \
  --source . \
  --region europe-west1 \
  --port 3000 \
  --allow-unauthenticated \
  --cpu 1 --memory 512Mi \
  --min-instances 1 \
  --add-cloudsql-instances PROJECT_ID:europe-west1:INSTANCE \
  --set-env-vars APP_ENV=production,APP_TOTAL_ISOLATE=1,DB_CONNECTION=postgres,DB_HOST=/cloudsql/PROJECT_ID:europe-west1:INSTANCE,DB_PORT=5432,DB_NAME=blog,DB_USERNAME=blog \
  --set-secrets APP_KEY=blog-app-key:1,DB_PASSWORD=blog-db-password:1
```

| Flag | Why |
| --- | --- |
| `--port 3000` | the port Cloud Run sends requests to. It also sets `PORT=3000`, and Dox listens on `PORT`. See [the port](#the-port-port-and-app_port) |
| `--min-instances 1` | keeps one instance warm, so the first request does not wait for a cold start. The default is `0`. An idle instance still costs money |
| `--add-cloudsql-instances` | makes the Cloud SQL Unix socket in `/cloudsql/...` |
| `--set-env-vars` | config that is not secret |
| `--set-secrets` | `ENV_NAME=SECRET:VERSION`. Cloud Run reads the secret when an instance starts. Pin a version number, not `latest` |
| `APP_TOTAL_ISOLATE=1` | one isolate per CPU. Set it to the `--cpu` value |

To build the image yourself instead, push it to Artifact Registry and deploy it with `--image`:

```bash
docker build --platform linux/amd64 -t europe-west1-docker.pkg.dev/PROJECT_ID/blog/api:1 .
docker push europe-west1-docker.pkg.dev/PROJECT_ID/blog/api:1
gcloud run deploy blog --image europe-west1-docker.pkg.dev/PROJECT_ID/blog/api:1 --region europe-west1 --port 3000 ...
```

Use the same other flags as above.

## Check it

`gcloud run deploy` prints the service URL at the end.

```bash
curl https://blog-xxxxxxxx-ew.a.run.app/api/ping
```

```text
pong
```

```bash
gcloud run services logs read blog --region europe-west1 --limit 20
gcloud beta run services logs tail blog --region europe-west1   # live, needs the log-streaming component
```

The first log lines after a start:

```text
Migrating: 2026_10_22_205345_create_posts_table
Migrated: 2026_10_22_205345_create_posts_table
{"level":"INFO","name":"dox","message":"Server started at http://[::]:3000 with 1 isolate (native)", ...}
```

If the deploy fails with "the container did not listen on the port", the app listens on a different port than `--port`. Check `APP_PORT` and `--port`.

## HTTPS and the client IP

Cloud Run ends TLS and sends plain HTTP to the container. Only the Cloud Run front end can reach the container port.
So `['*']` in `trustedProxies` is safe, and `req.ip()` and `req.scheme()` then show the real client:

```dart title="lib/config/app.dart"
AppConfig appConfig = AppConfig(
  // ...
  trustedProxies: <String>['*'],
);
```

See [Deployment: HTTPS](../digging-deeper/deployment.md#https-put-a-proxy-in-front).

## Update the app

```bash
gcloud run deploy blog --source . --region europe-west1
```

- Cloud Run keeps the flags of the last revision. You only pass what changes.
- A new revision starts, runs new migrations, and takes the traffic when it listens on the port. The old one then stops.
- When many instances start at the same time, each one runs the migrations. Keep migrations safe to run twice, or run one instance during a deploy with a migration.
- A new secret version: create it with `gcloud secrets versions add`, then deploy with the new number in `--update-secrets APP_KEY=blog-app-key:2`.

## See also

- [Deployment](../digging-deeper/deployment.md) for the bundle and the `Dockerfile`
- [Environments](environments.md) for all env keys and `APP_KEY`
- [Docker](docker.md) for a health check binary and Docker Compose
- Cloud Run docs: [container contract](https://cloud.google.com/run/docs/container-contract), [deploy from source](https://cloud.google.com/run/docs/deploying-source-code), [secrets](https://cloud.google.com/run/docs/configuring/services/secrets), [minimum instances](https://cloud.google.com/run/docs/configuring/min-instances), [Cloud SQL](https://cloud.google.com/sql/docs/postgres/connect-run)

# Cheat sheet

Source: https://dartondox.dev/latest/3.xreference/cheat-sheet/

# Cheat sheet

One page to keep open while you work. Each section links to its full page.

## Project layout

| Path | What is in it |
| --- | --- |
| `bin/server.dart` | starts the app: `Dox().initialize()`, migrations, `startServer()` |
| `bin/migrate.dart` | runs migrations for `dox migration:*` |
| `bin/openapi.dart` | writes the OpenAPI files for `dox openapi:generate` |
| `lib/config/` | `app.dart` (`AppConfig`), `env.dart`, `database.dart`, `cors.dart`, `cache.dart`, `storage.dart`, `openapi.dart`, `services.dart`, `logger.dart`, `socketio.dart` |
| `lib/routes/` | `api.dart`, `web.dart`, `websocket.dart`: one `Router` class each |
| `lib/app/http/controllers/` | `<name>.controller.dart` |
| `lib/app/http/dtos/` | `<name>.dto.dart` |
| `lib/app/http/middleware/` | `<name>.middleware.dart` |
| `lib/app/http/serializers/` | `<name>.serializer.dart` |
| `lib/app/models/<name>/` | `<name>.model.dart` |
| `lib/services/` | `DoxService` classes: ORM, auth, websocket |
| `lib/dtos.g.dart`, `lib/openapi.g.dart` | made by `build_runner`. Do not edit. |
| `db/migration/` | migrations and `migrations.dart` (the registry) |

See [CLI](cli.md) and [App config](app-config.md).

## CLI

```bash
dox create my_app --version 3.0.0-alpha.4
dox serve                          # dev server + build_runner watch
dox build                          # AOT bundle in build/bundle
dox build_runner:build             # make .g.dart files
dox key:generate                   # APP_KEY in .env
dox env:generate                   # lib/config/env.dart from .env.example
dox env:check                      # check the env, exit 1 when bad
dox create:controller Blog [-r] [-ws]
dox create:middleware Auth
dox create:dto CreateBlog
dox create:serializer Blog
dox create:model Blog -m           # model + migration
dox make:migration create_blogs_table [--sql]
dox migrate                        # migration:run
dox migration:rollback --step=1
dox migration:status
dox openapi:generate [dir]
```

See [CLI](cli.md).

## Routes

```dart
class ApiRouter extends Router {
  @override
  String get prefix => 'api';

  @override
  List<dynamic> get middleware => <dynamic>[];

  @override
  void register() {
    Route.get('/ping', (DoxRequest req) => 'pong');
  }
}
```

| Code | Does |
| --- | --- |
| `Route.get('/blogs', c.index)` | also `post`, `put`, `patch`, `delete`, `options` |
| `Route.post('/blogs', c.store, body: schema)` | `body:` is for the docs only. It checks nothing. |
| `Route.get('/blogs/{id}', c.show)` | path param. `show(int id)` |
| `Route.get('/posts/{page?}', c.list)` | optional param. `list(int? page)` |
| `Route.get('/docs/{path*}', c.page)` | rest of the path, with `/` |
| `Route.get('/me', <dynamic>[AuthMiddleware(), c.me])` | middleware first, controller last |
| `Route.group('/blogs', () { ... })` | prefix. Dox adds the `/` between parts. |
| `Route.middleware(<dynamic>[M()], () { ... })` | middleware for a group |
| `Route.domain('api.app.com', () { ... })` | match by `Host` |
| `Route.resource('blogs', BlogController())` | `index`, `create`, `store`, `show`, `edit`, `update`, `destroy` |
| `Route.files('files')` | serve a storage disk, signed URLs only |
| `Route.enabledCors(() { ... })` / `Route.disabledCors(...)` | CORS for some routes |
| `Route.websocket('ws', (WebsocketEvent e) { ... })` | needs `dox_websocket` |

Controller parameters, by type: `DoxRequest`, one `@Dto` class, `String`/`int`/`double`/`num`/`bool` for path params (by position). Only positional parameters.

Middleware order: `globalMiddleware`, router `middleware`, group, route.

See [Routing](../the-basic/routing.md), [Controller](../the-basic/controller.md), [Middleware](../the-basic/middleware.md).

## Middleware

```dart
class ApiKeyMiddleware implements IDoxMiddleware {
  @override
  dynamic handle(IDoxRequest req) {
    if (req.header('X-Api-Key') != 'secret') {
      return response('no').statusCode(401); // stop here
    }
    return req; // go on
  }
}
```

See [Middleware](../the-basic/middleware.md).

## Request

| Code | Gives |
| --- | --- |
| `await req.validate<CreateBlog>()` | checked DTO, or `422` |
| `req.input('name')` | one value, query or body (body wins) |
| `req.all()` / `req.only(<String>['a', 'b'])` | many values |
| `req.has('name')` | key is there and not empty |
| `req.body` / `req.query` / `req.param['id']` | one source only |
| `req.header('X-Token')` / `req.headers` | headers |
| `req.cookie('token')` | decrypted cookie |
| `req.ip()` / `req.scheme()` / `req.isSecure()` | client info. Needs `trustedProxies` behind a proxy. |
| `req.userAgent()` / `req.host()` / `req.origin()` / `req.locale` | more headers |
| `req.isJson()` / `req.isFormData()` | content type |
| `req.auth?.user<User>()` | logged in user (after `AuthMiddleware`) |
| `req.method` / `req.uri` | method and URI |

Files:

```dart
RequestFile file = req.input('avatar');
file.filename; file.extension; file.length;   // bytes
String path = await file.store('avatars');    // save before you return
```

See [Request](../the-basic/request.md) and [Request and response](request-and-response.md).

## Response

| Return | Client gets |
| --- | --- |
| `String` | text |
| `Map`, `List`, model, `Pagination`, serializer | JSON |
| `File` | streamed file, `Range` supported |
| `Storage().stream(path)` / `Storage().download(path)` | file / download |
| `Stream<List<int>>` | streamed bytes |
| `throw NotFoundHttpException()` | `404 Not Found` |
| `response(...)` | full control |

```dart
return response(<String, dynamic>{'id': 1})
    .statusCode(201)
    .header('X-Request-Id', 'abc')
    .contentType(ContentType.json)
    .cache(Duration(minutes: 5))
    .cookie(DoxCookie('theme', 'dark', httpOnly: true, secure: true));

response('ok').cookie(DoxCookie('token', ''), setExpire: true); // delete
```

| Exception | Status |
| --- | --- |
| `BadRequestException()` | `400` |
| `UnAuthorizedException()` (`dox_auth`) | `401` |
| `NotFoundHttpException()` | `404` |
| `PayloadTooLargeException()` | `413` |
| `UnsupportedMediaTypeException()` | `415` |
| `ValidationException()` | `422` |
| `InternalErrorException()` | `500` |

See [Response](../the-basic/response.md) and [HTTP exceptions](http-exceptions.md).

## DTO validation

```dart
@Dto()
class CreateBlog {
  @Length(min: 3, max: 200)
  @Trim()
  final String title;

  final String? body;            // nullable = optional
  final Status status;           // enum = only its names

  const CreateBlog({required this.title, this.body, this.status = Status.draft});

  static const DtoSchema<CreateBlog> schema = $CreateBlogDto;
}
```

Then `dox build_runner:build`, and `dtos: dtos` in `AppConfig`.

| Kind | Annotations |
| --- | --- |
| Text | `@Length(min:, max:)`, `@MinLength(3)`, `@MaxLength(50)`, `@Email()`, `@Url()`, `@Uuid()`, `@Ip()`, `@Regex(r'..')`, `@In([..])`, `@NotIn([..])`, `@StartsWith('a')`, `@EndsWith('b')`, `@Alpha()`, `@AlphaNumeric()`, `@AlphaDash()` |
| Change text | `@Trim()`, `@Lowercase()`, `@Uppercase()`, `@AllowEmpty()` |
| Numbers | `@Min(1)`, `@Max(9)`, `@Range(1, 9)`, `@Positive()`, `@GreaterThan(0)`, `@LessThan(9)`, `@In`, `@NotIn` |
| Lists | `@MinItems(1)`, `@MaxItems(5)`, `@UniqueItems()` |
| Dates | `@After('2000-01-01')`, `@Before('now')` |
| Files | `@MaxSize('2MB')`, `@Mimes(['pdf'])`, `@Image()` |
| Database (`dox_orm`) | `@Unique('users', column: 'email', ignoreParam: 'id')`, `@Exists('teams')` |
| Keys | `@Name('emailAddress')` |
| Class | `@Dto(source: Source.query, keyCase: KeyCase.field, strict: true, messages: {...})` |

Cross field check: add `void validate(DtoErrors errors)` to the DTO. PATCH "missing or null": `Maybe<T>` with `const Maybe.missing()`.

See [Validation](../the-basic/validation.md) and [Validation rules](../the-basic/validation-rules.md).

## Model

```dart
@DoxModel(table: 'blogs', softDelete: true)
class Blog extends BlogGenerator {
  @Column()
  String? title;

  @Column(name: 'user_id')
  int? userId;

  @BelongsTo(User)
  User? user;

  @HasMany(Comment)
  List<Comment> comments = <Comment>[];

  @override
  List<String> get hidden => <String>['secret'];
}
```

| Code | Does |
| --- | --- |
| `await Blog().find(1)` / `find('slug', 'a')` | one row or `null` |
| `await Blog().all()` | every row (ignores `where`) |
| `await Blog().where('status', 'live').get()` | rows that match |
| `await Blog().where('id', '>', 5).getFirst()` | first match or `null` |
| `await Blog().count()` | `int` |
| `await Blog().paginate(currentPage: 1, perPage: 20)` | `Pagination<Blog>`, rows in `data` |
| `await Blog().create(<String, dynamic>{'title': 'a'})` | insert and return the model |
| `blog.title = 'b'; await blog.save()` | insert or update |
| `await blog.delete()` | soft delete when `softDelete: true` |
| `await blog.forceDelete()` / `await blog.restore()` | real delete / undo soft delete |
| `Blog().withTrash()` | include soft deleted rows |
| `Blog().preload('comments').get()` | load a relation, one query |
| `await blog.$getRelation('user')` | load a relation on one model |
| `blog.related<Comment>('comments')?.where(...).get()` | relation query |
| `blog.toJson()` / `blog.toMap()` | map, `hidden` left out of `toJson()` |
| `Blog().query()` | a new, empty query |

Relations: `@HasOne(T)`, `@HasMany(T)`, `@BelongsTo(T)`, `@ManyToMany(T)`. Options: `foreignKey`, `localKey`, `onQuery`, `eager`.

Events: override `onCreating()`, `onCreated()`, `onSaving()`, `onUpdated()`, `onDeleting()`, ... or `Model.observe<Blog>(BlogObserver())`. `throw CancelModelEvent('why')` in a "before" event stops it. `saveQuietly()` skips events.

See [Model](../database/model/index.md), [Events](../database/model/events.md), [HasMany](../database/model/relationship/has-many.md).

## Query builder

```dart
List<Map<String, dynamic>> rows = await QueryBuilder.table('blogs')
    .select(<String>['id', 'title'])
    .where('status', 'live')
    .orWhere('views', '>', 100)
    .whereIn('id', <int>[1, 2, 3])
    .whereNull('deleted_at')
    .join('users', 'users.id', 'blogs.user_id')
    .orderBy('id', 'desc')
    .limit(10)
    .offset(20)
    .get();
```

| Code | Does |
| --- | --- |
| `whereNotIn`, `whereNotNull`, `orWhereIn`, `orWhereNull` | more filters |
| `whereRaw('lower(name) = @n', <String, dynamic>{'n': 'a'})` | raw SQL, bound values |
| `leftJoin`, `rightJoin`, `joinRaw` | joins |
| `groupBy('age')`, `selectRaw('DISTINCT name')` | groups, raw select |
| `insert({...})`, `insertMultiple([...])` | insert |
| `where(...).update({...})` | update, no events, no `updated_at` |
| `where(...).delete()`, `truncate()` | delete |
| `QueryBuilder.query('select 1', substitutionValues: {...})` | raw query |
| `withConnection('mysql')` | another connection |
| `toSql()`, `debug(true)` | see the SQL |

See [Query builder](../database/query-builder.md).

## Migrations and schema

```dart
class CreateBlogsTable extends Migration {
  @override
  Future<void> up(Schema schema) async {
    await schema.create('blogs', (Table table) {
      table.id();
      table.foreignId('user_id').constrained('users').cascadeOnDelete();
      table.string('title');
      table.text('body').nullable();
      table.enumeration('status', <String>['draft', 'live']).defaultTo('draft');
      table.timestamps();
      table.softDeletes();
    });
  }

  @override
  Future<void> down(Schema schema) async {
    await schema.dropIfExists('blogs');
  }
}
```

| Column types |
| --- |
| `id()`, `increments`, `bigIncrements`, `string(c, [255])`, `char`, `text`, `mediumText`, `longText` |
| `integer`, `bigInteger`, `smallInteger`, `tinyInteger`, `unsignedInteger` (and `Big`, `Small`, `Tiny`) |
| `float`, `double`, `decimal(c, [8], [2])`, `boolean` |
| `date`, `dateTime`, `dateTimeTz`, `time`, `timestamp`, `timestampTz` |
| `json`, `jsonb`, `uuid`, `binary`, `enumeration(c, [...])`, `foreignId`, `foreignUuid` |
| `timestamps()`, `softDeletes()`, `rememberToken()`, `morphs('owner')` |

| Modifiers |
| --- |
| `nullable()`, `defaultTo(v)`, `defaultRaw('sql')`, `useCurrent()`, `useCurrentOnUpdate()` |
| `unique()`, `index()`, `primary()`, `unsigned()`, `comment('t')`, `after('c')`, `change()` |
| keys: `constrained([table])`, `references('id').on('t')`, `onDelete('cascade')`, `cascadeOnDelete()`, `nullOnDelete()` |

Change a table: `schema.table('t', (Table table) { table.string('a').nullable().change(); table.renameColumn('b', 'c'); table.dropColumn('d'); })`.

See [Migration](../database/migration.md) and [Schema](../database/schema.md).

## Transactions

```dart
int? id = await QueryBuilder.transaction(() async {
  Blog blog = await Blog().create(<String, dynamic>{'title': 'a'});
  await QueryBuilder.table('blog_info').insert(<String, dynamic>{'blog_id': blog.id});
  return blog.id;
}); // throw inside = rollback
```

See [Transactions](../database/transactions.md).

## Cache

```dart
await Cache().put('k', 'v', duration: Duration(minutes: 10));
await Cache().get('k', 'default');
await Cache().remember('posts', Duration(minutes: 5), () => Post().all());
await Cache().forget('k');
await Cache().store('redis').increment('hits');
await Cache().tag('users').flush();
CacheLock lock = Cache().store('redis').lock('report', Duration(seconds: 30));
```

Values must be JSON types. `memory` is per isolate. See [Cache](../digging-deeper/cache.md).

## Storage

```dart
String path = await Storage().putRequestFile('avatars', file); // '/avatars/<uuid>.png'
Uint8List? bytes = await Storage().get(path);
await Storage().exists(path);
await Storage().delete(path);
String url = await Storage().signedUrl(path, expiresIn: Duration(minutes: 10));
await Storage().disk('s3').put('reports', bytes, extension: 'pdf');
return Storage().download(path); // from a controller
```

See [File storage](../digging-deeper/file-storage.md).

## Env

```dart
@DoxEnv()
abstract class AppEnv {
  static AppEnv load([EnvReader? reader]) => _$AppEnv.load(reader);

  String get appKey;              // APP_KEY, required
  int get appPort => 3000;        // APP_PORT, default 3000
  String? get awsBucket;          // AWS_BUCKET, optional
}

final AppEnv env = AppEnv.load();
```

A new project has this class in `lib/config/env.dart`. Use `env.appPort` in code. After you add a getter, run `dart run build_runner build`.

`Env.get<int>('APP_PORT', 3000)` is the low-level way. It reads a key by name. A real env var wins over `.env`. In `.env`, a `#` after a space starts a comment.

See [Environment variables](../digging-deeper/env.md) and [Env reference](env.md).

## Auth

```dart
Auth.initialize(AuthConfig(
  defaultGuard: 'web',
  guards: <String, AuthGuard>{
    'web': AuthGuard(
      driver: JwtAuthDriver(secret: SecretKey(env.appKey), expiresIn: Duration(days: 7)),
      provider: AuthProvider(model: () => User()),
    ),
  },
));

String? token = await Auth().attempt(<String, dynamic>{'email': e, 'password': p});
String? token2 = Auth().login(user);
user.password = Hash.make(password);
bool ok = Hash.verify(password, hash);
```

Protect a route with `AuthMiddleware()`. Client sends `Authorization: Bearer <token>`.

See [Authentication](../security/authentication.md) and [Hashing](../security/hashing.md).

## WebSocket

```dart
// a service
WebsocketServer(Dox());

// a route
Route.websocket('ws', (WebsocketEvent event) {
  event.on('intro', chat.intro);
});

// a controller method
void intro(WebsocketEmitter emitter, dynamic message) {
  emitter.room('chat').emitExceptSender('intro', message);
}
```

Client sends `{"event": "joinRoom", "message": "chat"}`. Many isolates need `WebsocketRedisAdapter`.

See [WebSocket](../digging-deeper/websocket.md).

## OpenAPI

```dart
OpenApiConfig openApi = OpenApiConfig(
  info: Info(title: 'Blog API', version: '1.0.0'),
  registry: openApiRegistry, // lib/openapi.g.dart
);
```

Docs at `/docs`, `/openapi.json`, `/openapi.yaml`. On only when `APP_ENV` is `development` or `local`, unless `enabled: true`. Change one route with `@Summary`, `@Tags`, `@Request(T)`, `@Response(200, T)`, `@ApiIgnore()`.

See [OpenAPI](../packages/openapi.md).

## Testing

```dart
setUpAll(() async {
  Dox().initialize(appConfig);
  Dox().totalIsolate(1);
  await Dox().startServer();
});
tearDownAll(() async => Dox().server.close());

test('ping', () async {
  http.Response res = await http.get(Uri.parse('http://localhost:3000/api/ping'));
  expect(res.statusCode, 200);
});
```

| Fake | Code |
| --- | --- |
| cache | `Dox().cache = CacheManager(CacheConfig(defaultStore: 'memory', stores: {...}))` |
| storage | `Disk fake = Dox().storage.fake('s3');` then `Dox().storage.restore('s3')` |
| env | `AppEnv.load(EnvReader(environment: {...}, dotEnv: {...}))` |
| DTO | `await CreateBlog.schema.safeValidateMap(<String, dynamic>{...})` |

Run with `dart test --concurrency=1` when files share a port or tables.

See [Testing](../digging-deeper/testing.md).
