# App config

Source: https://dartondox.dev/latest/3.xreference/app-config/

# App config

`AppConfig` is the one object you give to `Dox().initialize()`. It lives in `lib/config/app.dart`.
This page lists every field, with its type, its default and what it does.

Source: `packages/dox-core/lib/interfaces/app_config.dart`.

## Server

| Field | Type | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `appKey` | `String` | required | Encrypts cookies (`req.cookie()`, `DoxCookie`) and signs local storage URLs. In production the app stops at start when it is empty. Make one with `dox key:generate`. |
| `serverPort` | `int` | `3000` | The port the HTTP server listens on. When the env has no `APP_PORT` but has `PORT`, Dox listens on `PORT` instead (Cloud Run, Fly, Render and Heroku set it). |
| `host` | `String?` | `null`: `APP_HOST`, else all interfaces | The network interface to listen on, like `127.0.0.1`. `null` reads the env var `APP_HOST`. With neither, Dox listens on all interfaces, IPv6 and IPv4 (`::`). |
| `totalIsolate` | `int?` | `Platform.numberOfProcessors` | Isolates (threads) that serve HTTP, all on the same port. On Windows the native server runs on one isolate. |
| `server` | `ServerBackend` | `ServerBackend.native` | Which HTTP server runs: `native` (Rust, `dox_http_native`) or `dartIo`. The env var `DOX_SERVER` wins over this value. See [Native server](../digging-deeper/native-server.md). |
| `compress` | `bool` | `false` | gzip responses in Dart (`HttpServer.autoCompress`). It costs CPU on every response. Let a proxy do it when you have one. |
| `maxBodySize` | `int` | `10 * 1024 * 1024` (10 MB) | Biggest JSON or urlencoded body in bytes. Bigger gets `413`. |
| `maxMultipartSize` | `int` | `100 * 1024 * 1024` (100 MB) | Biggest `multipart/form-data` body (file uploads) in bytes. Bigger gets `413`. |
| `shutdownTimeout` | `Duration` | `Duration(seconds: 8)` | On `SIGTERM` or `SIGINT`, how long open requests may run before Dox closes them. Keep it below the kill timeout of your platform. See [Graceful shutdown](../digging-deeper/deployment.md#graceful-shutdown). |
| `trustedProxies` | `List<String>` | `[]` | IPs or CIDR ranges of reverse proxies. Only when the direct client is in this list does Dox read `X-Forwarded-For` for `req.ip()` and `X-Forwarded-Proto` for `req.scheme()`. `['*']` trusts any client. |

## Routing and request handling

| Field | Type | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `routers` | `List<Router>` | `[]` | The router classes that register routes. |
| `globalMiddleware` | `List<dynamic>` | `[]` | Middleware that runs on every route. A function or an `IDoxMiddleware`. |
| `dtos` | `List<DtoSchema<Object>>` | `[]` | Every DTO of the app: `dtos` from `lib/dtos.g.dart`. Dox finds the DTO of a controller parameter and of `req.validate<T>()` with it. |
| `validationMessages` | `MessageResolver?` | `null` (English messages) | Messages for validation errors, for example in other languages. |
| `responseHandler` | `ResponseHandlerInterface?` | `null` | A class with `DoxResponse handle(DoxResponse res)`. It sees every response before it is sent. |
| `errorHandler` | `Function(Object?, StackTrace)` | `defaultErrorHandler` | Called for every unhandled error. The default logs the error with `Logger.warn` and the stack with `Logger.danger`. |
| `services` | `List<DoxService>` | `[]` | Classes with a `setup()` method. Dox runs them in every isolate at start. The ORM, auth and WebSocket are set up here. |

## Sub configs

| Field | Type | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `cors` | `CORSConfig` | `CORSConfig()` | CORS headers. See [CORSConfig](#corsconfig). |
| `logger` | `LoggerConfig` | `LoggerConfig()` | The `Logger` output. See [LoggerConfig](#loggerconfig). |
| `cache` | `CacheConfig` | `file` store in `storage/cache`, plus a `memory` store | Cache stores for `Cache()`. See [CacheConfig](#cacheconfig). |
| `storage` | `StorageConfig` | `local` disk with root `storage` | Storage disks for `Storage()`. See [StorageConfig](#storageconfig). |
| `openApi` | `OpenApiConfig` | `OpenApiConfig()` | `/docs`, `/openapi.json` and `/openapi.yaml`. See [OpenApiConfig](#openapiconfig). |
| `socketIo` | `SocketIoConfig` | `SocketIoConfig()` (off) | Socket.IO on the HTTP port. See [SocketIoConfig](#socketioconfig). |

## CORSConfig

Source: `packages/dox-core/lib/interfaces/app_config.dart`. Headers are set in `packages/dox-core/lib/http/http_cors_handler.dart`.

A value can be a `String` (`'*'` or a comma list) or a `List<String>`. A `null` value sends no header.

| Field | Type | Default | Header |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `enabled` | `bool` | `true` | Send CORS headers. A route can override it with its own `cors` setting. |
| `origin` | `dynamic` | `null` | `Access-Control-Allow-Origin`. One origin, `'*'`, or a list. With a list, Dox sends back only the request origin if it is in the list. |
| `methods` | `dynamic` | `null` | `Access-Control-Allow-Methods` |
| `headers` | `dynamic` | `null` | `Access-Control-Allow-Headers` |
| `exposeHeaders` | `dynamic` | `null` | `Access-Control-Expose-Headers` |
| `credentials` | `bool?` | `null` | `Access-Control-Allow-Credentials` |
| `maxAge` | `num?` | `null` | `Access-Control-Max-Age` in seconds |

!!! note
    With the default `CORSConfig()` every value is `null`. So `enabled: true` alone sends no header. Set `origin` at least.

## LoggerConfig

| Field | Type | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `name` | `String` | `''` | The `name` field in each JSON log line. |
| `enabled` | `bool` | `false` | Turn the `Logger` on. |
| `prettyPrint` | `bool` | `false` | `true` prints colored text. `false` prints one JSON object per line (for log services). |
| `level` | `String` | `'info'` | The lowest level to print: `debug`, `info`, `warn` or `error`. `Logger.success` counts as `info`. `Logger.danger` counts as `error`. An unknown value prints every line. |

## CacheConfig

Source: `packages/dox-cache/lib/src/cache_config.dart`. Option keys: `packages/dox-cache/lib/src/constants/cache_constants.dart`.

| Field | Type | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `defaultStore` | `String` | required | The store `Cache()` uses when no store is named. |
| `stores` | `Map<String, Map<String, dynamic>>` | required | Store name to options. Each store needs a `driver` option. |

Options of each driver:

| Driver | Option | Type | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| all | `driver` | `String` | required | `file`, `memory`, `redis` or `null` |
| all | `prefix` | `String` | `dox_cache:` | Text in front of every key. |
| `file` | `path` | `String` | `storage/cache` | Folder of the cache files. |
| `memory` | `max_size` | `int` | no limit | Most items in the map. |
| `redis` | `host` | `String` | `127.0.0.1` | Redis host. |
| `redis` | `port` | `int` | `6379` | Redis port. |
| `redis` | `username` | `String` | none | Redis user. |
| `redis` | `password` | `String` | none | Redis password. |
| `redis` | `db` | `int` | `0` | Redis database number. |
| `redis` | `tls` | `bool` | `false` | Use TLS. |
| `redis` | `pool_size` | `int` | `10` | Most connections per store. |

## StorageConfig

Source: `packages/dox-core/lib/storage/storage_config.dart`.

| Field | Type | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `defaultDisk` | `String` | `'local'` | The disk `Storage()` uses when no disk is named. |
| `disks` | `Map<String, Map<String, dynamic>>` | `{'local': {'driver': 'local', 'root': 'storage'}}` | Disk name to options. Each disk needs a `driver` option. |

Options of each driver:

| Driver | Option | Type | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| all | `driver` | `String` | required | `local`, `s3` or `memory` |
| `local` | `root` | `String` | `storage` | Folder of the files. |
| `local` | `url` | `String` | none | Base of the public URLs, like `http://localhost:3000/files`. |
| `local` | `app_key` | `String` | `AppConfig.appKey` | Key that signs the URLs. |
| `local` | `visibility` | `String` | `public` | `public` or `private`. |
| `s3` | `bucket` | `String` | required | Bucket name. |
| `s3` | `region` | `String` | `us-east-1` | Region. |
| `s3` | `key` | `String` | required | Access key id. |
| `s3` | `secret` | `String` | required | Secret access key. |
| `s3` | `token` | `String` | none | Session token. |
| `s3` | `endpoint` | `String` | none | Custom endpoint (R2, MinIO, Spaces). |
| `s3` | `path_style` | `bool` | `false` | Use path style URLs. |
| `s3` | `url` | `String` | none | Base of the public URLs. |
| `s3` | `visibility` | `String` | `private` | `public` or `private`. |
| `s3` | `acl` | `bool` | `true` | The service supports ACLs. |
| `s3` | `batch_delete` | `bool` | `true` | The service supports batch delete. |

An unknown driver throws `ArgumentError('Storage disk "<name>" has unknown driver "<type>"')`.

## OpenApiConfig

Source: `packages/dox-core/lib/openapi/openapi_config.dart`.

| Field | Type | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `enabled` | `bool?` | `null` | Serve the docs routes. `null` means: on only when `APP_ENV` is `development` or `local`. |
| `info` | `Info` | `Info(title: 'Dox API', version: '1.0.0')` | Title and version of the API. |
| `servers` | `List<Server>` | `[]` | Base URLs of the API. |
| `securitySchemes` | `Map<String, SecurityScheme>` | `{}` | Ways to log in, like `{'bearerAuth': SecurityScheme.bearer()}`. |
| `securityByMiddleware` | `Map<String, List<Map<String, List<String>>>>` | `{}` | Security for routes that use a middleware class with this name. `AuthMiddleware` gets `bearerAuth` when it is not in the map. |
| `registry` | `OpenApiRegistry` | `OpenApiRegistry()` (empty) | What `dox_builder` found in the code. Pass `openApiRegistry` from `lib/openapi.g.dart`. |
| `ui` | `DocsUi` | `DocsUi.scalar` | `scalar` or `swagger`. |
| `scalar` | `ScalarOptions` | `ScalarOptions()` | Options of the Scalar page. See below. |
| `pageTitle` | `String?` | `null` (uses `info.title`) | Title of the `/docs` page. |

`ScalarOptions` (`packages/dox-openapi/lib/src/docs_ui.dart`):

| Field | Type | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `theme` | `ScalarTheme` | `ScalarTheme.default_` | One of `default_`, `alternate`, `moon`, `purple`, `solarized`, `bluePlanet`, `deepSpace`, `saturn`, `kepler`, `elysiajs`, `fastify`, `mars`, `laserwave`, `none`. |
| `darkMode` | `bool` | `false` | Start in dark mode. |
| `showDownloadButton` | `bool` | `true` | Show the download button for the OpenAPI document. |
| `proxyUrl` | `String?` | `null` | Send "Try it" requests through this proxy. |

## SocketIoConfig

Source: `packages/dox-core/lib/socketio/socket_io_config.dart`.

| Field | Type | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `enabled` | `bool` | `false` | Mount Socket.IO on the HTTP port at `/socket.io/`. |
| `options` | `ServerOptions` | `ServerOptions()` | Engine options. See below. |
| `namespaces` | `List<NamespaceHandler>` | `[]` | Namespaces to register, like `ChatNamespace()`. |
| `adapter` | `SocketAdapterFactory?` | `null` (in memory) | Makes the adapter in each isolate. Use a Redis adapter with many isolates. |

`ServerOptions` (`packages/dox-socketio/lib/src/engine/server_options.dart`). The defaults match the Node.js server.

| Field | Type | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `path` | `String` | `/socket.io/` | URL path. Must end with `/`. |
| `pingInterval` | `Duration` | 25 s | Time between two server pings. |
| `pingTimeout` | `Duration` | 20 s | Time to wait for a pong before the session is closed. |
| `upgradeTimeout` | `Duration` | 10 s | Time a websocket upgrade may take. |
| `connectTimeout` | `Duration` | 45 s | Time a client has to join a namespace after the handshake. |
| `maxHttpBufferSize` | `int` | `1000000` | Biggest message in bytes a client may send. |
| `transports` | `List<String>` | `['polling', 'websocket']` | Allowed transports. |
| `allowUpgrades` | `bool` | `true` | Allow upgrades from polling to websocket. |
| `cors` | `CorsOptions?` | `null` (no CORS headers) | CORS for the long-polling requests. |

`CorsOptions`:

| Field | Type | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `origins` | `List<String>` | `['*']` | Allowed origins. |
| `credentials` | `bool` | `false` | Send `Access-Control-Allow-Credentials: true`. |
| `methods` | `List<String>` | `['GET', 'POST']` | Allowed methods for preflight. |
| `allowedHeaders` | `List<String>?` | `null` (the requested headers) | Allowed request headers. |
| `maxAge` | `Duration?` | `null` | How long a browser may cache the preflight answer. |

## DatabaseConfig

The database is not a field of `AppConfig`. A service calls `SqlQueryBuilder.initializeWithDatabaseConfig(databaseConfig)` in its `setup()`.
Source: `packages/dox-orm/lib/src/types/database_config.dart` and `connection_config.dart`.

| Field | Type | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `connection` | `String` | required | Name of the connection to use. A missing name throws `Exception('<name> not found')`. |
| `connections` | `Map<String, ConnectionConfig>` | required | Connection name to config. |

`ConnectionConfig`:

| Field | Type | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `driver` | `Driver` | required | `Driver.postgres`, `Driver.mysql` (also MariaDB) or `Driver.sqlite`. |
| `host` | `String` | `'localhost'` | Database host. Not used by sqlite. |
| `port` | `int` | `0` | Database port. Not used by sqlite. |
| `user` | `String` | `''` | Database user. Not used by sqlite. |
| `password` | `String` | `''` | Database password. Not used by sqlite. |
| `database` | `String` | required | Database name. For sqlite: the file path, or `:memory:`. |
| `useSSL` | `bool` | `false` | Use TLS. Postgres with TLS uses the Dart driver, not the native one. |
| `debug` | `bool` | required | Print every query with `printer`. |
| `printer` | `QueryPrinter?` | `null` | `ConsoleQueryPrinter()`, `PrettyQueryPrinter()`, `FileQueryPrinter()` or your own. |
| `extra` | `Map<String, dynamic>` | `{}` | Driver options. See below. |
| `driverFactory` | `DBDriver Function(ConnectionConfig)?` | `null` | Your own driver class. It wins over every other setting. |

Keys of `extra`:

| Driver | Key | Type | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| postgres, mysql | `native` | `bool` | `true` | `false` uses the Dart driver instead of the native (Rust) one. |
| postgres, mysql | `maxConnectionCount` | `int` | `10` | Most open connections. |
| postgres, mysql | `preparedStatementCacheSize` | `int` | `100` | Prepared statements kept per connection. |
| postgres | `sslMode` | postgres `SslMode` | none | Setting it uses the Dart driver. |
| mysql | `collation` | `String` | `utf8mb4_general_ci` | Connection collation. |
| mysql | `timeoutMs` | `int` | `10000` | Connect timeout. |
| mysql | `allowPublicKeyRetrieval` | `bool` | `true` | Ask the server for its RSA key (needed for `caching_sha2_password` without TLS). |
| mysql | `serverPublicKey` | `String` | none | The server RSA key, so it is not asked for. |
| mysql | `timeZone` | `String` | none | Session time zone. |
| mysql | `maxConnectionAge` | `Duration` | 12 hours | Close and reopen a connection after this time. |
| sqlite | `busyTimeout` | `int` | `5000` | `PRAGMA busy_timeout` in milliseconds. |

## AuthConfig

Auth is not a field of `AppConfig`. A service calls `Auth.initialize(AuthConfig(...))` in its `setup()`.
Source: `packages/dox-auth/lib/src/interfaces.dart`.

| Class | Field | Type | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `AuthConfig` | `defaultGuard` | `String` | required | The guard `Auth()` uses when no guard is named. |
| `AuthConfig` | `guards` | `Map<String, AuthGuard>` | `{}` | Guard name to guard. |
| `AuthGuard` | `driver` | `AuthDriver` | required | How a token is made and checked, like `JwtAuthDriver(secret: SecretKey(...))`. |
| `AuthGuard` | `provider` | `AuthProvider` | required | Where users come from. |
| `AuthProvider` | `model` | `dynamic Function()` | required | Makes the user model, like `() => User()`. |
| `AuthProvider` | `identifierFields` | `List<String>` | `['email']` | Columns `attempt()` matches the login with. |
| `AuthProvider` | `passwordField` | `String` | `'password'` | Column with the bcrypt hash. |

## Full example

This is the `lib/config/app.dart` of a new project. The sub configs live in their own files in `lib/config/`.

```dart title="lib/config/app.dart"
import 'dart:io';

import 'package:dox_core/dox_core.dart';
import 'package:my_app/app/http/response_handler.dart';
import 'package:my_app/config/cache.dart';
import 'package:my_app/config/cors.dart';
import 'package:my_app/config/logger.dart';
import 'package:my_app/config/services.dart';
import 'package:my_app/config/storage.dart';
import 'package:my_app/routes/api.dart';
import 'package:my_app/routes/web.dart';
import 'package:my_app/config/env.dart';

AppConfig appConfig = AppConfig(
  /// Application secret key
  /// -------------------------------
  /// This key is use to encrypt/decrypt the data such as cache and cookies.
  /// Make sure to keep the `APP_KEY` as an environment variable and secure.
  ///
  /// Note: Changing the application key for an existing app will make all
  /// the cookies and cache invalid and also the existing encrypted data
  /// will not be decrypted.
  appKey: env.appKey,

  /// Server port
  /// -------------------------------
  /// App will be running on this port.
  serverPort: env.appPort,

  /// Total isolate (multi thread)
  /// -------------------------------
  /// Isolates that serve http requests, all on the same port.
  /// Default is one per CPU core, so the app uses all cores.
  /// Set `APP_TOTAL_ISOLATE` to change it.
  totalIsolate: env.appTotalIsolate ?? Platform.numberOfProcessors,

  /// Global middleware
  /// -------------------------------
  /// By registering global middleware here,
  /// middleware will be applied to all the routes.
  globalMiddleware: <dynamic>[LogMiddleware(enabled: true)],

  /// Routers
  /// -------------------------------
  /// Register routers to create route to dox framework.
  routers: <Router>[WebRouter(), ApiRouter()],

  /// Response handler
  responseHandler: ResponseHandler(),

  /// Cache stores (config/cache.dart)
  cache: cache,

  /// Storage disks (config/storage.dart)
  storage: storage,

  /// Cors configuration
  cors: cors,

  /// Service to run on multithread server
  services: services,

  /// logger configuration
  logger: logger,
);
```

The config files read their values from `env`, the typed env class in `lib/config/env.dart`. See [Env reference](env.md).

The sub config files, with the values a new project ships:

```dart title="lib/config/cache.dart"
import 'package:dox_core/dox_core.dart';
import 'package:my_app/config/env.dart';

/// Cache stores
/// -------------------------------
/// `Cache()` uses the default store. `Cache().store('memory')` picks one.
/// Drivers: file, memory, redis, null. Values must be JSON types.
CacheConfig cache = CacheConfig(
  defaultStore: env.cacheStore,
  stores: <String, Map<String, dynamic>>{
    'file': <String, dynamic>{'driver': 'file', 'path': 'storage/cache'},

    /// one map per isolate, fast, not shared
    'memory': <String, dynamic>{'driver': 'memory', 'max_size': 10000},
  },
);
```

```dart title="lib/config/storage.dart"
import 'package:dox_core/dox_core.dart';
import 'package:my_app/config/env.dart';

/// Storage disks
/// -------------------------------
/// `Storage()` uses the default disk. `Storage().disk('local')` picks one.
/// Drivers: local, s3 (also R2, MinIO, Spaces), memory.
StorageConfig storage = StorageConfig(
  defaultDisk: env.storageDisk,
  disks: <String, Map<String, dynamic>>{
    /// files in the `storage` folder
    'local': <String, dynamic>{'driver': 'local', 'root': 'storage'},
  },
);
```

```dart title="lib/config/logger.dart"
import 'package:dox_core/dox_core.dart';
import 'package:my_app/config/env.dart';

LoggerConfig logger = LoggerConfig(
  /// Application name
  /// -------------------------------
  /// The name of the application you want to add to the log.
  name: env.appName,

  /// Toggle logger
  /// -------------------------------
  /// Enable or disable logger in application.
  enabled: true,

  /// Logging level
  /// -------------------------------
  /// The level from which you want the logger to flush logs.
  level: env.logLevel,

  /// Pretty print
  /// -------------------------------
  /// It is highly advised NOT to use `prettyPrint` in production, since it
  /// can have huge impact on performance.
  prettyPrint: env.isDevelopment,
);
```

```dart title="lib/config/database.dart"
import 'package:dox_orm/dox_orm.dart';
import 'package:my_app/config/env.dart';

/// Print every SQL query only in development.
/// Printing each query costs time, so it is off in production.
bool _debug = env.isDevelopment;

DatabaseConfig databaseConfig = DatabaseConfig(
  /// Connection
  /// -------------------------------
  /// The connection to use. It is one key of `connections` below.
  connection: env.dbConnection,

  connections: <String, ConnectionConfig>{
    /// Postgres
    'postgres': ConnectionConfig(
      driver: Driver.postgres,
      host: env.dbHost,
      port: env.dbPort ?? 5432,
      user: env.dbUsername,
      password: env.dbPassword,
      database: env.dbName,
      extra: <String, dynamic>{
        /// Each isolate has its own pool.
        'maxConnectionCount': 10,
        'maxConnectionAge': Duration(hours: 1),
      },
      debug: _debug,
      printer: PrettyQueryPrinter(),
    ),

    /// MySQL and MariaDB
    'mysql': ConnectionConfig(
      driver: Driver.mysql,
      host: env.dbHost,
      port: env.dbPort ?? 3306,
      user: env.dbUsername,
      password: env.dbPassword,
      database: env.dbName,
      extra: <String, dynamic>{'collation': 'utf8mb4_general_ci'},
      debug: _debug,
      printer: PrettyQueryPrinter(),
    ),

    /// SQLite. `DB_NAME` is a file path, or `:memory:`.
    'sqlite': ConnectionConfig(
      driver: Driver.sqlite,
      database: env.dbName,
      debug: _debug,
      printer: PrettyQueryPrinter(),
    ),
  },
);
```

```dart title="lib/config/cors.dart"
import 'package:dox_core/dox_core.dart';

CORSConfig cors = CORSConfig(
  /// Enabled
  /// -------------------------------
  /// A boolean to enable or disable CORS integration.
  /// Setting to true will enable the CORS for all HTTP request.
  enabled: false,

  /// Origin
  /// -------------------------------
  /// Set the origins to be allowed for `Access-Control-Allow-Origin`.
  /// The value can be one of the following:
  /// List        : Allowed origins. Dox sends back only the request origin
  ///               when it is in the list.
  /// String      : One allowed origin.
  /// String (*)  : A wildcard (*) to allow all request origins.
  origin: '*',

  /// Methods
  /// -------------------------------
  /// Set a list of origins to be allowed for `Access-Control-Request-Method`.
  /// The value can be one of the following:
  /// Array       : An array of request methods.
  /// String      : Comma separated list of request methods.
  /// String (*)  : A wildcard (*) to allow all request methods.
  methods: '*',

  /// Headers
  /// -------------------------------
  /// Set a list of origins to be allowed for `Access-Control-Allow-Headers`.
  /// The value can be one of the following:
  /// Array       : An array of allowed headers.
  /// String      : Comma separated list of allowed headers.
  /// String (*)  : A wildcard (*) to allow all request headers.
  headers: '*',

  /// Expose Headers
  /// -------------------------------
  /// Set a list of origins to be allowed for `Access-Control-Expose-Headers`.
  /// The value can be one of the following:
  /// Array       : An array of expose headers.
  /// String      : Comma separated list of expose headers.
  exposeHeaders: <String>[
    'cache-control',
    'content-language',
    'content-type',
    'expires',
    'last-modified',
    'pragma',
  ],

  /// Credentials
  /// -------------------------------
  /// Toggle `Access-Control-Allow-Credentials` header.
  credentials: true,

  /// MaxAge
  /// -------------------------------
  /// Define `Access-Control-Max-Age` header in seconds.
  maxAge: 90,
);
```

```dart title="lib/config/services.dart"
import 'package:dox_core/dox_core.dart';
import 'package:my_app/services/orm_service.dart';

/// Services to register on dox
/// -------------------------------
/// Since dox run on multi thread isolate, we need to register
/// below extra services to dox so that dox can
/// register again on new isolate.
List<DoxService> services = <DoxService>[ORMService()];
```

```dart title="lib/services/orm_service.dart"
import 'package:dox_core/dox_core.dart';
import 'package:dox_orm/dox_orm.dart';
import 'package:my_app/config/database.dart';

/// Query builder service
/// --------------------------
/// Sets up the query builder, so this project can use the ORM.
/// If this project does not need a database, delete this file
/// and remove it from config/services.dart.
class ORMService implements DoxService {
  @override
  Future<void> setup() async {
    SqlQueryBuilder.initializeWithDatabaseConfig(databaseConfig);
  }
}
```

A new project has no `openapi.dart`, `socketio.dart` or auth service. You add them when you need them. See [OpenAPI](../packages/openapi.md), [Socket.IO](../packages/socketio.md) and [Authentication](../security/authentication.md).


---

# CLI

Source: https://dartondox.dev/latest/3.xreference/cli/

# CLI

Every `dox` command, from the command registry in `packages/dox-cli/lib/src/command_registry.dart`.
The file templates are Dart strings inside `packages/dox-cli/lib/src/tools/`. The path of each template is given below.

How to install the CLI is on the [Dox CLI](../digging-deeper/dox-cli.md) page.

Rules that apply to every command:

- `dox` with no command prints `Could not find a command. Run `dox help` for more information.`
- An unknown command prints `Could not find a command named "<name>".`
- Too few or too many arguments prints `Invalid number of arguments for command "<name>".` with the expected count.
- A name you pass is turned into `snake_case` for the file and `PascalCase` for the class. `BlogPost` and `blog_post` give the same result.
- A `create:*` command does not overwrite. When the file exists it prints `<name> already exists` and stops.

## Project

### `dox create`

```
dox create <project_name> [--version <version>]
```

Makes a new project from the [dox-sample](https://github.com/dartondox/dox-sample) repo.

| Option | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `--version <v>` (or `--v`) | The release tag to clone, like `3.0.0-alpha.4` or `v3.0.0-alpha.4`. Without it, the newest `dox-sample` release with the same major version as the CLI is used (pre-releases included). |

What it does:

1. Turns the name into `snake_case`. Stops with `Folder name "<name>" already exist` when the folder is there.
2. Reads the release list of `dartondox/dox-sample` and takes the newest release with the same major version as the CLI.
3. Runs `git clone --depth 1 --branch v<version> https://github.com/dartondox/dox-sample.git <name>`.
4. Deletes the `.git` folder.
5. Replaces `dox_sample` with your project name in every file, except files under `bin/dox`.

Needs `curl` and `git` on the `PATH`.

!!! warning "Known bug: `dox create my_app` without `--version` throws `RangeError`"
    The command reads `args[1]` before it checks how many arguments there are.
    With only the project name you get `RangeError (index): Invalid value: Only valid value is 0: 1`.
    Workaround: always pass the version, `dox create my_app --version 3.0.0-alpha.4`.

Source: `packages/dox-cli/lib/src/tools/create_project.dart`.

### `dox serve`

```
dox serve [--ignore-build-runner]
dox s
dox server
```

Starts the dev server.

| Option | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `--ignore-build-runner` | Do not start `dart run build_runner watch`. |

What it does:

1. Starts `dart run build_runner watch` (unless the option is set).
2. Starts `dart run bin/server.dart` and prints its output.
3. Watches the project folder. When a `.dart` file changes it prints `[Dox] File changed: <file>`, waits 500 ms, kills the server and starts it again.

Source: `packages/dox-cli/lib/src/tools/server_serve.dart`.

### `dox build`

```
dox build
```

AOT compiles the app for production into `build/bundle`. Use this in production, not `dart run`.

What it does:

1. When `pubspec.yaml` contains `build_runner`: runs `dart run build_runner build`. Stops with exit code 1 when it fails.
2. Runs `dart build cli --target bin/server.dart --output build`.
3. Copies `db/` to `build/bundle/db` (migrations are read at start).
4. Copies `.env.example` to `build/bundle/.env.example`.
5. Prints `[Dox] Built build/bundle. Run it with: cd build/bundle && ./bin/server`.

Output:

| Path | What |
| --- | --- |
| `build/bundle/bin/server` | the native binary, no Dart SDK needed |
| `build/bundle/lib/` | native libraries from build hooks (SQLite, `dox_http_native`, ...) |
| `build/bundle/db/` | your migrations |
| `build/bundle/.env.example` | copy it to `.env` or set real env vars |

`dart compile exe` can not build packages with build hooks, so the CLI uses `dart build cli`.

Source: `packages/dox-cli/lib/src/tools/server_serve.dart` (`buildServer`).

### `dox build_runner:build` and `dox build_runner:watch`

```
dox build_runner:build
dox build_runner:watch
```

Run `dart run build_runner build` once, or `dart run build_runner watch`. No options.
The CLI does not pass `--delete-conflicting-outputs` (build_runner removed that flag).

### `dox key:generate`

```
dox key:generate
```

Makes a 32 character key (A-Z, a-z, 0-9, from `Random.secure()`) and writes it to `APP_KEY` in `.env`.
Prints `<key> : Key have been updated successfully in .env!`.

What it does with `.env`:

- Reads `.env` in the current folder. The file must exist, else the command fails with a file error.
- Keeps every `KEY=value` line. Replaces the value of `APP_KEY`.
- Adds `APP_KEY=<key>` as the first line when there is no `APP_KEY`.

!!! warning
    The rewrite only keeps lines with exactly one `=`. A line like `DATABASE_URL=postgres://u:p@h/db?a=b` has two `=` and is dropped from `.env`. Comment lines are dropped too. Back up `.env` first when it has such lines.

Source: `packages/dox-cli/lib/src/tools/generate_key.dart`.

### `dox env:generate`

```
dox env:generate
```

Writes `lib/config/env.dart`, the typed env class, from `.env.example`.

- Stops with `.env.example is missing.` (exit code 1) when there is no example file.
- Stops with `lib/config/env.dart is already there. Delete it to make it again.` (exit code 1) when the file exists.
- Prints `Run `dart run build_runner build` to make env.g.dart.` when done.

Rules for each key: digits give `int get x => <value>;`, `true`/`false` give `bool`, an empty value gives `String? get x;`, any other value gives `String get x;` (required, no default). `#` comment lines above a key become its doc comment. A key that does not map back from `camelCase` gets `@EnvKey('KEY')`.

Source: `packages/dox-cli/lib/src/tools/env_tools.dart` (`EnvScaffold`).

### `dox env:check`

```
dox env:check
```

Loads `AppEnv` from `lib/config/env.dart` with the real environment and `.env`. Prints `The env is valid.` or an `EnvException` with every missing or bad key (exit code 1).

It writes a small script to `.dart_tool/dox/env_check.dart` and runs it with `dart run`. It needs `lib/config/env.dart` and a `name:` in `pubspec.yaml`.

Source: `packages/dox-cli/lib/src/tools/env_tools.dart` (`envCheck`).

### `dox openapi:generate`

```
dox openapi:generate [dir]
```

Runs `dart run bin/openapi.dart [dir]`. That file writes `openapi.json` and `openapi.yaml` into `dir` (default `storage/openapi`).
Stops with `bin/openapi.dart is missing.` (exit code 1) when the file is not there. See [OpenAPI](../packages/openapi.md).

Source: `packages/dox-cli/lib/src/tools/openapi_generate.dart`.

### `dox update`

```
dox update
```

Installs the newest CLI with the same major version as the one you have. Pre-releases count.
So a 3.x alpha CLI updates to the newest 3.x alpha, not to the old 2.x stable.
It reads the version list from pub.dev, then runs `dart pub global activate dox <version>`.

Source: `packages/dox-cli/lib/src/tools/update_dox.dart`.

### `dox version`

```
dox version
dox v
dox -v
dox --version
```

Prints `Dox version: <version>`. Aliases: `--version`, `-version`, `v`, `-v`, `--v`.

### `dox help`

```
dox help [command]
```

Without a command: lists every command by category. With a command: prints its usage, description, category, aliases and argument count.

## Create files

### `dox create:controller`

```
dox create:controller <name> [-r] [-ws]
```

| Option | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `-r` | A resource controller with `index`, `create`, `store`, `show`, `edit`, `update`, `destroy`. |
| `-ws` | A WebSocket controller. |

A trailing `Controller` in the name is removed: `UserController` and `User` give the same file.

| Form | Writes | Template |
| --- | --- | --- |
| plain | `lib/app/http/controllers/<name>.controller.dart` | `_getSample` in `packages/dox-cli/lib/src/tools/create_controller.dart` |
| `-r` | `lib/app/http/controllers/<name>.controller.dart` | `_getResourceSample` in the same file |
| `-ws` | `lib/app/ws/controllers/<name>.controller.dart` | `_getWsSample` in the same file |

The plain and resource templates also make an instance: `<Name>Controller <name>Controller = <Name>Controller();`.

### `dox create:middleware`

```
dox create:middleware <name>
```

Writes `lib/app/http/middleware/<name>.middleware.dart`: a class `<Name>Middleware extends IDoxMiddleware` with a `handle(IDoxRequest req)` that returns `req`.
A trailing `Middleware` in the name is removed.

Template: `_getSample` in `packages/dox-cli/lib/src/tools/create_middleware.dart`.

### `dox create:dto`

```
dox create:dto <name>
```

Writes `lib/app/http/dtos/<name>.dto.dart`: a `@Dto()` class with one `name` field and `part '<name>.dto.g.dart';`.
A trailing `Dto` in the name is removed. Prints `Run `dox build_runner:build` to make <name>.dto.g.dart.`

Template: `_getSample` in `packages/dox-cli/lib/src/tools/create_dto.dart`.

### `dox create:serializer`

```
dox create:serializer <name>
```

Writes `lib/app/http/serializers/<name>.serializer.dart`: a class `<Name>Serializer extends Serializer<<Name>>`. It imports the model from `lib/app/models/<name>/<name>.model.dart`.
A trailing `Serializer` in the name is removed.

Template: `_getSample` in `packages/dox-cli/lib/src/tools/create_serializer.dart`.

### `dox create:model`

```
dox create:model <name> [-m|--migration]
dox make:model <name> [-m|--migration]
```

Writes `lib/app/models/<name>/<name>.model.dart`: a `@DoxModel()` class with `part '<name>.model.g.dart';`.

| Option | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `-m` or `--migration` | Also make a `create_<table>_table` migration. The table is the plural snake name: `BlogPost` gives `blog_posts`. The model then gets `@DoxModel(table: 'blog_posts')`. |

Any other second argument prints `Invalid option <x>, use -m or --migration` (exit code 1).

Template: `_getSample` in `packages/dox-cli/lib/src/tools/create_model.dart`.

### `dox make:migration`

```
dox make:migration <name> [--sql]
dox create:migration <name> [--sql]
```

| Option | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `--sql` | Make a `.sql` file with `-- up` and `-- down` sections instead of a Dart class. |

Writes `db/migration/<yyyy>_<mm>_<dd>_<hhmmss>_<name>.dart` (or `.sql`). Characters that are not letters, digits or `_` are removed from the name.

For a Dart migration it also:

- writes `db/migration/migrations.dart`, the registry of every Dart migration in the folder, sorted by name;
- writes `bin/migrate.dart` when it is missing, and prints `bin/migrate.dart created.`

The Dart template depends on the name:

| Name | `up()` | `down()` |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `create_<table>_table` | `schema.create('<table>', ...)` with `id()` and `timestamps()` | `schema.dropIfExists('<table>')` |
| `<x>_to_<table>_table` (also `from`, `in`, `on`) | `schema.table('<table>', ...)` | `schema.table('<table>', ...)` |
| anything else | a comment | a comment |

Templates: `dartMigrationSource`, `migrateEntrySource` and `_sampleSql` in `packages/dox-cli/lib/src/tools/create_migration.dart`.

## Migrations

All `migration:*` commands work the same way:

1. When `bin/migrate.dart` exists: write the registry again, then run `dart run bin/migrate.dart <command> [args]`. Your app code runs, so Dart migrations work.
2. When there is no `bin/migrate.dart` but `db/migration` has Dart files: print `db/migration has Dart migrations, but bin/migrate.dart is missing.` (exit code 1).
3. Else: run the `.sql` migrations with `Migrator()` from `dox_migration` in the CLI process.

The database comes from `DB_CONNECTION`, `DB_HOST`, `DB_PORT`, `DB_USERNAME`, `DB_PASSWORD` and `DB_DATABASE` (or `DB_NAME`). See [Environment variables](env.md).
A failed run prints the error and sets exit code 1.

| Command | Aliases | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `dox migration:run` | `dox migrate` | Run the migrations that did not run yet. |
| `dox migration:rollback [--step=<count>]` | `dox migrate:rollback` | Undo the last batch, or the last `<count>` migrations. Any other option prints `Invalid option <x>, use --step=<count>` (exit code 1). |
| `dox migration:reset` | `dox migrate:reset` | Undo every migration. |
| `dox migration:refresh` | `dox migrate:refresh` | Undo every migration, then run them all again. |
| `dox migration:status` | `dox migrate:status` | Print which migrations ran, and their batch. |

## Command list

| Command | Aliases | Category |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `create` | | Project |
| `serve` | `server`, `s` | Development |
| `create:controller` | | Development |
| `create:middleware` | | Development |
| `create:dto` | | Development |
| `build` | | Build |
| `build_runner:build` | | Build Runner |
| `build_runner:watch` | | Build Runner |
| `create:model` | `make:model` | Generation |
| `create:serializer` | | Generation |
| `key:generate` | | Generation |
| `env:generate` | | Generation |
| `openapi:generate` | | Generation |
| `migration:run` | `migrate` | Database |
| `migration:rollback` | `migrate:rollback` | Database |
| `migration:reset` | `migrate:reset` | Database |
| `migration:refresh` | `migrate:refresh` | Database |
| `migration:status` | `migrate:status` | Database |
| `make:migration` | `create:migration` | Database |
| `version` | `--version`, `-version`, `v`, `-v`, `--v` | System |
| `update` | | System |
| `env:check` | | System |
| `help` | | System |

# Environment variables

Source: https://dartondox.dev/latest/3.xreference/env/

# Environment variables

Every env var the framework and its packages read. How to read your own keys with the typed env class is on the [Environment Variables](../digging-deeper/env.md) page.

The code reads env vars in three ways:

- `Env.get()` and `EnvReader` (`dox_core`): a real environment variable wins over the `.env` file.
- `Platform.environment` straight: only the real environment, `.env` is not read.
- `dox_migration` has its own `loadEnv()`: it reads `.env` and the real environment. A real environment variable wins, the same as `Env.get()`.

## Read by the framework

| Variable | Who reads it | Default | Meaning | Example |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `APP_ENV` | `dox_core` (`Dox().checkAppKey()`, `OpenApiConfig.isEnabled`) | empty | `production` makes a missing `APP_KEY` a startup error. `development` or `local` turn the `/docs` routes on when `openApi.enabled` is `null`. Read with `Env.get`. | `APP_ENV=production` |
| `PORT` | `dox_core` (`DoxServer.portFor()`) | not set | The port to listen on, when `APP_PORT` is not set. Cloud Run, Fly, Render and Heroku set it. `APP_PORT` wins when both are set. Read with `Env.get`. | `PORT=8080` |
| `APP_HOST` | `dox_core` (`DoxServer.hostFor()`) | not set (all interfaces, `::`) | The host to listen on. `127.0.0.1` keeps the app off the network, for an app behind a proxy on the same machine. `AppConfig.host` wins over it. Read with `Env.get`. | `APP_HOST=127.0.0.1` |
| `DOX_SERVER` | `dox_core` (`DoxServer.usesNative()`) | not set (uses `AppConfig.server`) | `dartio`, `dart_io` or `dart:io` forces the `dart:io` server. `native` forces the native server, also for an app with WebSocket routes. Real environment only. | `DOX_SERVER=dartio` |
| `DOX_HTTP_THREAD` | `dox_http_native` (Rust, `shared_thread()`) | not set (one thread per isolate) | `shared` puts the servers of all isolates on one network thread. Off by default: on 2 cores it cut req/s by a quarter. Real environment only. | `DOX_HTTP_THREAD=shared` |
| `DOX_DB_DRIVER` | `dox_orm` (`NativeDrivers.wanted()`) | not set (native driver) | `dart` uses the Dart `postgres` / `mysql_dart` driver instead of the native (Rust) one. Same as `extra: {'native': false}`. Real environment only. | `DOX_DB_DRIVER=dart` |
| `DATABASE_URL` | `dox_orm` (`DatabaseConfig.url`), `dox_migration` | not set | A database url. When it is set, it wins over `DB_CONNECTION` and the other `DB_*` keys. `dox_orm` reads it from the real environment only. See [Database url](../database/index.md#database_url). | `DATABASE_URL=postgres://app:secret@db:5432/blog?sslmode=require` |
| `DB_CONNECTION` | `dox_migration` (`DbConnection.open()`) | postgres | `postgres`, `mysql` or `sqlite`. Any other value means postgres. | `DB_CONNECTION=sqlite` |
| `DB_HOST` | `dox_migration` | `localhost` | Database host. A path that starts with `/` is a Postgres Unix socket folder. | `DB_HOST=127.0.0.1` |
| `DB_PORT` | `dox_migration` | `5432` (postgres), `3306` (mysql) | Database port. | `DB_PORT=5432` |
| `DB_USERNAME` | `dox_migration` | `postgres` (postgres), `root` (mysql) | Database user. | `DB_USERNAME=app` |
| `DB_PASSWORD` | `dox_migration` | `postgres` (postgres), empty (mysql) | Database password. | `DB_PASSWORD=secret` |
| `DB_DATABASE` | `dox_migration` | falls back to `DB_NAME`, then `dox` | Database name. For sqlite: the file path. | `DB_DATABASE=dox` |
| `DB_NAME` | `dox_migration` | `dox` | Same as `DB_DATABASE`. `DB_DATABASE` wins when both are set. | `DB_NAME=dox` |
| `HOME` / `USERPROFILE` | build hooks of `dox_http_native`, `dox_postgres_native`, `dox_mysql_native` | empty | Used to find `~/.cargo/bin/cargo` when the library must be built from source. | set by the OS |
| `DART_VM_OPTIONS` | the Dart VM | not set | Flags for the VM. The AOT binary from `dox build` reads it. Dox never sets VM flags for you. See [Performance](../digging-deeper/performance.md#dart-vm-flags). | `DART_VM_OPTIONS=--new_gen_semi_max_size=64` |

`DOX_SERVER`, `DOX_HTTP_THREAD` and `DOX_DB_DRIVER` are read with `Platform.environment` or `std::env::var`. They do not work from `.env`.

## Read by a new project

A new project (`dox create`) reads these keys through its typed env class, `lib/config/env.dart`. The framework itself does not read them. In code, use the getter: `env.appPort`.

| Variable | Getter | Type | Default | Used for |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `APP_NAME` | `appName` | `String` | `dox` | `LoggerConfig.name`. |
| `APP_ENV` | `appEnv` | `String` | `development` | `development`, `staging` or `production`. `env.isDevelopment` is `true` for `development`. It turns on `prettyPrint` of the logger and the query log of the database. Also read by the framework (see above). |
| `APP_PORT` | `appPort` | `int` | `3000` | `AppConfig.serverPort`. When `APP_PORT` is not set, Dox listens on `PORT` if the env has it. |
| `APP_KEY` | `appKey` | `String` | required | `AppConfig.appKey`. The app stops at start when it is missing. |
| `APP_TOTAL_ISOLATE` | `appTotalIsolate` | `int?` | not set: one per CPU core | `AppConfig.totalIsolate`. |
| `LOG_LEVEL` | `logLevel` | `String` | `info` | `LoggerConfig.level`. |
| `CACHE_STORE` | `cacheStore` | `String` | `file` | `CacheConfig.defaultStore`: `memory`, `file` or `redis`. |
| `STORAGE_DISK` | `storageDisk` | `String` | `local` | `StorageConfig.defaultDisk`: `local`, `s3` or `memory`. |
| `DB_CONNECTION` | `dbConnection` | `String` | `sqlite` | `DatabaseConfig.connection`: `sqlite`, `postgres` or `mysql`. |
| `DB_NAME` | `dbName` | `String` | `db/dox.sqlite` | The database name. For SQLite: the file path. |
| `DB_HOST` | `dbHost` | `String` | `localhost` | Database host. |
| `DB_PORT` | `dbPort` | `int?` | not set: `5432` for Postgres, `3306` for MySQL | Database port. |
| `DB_USERNAME` | `dbUsername` | `String` | `postgres` | Database user. |
| `DB_PASSWORD` | `dbPassword` | `String` | empty | Database password. |

To add a key, add a getter to `AppEnv` and run `dart run build_runner build`. See [Environments](../guides/environments.md#2-add-a-key).

The `.env.example` of a new project:

```ini title=".env.example"
APP_NAME=dox
APP_ENV=development
APP_PORT=3000
APP_KEY=KKep5qC6uHlAgrwaQTQewgMRSIqQnoj0

CACHE_STORE=file
STORAGE_DISK=local

# SQLite needs no setup. The file is created at the first start.
DB_CONNECTION=sqlite
DB_NAME=db/dox.sqlite

# Postgres or MySQL: set DB_CONNECTION=postgres or mysql and fill these in.
DB_HOST=localhost
DB_PORT=5432
DB_USERNAME=postgres
DB_PASSWORD=postgres
```

## Only for work on Dox itself

| Variable | Who reads it | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `PG_URL` | Rust tests of `dox_postgres_native` | A Postgres URL. The test is skipped when it is not set. |
| `DB_HOST`, `DB_PORT`, `THREADS` | `packages/dox-postgres-native/tool/stress.dart` | The stress tool. |

## How `.env` is parsed

`Env._loadEnv()` in `packages/dox-core/lib/env/env.dart`:

- One `KEY=value` per line. The key is trimmed.
- The value is everything after the first `=`. A second `=` is kept.
- Every `"`, `'` and `` ` `` character is removed from the value. Then it is trimmed.
- `#` is not special. `KEY=abc # note` gives the value `abc # note`.
- An empty value, or the text `null`, counts as missing.
- The file is read once per isolate, from the current working directory.


---

# Request and response

Source: https://dartondox.dev/latest/3.xreference/request-and-response/

# Request and response

A compact list of the members. Examples and explanations are on the [Request](../the-basic/request.md) and [Response](../the-basic/response.md) pages.

## `DoxRequest`

Source: `packages/dox-core/lib/http/request/dox_request.dart`. It implements `IDoxRequest` from `dox_annotation`.
A middleware gets an `IDoxRequest`. A controller gets a `DoxRequest`. The members marked `IDoxRequest` are on both.

### Input

| Member | Returns | What it gives | On `IDoxRequest` |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `validate<T>({Source? source})` | `Future<T>` | The request checked with the DTO `T`. Throws the `422` `ValidationException` on bad input. Throws `StateError` when `T` is not in `AppConfig.dtos`. | no |
| `validateSchema<O>(Schema<O> schema)` | `Future<O>` | Query and body checked with a fluent `dox_validation` schema. | no |
| `all()` | `Map<String, dynamic>` | Query and body together. Body wins on the same key. | yes |
| `only(List<String> keys)` | `Map<String, dynamic>` | Only these keys from `all()`. A missing key gives `null`. | yes |
| `input(String key)` | `dynamic` | One value from `all()`. | yes |
| `has(String key)` | `bool` | `true` when the key is there and its text is not empty. | yes |
| `add(String key, dynamic value)` | `void` | Adds a value to `all()` and `body`. | yes |
| `merge(Map<String, dynamic> values)` | `void` | Adds many values to `all()` and `body`. | yes |
| `body` | `Map<String, dynamic>` | The parsed body (JSON or form fields). Files are `RequestFile`. | no |
| `query` | `Map<String, dynamic>` | The query string. | no |
| `param` | `Map<String, dynamic>` | The route params, like `{'id': '5'}`. | no |
| `pathParams` | `Map<String, String>` | The route params as text. `null` values are left out. | no |
| `requestBody` | `RequestBody` | The body as it was read, for DTOs. | no |
| `isJson()` | `bool` | The content type is JSON. | yes |
| `isFormData()` | `bool` | The content type is form data (`multipart/form-data` or urlencoded). | yes |
| `toJson()` | `Map<String, dynamic>` | `all()` with files replaced by their file name. Lets `jsonEncode(req)` work. | yes |

### Headers, cookies and client

| Member | Returns | What it gives | On `IDoxRequest` |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `header(String key)` | `String?` | One header. `null` when it is not there. | yes |
| `headers` | `Map<String, dynamic>` | Every header. Many values of one name are joined. | yes |
| `httpHeaders` | `HttpHeaders` | The `dart:io` headers object. | no |
| `contentType` | `ContentType?` | The parsed `Content-Type`. | yes |
| `cookie(String key, {bool decrypt = true})` | `String?` | One cookie. Decrypted with `appKey` unless `decrypt: false`. | yes |
| `ip()` | `String` | The client IP, or `unknown`. From `X-Forwarded-For` only behind a trusted proxy. | yes |
| `scheme()` | `String` | `http` or `https`. From `X-Forwarded-Proto` only behind a trusted proxy. | no |
| `isSecure()` | `bool` | `scheme()` is `https`. | no |
| `clientIp` | `String?` | The client IP, or `null`. | no |
| `userAgent()` | `String` | The `User-Agent` header, or `unknown`. | yes |
| `host()` | `String` | The `Host` header, or `unknown`. | yes |
| `origin()` | `String?` | The `Origin` header. | yes |
| `referer()` | `String?` | The `Referer` header. | yes |
| `locale` | `String?` | The first language of `Accept-Language`, like `th`. `null` when there is none or it is `*`. | no |
| `auth` | `IAuth?` | The auth object set by `AuthMiddleware`, or `null`. | yes |

### Route and raw request

| Member | Returns | What it gives | On `IDoxRequest` |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `method` | `String` | The HTTP method in upper case. | yes |
| `uri` | `Uri` | The request URI. | yes |
| `route` | `RouteData` | The matched route. | no |
| `getRouteData()` | `RouteData` | Same as `route`. | yes |
| `getRouteIdentifier()` | `String` | base64 of `<method>|<domain><path>`. Useful as a cache or rate limit key. | yes |
| `httpRequest` | `HttpRequest` | The `dart:io` request. Use it for raw access. | yes |

## `DoxResponse`

Source: `packages/dox-core/lib/http/response/dox_response.dart`.
Every setter returns the same `DoxResponse`, so calls chain.

| Member | Returns | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `DoxResponse(dynamic content)` | `DoxResponse` | The constructor. `content` can be a `String`, number, `Map`, `List`, a JSON serializable object, a `Stream<List<int>>`, a `File`, a `StreamFile` or a `DownloadableFile`. |
| `response([dynamic content])` | `DoxResponse` | Top level helper. Same as `DoxResponse(content)`. |
| `statusCode(int code)` | `DoxResponse` | Sets the status. Default `200`. |
| `content(dynamic content)` | `DoxResponse` | Replaces the content. |
| `getContent()` | `dynamic` | The content as it was given. |
| `stream(Stream<List<int>> stream)` | `DoxResponse` | Sets a byte stream as content. |
| `contentType(ContentType type)` | `DoxResponse` | Sets `Content-Type`. A `File` without it gets the type from its extension. |
| `header(String key, dynamic value)` | `DoxResponse` | Adds one header. |
| `withHeaders(Map<String, dynamic> values)` | `DoxResponse` | Replaces every header set so far with this map. |
| `cookie(DoxCookie cookie, {bool setExpire = false})` | `DoxResponse` | Adds a `Set-Cookie` header. `setExpire: true` sends the cookie as expired, which removes it. |
| `cache(Duration duration)` | `DoxResponse` | Sets `Cache-Control: max-age=<seconds>`. |
| `process(HttpRequest request)` | `dynamic` | Internal. Writes headers, status, cookies and the body. |

How the content is sent (`responseDataHandler` in `packages/dox-core/lib/http/http_response_handler.dart`):

| Content | Sent as |
| --- | --- |
| `null` | an empty body |
| `String` | text, as it is |
| `Map`, `List`, number, `bool`, object with `toJson()` | JSON, `Content-Type: application/json` |
| `DateTime` | its ISO 8601 text |
| `File` | streamed, with `Content-Length`, `Accept-Ranges` and one `Range` supported |
| `StreamFile` | streamed with its content type |
| `DownloadableFile` | streamed with `Content-Disposition: attachment` |
| `Stream<List<int>>` | streamed chunk by chunk |
| `IHttpException` | its status and `toResponse()`, see [HTTP exceptions](http-exceptions.md) |
| other `Exception` or `Error` | `500` with `toString()` as text |

A plain value returned from a controller (not a `DoxResponse`) is sent the same way. It only goes through a `DoxResponse` when `AppConfig.responseHandler` is set, or when it is a `File`, `StreamFile` or `DownloadableFile`.


---

# HTTP exceptions

Source: https://dartondox.dev/latest/3.xreference/http-exceptions/

# HTTP exceptions

An exception that extends `IHttpException` turns into an HTTP error answer.
You can `throw` it or `return` it from a middleware or a controller.

`IHttpException` is in `packages/dox-annotation/lib/src/core_annotation.dart`:

```dart
abstract class IHttpException {
  int code = 500;
  String errorCode = 'server_error';
  dynamic message = 'Server Error';

  dynamic toResponse() {
    if (message is Map) {
      return message;
    }
    return <String, dynamic>{'code': errorCode, 'message': message.toString()};
  }
}
```

## The classes

Every class takes the named parameters `message`, `errorCode` and `code`. The table shows the defaults.

| Class | Package | Status `code` | `errorCode` | Default `message` | Dox throws it when |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `BadRequestException` | `dox_core` | `400` | `bad_request` | `Bad Request` | the body can not be read, like JSON that is not valid |
| `UnAuthorizedException` | `dox_auth` | `401` | `unauthorized` | `Authentication failed` | `AuthMiddleware` finds no valid token |
| `NotFoundHttpException` | `dox_core` | `404` | `not_found` | `Not Found` | a typed path param does not fit (`{id}` is not an `int`) |
| `PayloadTooLargeException` | `dox_core` | `413` | `payload_too_large` | `Payload Too Large` | the body is bigger than `maxBodySize` or `maxMultipartSize` |
| `UnsupportedMediaTypeException` | `dox_core` | `415` | `unsupported_media_type` | `Unsupported Media Type` | a DTO reads a body that is not JSON and not form data |
| `ValidationException` | `dox_core` | `422` | `validation_failed` | `{}` (a `Map`) | a DTO or `req.validate()` finds bad input |
| `InternalErrorException` | `dox_core` | `500` | `server_error` | `Server Error` | never by itself; for your own use |
| `QueryException` | `dox_core` | `500` | `sql_query_error` | `Error in sql query` | never by itself; for your own use |

Source files: `packages/dox-core/lib/exception/*.dart` and `packages/dox-auth/lib/src/auth_exception.dart`.

## What the client gets

`responseDataHandler` in `packages/dox-core/lib/http/http_response_handler.dart` sends the answer:

1. The status is set to `code`.
2. The body is `toResponse()`.
3. The body is sent as JSON with `Content-Type: application/json`.

A text message gives a JSON body with the `errorCode` and the `message`:

```
HTTP/1.1 404 Not Found
content-type: application/json

{"code":"not_found","message":"Not Found"}
```

```dart
throw NotFoundHttpException(message: 'Blog not found');
```

```
HTTP/1.1 404 Not Found
content-type: application/json

{"code":"not_found","message":"Blog not found"}
```

A `Map` message is sent as it is, with no `code` key. `ValidationException` always has a map, one entry per field:

```
HTTP/1.1 422 Unprocessable Entity
content-type: application/json

{"email":"The email is not a valid email","name":"The name is required"}
```

A request for a path that has no route answers like a `NotFoundHttpException` with the message `<METHOD> <path> not found`: `{"code":"not_found","message":"GET /nothing not found"}`. Your `responseHandler` gets it too, so you can change its shape.

To send your own JSON shape from one exception, pass a map:

```dart
throw NotFoundHttpException(
  message: <String, dynamic>{'error': 'not_found', 'message': 'Blog not found'},
);
```

Other errors: any `Exception` or `Error` that is not an `IHttpException` gets `500` with `error.toString()` as text body. It is also passed to `errorHandler` in `AppConfig`. An `IHttpException` is not passed to `errorHandler`.

A `ValidationException` from `dox_validation` (thrown by `schema.parse()` in a controller) is turned into the `422` `ValidationException` of `dox_core` with the same errors.

## Make your own

Extend `IHttpException` and set the three fields in the constructor:

```dart
import 'dart:io';

import 'package:dox_core/dox_core.dart';

class ForbiddenException extends IHttpException {
  ForbiddenException({
    dynamic message = 'Forbidden',
    String errorCode = 'forbidden',
    int code = HttpStatus.forbidden,
  }) {
    super.code = code;
    super.errorCode = errorCode;
    super.message = message;
  }
}
```

Use it:

```dart
Future<dynamic> destroy(DoxRequest req, int id) async {
  if (req.auth?.user<User>()?.id != id) {
    throw ForbiddenException();
  }
}
```

Override `toResponse()` when every error of your app should have the same JSON shape:

```dart
class ApiException extends IHttpException {
  ApiException(int code, String errorCode, String message) {
    super.code = code;
    super.errorCode = errorCode;
    super.message = message;
  }

  @override
  dynamic toResponse() {
    return <String, dynamic>{'code': errorCode, 'message': message};
  }
}
```

More examples are on the [Response](../the-basic/response.md#errors) page.


---

# Production checklist

Source: https://dartondox.dev/latest/3.xreference/production-checklist/

# Production checklist

Check each item before you deploy. Each item says what to check, how to do it, and where to read more.

Items marked **Dox limit** are things Dox does not do for you. You must handle them outside Dox.

## Secrets and config

| Check | How | Read more |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `APP_KEY` is set, long and secret | `dox key:generate`, or a 32 character random value in the real env. It signs JWT tokens and encrypts cookies. Never use the value from `.env.example`. | [Encryption](../security/encryption.md) |
| `APP_ENV=production` | With it, an empty `APP_KEY` stops the app at start (`StateError`). Without it, Dox only logs a warning and runs with an empty key. | [Env reference](env.md) |
| The env is complete | Run `dox env:check` in CI or before the deploy. It exits with code 1 when a key is missing or bad. | [CLI](cli.md) |
| No secrets in the image or in git | `.env` in `.dockerignore` and `.gitignore`. Pass values as env vars (`docker run -e`, `env_file:`, systemd `EnvironmentFile=`). `dox build` copies `.env.example` only. | [Docker](../guides/docker.md) |
| No comments after values in `.env` | `KEY=abc # note` gives the value `abc # note`. Put comments on their own line. | [Troubleshooting](troubleshooting.md) |

## Auth and passwords

| Check | How | Read more |
| --- | --- | --- |
| JWT tokens expire | `JwtAuthDriver.expiresIn` is 1 hour by default. Pick a time that fits your app, like `JwtAuthDriver(secret: SecretKey(env.appKey), expiresIn: Duration(hours: 12))`. | [Authentication](../security/authentication.md) |
| You can not revoke one token | **Dox limit.** There is no token list on the server. To log out everyone, change `APP_KEY`. | [Authentication](../security/authentication.md) |
| Passwords are hashed | `user.password = Hash.make(input)` (bcrypt). Never store or encrypt a plain password. | [Hashing](../security/hashing.md) |
| The hash is never sent | `List<String> get hidden => <String>['password'];` in the user model. The JWT payload is `user.toJson()`, and anyone can read it. | [Authentication](../security/authentication.md) |
| Passwords have a max length | bcrypt throws on input over 72 bytes. Add `@MaxLength(72)` to the password field of the DTO. It counts characters, so non-ASCII text can still pass 72 bytes. | [Troubleshooting](troubleshooting.md) |

## HTTP and network

| Check | How | Read more |
| --- | --- | --- |
| HTTPS at the proxy | Dox has no TLS server. Run Caddy or nginx in front. Keep the app port private. | [Deployment](../digging-deeper/deployment.md) |
| `trustedProxies` is set behind a proxy | `AppConfig(trustedProxies: <String>['127.0.0.1', '::1'])`, or the proxy network, like `'172.16.0.0/12'`. Without it, `req.ip()` is the proxy and `req.scheme()` is `http`. Do not use `['*']` when the app port is public. | [App config](app-config.md) |
| Body limits are on | Keep `maxBodySize` (10 MB) and `maxMultipartSize` (100 MB), or lower them. Set the same limit in the proxy: `client_max_body_size 100m;` | [Request](../the-basic/request.md) |
| CORS has real origins | `CORSConfig(origin: 'https://my.app')`, or a list like `<String>['https://my.app', 'https://admin.my.app']`. With a list, Dox sends back only the request origin when it is in the list. | [CORS](../security/cors.md) |
| No `credentials: true` with `origin: '*'` | The new project's `cors.dart` has `origin: '*'` and `credentials: true` with `enabled: false`. When you turn CORS on, set a real origin first. | [CORS](../security/cors.md) |
| Rate limiting | **Dox limit.** Dox has no rate limiter. Do it at the proxy. See [below](#rate-limit-at-the-proxy). | [Deployment](../digging-deeper/deployment.md) |
| gzip at the proxy | Keep `compress: false`. Turn on gzip in Caddy (`encode gzip`) or nginx (`gzip on;`). | [Performance](../digging-deeper/performance.md) |
| OpenAPI docs | Off in production by default (on only for `APP_ENV` `development` or `local`). Do not set `enabled: true` for a private API. | [OpenAPI](../packages/openapi.md) |

## Build and run

| Check | How | Read more |
| --- | --- | --- |
| AOT binary, not `dart run` | `dox build`, then run `build/bundle/bin/server`. Keep `bin/` and `lib/` together. Not `dart compile exe`. | [Deployment](../digging-deeper/deployment.md) |
| Native server is on | The start line says `(native)`. When it says `(dart:io)`, look for the `[dox] warning: dox_http_native did not load` line. | [Native server](../digging-deeper/native-server.md) |
| Native database driver is on | No `[dox] warning: dox_postgres_native did not load` (or `mysql`) line at start. Do not set `DOX_DB_DRIVER=dart`. Postgres with TLS uses the Dart driver. | [Postgres native](../database/postgres-native.md) |
| Isolates = cores | Keep the default `totalIsolate` (`Platform.numberOfProcessors`), or set `APP_TOTAL_ISOLATE` to the cores the container really gets. Use fewer when the database runs on the same machine. | [Isolate](../digging-deeper/isolate.md) |
| Shared state across isolates | Cache: `redis`, not `memory`. WebSocket: `WebsocketRedisAdapter`. Socket.IO: a Redis adapter and `transports: ['websocket']`. | [Isolate](../digging-deeper/isolate.md) |
| A supervisor restarts the process | Docker `restart: unless-stopped`, or systemd `Restart=always`. Dox restarts a dead worker isolate, but not the main isolate. | [Deployment](../digging-deeper/deployment.md) |
| Writable temp folder | Uploads over 1 MB go to a temp file. A `FROM scratch` image needs `/tmp` with mode `1777`. | [Docker](../guides/docker.md) |
| Uploads live on a volume or S3 | The `local` disk writes to `storage/`. Mount it as a volume, or use the `s3` disk. | [File storage](../digging-deeper/file-storage.md) |

## Database

| Check | How | Read more |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Postgres or MySQL for a busy app | SQLite has one connection per isolate, and a query blocks the isolate. Use it for small apps only. With SQLite use an absolute file path, never `:memory:` with many isolates. | [Database](../database/index.md) |
| Migrations run once per deploy | The new project runs `Migrator(migrations: migrations).migrate()` in `bin/server.dart` before `startServer()`. Or run `dart run bin/migrate.dart run` (or `dox migrate`) in CI. Do one, not both at the same time on many machines. | [Migration](../database/migration.md) |
| Migrations use the right database | `dox_migration` reads `.env` when the file exists, and ignores the real env then. Do not ship a `.env` next to the binary, or give `Migrator(connection: ...)` your own pool. | [Troubleshooting](troubleshooting.md) |
| Small MySQL migrations | MySQL saves `CREATE`, `ALTER` and `DROP` at once. A failed migration can leave half the changes. One table change per migration. | [Migration](../database/migration.md) |
| Pool size fits the database | `extra: {'maxConnectionCount': 10}` is per isolate. Total = isolates x pool size. Keep it under the database `max_connections`. | [Database](../database/index.md) |
| Query logging is off | The new project's `database.dart` has `debug: true` on every connection, which prints every query. Set `debug: false` in production. | [Database](../database/index.md) |
| Backups | **Dox limit.** Dox has no backup tool. Use `pg_dump`, `mysqldump`, managed database snapshots, or a copy of the SQLite file (with the `-wal` file, or `sqlite3 app.db ".backup x.db"`). Test a restore. | |

## Logs and errors

| Check | How | Read more |
| --- | --- | --- |
| JSON logs | `LoggerConfig(enabled: true, prettyPrint: false)`. The new project sets `prettyPrint` only when `APP_ENV=development`. | [App config](app-config.md) |
| Log level | Set `LOG_LEVEL=warn` to print only warnings and errors. | [App config](app-config.md) |
| Access logs in one place | `LogMiddleware` writes one line per request, every 20 ms. A hard kill can lose the last lines. Turn it off when the proxy already logs requests. | [Performance](../digging-deeper/performance.md) |
| Errors go to your tracker | Set `AppConfig.errorHandler`. Any non-HTTP error is passed to it. The client gets `500` with the error text, so do not put secrets in exception messages. | [HTTP exceptions](http-exceptions.md) |

## Health and shutdown

| Check | How | Read more |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Health route | **Dox limit.** Dox has no built-in health route. Add one that asks the database: `Route.get('/health', healthController.check)` with `await QueryBuilder.query('select 1');`. | [Docker](../guides/docker.md) |
| Graceful shutdown | On `SIGTERM` or `SIGINT`, Dox stops taking connections and lets open requests finish, in every isolate. Set `shutdownTimeout` below the kill timeout of your platform. Close connections in a `DoxShutdown` service. | [Deployment](../digging-deeper/deployment.md#graceful-shutdown) |
| Zero downtime deploys | Run two processes (or machines) behind the proxy. Restart one at a time. | [Deployment](../digging-deeper/deployment.md) |

## Rate limit at the proxy

Dox has no rate limiter. Add one in the proxy.

nginx:

```nginx
# in http { }
limit_req_zone $binary_remote_addr zone=api:10m rate=10r/s;

# in server { location / { } }
limit_req zone=api burst=20 nodelay;
limit_req_status 429;
```

Caddy needs the [`caddy-ratelimit`](https://github.com/mholt/caddy-ratelimit) plugin (build Caddy with `xcaddy build --with github.com/mholt/caddy-ratelimit`):

```
example.com {
  rate_limit {
    zone api {
      key    {remote_host}
      events 100
      window 1m
    }
  }
  reverse_proxy 127.0.0.1:3000
}
```

!!! note
    The proxy must see the real client IP. When there is a load balancer in front of the proxy, set the real IP module of the proxy first.


---

# Troubleshooting

Source: https://dartondox.dev/latest/3.xreference/troubleshooting/

# Troubleshooting

Real problems, with the text you see, the cause and the fix. The texts come from the source code.

## The native HTTP library did not load

**Symptom.** One line at start, on stderr:

```
[dox] warning: dox_http_native did not load, using the dart:io server (<reason>)
```

and the start line says `(dart:io)` instead of `(native)`:

```
Server started at http://[::]:3000 with 8 isolate (dart:io)
```

At build time (`dart pub get`, `dox serve` or `dox build`) you may also see one of these:

```
dox_http_native: no native library for <os>-<arch>. Dox will use dart:io.
dox_http_native: download dox_http_native-<os>-<arch>.<ext>: 404
dox_http_native: download dox_http_native-<os>-<arch>.<ext> failed: <error>
dox_http_native: sha256 of dox_http_native-<os>-<arch>.<ext> does not match
dox_http_native: cargo build failed
```

**Cause.** The build hook of `dox_http_native` (`packages/dox-http-native/hook/build.dart`) tries, in this order: the `lib_path` user define, a local `native/target/release` build, the GitHub release download, and `cargo build`. None worked. Common reasons:

- No internet during `dart pub get`, or the release has no build for your OS and CPU (there are builds for macOS arm64 and x64, Linux x64 and arm64, Windows x64).
- Rust is not installed, so the fallback `cargo build` can not run.
- You compiled with `dart compile exe`. It does not run build hooks, so no native library is in the binary.
- The `<reason>` is `native library ABI <x>, expected <y>`: the library on disk is from another version of the package.

**Fix.** Pick one:

1. Accept `dart:io`. The app works, only slower. To hide the warning set `DOX_SERVER=dartio` or `server: ServerBackend.dartIo` in `AppConfig`.
2. Install Rust with [rustup](https://rustup.rs) and run `dart pub get` again. The hook builds the library with `cargo`.
3. Download the library from the GitHub release `dox_http_native-v<version>` yourself and point to it in the root `pubspec.yaml`:

    ```yaml
    hooks:
      user_defines:
        dox_http_native:
          lib_path: /path/to/libdox_http_native.so
    ```

4. Build with `dox build` (it runs `dart build cli`), not with `dart compile exe`.

The same applies to the native database drivers. The warning is then:

```
[dox] warning: dox_postgres_native did not load, using the Dart postgres driver (<reason>)
[dox] warning: dox_mysql_native did not load, using the Dart mysql driver (<reason>)
```

The Dart driver is used. To choose it on purpose set `DOX_DB_DRIVER=dart` or `extra: {'native': false}` on the connection.

See [Native server](../digging-deeper/native-server.md), [Postgres native](../database/postgres-native.md) and [MySQL native](../database/mysql-native.md).

## Port already in use

**Symptom.** With the `dart:io` server:

```
SocketException: Failed to create server socket (OS Error: Address already in use, errno = 48), address = ::, port = 3000
```

(`errno = 48` on macOS, `errno = 98` on Linux.) With the native server:

```
SocketException: dox_http_native: bind failed (<code>), port = 3000
```

**Cause.** Another process listens on the port. Often it is an old `bin/server.dart` that `dox serve` did not stop, or a second copy of the app.

**Fix.** Find and stop the process, or use another port.

```bash
lsof -i :3000          # macOS and Linux: who has the port
kill <pid>
```

Or set `APP_PORT=3001` in `.env` (a new project reads it into `serverPort`).

## build_runner: conflicting outputs

**Symptom.** `dox build_runner:build`, `dox serve` or `dox build` stops with a build_runner message that starts with `Conflicting outputs were detected`, and names files like `lib/dtos.g.dart` or `lib/app/models/user/user.model.g.dart`.

**Cause.** The generated `.g.dart` files are on disk, but `.dart_tool/build` does not know them. This happens after a `git clone` with committed `.g.dart` files, after deleting `.dart_tool`, or after a Dart SDK update.

**Fix.** Delete the build cache and build again:

```bash
rm -rf .dart_tool/build
dart run build_runner build
```

If that is not enough, delete the named `.g.dart` files and build again. Older build_runner versions accept `dart run build_runner build --delete-conflicting-outputs`. Newer versions removed that flag, so the Dox CLI does not pass it.

## `dox create` throws `RangeError`

**Symptom.**

```
dox create my_app
RangeError (index): Invalid value: Only valid value is 0: 1
```

**Cause.** A bug in the `dox` CLI up to `3.0.0-alpha.4`: the `create` command read the `--version` flag before it checked that one was given. The same versions also downloaded an old project template.

**Fix.** Update the CLI. The fix is in the version after `3.0.0-alpha.4`:

```bash
dart pub global activate dox
```

Until then, pass the version by hand:

```bash
dox create my_app --version 3.0.0-alpha.4
```

## A `.env` value with `#`

A `#` after a space starts a comment. The comment is not part of the value.

```ini
APP_PORT=3000 # dev port   -> 3000
DB_PASSWORD=abc#123        -> abc#123 (no space before the #)
DB_PASSWORD="abc # 123"    -> abc # 123 (quotes keep the #)
```

When a value must have ` #` in it (a space, then `#`), put the value in quotes. The quotes are removed.

## `Hash.verify` throws on a bad hash

**Symptom.**

```
Invalid argument(s) (salt): Invalid salt length (The length should be greater than or equal to 28): "..."
```

or

```
Invalid argument(s) (salt): Invalid salt version: "..."
```

or, when the password is long:

```
Invalid argument(s) (password): Password is too long (The length should be less than or equal to 72): "..."
```

**Cause.** `Hash.verify(password, hash)` calls `BCrypt.checkpw` from the `bcrypt` package. It throws an `ArgumentError` when `hash` is not a bcrypt hash (it must start with `$2` and be at least 28 characters), for example when the column holds a plain password, an empty string or a hash from another algorithm. It also throws when the password is longer than 72 bytes.

**Fix.**

- Make sure every stored password went through `Hash.make()`. A plain password in the column is a bug in the code that saved it.
- Check the hash before you compare it, and treat a bad one as a failed login:

    ```dart
    bool ok = hash.startsWith(r'$2') && Hash.verify(password, hash);
    ```

- Refuse passwords longer than 72 bytes in your DTO, for example `@Length(max: 72)`.

For normal login use `Auth().attempt()` from `dox_auth`. See [Hashing](../security/hashing.md).

## MySQL 8 login fails

**Symptom.** The connection to MySQL 8 is refused at login, while the same user works from the `mysql` client. Often the user was made with the default `caching_sha2_password` plugin.

**Cause.** `caching_sha2_password` needs either TLS or the server RSA public key to send the password. A client that has neither can not log in.

**Fix.** Both Dox drivers handle this by default:

- The native driver (`dox_mysql_native`) works with MySQL 8.4 `caching_sha2_password` and MariaDB 11.
- The Dart driver asks the server for its RSA key (`allowPublicKeyRetrieval` is `true` by default), so it works without TLS. Migrations do the same.

So check these settings on the connection in `lib/config/database.dart`:

| Setting | What to do |
| --- | --- |
| `extra: {'allowPublicKeyRetrieval': false}` | Remove it, or give the key in `extra: {'serverPublicKey': '...'}`. |
| `useSSL: true` | The server must have TLS on. |
| `host`, `port`, `user`, `password` | A wrong value gives the same login error. `DB_PORT` is `3306` by default for MySQL. |

As a last resort, change the user on the server:

```sql
ALTER USER 'app'@'%' IDENTIFIED WITH mysql_native_password BY 'secret';
```

## SQLite: the database file

**Symptom.** An `SqliteException` with `unable to open database file`, or an empty database after `dox build`.

**Cause.** `database` is a file path. A relative path is relative to the folder you start the app from. `dox build` tells you to run `cd build/bundle && ./bin/server`, so `dox.sqlite` is then `build/bundle/dox.sqlite`. SQLite makes a missing file, but not a missing folder.

**Fix.**

- Use an absolute path, or make the folder first.
- Set it with `DB_NAME` (a new project reads it): `DB_NAME=/var/lib/my_app/dox.sqlite`.
- Migrations use `DB_DATABASE` or `DB_NAME` as the path too. Use the same value for both.

!!! warning "`:memory:` and isolates"
    `:memory:` opens a new empty database in each isolate. With `totalIsolate` above 1, every isolate sees different data. Use a file, or `totalIsolate: 1`.

Dox opens a file database with `journal_mode = WAL`, `synchronous = NORMAL`, `foreign_keys = ON` and `busy_timeout = 5000` (change it with `extra: {'busyTimeout': ...}`).

## `dox: command not found` after `dart pub global activate`

**Symptom.**

```
zsh: command not found: dox
```

right after `dart pub global activate dox 3.0.0-alpha.4`.

**Cause.** `dart pub global activate` puts the `dox` script in `$HOME/.pub-cache/bin`. That folder is not in your `PATH`.

**Fix.** Add it to your shell profile and open a new terminal:

```bash
export PATH="$PATH":"$HOME/.pub-cache/bin"
```

On Windows the folder is `%LOCALAPPDATA%\Pub\Cache\bin`.

## Other startup errors

| Text | Cause | Fix |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `APP_KEY is not set. Run `dox key:generate` and put the key in .env` | `appKey` is empty. A warning in development, a `StateError` that stops the app when `APP_ENV=production`. | Run `dox key:generate`, or set `APP_KEY` in the environment. |
| `Env key "<KEY>" is not set and has no default` | `Env.get<int>()`, `<num>`, `<double>` or `<bool>` with no value and no default. | Set the key, or pass a default. |
| `<T> is not a known DTO. Add @Dto() to it, run `dart run build_runner build` and set `dtos: dtos` (lib/dtos.g.dart) in AppConfig.` | `req.validate<T>()` can not find the DTO. | Do what the text says. |
| `Route <METHOD> <path>: the controller parameter type <T> is not known. ...` | A controller parameter is not `DoxRequest`, a DTO, or `String`, `int`, `double`, `num`, `bool`. | Change the type, or add the DTO to `AppConfig.dtos`. |
| `Route <METHOD> <path>: a controller can have one @Dto only.` | Two DTO parameters on one controller. | Merge them into one DTO. |
| `Route <METHOD> <path>: only positional parameters are supported, not named or [optional] ones` | The controller has named or `[optional]` parameters. | Use positional parameters. |
| `db/migration has Dart migrations, but bin/migrate.dart is missing.` | `dox migration:*` found Dart migration files but no entry point. | Run `dox make:migration <name>` once. It writes `bin/migrate.dart`. |
| `<name> not found` (an `Exception` from `DatabaseConfig`) | `DatabaseConfig.connection` names a key that is not in `connections`. | Fix `DB_CONNECTION` or the map. |
| `Storage disk "<name>" has unknown driver "<type>"` | A disk in `StorageConfig` has a `driver` other than `local`, `s3` or `memory`. | Fix the driver name. |
| `Windows: the native server runs on one isolate` | Windows has no `SO_REUSEPORT`. | Not an error. Use `DOX_SERVER=dartio` to use every core on Windows. |
| `WebSocket or Socket.IO routes: using the dart:io server` | The native server can not upgrade to WebSocket yet. | Not an error. `DOX_SERVER=native` forces native, then WebSocket upgrades fail with `500`. |
