# Error index

Source: https://dartondox.dev/latest/3.xreference/errors/

# Error index

A lookup table of the messages Dox prints or throws. Search this page for the text you see.

- `<...>` is a part that changes, like a name or a number.
- Dart adds a prefix to some errors: `Bad state:` (`StateError`), `Invalid argument(s):` (`ArgumentError`), `Unsupported operation:` (`UnsupportedError`), `Exception:` (`Exception`).
- For problems that need a longer story, see [Troubleshooting](troubleshooting.md).

## dox_core: start of the app

| Text | When | What to do |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `APP_KEY is not set. Run `dox key:generate` and put the key in .env` | `appKey` is empty. A warning, or a `StateError` that stops the app when `APP_ENV=production`. | Run `dox key:generate`, or set `APP_KEY` in the env. |
| `[dox] warning: dox_http_native did not load, using the dart:io server (<reason>)` | The native HTTP library is missing or from another version. | See [Troubleshooting](troubleshooting.md#the-native-http-library-did-not-load). Or set `DOX_SERVER=dartio`. |
| `Server started at http://<host>:<port> with <n> isolate (<backend>)` | Normal start. `<host>` is the address it listens on: `[::]` means all interfaces. `<backend>` is `native` or `dart:io`. | Nothing. |
| `WebSocket or Socket.IO routes: using the dart:io server` | The app has WebSocket or Socket.IO. The native server can not upgrade yet. | Nothing. This is info. |
| `Windows: the native server runs on one isolate` | Windows has no `SO_REUSEPORT`. | Nothing, or `DOX_SERVER=dartio` to use every core. |
| `Socket.IO runs on <n> isolates: clients should use transports: ['websocket'] ...` | Socket.IO with more than one isolate and long-polling on. | Use a Redis adapter, and `transports: ['websocket']` in the client. |
| `[dox] isolate <n> error: <error>` | An error killed a worker isolate. The stack is on the next line. | Fix the error. Dox restarts the isolate. |
| `[dox] isolate <n> exited, restarting` | A worker isolate died. A new one starts after 1 second. | Look at the error line above it. |
| `SocketException: Failed to create server socket (OS Error: Address already in use, ...)` | The port is in use (`dart:io` server). | See [Troubleshooting](troubleshooting.md#port-already-in-use). |
| `SocketException: dox_http_native: bind failed (<code>), port = <port>` | The port is in use (native server). | Same as above. |

## dox_core: routes and controllers

These stop the app at start, so a bad route never reaches a request.

| Text | When | What to do |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `Route <where>: the controller parameter type <T> is not known. Use DoxRequest, a @Dto class, or String, int, double, num, bool for path params. ...` | A controller parameter has another type, or the DTO is not in `AppConfig.dtos`. | Change the type, or run `dart run build_runner build` and set `dtos: dtos`. |
| `Route <where>: the controller has more path params than the route has {...} params (<n>).` | The method asks for more path params than the path has. | Add the `{param}` to the path, or remove the parameter. |
| `Route <where>: a controller can have one @Dto only.` | Two DTO parameters. | Merge them into one DTO. |
| `Route <where>: only positional parameters are supported, not named or [optional] ones (<type>).` | Named or `[optional]` parameters. | Use positional parameters. Use `int?` with `{id?}` for an optional param. |
| `Route <where>: a controller can not be generic.` | The handler has type parameters. | Remove them. |
| `Route <where>: can not read the controller type <type>.` | Dox can not read the function type of the handler. | Use a plain method or function. |
| `Exception: websocket is not registered` | `Route.websocket()` runs before a `WebsocketServer(Dox())` exists. | Add the WebSocket service to `services`. See [WebSocket](../digging-deeper/websocket.md). |

## dox_core: env

| Text | When | What to do |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `EnvException: the env is not valid` then `  - <KEY> is missing` | `AppEnv.load()` found a required key with no value. | Set the key, or give the getter a default. |
| `  - <KEY> must be <type>, not "<value>"` | A value does not fit the getter type. | Fix the value. Check for a `# comment` after it. |
| `Env key "<KEY>" is not set and has no default` | `Env.get<int>()`, `<num>`, `<double>` or `<bool>` with no value and no default. | Set the key, or pass a default. |
| `Env key "<KEY>" is not a valid <type>: "<value>"` | `Env.get<int>()` (or another type) got text that is not that type. | Fix the value. |

See [Environment variables](../digging-deeper/env.md).

## dox_core: requests (what the client gets)

An `IHttpException` with a text message answers `{"code":"<errorCode>","message":"<text>"}`.
The table shows the `message` text.

| Status | Message | When | What to do |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `404` | `<METHOD> <path> not found` | No route matches. | Check the method, the path and the router `prefix`. |
| `404` | `Not Found` | A typed path param does not fit, like `abc` for `int id`. | Send a valid value. |
| `400` | `The body is not valid JSON` | A DTO reads a JSON body that does not parse. | Send valid JSON. |
| `400` | `The form body is not valid` | A urlencoded body that can not be decoded. | Fix the client encoding. |
| `415` | `Unsupported Media Type` | A DTO reads a body that is not JSON or form data. | Send `Content-Type: application/json` or form data. |
| `413` | `Payload Too Large` | The body is bigger than `maxBodySize` or `maxMultipartSize`. | Send less, or raise the limit. |
| `422` | `{"_root":"The input has too many items (max 1000) or levels (max 10)"}` | Form or query keys with more than 1000 list items or 10 levels. | Send less nested data. |
| `422` | `{"<field>":"<message>"}` | A DTO check failed. | See [Validation rules](../the-basic/validation-rules.md). |
| `431` | (no text) | Native server: request line plus headers over 16 KB. | Send smaller headers or cookies. |
| `500` | `<error>.toString()` | Any error that is not an `IHttpException`. It also goes to `errorHandler`. | Look at the server log. |

## dox_core: DTOs, storage and config

| Text | When | What to do |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `Bad state: <T> is not a known DTO. Add @Dto() to it, run `dart run build_runner build` and set `dtos: dtos` (lib/dtos.g.dart) in AppConfig.` | `req.validate<T>()` can not find `T`. | Do what the text says. |
| `Invalid argument(s): Storage disk "<name>" has unknown driver "<type>"` | A disk in `StorageConfig` has a `driver` other than `local`, `s3` or `memory`. | Fix the driver name. |
| `Invalid argument(s): Storage disk "<name>" needs the "<setting>" setting. It is missing or empty.` | An `s3` disk without `bucket`, `key` or `secret`, on its first use. | Set `AWS_BUCKET`, `AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID` and `AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY`. |
| `Invalid argument(s): invalid file` | `Storage().put()` with no `extension:`, and Dox can not find the type from the bytes. | Pass `extension: 'pdf'`. |
| `403` `invalid or expired signature` | A `Route.files()` URL without a valid `signature`, or after `expires`. | Make a new link with `Storage().signedUrl()`. |
| `404` `file not found` | `Storage().stream()` or `download()` of a missing file. | Check the path. |
| `Invalid argument (trustedProxies): not an ip or cidr: "<value>"` | A bad entry in `AppConfig.trustedProxies`. | Use an IP, a CIDR like `10.0.0.0/8`, or `*`. |
| `Invalid argument (type): must be asc or desc: "<value>"` | `orderBy(column, type)` with another direction. | Use `asc` or `desc`. |
| `400` `decrypt_failed` | `AESEncryptor.decode` got changed text or a wrong key. It throws `DecryptException`. `req.cookie()` catches it and returns `null`. | Check the key. For a cookie, ask the user to log in again. |

## dox_auth

| Text | When | What to do |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `401` `Authentication failed` | `AuthMiddleware` finds no token, a bad or expired token, or the user is deleted. | Send `Authorization: Bearer <token>`. Log in again. |
| `Invalid argument(s) (salt): Invalid salt length ...` | `Hash.verify()` with a value that is not a bcrypt hash. | See [Troubleshooting](troubleshooting.md#hashverify-throws-on-a-bad-hash). |
| `Invalid argument(s) (password): Password is too long ...` | bcrypt with a password over 72 bytes. | Limit the length in the DTO. |

`Auth().attempt()` returns `null` for a wrong password. It does not throw. See [Authentication](../security/authentication.md).

## dox_orm

| Text | When | What to do |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `[dox] warning: dox_postgres_native did not load, using the Dart postgres driver (<reason>)` | The native Postgres library did not load. | See [Postgres native](../database/postgres-native.md). Or set `DOX_DB_DRIVER=dart`. |
| `[dox] warning: dox_mysql_native did not load, using the Dart mysql driver (<reason>)` | The native MySQL library did not load. | See [MySQL native](../database/mysql-native.md). |
| `Exception: <name> not found` | `DatabaseConfig.connection` (or `withConnection()`) names a connection that is not in `connections`. | Fix `DB_CONNECTION` or the map. |
| `Exception: Invalid driver or not supported` | A `ConnectionConfig.driver` Dox can not open. | Use `Driver.postgres`, `Driver.mysql` or `Driver.sqlite`. |
| `Invalid argument(s): dox_postgres_native: bad connection config` | The native driver can not read the connection values. | Check `host`, `port`, `user`, `database`. |
| `Invalid argument(s): dox_mysql_native: bad connection config` | Same, for MySQL. | Same. |
| `SqliteException` with `unable to open database file` | The SQLite folder does not exist. | See [Troubleshooting](troubleshooting.md#sqlite-the-database-file). |

## dox_orm: schema builder

| Text | When | What to do |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `Bad state: foreign key <name>: call on(table)` | `table.foreign('x').references('id')` with no `.on('table')`. | Add `.on('table')`, or use `foreignId('x').constrained()`. |
| `Unsupported operation: postgres: change() of an auto increment column is not supported` | `change()` on an `id()` or `increments()` column. | Write the `ALTER` by hand with `schema.driver.execute()`. |
| `Unsupported operation: sqlite: can not add a primary key to an existing table` | `primary(...)` in `schema.table()` on SQLite. | Make the table again with the key in `schema.create()`. |
| `Unsupported operation: sqlite: can not rebuild <table>, it has CHECK constraints` | A SQLite rebuild (`change()`, `foreign()`, `dropForeign()`) on a table with other `CHECK`s. | Make the new table by hand in the migration. |
| `Unsupported operation: sqlite: can not rebuild <table>, it has generated columns` | Same, on a table with generated columns. | Same. |
| `Bad state: sqlite: table <table> not found` | A SQLite rebuild of a missing table. | Check the table name. |
| `Bad state: sqlite: column <table>.<column> not found` | `change()` or `renameColumn()` of a missing column on SQLite. | Check the column name. |
| `Bad state: sqlite: foreign key <names> not found` | `dropForeign()` of a key the table does not have. | Check the key name or columns. |
| `Bad state: sqlite: rebuild of <table> breaks foreign keys` | After the rebuild, rows point to missing parent rows. | Fix the data first. |
| `Unsupported operation: sqlite: change() rebuilds the table, it only runs on a database` | `table.toSql(SqliteGrammar())` with `change()`. | Run it on a database, not as text. |

## dox_migration

| Text | When | What to do |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `Exception: Could not connect to database: <error>` | The migrator can not open the database. | Check `DATABASE_URL` or the `DB_*` values. A real env var wins over `.env`. |
| `Unknown migration command: <cmd> (use run, rollback, reset, refresh or status)` | `dart run bin/migrate.dart <cmd>` with another command. | Use one of the five. |
| `Invalid argument(s): Invalid option <x>, use --step=<count>` | `rollback` with a bad option. | Use `--step=2`. |
| `Bad state: Migration <name> is both a Dart and a .sql migration` | Two files with the same name in `db/migration`. | Rename or delete one. |
| `Bad state: foreign key check failed: <table> points to a missing <parent> row` | SQLite: a migration left a broken foreign key. | Fix the data in the migration. |
| `Migrating: <name>` / `Migrated: <name>` | Normal progress. | Nothing. |
| `Migrations are already up to date!` | Nothing to run. | Nothing. |
| `Nothing to rollback!` | No batch to undo. | Nothing. |
| `No migrations found.` | `status` with no migrations. | Check `db/migration`. |

See [Migration](../database/migration.md).

## dox_cache

| Text | When | What to do |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `Invalid argument(s): Cache store "<name>" is not configured` | `Cache().store('<name>')` or `defaultStore` names a missing store. | Add the store to `CacheConfig.stores`, or fix `CACHE_STORE`. |
| `Invalid argument(s): Cache driver "<driver>" of store "<name>" is not supported` | A store has a `driver` other than `file`, `memory`, `redis` or `null`. | Fix the driver name. |
| `Unsupported operation: <Driver> does not support locks` | `lock()` on the `file` or `null` store. | Use the `memory` or `redis` store. |
| `Bad state: Cache value of "<key>" is not an integer` | `increment()` or `decrement()` on a value that is not an `int`. | Store an `int`, or `forget()` the key. |
| `Invalid argument(s): Cache value of "<key>" is bigger than <limit> bytes` | A Redis value is too big. | Store less, or use files or a database. |
| `Bad state: RedisDriver.flush needs a prefix. It will not delete the whole database.` | `flush()` on a Redis store with an empty `prefix`. | Set a `prefix`. |

See [Cache](../digging-deeper/cache.md).

## dox_storage

The text has the form `<Exception>: <message> (key: "<key>")`.

| Text | When | What to do |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `FileNotFoundException: File not found` | The file is not on the disk. | Check the path. `Storage()` paths start with `/`, `Disk` keys do not. |
| `PermissionDeniedException: Permission denied` | The OS (local) or S3 (`403`) refused it. | Check file rights, or the S3 key and bucket policy. |
| `InvalidKeyException: Invalid key: path traversal is not allowed` | A key with `..`. | Do not build keys from user input. |
| `InvalidKeyException: Invalid key: absolute paths are not allowed` | A `Disk` key that starts with `/` or a drive letter. | Remove the first `/`. |
| `InvalidKeyException: Invalid key: key is empty` | An empty key. | Pass a file name. |
| `UnsupportedOperationException: urlBase is not configured` | `Storage().url()` on a local disk with no `url` option. | Set `url` on the disk. |
| `UnsupportedOperationException: urlBase and appKey are needed for signed URLs` | `signedUrl()` on a local disk with no `url`, or no `APP_KEY`. | Set both. |
| `UnsupportedOperationException: S3 signed URLs must expire within 1 second and 7 days` | `signedUrl()` on S3 with a bad `expiresIn`. | Use a time up to 7 days. |
| `UnsupportedOperationException: Disk "<name>" is not registered` | `Storage().disk('<name>')` with a missing disk. | Add the disk to `StorageConfig.disks`. |
| `DriverException: <S3 error>` | Any other S3 error (network, `500`, wrong bucket). | Read the S3 code in the text. |

See [File storage](../digging-deeper/file-storage.md).

## dox_validation

| Text | When | What to do |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `Bad state: Schema has async rules. Use parseAsync() instead.` | `schema.parse()` on a schema with an async rule. | Use `await schema.parseAsync()`. |
| `Bad state: Rule "<name>" is async. Use parseAsync() instead.` | Same, for one `AsyncRule`. | Same. |
| `Bad state: This refine is async. Use parseAsync() instead.` | `refine()` with an async function and sync parse. | Same. |
| `Bad state: DTO <name> has an async validate(). Use parseAsync() instead.` | A DTO with `Future<void> validate()` checked with a sync call. | Use the async call, like `req.validate<T>()`. |
| `Bad state: No value: the key was missing. Check isPresent.` | `maybe.value` on a `Maybe<T>` that is missing. | Check `isPresent` first. |

See [dox_validation](../packages/validation.md).

## dox_builder (`build_runner`)

These stop `dart run build_runner build`.

| Text | When | What to do |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `The @Dto class <Name> has problems:` then a `- ...` list | One or more lines below. | Fix each line. |
| `- The field <Class.field> must be final.` | A DTO field is not `final`. | Add `final`. |
| `- The field <Class.field> must be a `this.<field>` parameter of the unnamed constructor.` | The field is not set by the constructor. | Add `this.<field>` to the constructor. |
| `- A @Dto class needs an unnamed constructor.` | Only named constructors. | Add `const Name({...})`. |
| `- A @Dto class can not extend another class (<Parent>).` | The DTO extends a class. | Copy the fields in. |
| `- A @Dto class can not be generic.` | The DTO has type parameters. | Remove them. |
| `- The type <T> of <where> is not supported. Use a basic type, an enum, DateTime, RequestFile, a @Dto class, or a List or Map of them.` | Field type not supported. | Change the type. |
| `- @<Rule> does not fit the type <T> of <where>.` | A rule on the wrong type, like `@Email()` on an `int`. | Move the rule, or change the type. |
| `- @Length on <where> needs min:, max: or both.` | `@Length()` with no limit. | Add `min:` or `max:`. |
| `- The @Regex on <where> is not a valid regex: <reason>` | The pattern does not compile. | Fix the pattern. |
| `- @MaxSize on <where> needs a size like '2MB' (units B, KB, MB, GB), not "<text>".` | Bad size text. | Use `'2MB'`. |
| `- The Maybe field <where> needs the default `const Maybe.missing()`.` | A `Maybe<T>` field without that default. | Add it. |
| `- <where> can not have both @Lowercase and @Uppercase.` | Both on one field. | Keep one. |
| `- The validate method of <Name> must take one DtoErrors: `void validate(DtoErrors errors)`.` | Wrong `validate` signature. | Use that signature. |
| `Two @Dto classes are named <Name>: in <a> and <b>. Dox finds DTOs by name, so rename one.` | Two DTOs with the same class name. | Rename one. |
| `Env getter "<name>" has type <T>. Use String, int, double, num, bool, Uri, Duration, an enum or List<String>.` | A `@DoxEnv` getter with another type. | Change the type. |
| `@DoxModel can only be used on a class.` / `@DoxEnv can only be used on a class.` | The annotation is on something else. | Put it on a class. |
| `Conflicting outputs were detected ...` | `build_runner` cache is out of date. | See [Troubleshooting](troubleshooting.md#build_runner-conflicting-outputs). |

## Native libraries (build hooks)

Printed during `dart pub get`, `dox serve` or `dox build`. `<pkg>` is `dox_http_native`, `dox_postgres_native` or `dox_mysql_native`. The app still runs, on the Dart fallback.

| Text | When | What to do |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `<pkg>: no native library for <os>-<arch>.` | No ready build for this OS and CPU. | Install Rust, or accept the fallback. |
| `<pkg>: download <file>: <status>` / `<pkg>: download <file> failed: <error>` | The GitHub download failed. | Check the network, then `dart pub get` again. |
| `<pkg>: sha256 of <file> does not match` | The downloaded file is not the expected one. | Delete `.dart_tool` and try again. |
| `<pkg>: cargo build failed` | The build from source failed. | Read the cargo output below it. |
| `Bad state: <pkg>: <path> does not exist` | The `lib_path` user define points to a missing file. | Fix the path in `pubspec.yaml`. |
| `Unsupported operation: dox_http_native can not detach the socket` | `DOX_SERVER=native` with a WebSocket route. The upgrade fails with `500`. | Do not force native for WebSocket apps. |

See [Native server](../digging-deeper/native-server.md).

## dox_socketio

Printed to stderr. The connection or the request fails, the app keeps running.

| Text | When | What to do |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `dox_socketio: handler error: <error>` | Your namespace handler threw. The stack follows. | Fix the handler. |
| `dox_socketio: request error: <error>` | A Socket.IO HTTP request failed. The client gets `500`. | Check the client version and transport. |
| `dox_socketio: redis publish failed: <error>` | The Redis adapter could not publish. | Check Redis. |
| `dox_socketio: bad redis message: <error>` | The Redis adapter got a message it can not read. | Check that every app on the channel runs the same version. |

## CLI

| Text | When | What to do |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `Could not find a command. Run `dox help` for more information.` | `dox` with no command. | Run `dox help`. |
| `Could not find a command named "<name>". Run `dox help` for more information.` | Unknown command. | Check the spelling. |
| `Invalid number of arguments for command "<name>".` | Too few or too many arguments. | Run `dox help <name>`. |
| `Command "<name>" not found.` | `dox help <name>` with an unknown command. | Run `dox help`. |
| `<name> already exists` | A `create:*` file is already there. | Pick another name, or delete the file. |
| `Folder name "<name>" already exist` | `dox create` into a folder that exists. | Pick another name. |
| `RangeError (index): Invalid value: Only valid value is 0: 1` | `dox create <name>` without `--version`, in `3.0.0-alpha.4`. | Pass `--version 3.0.0-alpha.4`. |
| `Invalid option <x>, use -m or --migration` | `dox create:model` with another option. | Use `-m`. |
| `Invalid option <x>, use --step=<count>` | `dox migration:rollback` with another option. | Use `--step=2`. |
| `db/migration has Dart migrations, but bin/migrate.dart is missing. ...` | Dart migrations but no entry file. | Run `dox make:migration <name>` once. |
| `Skip <file>: no class that extends Migration.` | A Dart file in `db/migration` has no migration class. | Add `class X extends Migration`, or move the file. |
| `.env.example is missing.` | `dox env:generate` with no example file. | Make `.env.example`. |
| `lib/config/env.dart is already there. Delete it to make it again.` | `dox env:generate` again. | Delete the file, or edit it by hand. |
| `lib/config/env.dart is missing. Run `dox env:generate` first.` | `dox env:check` with no env class. | Run `dox env:generate`. |
| `pubspec.yaml has no name.` | `dox env:check` can not find the package name. | Add `name:` to `pubspec.yaml`. |
| `bin/openapi.dart is missing. Make it with: ...` | `dox openapi:generate` with no entry file. | Make `bin/openapi.dart`. See [OpenAPI](../packages/openapi.md). |
| `zsh: command not found: dox` | `$HOME/.pub-cache/bin` is not in `PATH`. | See [Troubleshooting](troubleshooting.md#dox-command-not-found-after-dart-pub-global-activate). |

See [CLI](cli.md).

# Changelog

Source: https://dartondox.dev/latest/3.xreference/changelog/

# Changelog

What changed in each package, newest first. This page is made from the
`CHANGELOG.md` files in the repo when the docs are built.

## dox_annotation

### Unreleased

- New `timestamps` option on `@DoxModel`. `timestamps: false` turns off `created_at` and `updated_at`, like `$timestamps = false` in Laravel. `createdAt: null` or `updatedAt: null` turns off one of them.
- New `primaryKeyType` option on `@DoxModel`. Use `primaryKeyType: String` for a UUID key. The default is `int`.
- Fix: `IHttpException.toResponse()` now returns `{"code": errorCode, "message": message}` for a text message, so the client gets the `errorCode`. A `Map` message is returned as it is.

### 3.0.0-alpha.4

- Version bump only, to match the other packages.

### 3.0.0-alpha.3

- Version bump only, to match the other packages.

### 3.0.0-alpha.2

- Needs Dart 3.13 or newer.
- All dependencies updated to their latest versions.
- OpenAPI annotations, all optional: `@Summary`, `@Description`, `@Tags`, `@Request`, `@Body`, `@Query`, `@Response`, `@ApiDeprecated`, `@ApiIgnore`, `@DoxController`. Lower case names work too (`@summary(...)`), except `@Response`.
- The DTO annotations (`@Dto`, `@Length`, `@Email`, ...) live in `dox_validation`. `dox_core` exports them.
- `IDoxRequest` has no `validate()` and no `processInputMapper()` any more. Use a DTO.
- Breaking (small): these names are exported by `dox_core` too. If a file also imports a package with a `Request` or `Response` class (like `package:http`) without a prefix, add a prefix to that import.
- New `@DoxEnv()` and `@EnvKey('X')` for the typed env class.

### 3.0.0-alpha.1

- Version 3 of Dox. All Dox packages now share one version.
- Needs Dart 3.6 or newer.
- See the [release notes](https://github.com/dartondox/dox/pull/112) for all main changes.

## dox_auth

### Unreleased

- Breaking: `JwtAuthDriver.expiresIn` is 1 hour by default. Before, it was `null`, and tokens never expired.
- New: named guards work. Use `Auth(guard: 'admin')` and `AuthMiddleware(guard: 'admin')`. Before, only `defaultGuard` was used.
- A token keeps its guard name in the `aud` claim. A token from one guard does not work on another guard.
- `verifyToken` checks the `iss` claim when `issuer` is set.
- Breaking: `AuthDriver` methods get the guard name as a new parameter. `AuthEngine().guard(name)` replaces `AuthEngine().driver` and `AuthEngine().provider`.

### 3.0.0-alpha.4

- Version bump only, to match the other packages.

### 3.0.0-alpha.3

- Version bump only, to match the other packages.

### 3.0.0-alpha.2

- Needs Dart 3.13 or newer.
- All dependencies updated to their latest versions.
- `dart_jsonwebtoken` 3.4 (`pointycastle` 4).

### 3.0.0-alpha.1

- Version 3 of Dox. All Dox packages now share one version.
- Needs Dart 3.6 or newer.
- See the [release notes](https://github.com/dartondox/dox/pull/112) for all main changes.
- Uses `dox_orm` (was `dox_query_builder`).
- `dart_jsonwebtoken` 3.

## dox_builder

### Unreleased

- `@DoxModel(timestamps: false)` makes a model without `createdAt` and `updatedAt`. `createdAt: null` or `updatedAt: null` turns off only one.
- The primary key field has the type of `@DoxModel(primaryKeyType: ...)`. It was always `int?`. The default is still `int`. The OpenAPI model schema uses the same type.
- Fix: a preloaded relation with a two word name (like `userInfo`) was missing from `toJson()`. The generator looked for `user_info` in the preload list, but the list has `userInfo`.
- Fix: the OpenAPI route scanner now puts one `/` between a group and a route path, like the router does.

### 3.0.0-alpha.4

- Version bump only, to match the other packages.

### 3.0.0-alpha.3

- Version bump only, to match the other packages.

### 3.0.0-alpha.2

- Needs Dart 3.13 or newer.
- All dependencies updated to their latest versions.
- New builder `dox_builder:openapi`. It writes `lib/openapi.g.dart` with the OpenAPI docs of the app: it reads the `Route.*` calls, the controllers, the `@Dto` classes and the models. It writes nothing when the package has no controllers.
- `DtoJsonSchema`, `ModelSchema` and `JsonSchemaReader`: the JSON Schema of a `@Dto` class, a model or any Dart type. Other builders can use them.
- New: the DTO generator. For each `@Dto` class it writes `$<Name>Dto` (a `const DtoSchema<Name>`) into the `.g.dart` part: plain `if` checks per field, the converter, `fromMap`, `toMap` and the JSON Schema. It stops the build with a clear error for a bad DTO (a field that is not final, a type that is not supported, a rule that does not fit, a bad regex, ...).
- New builder `dox_builder:dtos`. It writes `lib/dtos.g.dart` with every DTO of the app, for `AppConfig(dtos: dtos)`. Two DTOs with the same name stop the build.
- `DtoReader`: the one place that knows DTO keys. The OpenAPI docs use the same keys as the DTO (snake_case by default, `@Name`, `@Dto(keyCase:)`).
- OpenAPI: `@Regex` (was `@Pattern`). `@Format` is removed. Form requests are removed.
- Fix: the OpenAPI route list has the full path, with the `Router` prefix and `Route.group()` prefixes. Two `'/'` routes in two groups now each get their docs.
- OpenAPI path params: every positional argument that is not the request and not a DTO.
- New: `@DoxEnv()` classes get `_$<Class>` in the `.g.dart` part. Each getter is read from the env once, converted to its type (String, int, double, num, bool, Uri, Duration, enum, List<String>) and kept in a final field. A getter body is the default. A nullable getter is optional. `load()` throws one `EnvException` with every missing or bad key.

### 3.0.0-alpha.1

- Version 3 of Dox. All Dox packages now share one version.
- Needs Dart 3.6 or newer.
- See the [release notes](https://github.com/dartondox/dox/pull/112) for all main changes.
- Works with analyzer 5 and 6.

## dox_cache

### 3.0.0-alpha.4

- Version bump only, to match the other packages.

### 3.0.0-alpha.3

- New: `getRaw(key)` gives the stored value as JSON text, with no decode. Use it to send a cached value as a JSON response. Memory and Redis return the stored text as is. A stored String comes back with its quotes (`"bar"`). The stored format did not change, so old values still read the same.
- Faster `get`: a plain store builds the key with no async step. `itemKey` now returns `FutureOr<String>`. Memory `get` costs about 0.6 µs instead of 0.86 µs. Memory `getRaw` costs about 0.3 µs.
- New Redis option `pool_size`: the most connections one store opens (ioredis `maxConnection`). Default is 10, the same as before.
- Uses `ioredis` 2.0.0-alpha.2. It sends all commands on one shared connection and writes them together (auto-pipelining). A Redis read costs much less CPU. The cache now uses one connection per store, so `pool_size` rarely matters.

### 3.0.0-alpha.2

- Needs Dart 3.13 or newer.
- All dependencies updated to their latest versions.

### 3.0.0-alpha.1

- Uses `ioredis` 2. Redis error replies throw `RedisError`.
- Redis: no value size limit by default (was 60 KB). `maxValueBytes` is still there if you want one.
- Redis: `many` uses one `MGET`, `putMany` uses one pipeline, `flush` uses `SCAN` + `DEL` (no Lua).
- First release.
- `CacheManager` with named stores and custom drivers.
- Drivers: memory (with LRU), file, Redis, null.
- `remember`, `pull`, `add`, `increment`, `many`, tags and atomic locks.

## dox

### Unreleased

- Fix: `dox create my_app` without `--version` crashed with a `RangeError`.
- Fix: `dox create` picked the GitHub "latest" template release, which skips pre-releases. During the 3.x alpha that gave the old 2.x template. It now takes the newest template with the same major version as the CLI.
- Fix: `dox env:generate` read `KEY=3000 # note` as text, not as an `int`. A `#` after a space is now a comment.
- Fix: `dox update` ran a plain `dart pub global activate dox`, which skips pre-releases. During the 3.x alpha it installed the old 2.x CLI. It now installs the newest version with the same major version as the CLI, from the pub.dev version list.

### 3.0.0-alpha.4

- Version bump only, to match the other packages.

### 3.0.0-alpha.3

- Version bump only, to match the other packages.

### 3.0.0-alpha.2

- Fix: `dox build` no longer passes `--delete-conflicting-outputs` to build_runner (it was removed and printed a warning).
- Needs Dart 3.13 or newer.
- All dependencies updated to their latest versions.
- `dox build` now runs `dart build cli` (AOT, with build hooks). The output is `build/bundle/`. Start it with `cd build/bundle && ./bin/server`.
- New `dox create:dto <name>`: makes `lib/app/http/dtos/<name>.dto.dart`. `dox create:request` is removed.
- `dox create:controller -r` uses `int id` for the resource methods.
- New `dox openapi:generate [dir]`. It runs the app's `bin/openapi.dart` and writes `openapi.json` and `openapi.yaml` (default `storage/openapi`).
- New `dox env:generate`: makes `lib/config/env.dart` (the typed env class) from `.env.example`.
- New `dox env:check`: loads the typed env and prints every missing or bad key (exit code 1).

### 3.0.0-alpha.1

- Version 3 of Dox. All Dox packages now share one version.
- Needs Dart 3.6 or newer.
- See the [release notes](https://github.com/dartondox/dox/pull/112) for all main changes.
- Generated models import `package:dox_orm/dox_orm.dart`.

## dox_core

### Unreleased

- Fix: CORS `origin` can be a list. Dox compares the request `Origin` with the list and sends back only the origin that matches, or no header. Before, it joined the list with commas, and browsers rejected it. A list also sends `Vary: Origin`.
- Breaking: `AESEncryptor` now uses AES-GCM with a random nonce for each message. Before, it used AES-CTR with an all-zero nonce and no message check. Old encrypted cookies and values can not be read.
- Breaking: `AESEncryptor.decode` throws `DecryptException` (400) when the text was changed or the key is wrong. Before, it printed an error and returned `''`.
- `req.cookie()` returns `null` for an encrypted cookie that can not be decrypted.
- Fix: `Hash.verify` returns `false` for a malformed hash. Before, it threw.
- `AESEncryptor` and `DecryptException` are now exported from `package:dox_core/dox_core.dart`.
- Fix: in `.env`, `KEY=value # note` gave the value `value # note`. A `#` after a space now starts a comment. A `#` inside quotes, or with no space before it, is kept.
- Fix: the `.env` parser removed every quote character inside a value. Now only the quotes around the value are removed.
- Fix: `HEAD` requests got 404, also `HEAD /docs`. A `HEAD` request now runs the `GET` route of the same path. The answer has the status and headers of `GET`, with no body.
- New: Dox listens on `PORT` when `APP_PORT` is not set. Cloud Run, Fly, Render and Heroku set `PORT`. `APP_PORT` still wins.
- New: `AppConfig.host` and the env var `APP_HOST` pick the network interface to listen on, like `127.0.0.1`. The default is the same as before: all interfaces (`::`, IPv6 and IPv4).
- Fix: the start log always said `http://127.0.0.1:<port>`. It now shows the real host and port, like `http://[::]:3000`.
- Removed the unused `sprintf` dependency.
- New: graceful shutdown. On `SIGTERM` or `SIGINT` every isolate stops taking new connections and lets open requests finish, up to `AppConfig.shutdownTimeout` (default 8 seconds). Then Dox runs `DoxShutdown` services and exits with code 0. Before, open requests were cut. A second signal stops at once.
- New: `DoxShutdown`. A service that also implements it gets `shutdown()` in every isolate on stop, to close connections.
- New: `await Dox().stop()` stops the server gracefully in every isolate, without exit.
- Fix: an `s3` storage disk without `bucket`, `key` or `secret` failed with `Null is not a subtype of String`. Now it fails with a clear message that names the missing setting.
- Fix: a URL with no route now answers like a thrown `NotFoundHttpException`. The body is JSON (`{"code": "not_found", "message": "GET /x not found"}`), and the app `responseHandler` runs for it, so apps can format it.
- Fix: the error answer of an `IHttpException` now has its `errorCode`. A text message gives `{"code": "<errorCode>", "message": "<text>"}` as JSON. Before, the body was plain text and `errorCode` was never sent. A `Map` message (like validation errors) is still sent as it is.
- Fix: the `Logger` now reads `LoggerConfig.level`. Lines below that level are not printed. Levels from low to high: `debug`, `info` (and `success`), `warn`, `error` (and `danger`).
- Fix: `Route.group('blogs')` with `Route.get('all')` made `/blogsall`. Path parts now join with one `/`. This also works for nested groups, `Route.prefix` and `Route.resource`.
- Fix: `Route.resource` hid every error from the controller. Now it only skips methods the controller does not have.

### 3.0.0-alpha.4

- Version bump only, to match the other packages.

### 3.0.0-alpha.3

- New: `Cache().getRaw(key)` gives the cached value as JSON text, with no decode. Send it as a JSON response with no extra encode step.
- New Redis cache option `pool_size` (see `dox_cache`).

### 3.0.0-alpha.2

- New default server: `dox_http_native` (Rust hyper parses HTTP, your code stays in Dart). Hello world goes from about 41k to about 144k req/s on one isolate. Set `server: ServerBackend.dartIo` in `AppConfig` (or `DOX_SERVER=dartio`) to use `dart:io`. Dox uses `dart:io` by itself, with one warning line, when the native library does not load, and for apps with WebSocket or Socket.IO routes.
- Faster requests: a simple `GET` hello world went from about 31k to about 40k req/s on one isolate (plain `dart:io` is about 46k). A request with no body and sync middleware and controller now runs with no `Future`. `req.ip()`, the query, `req.all()` and cookies are read on first use only. Reading the client ip was the biggest cost, because it asks the socket. Clean paths skip the two regex calls, and plain routes are found with a map lookup.
- Fix: a `@Dto` body with a `RequestFile` field shows as `multipart/form-data` in the OpenAPI docs.
- Fix: `req.ip()` gave `::ffff:127.0.0.1` for IPv4 clients. Now it gives `127.0.0.1`. The same goes for `X-Forwarded-For` hops.
- Needs Dart 3.13 or newer.
- All dependencies updated to their latest versions.
- Removed the `encrypt` package (not maintained, and it blocked `pointycastle` 4). AES for cookies and the file cache now uses `pointycastle` 4. The output is the same, so old cookies and cache files still decode.
- Fix: `Env.get()` of a missing key with no default gave the text `"null"`. A missing `APP_KEY` became the key `"null"`, which anyone can guess. Now `String` gives `''`, `String?` gives `null`, and `int`/`num`/`double`/`bool` throw a clear error. New: `Env.get<bool>()`.
- Startup stops with an error when `APP_KEY` is empty and `APP_ENV=production`. Other environments log a warning.
- New: typed input with DTOs. A controller asks for a `@Dto` class by type: `store(CreateUser body)`. Dox reads the body (or the query for `GET`), checks it, and answers `422` with `{"items.1.quantity": "..."}` when it is wrong. `await req.validate<T>()` does the same inside a method. See the Validation guide.
- New: `AppConfig(dtos: dtos)` (from `lib/dtos.g.dart`) and `AppConfig(validationMessages:)` for other languages. `req.locale` is the first `Accept-Language`.
- New: typed controller parameters. `DoxRequest` anywhere, one `@Dto`, and `String`, `int`, `double`, `num`, `bool` path params by position. A path param that does not fit its type answers `404`. The types are read once at start; an unknown type stops the server with a clear error.
- New: optional path params `{id?}`.
- New: query strings and form data with repeated keys (`tags=a&tags=b`) and bracket keys (`address[city]`, `items[0][name]`) for DTOs.
- A DTO answers `400` for a body that is not valid JSON, and `415` for a body type it can not read.
- `RequestFile` implements `FileInput` and keeps its first bytes, so `@Mimes` and `@Image` check the real file type.
- Breaking: removed `req.validate(Map)`, `req.validateAsync()`, `FormRequest`, `AppConfig(formRequests:)`, `DoxValidator`, `IocContainer.registerRequest()` and `processInputMapper()`. Use a DTO. `req.validateSchema(schema)` stays for input you only know at runtime.
- Breaking: a controller with more path params than the route has `{...}` params stops the start. Before, the extra ones got `''`.
- Fix: a typed path param like `int id` gave a 500 (it was always a `String`).
- A `ValidationException` from `dox_validation` (for example `schema.parse()` in a controller) answers 422.
- `dox_core` exports `dox_validation` (not its `ValidationException`), with the DTO annotations. `dox_orm` also has `Schema`, and `package:uuid` has `Uuid`: use `hide` or a prefix in a file that needs both.
- Breaking: `Cache()` runs on `dox_cache`. `AppConfig.cache` is a `dox_cache` `CacheConfig(defaultStore:, stores:)` with option maps. `CacheDriverInterface` and `FileCacheDriver` are removed. Values must be JSON types. `put` without a duration keeps the value forever (was 1 hour). New: `add`, `pull`, `increment`, `decrement`, `remember`, `rememberForever`, `lock`, `tags`.
- Breaking: `Storage()` runs on `dox_storage`. `AppConfig.fileStorage` is now `AppConfig.storage` (`StorageConfig(defaultDisk:, disks:)` with option maps for `local`, `s3`, `memory`). `StorageDriverInterface` and `LocalStorageDriver` are removed. An unknown disk name throws.
- `Storage().stream()` and `download()` stream from any disk (S3 too), with `Content-Length`. New: `url`, `signedUrl`, `use()` for the full `Disk`.
- New `Route.files('files')` serves local signed URLs (403 for a bad signature). New catch-all route param `{path*}`.
- OpenAPI: `AppConfig(openApi: OpenApiConfig(...))` adds `/docs`, `/openapi.json` and `/openapi.yaml`. On by default only when `APP_ENV` is development or local. Bodies come from the route `body:` option or a DTO. `Dox().writeOpenApi(dir)` writes the files.
- `RouteData.preMiddleware` now holds the group and router middleware.
- Socket.IO: `AppConfig(socketIo: SocketIoConfig(enabled: true, ...))` serves `/socket.io/` on the app port, before the router. `Route.mount(prefix, handler)` is the raw hook. Off by default.
- No extra work per request when OpenAPI or Socket.IO is off.
- OpenAPI docs are automatic. `dart run build_runner build` writes `lib/openapi.g.dart`. Pass it as `OpenApiConfig(registry: openApiRegistry)`. Each route then gets its summary and description (from the `///` comment), tags, `Class.method` operation id, typed path params, request (a `@Dto` class) and answer schema (from the return type), plus `401`, `404`, `422` and `500`.
- A middleware whose class name ends with `AuthMiddleware` adds `bearerAuth` to the docs, with no config.
- A `GET` or `DELETE` request class becomes query params in the docs.
- `dox_core` exports `OpenApi`, `OpenApiRegistry`, `OpenApiOperation`, `OpenApiRouteBinding` and `ResponseDoc` of `dox_openapi`.
- The OpenAPI JSON and YAML are encoded once and kept, not on each request.
- New `EnvReader` and `EnvException` for the typed env class (`@DoxEnv()`). The real environment wins over `.env`, the same as `Env.get()`. `Env.get()` stays for dynamic keys.
- OpenAPI: `/docs` uses Scalar by default. `OpenApiConfig(ui: DocsUi.swagger)` gives Swagger UI. New `OpenApiConfig` options: `scalar: ScalarOptions(...)` (theme, dark mode, download button, proxy) and `pageTitle`.

### 3.0.0-alpha.1

- Version 3 of Dox. All Dox packages now share one version.
- Needs Dart 3.6 or newer.
- See the [release notes](https://github.com/dartondox/dox/pull/112) for all main changes.
- Faster: streamed bodies, all CPU cores, faster router.
- `uuid` 4 and `mime` 2.

## dox_http_native

### Unreleased

- New: `NativeHttpServer.bind(port, address: ...)` listens on one host, like `HttpServer.bind`. An `InternetAddress` or a host name. With no address it listens on all interfaces, as before. `server.address` is the real address.
- Fix: `close()` never finished when nobody called `listen()` on the server.
- Native ABI 3 (`dox_start` takes the host). Needs a new native library build. Until the next release, the build hook builds it with cargo.
- New: `close()` is graceful, like `dart:io`. The server stops taking connections at once, each open connection closes after its current answer, and the future completes when all are closed. `close(force: true)` closes every connection at once.

### 3.0.0-alpha.4

- Version bump only, to match the other packages.

### 3.0.0-alpha.3

- `DOX_HTTP_THREAD=shared` runs one `dox-http` thread for all isolates.
  Default is still one thread per isolate, which measured faster.
- Less work per request: request headers are read one name at a time,
  answers are not copied again in Rust, one wake per answer batch.
- Native ABI 2 (new header layout in the request record). Needs a new
  native library build.

### 3.0.0-alpha.2

- First release.
- Native HTTP/1.1 server: Rust (hyper, tokio) owns the sockets and parses
  HTTP. Handlers stay in Dart.
- Implements the `dart:io` `HttpServer`, `HttpRequest` and `HttpResponse`
  API, so code written for `dart:io` works unchanged.
- One server per isolate on the same port (`SO_REUSEPORT` on Linux and macOS).
- 400 for bad requests, 431 for big headers, 413 for big bodies.
- The build hook downloads a ready-built library. No Rust needed.

## dox_migration

### Unreleased

- `DATABASE_URL` support. When it is set, it wins over `DB_CONNECTION` and the other `DB_*` keys. Its `sslmode` (Postgres) or `ssl` (MySQL) option turns TLS on.
- A `DB_HOST` that starts with `/` is a Postgres Unix socket folder, like `/cloudsql/project:region:instance` on Cloud Run.
- Migrations read real environment variables too. Before, a `.env` file hid them. Now a real env var wins over `.env`, the same as `Env.get()` of dox_core. An empty value, or `null`, counts as missing.

### 3.0.0-alpha.4

- Version bump only, to match the other packages.

### 3.0.0-alpha.3

- Version bump only, to match the other packages.

### 3.0.0-alpha.2

- Needs Dart 3.13 or newer.
- All dependencies updated to their latest versions.
- `sqlite3` 3 (SQLite is bundled, no system library needed).

### 3.0.0-alpha.1

- Removed the `dox_migration` executable from pubspec (its script was removed before). Use the `dox` CLI.
- Added SQLite: `DB_CONNECTION=sqlite` and `DB_DATABASE=<file path>`.
- MySQL driver is now `mysql_dart` (was `mysql1`). The MySQL 8 default login (`caching_sha2_password`) works.
- `migrate()` and the other commands also take a pool (postgres `Pool`, mysql `MySQLConnectionPool`). Each file runs in one transaction on one connection.
- Breaking: a passed mysql connection must be a `mysql_dart` `MySQLConnection` or `MySQLConnectionPool` (not `mysql1`).
- Needs Dart 3.6 or newer.

### 3.0.0

- Support MySQL. Set `DB_CONNECTION=mysql` in `.env` (default is `postgres`)
- Run each statement of a `.sql` migration one by one, inside a transaction
- Rollback undoes only the last batch, newest first. Add `step`, `reset()` and `refresh()`
- Stop at the first failed migration
- Fix `.sql` parsing: a `-` in the sql no longer cuts the `up` or `down` part
- Fix statement split: `;` inside quotes, comments or `$$` bodies does not split

## dox_mysql_native

### Unreleased

- The hook comment says how to fill the sha256 list from a release: `dart run bin/native_hashes.dart <tag>`. The list stays empty until the first release.

### 3.0.0-alpha.4

- Version bump only, to match the other packages.

### 3.0.0-alpha.3

- Breaking: this package no longer depends on `dox_orm`. `MysqlNativeDriver` moved into `dox_orm`, which now uses it as its default MySQL driver. This package keeps `MysqlNativePool`, with the same API.

### 3.0.0-alpha.2

- First release.
- Native MySQL and MariaDB driver: Rust (mysql_async, tokio) runs the pool
  and a prepared statement cache per connection. Dart gets typed rows.
- `MysqlNativeDriver` plugs into the Dox ORM. The ORM gets the same types
  as with the Dart driver (mysql_dart).
- Works with MySQL 8.4 (caching_sha2_password) and MariaDB 11.
- The build hook downloads a ready-built library. No Rust needed.

## dox_openapi

### 3.0.0-alpha.4

- Version bump only, to match the other packages.

### 3.0.0-alpha.3

- Version bump only, to match the other packages.

### 3.0.0-alpha.2

- A request body with a file field (`format: binary`, also in a list) uses `multipart/form-data` instead of `application/json`, so the `/docs` page can send files. `RouteDoc(bodyMediaType:)` sets it by hand.
- Needs Dart 3.13 or newer.
- All dependencies updated to their latest versions.
- `DoxRouteAdapter` reads `preMiddleware` and `body` from a route when it has them.
- A Dox catch-all param `{path*}` and an optional param `{id?}` become `{path}` and `{id}` in the document.
- `OpenApiOperation.formRequest` is removed (form requests are gone).
- New `OpenApiRegistry`, `OpenApiOperation` and `OpenApiRouteBinding`: the docs that `dox_builder` finds in the code. `OpenApiRegistry.find()` matches them to a live route.
- `RouteDoc` and `ApiDoc.route()` take `deprecated`.
- `OpenApiServer` builds and encodes the document once, on the first call, and keeps it. Make a new `OpenApiServer` after you change the `OpenApi`.
- `OpenApi.yamlEmitter` is now a public field.
- `/docs` uses Scalar (`@scalar/api-reference` 1.75.1) by default. `OpenApiServer(ui: DocsUi.swagger)` gives Swagger UI. `ScalarOptions` sets the theme, dark mode, download button and proxy (off by default). The title and the config are escaped.
- Swagger UI updated to 5.34.0.

### 3.0.0-alpha.1

- First release.
- Build an OpenAPI 3.1 document with `OpenApi` and `ApiDoc`.
- Add undocumented Dox routes with `DoxRouteAdapter`.
- Output as JSON and YAML, write files, serve `/openapi.json`, `/openapi.yaml` and `/docs`.

## dox_orm

### Unreleased

- `DATABASE_URL` support. `ConnectionConfig.fromUrl()` reads `postgres://`, `postgresql://`, `mysql://`, `mariadb://`, `sqlite:` and `file:` urls: url-decoded user and password, host, port, database, `sslmode` and other options (they go to `extra`).
- `DatabaseConfig` has a new `url`. It is `DATABASE_URL` from the environment when not given. When it is set, it wins: it replaces the default connection. Pass `url: ''` to turn it off.
- Postgres Unix sockets. A host that starts with `/` is a socket folder, like `/cloudsql/project:region:instance` on Cloud Run. Works on the native and the Dart driver. Use `?host=/cloudsql/...` in a url.
- Breaking: the finders are typed. On a model, `get()` and `all()` give `Future<List<T>>`, `find()` and `getFirst()` give `Future<T?>`, and `paginate()` gives `Future<Pagination<T>>` (`page.data` is a `List<T>`). `QueryBuilder.table()` gives maps: `get()` is `Future<List<Map<String, dynamic>>>` and `getFirst()` is `Future<Map<String, dynamic>?>`. `QueryBuilder.table()` has no type argument and no second argument any more.
- Breaking: `groupBy()` and `rawQuery()` rows are maps, so use them on `QueryBuilder.table()`. On a model, `get()` throws a `StateError` for them. `count()` with `groupBy()` still works on a model.
- Breaking: the default foreign keys use the model name, like Laravel. A `User` model with `table: 'users'` gives `user_id`, not `users_id`. The default pivot table of `@ManyToMany` also uses the model names (`artist_song`). Keys you set yourself work as before. New `Model.foreignKeyName` gives the default key of a model.
- Breaking: `save()` inserts when the model is new and updates when the row is in the table (`model.exists`). Before, it updated when the primary key was set. So a new model with a key you set yourself, like a UUID, is now inserted.
- `QueryBuilder.query()` has a new `connection` parameter, to run a raw query on a named connection.
- Fix: `withConnection()` did not reach `save()`, `delete()`, `forceDelete()` and `restore()`. They used the default connection. Now they use the connection of the model. Models that a query returns keep the connection of the query, and relation queries use the connection of the parent model. `Model.withConnection()` returns the model, so `Blog()..withConnection('other')` works.

### 3.0.0-alpha.4

- Version bump only, to match the other packages.

### 3.0.0-alpha.3

- Postgres and MySQL/MariaDB now use the native drivers by default (`dox_postgres_native` and `dox_mysql_native`). You do not change any config. If the native library does not load, the ORM uses the Dart driver and prints one warning line. Set `DOX_DB_DRIVER=dart`, or `extra: {'native': false}` on one connection, to use the Dart driver. `driverFactory` still wins over all of this.
- Breaking: `PostgresNativeDriver` and `MysqlNativeDriver` moved into `dox_orm`. Import them from `package:dox_orm/dox_orm.dart`.
- `PostgresNativeDriver.query` does one less async step per query.
- Faster queries on all databases. Each connection keeps its prepared statements (LRU, 100 by default, `extra['preparedStatementCacheSize']`). The same query now has the same sql text, so the statements are reused. `find()` no longer sends `LIMIT 1 OFFSET 0`: LIMIT and OFFSET are only sent when set, and never `OFFSET 0`. Less work per row when models are built. A find by id on SQLite went from 23 µs to 6 µs.
- Less Dart work per query. A plain `find()` builds its SQL once per driver, table and column, and reuses it. A model makes its maps and lists only when they are used. Rows become models without one more `await` when there is nothing to preload. ORM work per `World().find(id)` went from 2.6 µs to 1.0 µs (no database, AOT).
- New `ConnectionConfig.driverFactory`: plug in your own driver class with one line. The default and the named connections use it.

### 3.0.0-alpha.2

- Needs Dart 3.13 or newer.
- All dependencies updated to their latest versions.
- `sqlite3` 3. SQLite is now bundled by a build hook, so no system `libsqlite3` is needed.
- Breaking: `dart compile exe` does not work with build hooks. Use `dart build cli` (or `dox build`).
- SQLite: set `busy_timeout` before `journal_mode = WAL`. Before, many isolates that opened the same file at start could fail with "database is locked".
- New DTO rules `@Unique('users', column: 'email', ignoreParam: 'id')` and `@Exists('teams')`. They run after all other checks. A `List` field is checked with one `WHERE IN` query. Soft-deleted rows count too.

### 3.0.0-alpha.1

- Renamed from `dox_query_builder` to `dox_orm`. Change `package:dox_query_builder/dox_query_builder.dart` to `package:dox_orm/dox_orm.dart`. The old package still works for now: it only re-exports this one.
- Added SQLite (`Driver.sqlite`, package `sqlite3`). `database` is a file path or `:memory:`. Uses WAL, `busy_timeout` and foreign keys. One connection per isolate. See the docs for limits.
- MySQL driver is now `mysql_dart` (was `mysql1`). The MySQL 8 default login (`caching_sha2_password`) works. It uses a real connection pool (`maxConnectionCount`, default 10), prepared statements with bound values, and one pooled connection per transaction.
- Breaking: `extra['characterSet']` (a `mysql1` type) is no longer read. Use `extra['collation']` (default `utf8mb4_general_ci`). `getDatabaseConnection()` for MySQL now returns a `MySQLConnectionPool`.
- Breaking: MySQL `TIME` columns are now a `String` (was a `Duration`). `BLOB` columns are `Uint8List` (was text).
- `ConnectionConfig`: `user`, `password` and `port` are optional (not used by SQLite).
- Needs Dart 3.6 or newer.
- Added `whereNull`, `whereNotNull`, `orWhereNull`, `orWhereNotNull`, `whereNotIn`, `orWhereIn`, `orWhereNotIn` and `selectRaw`.
- Added `QueryBuilder.transaction()`. Postgres now uses a real connection pool (`maxConnectionCount`) and no longer runs each query in its own transaction.
- Added `boolean()` schema column (Postgres `BOOLEAN`, MySQL `TINYINT(1)`, read as `bool`).
- Table and column names are now quoted (`"name"` on Postgres, `` `name` `` on MySQL). On Postgres, quoted names are case sensitive. Use `selectRaw`/`whereRaw` for raw SQL.
- `count()` ignores `limit`, `offset` and `orderBy`. With `groupBy` it now returns the number of groups (before: the size of the first group).
- `save()` can set a field to null on update.
- `insert()` works with any primary key type (uuid strings too).
- `model.delete()` and `model.forceDelete()` only delete that record. Before, they had no where condition.
- `forceDelete()` also deletes soft deleted rows. `withTrash(false)` on a model without soft deletes no longer adds a `deleted_at` filter.
- hasOne, hasMany and manyToMany work with a custom `localKey`.
- `insertMultiple()` uses keys from all rows. Missing keys use the column default.
- MySQL: only JSON columns are decoded (arrays too). MariaDB keeps decoding JSON-like text, because it stores JSON as text.
- Schema: `unique()` on a column that is already unique is skipped. Default values are escaped.

## dox_postgres_native

### Unreleased

- The hook comment says how to fill the sha256 list from a release: `dart run bin/native_hashes.dart <tag>`. The list stays empty until the first release.
- A `host` that starts with `/` is a Unix socket folder (eg. Cloud SQL `/cloudsql/project:region:instance`). A test checks it.

### 3.0.0-alpha.4

- Less work per request. Rust copies a batch of requests once and keeps slices of it, instead of one copy of the SQL and of each parameter. A batch of plain queries uses one timeout timer, not one per query. Dart keeps waiting requests in a list, not a map.

### 3.0.0-alpha.3

- Column names and types are decoded once per result shape. The next result with the same columns reuses them.
- Breaking: this package no longer depends on `dox_orm`. `PostgresNativeDriver` moved into `dox_orm`, which now uses it as its default Postgres driver. This package keeps `PgNativePool`.
- Fix: a request never got an answer in two cases. A value that Dart can
  not decode (eg. a timestamp out of the `DateTime` range) lost every other
  result of the same batch. A request sent to a transaction after its end
  (eg. a second rollback) was dropped. Both now fail with a clear error.
- A request that gets no answer in 5 minutes fails with a timeout error
  (like `queryTimeout` of the `postgres` package). Connect timeout is 15 s.
  A transaction that Dart does not end in 5 minutes is rolled back, so its
  connection goes back to the pool.
- `tool/stress.dart`: a stress test that finds requests that never finish.
- Faster queries. Plain queries now share connections: tokio-postgres
  sends the queries of one connection together (pipelining). One tokio task
  runs each batch from Dart, not one task per query. The SQL bytes are
  cached, and binding named parameters builds no extra `Set`.

### 3.0.0-alpha.2

- First release.
- Native Postgres driver: Rust (tokio-postgres, deadpool-postgres) owns the
  connections. Your code stays in Dart.
- `PostgresNativeDriver` for the Dox ORM. Same types and exceptions as the
  `postgres` package.
- `PgNativePool`: queries, transactions, one pool for many isolates.

## dox_validation

### 3.0.0-alpha.4

- Version bump only, to match the other packages.

### 3.0.0-alpha.3

- Version bump only, to match the other packages.

### 3.0.0-alpha.2

- A JSON body that is not an object now says `The request body must be a JSON object.` (key `_root`). Change it with the message key `_root.object`.
- Needs Dart 3.13 or newer.
- All dependencies updated to their latest versions.
- New: DTOs. A class with `@Dto()` and rule annotations (`@Length`, `@Email`, `@Min`, `@Regex`, `@MaxSize`, ...). `dox_builder` writes a `const DtoSchema<T>` with the checks, a converter and the JSON Schema. See the Validation guide.
- New: `DtoSchema<T>` with `validateMap`, `safeValidateMap`, `fromMap`, `toMap` and `toJsonSchema`. It is also a `Schema<T>`.
- New: `Maybe<T>` knows a missing key from `null`. `DtoErrors` for checks across fields in `validate()`.
- New: `FileTypes` finds the real type of a file from its first bytes. `@Image()` and `v.file().image()` do not allow `svg`.
- New: `MessageRequest.locale`, `ParseState.params`. A message set on a rule is used as it is; the resolver only fills its placeholders.
- `Rule` has a `const` constructor and a `final` `message`, so a rule class works as an annotation. `AsyncRule.failedItems()` checks a list in one call.
- `FileInput` has `length` and `head` (the first bytes).
- `Schema` has a `const` constructor. The fluent schemas extend `BaseSchema`.
- Text length messages say "characters".
- Breaking: removed `v.fromRules()`, `v.registerRule()`, `RuleRegistry`, `RuleDefinition`, `CallbackRule` and all rule strings. Use a DTO, or a `Rule<T>` class.

### 3.0.0-alpha.1

- First release of `dox_validation`.
- Fluent schema builder: string, int, num, bool, date, enum, literal, list, object, map, union, any, file.
- `optional`, `nullable`, `nullish`, `defaultTo`, `transform`, `refine`, `superRefine`, async refinements.
- Coercion with `v.coerce` for query strings and form data.
- `parse`, `safeParse`, `parseAsync`, `safeParseAsync` with issue paths.
- Standard Schema interface (`StandardSchema`).
- JSON Schema (draft 2020-12 / OpenAPI 3.1) export with `toJsonSchema()`.
- Custom `Rule` classes and a global `MessageResolver`.
- Laravel style string rules with `v.fromRules()`.

# Contribute

Source: https://dartondox.dev/latest/3.xothers/contribute/

# Contribute

This page shows how to work on Dox: set up the repo, run the tests, release packages and update the docs.

To send a change, fork the repo and open a pull request.

## Setting up local development

### 1. Clone the repo

```bash
git clone git@github.com:dartondox/dox.git
```

### 2. Install melos

The repo is a [Dart pub workspace](https://dart.dev/tools/pub/workspaces).
The melos config is in the root `pubspec.yaml` (under `melos:`). Use Dart 3.13 or newer.

```bash
dart pub global activate melos
```

### 3. Run melos bootstrap

It runs one `dart pub get` at the root. All local packages are linked.
There is one `pubspec.lock` for the whole repo.

```bash
melos bs
```

### 4. Useful commands

```bash
# Run all tests (not dox_orm and not dox_mysql_native).
# Use `melos run test`. `melos test` is a built-in melos command.
melos run test

# Analyze and check format (same as CI)
melos run analyze
melos run format_check

# Run tests for dox_orm with postgres, mysql or sqlite
DB_PORT=5432 melos run test_pg
DB_USER=dox DB_PORT=3306 melos run test_mysql
melos run test_sqlite

# Build the dox cli executable (AOT).
# `dart compile exe` does not work: sqlite3 has a build hook. Use `dart build cli`.
cd packages/dox-cli
dart build cli --target bin/dox.dart --output build

# Run dox cli executable file
build/bundle/bin/dox --version
```

### If the project does not run

1. Remove `pubspec.lock` and `.dart_tool` at the root.
2. Remove any old `pubspec_overrides.yaml` and `pubspec.lock` in `packages/*` (left from melos 3).
3. Run `melos bs` again.

## Release (maintainers)

The `Release` GitHub workflow (`.github/workflows/publish.yaml`) publishes all public packages to pub.dev.
It runs when you push a tag like `v3.0.0-alpha.4`.
It uses pub.dev automated publishing, so it needs no token or secret.

### Steps

1. Set the new version in the root `pubspec.yaml`, for example `version: 3.0.0-alpha.4`.
2. Run the script.
   ```bash
   bash bin/update_versions.sh
   ```
   It copies the version to every `packages/*/pubspec.yaml`.
   It sets every sibling dependency to `^3.0.0-alpha.4`.
   It also writes the CLI version constant in `packages/dox-cli/lib/src/version.dart`.
3. Add a `## 3.0.0-alpha.4` entry to the `CHANGELOG.md` of each package. pub.dev warns when it is missing.
4. **New package only:** turn on pub.dev automated publishing for it. See [One-time setup](#one-time-setup).
   If you skip this, the Release workflow fails on this package.
   A new package must first exist on pub.dev, so publish its first version by hand with `dart pub publish`.
5. Commit and push.
   ```bash
   git commit -am "release 3.0.0-alpha.4"
   git push
   ```
6. Wait until the `Test` workflow is green for this commit. The Release workflow does not run the tests.
7. Tag and push the tag. This starts the publish.
   ```bash
   git tag v3.0.0-alpha.4
   git push origin v3.0.0-alpha.4
   ```

### What the workflow does

1. It checks that the tag (without `v`) is the root version, and that every package has this version.
   If not, it stops. Run `bin/update_versions.sh` and try again.
2. It gets the publish order from `bin/publish_order.py`.
   The script reads every `packages/*/pubspec.yaml`.
   It puts each package after the sibling packages it depends on (`dependencies` and `dev_dependencies`).
   Packages with `publish_to: none` (like `dox_app`) are left out.
   A new package is picked up by itself.
3. It publishes each package in this order.
   After each one, it waits until `dart pub get` can find the new version. Then the next package can depend on it.

To see the order on your machine:

```bash
python3 bin/publish_order.py
```

A package is skipped when its version is already on pub.dev.
So if a run fails halfway, fix the problem and click "Re-run jobs". It continues where it stopped.

### Dry run

Open Actions > Release > "Run workflow".
It runs `dart pub publish --dry-run` for every package and publishes nothing.
Warnings (for example a missing CHANGELOG entry) show as yellow warnings. They do not fail the run.

### One-time setup

Do this once for each published package, and for every new package before its first tag.
The list of packages is the output of `python3 bin/publish_order.py`.

On pub.dev:

1. Open `https://pub.dev/packages/<name>/admin`.
2. Under "Automated publishing", click "Enable publishing from GitHub Actions".
3. Repository: `dartondox/dox`.
4. Tag pattern: `v{{version}}`.
5. Tick "Require GitHub Actions environment" and set the environment to `pub.dev`.
6. Save.

On GitHub, in `dartondox/dox` > Settings > Environments, there must be an environment named `pub.dev`.
The publish job runs in it.
Optional: add yourself as a required reviewer, and allow only tags `v*`.
The old `PUB_CREDENTIALS` secret is not used any more.

## Docs

The docs site is https://dartondox.dev. It is built with MkDocs Material and
[mike](https://github.com/jimporter/mike). mike keeps one folder per version on the `gh-pages` branch.

| URL | What it is |
| --- | --- |
| `/3.x/...` | 3.x docs, built from `develop` |
| `/latest/...` | a copy of the newest version (now 3.x) |
| `/2.x/...` | the old 2.x docs, built from the `v2.x` branch |
| `/` | redirects to `/latest/` |
| old links like `/the-basic/routing/` | redirect to `/latest/the-basic/routing/` |

### Write and preview

```bash
python3 -m venv .venv
.venv/bin/pip install mkdocs==1.6.1 mkdocs-material==9.7.7 mike==2.2.0
.venv/bin/mkdocs serve           # live preview of this branch
.venv/bin/mkdocs build --strict  # the same check as CI. Broken links fail.
```

### Deploy

- 3.x deploys by itself. The `Docs` workflow (`.github/workflows/docs.yaml`) runs on every push
  to `develop` that changes `docs/`, `mkdocs.yml` or the workflow.
  It runs `mike deploy --update-aliases 3.x latest`.
- 2.x deploys by hand. Open Actions > Docs > "Run workflow", pick version `2.x`.
  It builds from the `v2.x` branch (change it with the `ref` input).
- After each deploy, the workflow writes small redirect pages for the old root links,
  the root `index.html`, a `404.html` and the `CNAME` file. So `dartondox.dev` and old links keep working.
- The workflow pushes with the built-in `GITHUB_TOKEN`. This works because `gh-pages` is not a protected branch.

### Why mike

- Old docs stay online at `/2.x/`, and readers switch with the version menu.
- Each version is built once from its own branch. A new deploy does not touch the other versions.
- Old links from before versioning are kept with redirect pages, so search results and blog posts still work.

### New major version

When 4.x starts, deploy 4.x with `mike deploy --update-aliases 4.x latest`. Keep a `v3.x`
branch, and add `3.x` to the workflow input, so 3.x can still be fixed.
